declarations.name: Systems.MobusSystem.toRichBunge
declarations.doc:
Project a Mobus 8-tuple to a RichConcreteSystem with a 2-element
structure family: {internal edges, external edges}.

This preserves the internal/external distinction that the flat
toBunge discards when it takes their union as totalRelation.
declarations.signature:
Systems.MobusSystem.toRichBunge.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hflow : Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hedge : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) : Systems.RichConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Project a Mobus 8-tuple to a RichConcreteSystem with a 2-element
    structure family: {internal edges, external edges}.

    This preserves the internal/external distinction that the flat
    toBunge discards when it takes their union as totalRelation. -/
def MobusSystem.toRichBunge {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hflow : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hedge : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    RichConcreteSystem α where
  composition := sys.components
  environment := sys.environment.objects
  structureFamily := {sys.internalNetwork.toRelation, sys.externalFlows.toRelation}
  disjoint := sys.disjoint
  family_on := by
    intro R hR p hp
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hR
    rcases hR with rfl | rfl
    · -- Internal network relation: both endpoints in components
      have hon := sys.internalNetwork.toRelation_on p hp
      rw [sys.network_components] at hon
      exact ⟨Set.mem_union_left _ hon.1, Set.mem_union_left _ hon.2⟩
    · -- External flows relation: endpoints in env ∪ interfaces ⊆ env ∪ components
      have hon := sys.externalFlows.toRelation_on p hp
      constructor
      · rcases Set.mem_of_subset_of_mem sys.externalFlows_nodes hon.1 with h | h
        · exact Set.mem_union_right _ h
        · exact Set.mem_union_left _ (sys.interfaces_sub h)
      · rcases Set.mem_of_subset_of_mem sys.externalFlows_nodes hon.2 with h | h
        · exact Set.mem_union_right _ h
        · exact Set.mem_union_left _ (sys.interfaces_sub h)
  bondage_nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hedge
    have hon := sys.internalNetwork.edges_on e he
    rw [sys.network_components] at hon
    exact ⟨e.source, hon.1, e.target, hon.2,
           sys.internalNetwork.no_self_loops e he,
           Or.inl (hflow e he)⟩

declarations.name: Systems.MobusSystem.toRichBunge_flatten_eq
declarations.doc: The flatten of the 2-element family equals the original totalRelation.
declarations.source:
/-- The flatten of the 2-element family equals the original totalRelation. -/
theorem MobusSystem.toRichBunge_flatten_eq {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hf : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    (sys.toRichBunge hf hg).flatten = sys.totalRelation := by
  simp only [RichConcreteSystem.flatten, MobusSystem.toRichBunge,
    MobusSystem.totalRelation, Set.sUnion_pair]

declarations.name: Systems.toRichBunge_preserves_subsystem
declarations.doc:
toRichBunge preserves the Mobus subsystem ordering.
If sys₁ is a Mobus subsystem of sys₂, then their rich projections
stand in the flat subsystem relation.
declarations.source:
/-- toRichBunge preserves the Mobus subsystem ordering.
    If sys₁ is a Mobus subsystem of sys₂, then their rich projections
    stand in the flat subsystem relation. -/
theorem toRichBunge_preserves_subsystem
    {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {sys₁ sys₂ : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ}
    (hf₁ : FlowInducesAction sys₁.internalNetwork)
    (hg₁ : sys₁.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty)
    (hf₂ : FlowInducesAction sys₂.internalNetwork)
    (hg₂ : sys₂.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty)
    (hsub : MobusSubsystem sys₁ sys₂) :
    RichSubsystem_flat (sys₁.toRichBunge hf₁ hg₁) (sys₂.toRichBunge hf₂ hg₂) := by
  refine ⟨hsub.1, hsub.2.1, ?_⟩
  -- Flatten of toRichBunge = totalRelation (by toRichBunge_flatten_eq)
  rw [sys₁.toRichBunge_flatten_eq hf₁ hg₁, sys₂.toRichBunge_flatten_eq hf₂ hg₂]
  exact hsub.2.2

declarations.name: Systems.bridge_factors
declarations.doc:
The bridge factors: toBunge = toRichBunge followed by flatten.
This is the categorical content of Finding 6: the Mobus→Bunge passage
factors through the structure family as Mobus → Rich → Bunge.
declarations.signature:
Systems.bridge_factors.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hf : Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
  sys.toBunge hf hg = (sys.toRichBunge hf hg).toConcreteSystem
declarations.source:
/-- The bridge factors: toBunge = toRichBunge followed by flatten.
    This is the categorical content of Finding 6: the Mobus→Bunge passage
    factors through the structure family as Mobus → Rich → Bunge. -/
theorem bridge_factors {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hf : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    sys.toBunge hf hg = (sys.toRichBunge hf hg).toConcreteSystem := by
  -- Both sides have the same composition and environment.
  -- Structure: LHS is totalRelation, RHS is flatten of {internal, external}.
  -- These are equal by toRichBunge_flatten_eq.
  simp only [MobusSystem.toBunge, RichConcreteSystem.toConcreteSystem,
    MobusSystem.toRichBunge]
  congr 1
  exact (sys.toRichBunge_flatten_eq hf hg).symm

declarations.name: Systems.bridge_factors_functor
declarations.doc:
Restating bridge_factors using the flatten functor:
the object-level factorization holds through flattenFunctor.
declarations.signature:
Systems.bridge_factors_functor.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hf : Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
  sys.toBunge hf hg = Systems.flattenFunctor.obj (sys.toRichBunge hf hg)
declarations.source:
/-- Restating bridge_factors using the flatten functor:
    the object-level factorization holds through flattenFunctor. -/
theorem bridge_factors_functor {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hf : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    sys.toBunge hf hg = flattenFunctor.obj (sys.toRichBunge hf hg) := by
  rw [flattenFunctor_obj]
  exact bridge_factors sys hf hg

declarations.name: Systems.extended_diagram_commutes
declarations.doc:
The extended diagram commutes: Mobus → Rich → Bunge → Klir = Mobus → Klir.
Combines bridge_factors with the original commuting triangle.
declarations.signature:
Systems.extended_diagram_commutes.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hf : Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
  (sys.toRichBunge hf hg).toConcreteSystem.toKlir = sys.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- The extended diagram commutes: Mobus → Rich → Bunge → Klir = Mobus → Klir.
    Combines bridge_factors with the original commuting triangle. -/
theorem extended_diagram_commutes {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hf : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hg : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    (sys.toRichBunge hf hg).toConcreteSystem.toKlir = sys.toKlir := by
  rw [← bridge_factors sys hf hg]
  exact triangle_commutes sys hf hg

declarations.name: klir_relation_self
declarations.doc:
Every self-path at `relation` is the identity.
No arrow in the Klir quiver targets `relation`, so cons is impossible.
declarations.signature:
klir_relation_self (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.relation KlirPosition.relation) :
  p = Quiver.Path.nil
declarations.source:
/-- Every self-path at `relation` is the identity.
No arrow in the Klir quiver targets `relation`, so cons is impossible. -/
theorem klir_relation_self (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.relation KlirPosition.relation) :
    p = Quiver.Path.nil := by
  cases p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons _ e => exact nomatch e

declarations.name: klir_things_self
declarations.doc:
Every self-path at `things` is the identity.
Things is a sink: the only arrow targeting things is `relation_on_things`,
but a path from things through relation back to things would require
an arrow targeting relation, which doesn't exist.
declarations.signature: klir_things_self (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.things KlirPosition.things) : p = Quiver.Path.nil
declarations.source:
/-- Every self-path at `things` is the identity.
Things is a sink: the only arrow targeting things is `relation_on_things`,
but a path from things through relation back to things would require
an arrow targeting relation, which doesn't exist. -/
theorem klir_things_self (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.things KlirPosition.things) :
    p = Quiver.Path.nil := by
  cases p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p e =>
    cases e with
    | relation_on_things =>
      cases p with
      | cons _ e' => exact nomatch e'

declarations.name: klir_hom_unique
declarations.doc:
Every path from `relation` to `things` equals the generating arrow.
Hom(relation, things) is a singleton in the free category.
declarations.signature:
klir_hom_unique (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.relation KlirPosition.things) :
  p = Quiver.Hom.toPath KlirArrow.relation_on_things
declarations.source:
/-- Every path from `relation` to `things` equals the generating arrow.
Hom(relation, things) is a singleton in the free category. -/
theorem klir_hom_unique (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.relation KlirPosition.things) :
    p = Quiver.Hom.toPath KlirArrow.relation_on_things := by
  cases p with
  | cons p e =>
    cases e with
    | relation_on_things =>
      have h := klir_relation_self p
      subst h; rfl

declarations.name: klir_no_path_things_relation
declarations.doc:
There is no path from `things` to `relation`.
Things is a sink: no arrow in the Klir quiver targets `relation`.
declarations.signature: klir_no_path_things_relation (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.things KlirPosition.relation) : False
declarations.source:
/-- There is no path from `things` to `relation`.
Things is a sink: no arrow in the Klir quiver targets `relation`. -/
theorem klir_no_path_things_relation
    (p : Quiver.Path KlirPosition.things KlirPosition.relation) : False := by
  cases p with
  | cons _ e => exact nomatch e

declarations.name: klir_path_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
Every hom-set of `I_Klir` is a subsingleton: the four cases are
`{id}`, `∅`, `{relation_on_things}`, `{id}`.
declarations.signature: klir_path_subsingleton (a b : KlirPosition) (p q : Quiver.Path a b) : p = q
declarations.source:
/-- Every hom-set of `I_Klir` is a subsingleton: the four cases are
`{id}`, `∅`, `{relation_on_things}`, `{id}`. -/
theorem klir_path_subsingleton :
    ∀ (a b : KlirPosition) (p q : Quiver.Path a b), p = q := by
  intro a b p q
  cases a <;> cases b
  · rw [klir_things_self p, klir_things_self q]
  · exact (klir_no_path_things_relation p).elim
  · rw [klir_hom_unique p, klir_hom_unique q]
  · rw [klir_relation_self p, klir_relation_self q]

declarations.name: klirHomSubsingleton
declarations.signature: klirHomSubsingleton (X Y : CategoryTheory.Paths KlirPosition) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y)
declarations.source:
instance klirHomSubsingleton (X Y : Paths KlirPosition) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
  ⟨klir_path_subsingleton X Y⟩

declarations.name: faithful_of_subsingleton_hom
declarations.doc:
A functor out of a thin category is faithful: injectivity on a subsingleton
hom-set is vacuous. This is a property of the *source*, so it holds for every
functor out of `I_Klir` regardless of target.
declarations.source:
/-- A functor out of a thin category is faithful: injectivity on a subsingleton
hom-set is vacuous. This is a property of the *source*, so it holds for every
functor out of `I_Klir` regardless of target. -/
theorem faithful_of_subsingleton_hom {C : Type*} [Category C] {D : Type*} [Category D]
    [∀ X Y : C, Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y)] (F : C ⥤ D) : F.Faithful :=
  ⟨fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩

declarations.name: klir_has_two_elements
declarations.doc:
KlirPosition has exactly 2 elements: any function from a 3-element type
cannot be injective into KlirPosition (pigeonhole).
declarations.signature: klir_has_two_elements (f : Fin 3 → KlirPosition) : ¬Function.Injective f
declarations.source:
/-- KlirPosition has exactly 2 elements: any function from a 3-element type
cannot be injective into KlirPosition (pigeonhole). -/
theorem klir_has_two_elements : ∀ (f : Fin 3 → KlirPosition), ¬ Function.Injective f := by
  intro f hinj
  have h : f 0 = f 1 ∨ f 0 = f 2 ∨ f 1 = f 2 := by
    cases (f 0) <;> cases (f 1) <;> cases (f 2) <;> simp
  rcases h with h | h | h
  · exact absurd (hinj h) (by decide)
  · exact absurd (hinj h) (by decide)
  · exact absurd (hinj h) (by decide)

declarations.name: cyclePow
declarations.doc:
`cyclePow loop n` : the `n`-fold composite of a self-returning path with
itself — the `n`-th power of the loop.
declarations.signature: cyclePow.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V] {v : V} (loop : Quiver.Path v v) : ℕ → Quiver.Path v v
declarations.source:
/-- `cyclePow loop n` : the `n`-fold composite of a self-returning path with
itself — the `n`-th power of the loop. -/
def cyclePow (loop : Quiver.Path v v) : ℕ → Quiver.Path v v
  | 0 => Quiver.Path.nil
  | (n + 1) => (cyclePow loop n).comp loop

declarations.name: cyclePow_length
declarations.doc: The `n`-th power of a loop has length `n * loop.length`.
declarations.signature:
cyclePow_length.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V] {v : V} (loop : Quiver.Path v v) (n : ℕ) :
  (cyclePow loop n).length = n * loop.length
declarations.source:
/-- The `n`-th power of a loop has length `n * loop.length`. -/
theorem cyclePow_length (loop : Quiver.Path v v) (n : ℕ) :
    (cyclePow loop n).length = n * loop.length := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [cyclePow]
  | succ k ih => simp only [cyclePow, Quiver.Path.length_comp, ih, Nat.succ_mul]

declarations.name: cyclePow_injective
declarations.doc:
Distinct powers of a positive-length loop are distinct paths (their
lengths differ).
declarations.signature:
cyclePow_injective.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V] {v : V} (loop : Quiver.Path v v)
  (hlen : loop.length ≠ 0) : Function.Injective (cyclePow loop)
declarations.source:
/-- Distinct powers of a positive-length loop are distinct paths (their
lengths differ). -/
theorem cyclePow_injective (loop : Quiver.Path v v) (hlen : loop.length ≠ 0) :
    Function.Injective (cyclePow loop) := by
  intro a b h
  have := congrArg Quiver.Path.length h
  rw [cyclePow_length, cyclePow_length] at this
  exact Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hlen) this

declarations.name: infinite_path_of_cycle
declarations.doc:
A positive-length self-returning path makes the hom-set `v ⟶ v` of the
free category infinite.
declarations.signature:
infinite_path_of_cycle.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V] {v : V} (loop : Quiver.Path v v)
  (hlen : loop.length ≠ 0) : Infinite (Quiver.Path v v)
declarations.source:
/-- A positive-length self-returning path makes the hom-set `v ⟶ v` of the
free category infinite. -/
theorem infinite_path_of_cycle (loop : Quiver.Path v v) (hlen : loop.length ≠ 0) :
    Infinite (Quiver.Path v v) :=
  Infinite.of_injective (cyclePow loop) (cyclePow_injective loop hlen)

declarations.name: paths_no_faithful_functor_of_cycle
declarations.doc:
**A `Paths` category with a positive-length self-returning cycle admits no
faithful functor into any category with finite hom-sets.** The cycle's powers
make `v ⟶ v` infinite; faithfulness would inject it into the finite hom-set
of the target.

**In `Paths V`, drive hom inference through `Quiver.Path`, never through
object ascription** (`Paths V := V` lets `V`'s own `Quiver` instance shadow
the path category; see `JoslynIncomparability.lean`'s engineering note).
declarations.source:
/-- **A `Paths` category with a positive-length self-returning cycle admits no
faithful functor into any category with finite hom-sets.** The cycle's powers
make `v ⟶ v` infinite; faithfulness would inject it into the finite hom-set
of the target.

**In `Paths V`, drive hom inference through `Quiver.Path`, never through
object ascription** (`Paths V := V` lets `V`'s own `Quiver` instance shadow
the path category; see `JoslynIncomparability.lean`'s engineering note). -/
theorem paths_no_faithful_functor_of_cycle
    (loop : Quiver.Path v v) (hlen : loop.length ≠ 0)
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [∀ X Y : C, Finite (X ⟶ Y)]
    (F : Paths V ⥤ C) : ¬ F.Faithful := by
  intro hF
  haveI := hF
  haveI : Infinite (Quiver.Path v v) := infinite_path_of_cycle loop hlen
  have hmap : Function.Injective (fun p : Quiver.Path v v => F.map p) :=
    fun _ _ h => F.map_injective h
  haveI : Finite (Quiver.Path v v) := Finite.of_injective _ hmap
  exact not_finite (Quiver.Path v v)

declarations.name: BungeDiagram
declarations.doc:
A Bunge diagram is a concrete system equipped with morphism data that allows
it to be interpreted as a functor from the shape category to Type.

The three functions witness the structural dependencies encoded by the shape arrows:
- `proj_comp`: for each structural relation, identify a component it involves
- `proj_env`: for each structural relation, identify an environment element it involves
- `interact`: for each environment element, identify a component it interacts with
declarations.signature: BungeDiagram.{u} (α : Type u) [Systems.ActsOn α] : Type u
declarations.source:
/-- A Bunge diagram is a concrete system equipped with morphism data that allows
it to be interpreted as a functor from the shape category to Type.

The three functions witness the structural dependencies encoded by the shape arrows:
- `proj_comp`: for each structural relation, identify a component it involves
- `proj_env`: for each structural relation, identify an environment element it involves
- `interact`: for each environment element, identify a component it interacts with -/
structure BungeDiagram (α : Type u) [ActsOn α] where
  system : ConcreteSystem α
  proj_comp : ↥system.structure' → ↥system.composition
  proj_env : ↥system.structure' → ↥system.environment
  interact : ↥system.environment → ↥system.composition

declarations.doc:
The prefunctor from the Bunge quiver into the category of types,
determined by a `BungeDiagram`.

Objects map to subtypes of the carrier; each generating arrow maps to
the corresponding projection function provided by the diagram.
declarations.signature: BungeDiagram.pre.{u} {α : Type u} [Systems.ActsOn α] (d : BungeDiagram α) : BungePosition ⥤q Type u
declarations.source:
/-- The prefunctor from the Bunge quiver into the category of types,
determined by a `BungeDiagram`.

Objects map to subtypes of the carrier; each generating arrow maps to
the corresponding projection function provided by the diagram. -/
def BungeDiagram.pre {α : Type u} [ActsOn α] (d : BungeDiagram α) :
    Prefunctor BungePosition (Type u) where
  obj pos := match pos with
    | .composition => ↥d.system.composition
    | .environment => ↥d.system.environment
    | .structure'  => ↥d.system.structure'
  map {X Y} f := match X, Y, f with
    | .structure', .composition, .struct_on_comp => fun x => d.proj_comp x
    | .structure', .environment, .struct_on_env => fun x => d.proj_env x
    | .environment, .composition, .env_acts_on_comp => fun x => d.interact x

declarations.doc:

The internal structure of the flattened system equals the union of
the per-relation internal structures. This is a property of the
flatten functor's action on structure.

/-- Finding 3 restated: flattening preserves internal structure.
    The internal structure of the flattened system equals the union of
    the per-relation internal structures. This is a property of the

    (r : RichConcreteSystem α) :
    (flattenFunctor.obj r).internalStructure =
    ⋃₀ r.internalFamily := by

declarations.name: joslynLoop
declarations.doc:
The single efferent ∘ afferent feedback loop `effector ⟶ effector` —
the generating cycle of Joslyn's shape. Length 2.
declarations.signature: joslynLoop : Quiver.Path JoslynPosition.effector JoslynPosition.effector
declarations.source:
/-- The single efferent ∘ afferent feedback loop `effector ⟶ effector` —
the generating cycle of Joslyn's shape. Length 2. -/
def joslynLoop : Quiver.Path (JoslynPosition.effector) (JoslynPosition.effector) :=
  (Quiver.Path.nil.cons JoslynArrow.efferent).cons JoslynArrow.afferent

instInfinitePathJoslynPositionEffector :

declarations.source:
/-- The feedback hom-set `effector ⟶ effector` is infinite. -/
instance : Infinite (Quiver.Path (JoslynPosition.effector) (JoslynPosition.effector)) :=

declarations.name: joslyn_no_faithful_functor
declarations.signature:
joslyn_no_faithful_functor.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  [∀ (X Y : C), Finite (X ⟶ Y)] (F : CategoryTheory.Functor JoslynShape C) : ¬F.Faithful
declarations.source:
/-- **Joslyn's feedback shape admits no faithful functor into any category with
finite hom-sets.** The feedback loop makes `effector ⟶ effector` infinite;
faithfulness would inject it into the finite hom-set of the target. -/
theorem joslyn_no_faithful_functor
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [∀ X Y : C, Finite (X ⟶ Y)]
    (F : JoslynShape ⥤ C) : ¬ F.Faithful :=
  paths_no_faithful_functor_of_cycle joslynLoop (by simp [joslynLoop_length]) F

declarations.source:
/-- Klir's walking arrow has finite hom-sets: every hom-set is a subsingleton
(`klirHomSubsingleton`, acyclic two-object quiver), and a subsingleton is finite. -/
instance (X Y : KlirShape) : Finite (X ⟶ Y) := Finite.of_subsingleton

declarations.name: no_faithful_joslyn_to_klir
declarations.doc:
**Mapping 001's composed obstruction: no faithful functor Joslyn → Klir.**
The general theorem above, instantiated at the target the atlas's first mapping
argues about. The finite-hom-set hypothesis is discharged by the instance above
rather than by inspection-in-prose — this declaration is what lets the mapping's
evidence code read machine-checked instead of MDHC.

Presentation-relative, as the mapping states: both shapes are encodings of primary
texts as dependency quivers, and a different defensible encoding of Joslyn 1995 —
one that does not make the control loop a cycle at quiver level — could dissolve
the obstruction. Not a maximality result.
declarations.signature: no_faithful_joslyn_to_klir : ¬∃ F, F.Faithful
declarations.source:
/-- **Mapping 001's composed obstruction: no faithful functor Joslyn → Klir.**
The general theorem above, instantiated at the target the atlas's first mapping
argues about. The finite-hom-set hypothesis is discharged by the instance above
rather than by inspection-in-prose — this declaration is what lets the mapping's
evidence code read machine-checked instead of MDHC.

Presentation-relative, as the mapping states: both shapes are encodings of primary
texts as dependency quivers, and a different defensible encoding of Joslyn 1995 —
one that does not make the control loop a cycle at quiver level — could dissolve
the obstruction. Not a maximality result. -/
theorem no_faithful_joslyn_to_klir : ¬ ∃ F : JoslynShape ⥤ KlirShape, F.Faithful := by
  rintro ⟨F, hF⟩
  exact joslyn_no_faithful_functor F hF

declarations.name: myers_path_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
Myers's lens quiver is two arrows out of `state` with no composable pair,
so every hom-set of the free category has at most one element.
declarations.signature: myers_path_subsingleton (a b : MyersPosition) : Subsingleton (Quiver.Path a b)
declarations.source:
/-- Myers's lens quiver is two arrows out of `state` with no composable pair,
so every hom-set of the free category has at most one element. -/
theorem myers_path_subsingleton (a b : MyersPosition) :
    Subsingleton (Quiver.Path a b) := by
  constructor
  intro p q
  cases p with
  | nil =>
    cases q with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons q' f =>
      cases f with
      | expose => cases q' with | cons q'' g => cases g
      | update => cases q' with | cons q'' g => cases g
  | cons p' e =>
    cases e with
    | expose =>
      cases p' with
      | nil =>
        cases q with
        | cons q' f =>
          cases f with
          | expose => cases q' with | nil => rfl | cons q'' g => cases g
      | cons p'' e' => cases e'
    | update =>
      cases p' with
      | nil =>
        cases q with
        | cons q' f =>
          cases f with
          | update => cases q' with | nil => rfl | cons q'' g => cases g
      | cons p'' e' => cases e'

declarations.name: instSubsingletonHomPathsMyersPosition
declarations.signature:
instSubsingletonHomPathsMyersPosition (X Y : CategoryTheory.Paths MyersPosition) :
  Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y)
declarations.source:
instance (X Y : Paths MyersPosition) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
  myers_path_subsingleton X Y

declarations.name: myersToSpivak_faithful
declarations.doc:
**The commitments-ladder inclusion `I_Myers → I_Spivak` is faithful.**
Distinct Myers paths between the same endpoints map to distinct Spivak paths:
the ladder inclusion is an embedding, not merely a functor.
declarations.signature: myersToSpivak_faithful : myersToSpivak.Faithful
declarations.source:
/-- **The commitments-ladder inclusion `I_Myers → I_Spivak` is faithful.**
Distinct Myers paths between the same endpoints map to distinct Spivak paths:
the ladder inclusion is an embedding, not merely a functor. -/
theorem myersToSpivak_faithful : myersToSpivak.Faithful :=
  faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _

declarations.source:
/-- Flat subsystem ordering on FlatOrd. -/

  le r₁ r₂ := RichSubsystem_flat r₁.val r₂.val
  le_refl _ := ⟨Set.Subset.refl _, Set.Subset.refl _, Set.Subset.refl _⟩
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁₂ h₂₃ :=
    ⟨h₁₂.1.trans h₂₃.1, h₂₃.2.1.trans h₁₂.2.1, h₁₂.2.2.trans h₂₃.2.2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.instPreorderRefinementOrd
declarations.doc: Refinement subsystem ordering: ∀ R₁ ∈ F₁, ∃ R₂ ∈ F₂, R₁ ⊆ R₂.
declarations.signature:
Systems.instPreorderRefinementOrd.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Preorder (Systems.RefinementOrd α)
declarations.source:
/-- Refinement subsystem ordering: ∀ R₁ ∈ F₁, ∃ R₂ ∈ F₂, R₁ ⊆ R₂. -/
instance instPreorderRefinementOrd {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    Preorder (RefinementOrd α) where
  le r₁ r₂ := RichSubsystem_refinement r₁.val r₂.val
  le_refl _ :=
    ⟨Set.Subset.refl _, Set.Subset.refl _,
     fun R hR => ⟨R, hR, Set.Subset.refl _⟩⟩
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁₂ h₂₃ :=
    ⟨h₁₂.1.trans h₂₃.1, h₂₃.2.1.trans h₁₂.2.1,
     fun R₁ hR₁ => by
       obtain ⟨R₂, hR₂, h₁₂'⟩ := h₁₂.2.2 R₁ hR₁
       obtain ⟨R₃, hR₃, h₂₃'⟩ := h₂₃.2.2 R₂ hR₂
       exact ⟨R₃, hR₃, h₁₂'.trans h₂₃'⟩⟩

declarations.source:
/-- forgetRefinement is NOT full.
    Witness: sys_merged ≤_flat sys_split but ¬ (sys_merged ≤_ref sys_split).
    There is a morphism in FlatOrd with no preimage in RefinementOrd. -/
theorem not_full_forgetRefinement :
    ¬ (forgetRefinement (α := Fin 2)).Full := by
  intro ⟨hsurj⟩
  -- A morphism in FlatOrd from flat_holds
  have hmor : forgetRefinement.obj ⟨sys_merged⟩ ⟶ forgetRefinement.obj ⟨sys_split⟩ :=
    homOfLE flat_holds
  -- Surjectivity gives a preimage in RefinementOrd
  obtain ⟨g, _⟩ := hsurj hmor
  -- leOfHom extracts the refinement ordering, contradicting refinement_fails
  exact refinement_fails (leOfHom g)

declarations.name: Systems.not_full_forgetFamily
declarations.doc:
forgetFamily is NOT full.
Witness: sys_small ≤_ref sys_merged but ¬ (sys_small ≤_fam sys_merged).
There is a morphism in RefinementOrd with no preimage in FamilyOrd.
declarations.signature: Systems.not_full_forgetFamily : ¬Systems.forgetFamily.Full
declarations.source:
/-- forgetFamily is NOT full.
    Witness: sys_small ≤_ref sys_merged but ¬ (sys_small ≤_fam sys_merged).
    There is a morphism in RefinementOrd with no preimage in FamilyOrd. -/
theorem not_full_forgetFamily :
    ¬ (forgetFamily (α := Fin 2)).Full := by
  intro ⟨hsurj⟩
  have hmor : forgetFamily.obj ⟨sys_small⟩ ⟶ forgetFamily.obj ⟨sys_merged⟩ :=
    homOfLE refinement_small_merged
  obtain ⟨g, _⟩ := hsurj hmor
  exact family_small_merged_fails (leOfHom g)

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.Conjugate
declarations.doc:
Rosen's conjugacy (p. 185, diagram 7.10.2): a commuting square whose
vertical legs are equivalences.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.Conjugate.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B A' B' : C} (f : A ⟶ B) (f' : A' ⟶ B') : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Rosen's conjugacy (p. 185, diagram 7.10.2): a commuting square whose
vertical legs are equivalences. -/
def Conjugate {A B A' B' : C} (f : A ⟶ B) (f' : A' ⟶ B') : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : A ≅ A') (β : B ≅ B'), f ≫ β.hom = α.hom ≫ f'

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.conjugate_iff_iso
declarations.doc: Conjugacy is isomorphism in the arrow category.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.conjugate_iff_iso.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B A' B' : C} (f : A ⟶ B) (f' : A' ⟶ B') :
  Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f f' ↔ Nonempty (CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk f ≅ CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk f')
declarations.source:
/-- Conjugacy is isomorphism in the arrow category. -/
theorem conjugate_iff_iso {A B A' B' : C} (f : A ⟶ B) (f' : A' ⟶ B') :
    Conjugate f f' ↔ Nonempty (Arrow.mk f ≅ Arrow.mk f') := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨α, β, w⟩
    exact ⟨Arrow.isoMk' f f' α β w.symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨e⟩
    refine ⟨Arrow.leftFunc.mapIso e, Arrow.rightFunc.mapIso e, ?_⟩
    exact (Arrow.w e.hom).symm

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.conjugate_refl
declarations.doc:
"Conjugacy imposes an equivalence relation on the set of all mappings in
the category" (p. 186) — on arrows as objects of C^→.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.conjugate_refl.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B) : Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f f
declarations.source:
/-- "Conjugacy imposes an equivalence relation on the set of all mappings in
the category" (p. 186) — on arrows as objects of C^→. -/
theorem conjugate_refl {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B) : Conjugate f f :=
  (conjugate_iff_iso f f).2 ⟨Iso.refl _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.conjugate_symm
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.conjugate_symm.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B A' B' : C} {f : A ⟶ B} {f' : A' ⟶ B'} (h : Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f f') :
  Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f' f

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.conjugate_trans
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.conjugate_trans.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B A' B' A'' B'' : C} {f : A ⟶ B} {f' : A' ⟶ B'} {f'' : A'' ⟶ B''}
  (h₁ : Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f f') (h₂ : Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f' f'') :
  Systems.Rosen.Conjugate f f''

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.conjugate_equivalence
declarations.doc: The relation as a `Setoid`-shaped statement, for the record.
declarations.source:
/-- The relation as a `Setoid`-shaped statement, for the record. -/
theorem conjugate_equivalence :
    Equivalence (fun (x y : Arrow C) => Conjugate x.hom y.hom) :=
  ⟨fun x => conjugate_refl x.hom, conjugate_symm, conjugate_trans⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.collapse
declarations.doc: The collapse `Bool → Unit` as a morphism of `Type`.
declarations.signature: Systems.Rosen.collapse : Bool ⟶ Unit
declarations.source:
/-- The collapse `Bool → Unit` as a morphism of `Type`. -/
def collapse : (Bool : Type) ⟶ Unit := fun _ => ()

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.collapseSquare
declarations.doc:
The square: top the collapse, bottom `𝟙 Unit`, left leg the collapse. A
morphism of the arrow category with a non-invertible leg.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.collapseSquare :
  CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk Systems.Rosen.collapse ⟶
    CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id Unit)
declarations.source:
/-- The square: top the collapse, bottom `𝟙 Unit`, left leg the collapse. A
morphism of the arrow category with a non-invertible leg. -/
def collapseSquare : Arrow.mk collapse ⟶ Arrow.mk (𝟙 Unit) where
  left := collapse
  right := 𝟙 Unit
  w := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Rosen.square_not_conjugate
declarations.doc: It is not a conjugacy: no isomorphism `Bool ≅ Unit` exists in `Type`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Rosen.square_not_conjugate :
  ¬Systems.Rosen.Conjugate Systems.Rosen.collapse (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id Unit)
declarations.source:
/-- It is not a conjugacy: no isomorphism `Bool ≅ Unit` exists in `Type`. -/
theorem square_not_conjugate : ¬ Conjugate collapse (𝟙 Unit) := by
  rintro ⟨α, -, -⟩
  -- `α.hom true` and `α.hom false` are definitionally equal in `Unit`.
  have ht : α.inv (α.hom true) = true := congrFun α.hom_inv_id true
  have hf : α.inv (α.hom false) = false := congrFun α.hom_inv_id false
  exact absurd (ht.symm.trans hf) (by decide)

declarations.name: positionEquiv
declarations.doc: The positions correspond: elements ↔ things, interrelation ↔ relation.
declarations.signature: positionEquiv : BertalanffyPosition ≃ KlirPosition
declarations.source:
/-- The positions correspond: elements ↔ things, interrelation ↔ relation. -/
def positionEquiv : BertalanffyPosition ≃ KlirPosition where
  toFun := fun p => match p with
    | .elements => .things
    | .interrelation => .relation
  invFun := fun p => match p with
    | .things => .elements
    | .relation => .interrelation
  left_inv := by intro a; cases a <;> rfl
  right_inv := by intro a; cases a <;> rfl

*the interrelation depends on the environment*. -/

  | interrelation_on_elements : Bertalanffy72Arrow .interrelation .elements
  | interrelation_on_environment : Bertalanffy72Arrow .interrelation .environment

declarations.name: Bertalanffy72Shape
declarations.doc:
The shape category for the 1972 definition: three objects, two arrows radiating from
`interrelation`. The span `• ← • → •`.

Structurally this is the same span as `MesarovicShape` (Def 1.4, `globalState → input`,
`globalState → output`) — and the coincidence is worth naming rather than hiding, because the
readings are unrelated: Mesarović's arrows are projections of a response function, and these
are two clauses of one English sentence about what a relation holds between. Shape identity is
not semantic identity; see the predicate-gap caveat at the head of this file.

declarations.name: bert68To72Pre
declarations.doc:
The revision as a functor: everything the 1968 definition committed to is still committed
to in 1972, and the environment arrow is what was added. Injective on objects, so 1968 sits
inside 1972 as a proper subshape rather than being re-encoded.
declarations.signature: bert68To72Pre : BertalanffyPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths Bertalanffy72Position
declarations.source:
/-- The revision as a functor: everything the 1968 definition committed to is still committed
to in 1972, and the environment arrow is what was added. Injective on objects, so 1968 sits
inside 1972 as a proper subshape rather than being re-encoded. -/
def bert68To72Pre : Prefunctor BertalanffyPosition (Paths Bertalanffy72Position) where
  obj := fun p => match p with
    | .elements => .elements
    | .interrelation => .interrelation
  map := fun a => match a with
    | .interrelation_on_elements =>
        Quiver.Hom.toPath Bertalanffy72Arrow.interrelation_on_elements

declarations.name: bert68To72_obj_injective
declarations.signature: bert68To72_obj_injective : Function.Injective bert68To72Pre.obj
declarations.source:
theorem bert68To72_obj_injective : Function.Injective bert68To72Pre.obj := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [bert68To72Pre]

declarations.name: environment_is_new
declarations.doc:
What the revision added, stated as the thing the 1968 shape cannot reach: no position of
the 1968 quiver maps onto `environment`.
declarations.signature:
environment_is_new (p : BertalanffyPosition) :
  bert68To72Pre.obj p ≠ Bertalanffy72Position.environment
declarations.source:
/-- What the revision added, stated as the thing the 1968 shape cannot reach: no position of
the 1968 quiver maps onto `environment`. -/
theorem environment_is_new (p : BertalanffyPosition) :
    bert68To72Pre.obj p ≠ Bertalanffy72Position.environment := by
  cases p <;> simp [bert68To72Pre]

declarations.name: bertalanffy72_has_fork
declarations.doc:
The 1972 quiver HAS a fork — out-degree two at `interrelation`. This is the permissive
property; it is exhibited so the audit is a fact rather than a claim.
declarations.signature: bertalanffy72_has_fork : ∃ x y z x_1 x, y ≠ z
declarations.source:
/-- The 1972 quiver HAS a fork — out-degree two at `interrelation`. This is the permissive
property; it is exhibited so the audit is a fact rather than a claim. -/
theorem bertalanffy72_has_fork :
    ∃ (x y z : Bertalanffy72Position) (_ : Bertalanffy72Arrow x y) (_ : Bertalanffy72Arrow x z),
      y ≠ z :=
  ⟨.interrelation, .elements, .environment,
   .interrelation_on_elements, .interrelation_on_environment, by simp⟩

declarations.name: bertalanffy72_in_degree_le_one
declarations.doc: No cofork: every vertex still has in-degree at most one.

  (f : Bertalanffy72Arrow b c) : a = b
declarations.source:
/-- No cofork: every vertex still has in-degree at most one. -/
theorem bertalanffy72_in_degree_le_one {a b c : Bertalanffy72Position}
    (e : Bertalanffy72Arrow a c) (f : Bertalanffy72Arrow b c) : a = b := by
  cases e <;> cases f <;> rfl

declarations.name: bertalanffy72_no_composable

sinks, so no two edges compose.

bertalanffy72_no_composable {a b c : Bertalanffy72Position} (e : Bertalanffy72Arrow a b)
  (f : Bertalanffy72Arrow b c) : False
declarations.source:
/-- No two-chain: both arrows leave `interrelation`, and `elements` and `environment` are
sinks, so no two edges compose. -/
theorem bertalanffy72_no_composable {a b c : Bertalanffy72Position}
    (e : Bertalanffy72Arrow a b) (f : Bertalanffy72Arrow b c) : False := by
  cases e <;> cases f

declarations.name: bertalanffy72_no_parallel

declarations.name: BungeArrow
declarations.doc:
Generating morphisms for the Bunge shape quiver.

Each arrow encodes a structural dependency from Bunge Def 1.2:
- `struct_on_comp`: S is defined over C (Def 1.2iii: "relations among the components")
- `struct_on_env`: S is defined over E (Def 1.2iii: "among them and things in the environment")
- `env_acts_on_comp`: E constrains C (Def 1.2ii: things that "act on or are acted on by components")
declarations.signature: BungeArrow : BungePosition → BungePosition → Type
declarations.source:
/-- Generating morphisms for the Bunge shape quiver.

Each arrow encodes a structural dependency from Bunge Def 1.2:
- `struct_on_comp`: S is defined over C (Def 1.2iii: "relations among the components")
- `struct_on_env`: S is defined over E (Def 1.2iii: "among them and things in the environment")
- `env_acts_on_comp`: E constrains C (Def 1.2ii: things that "act on or are acted on by components")
-/
inductive BungeArrow : BungePosition → BungePosition → Type
  | struct_on_comp : BungeArrow .structure' .composition
  | struct_on_env : BungeArrow .structure' .environment
  | env_acts_on_comp : BungeArrow .environment .composition

These correspond to two genuinely different structural dependencies in Bunge's theory.

Embedding `I_Klir` into `I_CDL`: relation ↦ parameter, things ↦ output. The
weights are the relation, as in the Myers row where the state is.
declarations.signature: klirToCDLPre : KlirPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths CDLPosition

/-- Embedding `I_Klir` into `I_CDL`: relation ↦ parameter, things ↦ output. The
weights are the relation, as in the Myers row where the state is. -/

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.klirToCDLQuiver
declarations.doc: The Klir arrow embeds at the quiver level: edge to edge, injective on vertices.
declarations.signature: SharedPrimitive.klirToCDLQuiver : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding KlirPosition CDLPosition
declarations.source:
/-- The Klir arrow embeds at the quiver level: edge to edge, injective on vertices. -/
def klirToCDLQuiver : QuiverEmbedding KlirPosition CDLPosition where
  toPre :=
    { obj := fun | .things => .output | .relation => .parameter
      map := fun | .relation_on_things => CDLArrow.apply_parameter }
  obj_inj := by intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all
  map_inj := by
    intro x y e f _
    cases e; cases f; rfl

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.cdl_out_degree_le_one
declarations.doc: Every vertex of the parametric-map quiver has out-degree at most one.
declarations.signature: SharedPrimitive.cdl_out_degree_le_one {a b c : CDLPosition} (e : a ⟶ b) (f : a ⟶ c) : b = c
declarations.source:
/-- Every vertex of the parametric-map quiver has out-degree at most one. -/
theorem cdl_out_degree_le_one {a b c : CDLPosition} (e : a ⟶ b) (f : a ⟶ c) :
    b = c := by
  cases e <;> cases f <;> rfl

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.cdl_has_cofork
declarations.doc:
The parametric-map quiver has a cofork: two distinct sources, one target. It
therefore cannot replace Willems.
declarations.signature: SharedPrimitive.cdl_has_cofork : ∃ x y z x_1 x_2, x ≠ y
declarations.source:
/-- The parametric-map quiver has a cofork: two distinct sources, one target. It
therefore cannot replace Willems. -/
theorem cdl_has_cofork :
    ∃ (x y z : CDLPosition) (_ : x ⟶ z) (_ : y ⟶ z), x ≠ y :=
  ⟨.parameter, .input, .output, CDLArrow.apply_parameter, CDLArrow.apply_input,
    by decide⟩

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.no_fork_cdl
declarations.doc: No fork, from the parametric-map shape alone.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.no_fork_cdl.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eC : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V CDLPosition) {x y z : V} (e : x ⟶ y) (f : x ⟶ z) : y = z
declarations.source:
/-- No fork, from the parametric-map shape alone. -/
theorem no_fork_cdl (eC : QuiverEmbedding V CDLPosition) {x y z : V}
    (e : x ⟶ y) (f : x ⟶ z) : y = z :=
  eC.obj_inj (cdl_out_degree_le_one (eC.toPre.map e) (eC.toPre.map f))

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.zigzag_confined_cdl
declarations.doc: `zigzag_confined` with the parametric-map shape in place of Joslyn.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.zigzag_confined_cdl.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eC : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V CDLPosition)
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) {w : V} :
  SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x w → w = x ∨ w = y
declarations.source:
/-- `zigzag_confined` with the parametric-map shape in place of Joslyn. -/
theorem zigzag_confined_cdl (eC : QuiverEmbedding V CDLPosition)
    (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) :
    ∀ {w : V}, Zigzag x w → w = x ∨ w = y := by
  intro w hw
  induction hw with
  | refl => exact Or.inl rfl
  | fwd _ g ih =>
      rcases ih with rfl | rfl
      · exact Or.inr (no_fork_cdl eC e g).symm
      · exact (no_two_chain eW e g).elim
  | bwd _ g ih =>
      rcases ih with rfl | rfl
      · exact (no_two_chain eW g e).elim
      · exact Or.inl (no_cofork eW e g).symm

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.connected_is_single_arrow_cdl
declarations.doc:
**A parametric map can stand in for Joslyn.** A connected quiver embedding into
the parametric-map and Willems shapes, with at least one edge, has exactly two
vertices and exactly one edge.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.connected_is_single_arrow_cdl.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eC : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V CDLPosition)
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition)
  (conn : ∀ (a b : V), SharedPrimitive.Zigzag a b) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) :
  x ≠ y ∧ (∀ (w : V), w = x ∨ w = y) ∧ ∀ (u v : V) (x_1 : u ⟶ v), u = x ∧ v = y
declarations.source:
/-- **A parametric map can stand in for Joslyn.** A connected quiver embedding into
the parametric-map and Willems shapes, with at least one edge, has exactly two
vertices and exactly one edge. -/
theorem connected_is_single_arrow_cdl
    (eC : QuiverEmbedding V CDLPosition) (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition)
    (conn : ∀ a b : V, Zigzag a b) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) :
    x ≠ y ∧ (∀ w : V, w = x ∨ w = y) ∧ ∀ (u v : V) (_ : u ⟶ v), u = x ∧ v = y := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun w => zigzag_confined_cdl eC eW e (conn x w), ?_⟩
  · rintro rfl; exact no_loop eW e
  · intro u v f
    rcases zigzag_confined_cdl eC eW e (conn x u) with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨rfl, (no_fork_cdl eC e f).symm⟩
    · exact (no_two_chain eW e f).elim

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.tied_no_embedding_into_cdl
declarations.doc:
The tied shape does not embed into the untied cell, so the forcing property
of `connected_is_single_arrow_cdl` is a property of untied cells only.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.tied_no_embedding_into_cdl :
  ¬Nonempty (SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding SharedPrimitive.TiedPosition CDLPosition)
declarations.source:
/-- The tied shape does not embed into the untied cell, so the forcing property
of `connected_is_single_arrow_cdl` is a property of untied cells only. -/

  rintro ⟨eC⟩
  have := no_fork_cdl eC TiedArrow.apply_parameter₁ TiedArrow.apply_parameter₂
  exact absurd this (by decide)

declarations.name: comparisonObj
declarations.doc:
Object-level comparison: where each Mobus position lands in the Bunge schema.

Follows the `toBunge` bridge map:
- `components → composition` and `environment → environment` are canonical
- `internalNetwork, externalFlows → structure'` (both contribute to `totalRelation`)
- `boundary → composition` (interfaces are a subset of components)
- `transforms, history, timeScale → composition` (no Bunge counterpart; parametric discard)
declarations.signature: comparisonObj : MobusPosition → BungePosition
declarations.source:
/-- Object-level comparison: where each Mobus position lands in the Bunge schema.

Follows the `toBunge` bridge map:
- `components → composition` and `environment → environment` are canonical
- `internalNetwork, externalFlows → structure'` (both contribute to `totalRelation`)
- `boundary → composition` (interfaces are a subset of components)
- `transforms, history, timeScale → composition` (no Bunge counterpart; parametric discard)
-/
def comparisonObj : MobusPosition → BungePosition
  | .components       => .composition
  | .environment      => .environment
  | .internalNetwork  => .structure'
  | .externalFlows    => .structure'
  | .boundary         => .composition
  | .transforms       => .composition
  | .history          => .composition
  | .timeScale        => .composition

declarations.name: comparisonPre
declarations.doc:
The comparison as a prefunctor into the Bunge path category.

Each generating Mobus arrow maps to either a length-1 path (a generating Bunge arrow)
or a length-0 path (identity, when source and target collapse to the same Bunge position).
declarations.signature: comparisonPre : MobusPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths BungePosition
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison as a prefunctor into the Bunge path category.

Each generating Mobus arrow maps to either a length-1 path (a generating Bunge arrow)
or a length-0 path (identity, when source and target collapse to the same Bunge position).
-/
def comparisonPre : Prefunctor MobusPosition (Paths BungePosition) where
  obj := comparisonObj
  map := fun
    | .network_on_components    => Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_comp
    | .interfaces_in_components => Quiver.Path.nil
    | .external_on_env          => Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_env
    | .external_on_boundary     => Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_comp
    | .env_disjoint_comp        => Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.env_acts_on_comp

declarations.name: comparisonFunctor
declarations.doc:
The comparison functor from I_Mobus to I_Bunge, constructed via the universal property
of the free category. Any prefunctor from a quiver into a category lifts uniquely to a
functor from the path category.
declarations.signature:
comparisonFunctor :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Paths MobusPosition) (CategoryTheory.Paths BungePosition)
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison functor from I_Mobus to I_Bunge, constructed via the universal property
of the free category. Any prefunctor from a quiver into a category lifts uniquely to a
functor from the path category. -/
def comparisonFunctor : Paths MobusPosition ⥤ Paths BungePosition :=
  Paths.lift comparisonPre

declarations.name: comparisonFunctor_obj
declarations.signature: comparisonFunctor_obj (p : MobusPosition) : comparisonFunctor.obj p = comparisonObj p
declarations.source:
theorem comparisonFunctor_obj (p : MobusPosition) :
    comparisonFunctor.obj p = comparisonObj p := rfl

declarations.name: obj_collapse_network_external
declarations.doc: Spatial factoring: internal network and external flows both map to structure.
declarations.signature:
obj_collapse_network_external :
  comparisonObj MobusPosition.internalNetwork = comparisonObj MobusPosition.externalFlows
declarations.source:
/-- Spatial factoring: internal network and external flows both map to structure. -/
theorem obj_collapse_network_external :
    comparisonObj .internalNetwork = comparisonObj .externalFlows := rfl

declarations.name: obj_collapse_boundary
declarations.doc: Boundary collapses into composition (interfaces ⊆ components).
declarations.signature:
obj_collapse_boundary :
  comparisonObj MobusPosition.boundary = comparisonObj MobusPosition.components
declarations.source:
/-- Boundary collapses into composition (interfaces ⊆ components). -/
theorem obj_collapse_boundary :
    comparisonObj .boundary = comparisonObj .components := rfl

declarations.name: obj_collapse_parametric
declarations.doc: Temporal discarding: transforms, history, and timeScale all collapse to composition.
declarations.signature:
obj_collapse_parametric :
  comparisonObj MobusPosition.transforms = comparisonObj MobusPosition.history ∧
    comparisonObj MobusPosition.history = comparisonObj MobusPosition.timeScale ∧
      comparisonObj MobusPosition.timeScale = comparisonObj MobusPosition.components
declarations.source:
/-- Temporal discarding: transforms, history, and timeScale all collapse to composition. -/
theorem obj_collapse_parametric :
    comparisonObj .transforms = comparisonObj .history ∧
    comparisonObj .history = comparisonObj .timeScale ∧
    comparisonObj .timeScale = comparisonObj .components :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

declarations.name: arrow_collapse
declarations.doc:
Arrow collapse: two distinct Mobus arrows map to the same Bunge path.
`network_on_components` (N → C) and `external_on_boundary` (G → B) both become
`struct_on_comp` (S → C) in the Bunge shape.
declarations.signature:
arrow_collapse :
  comparisonPre.map MobusArrow.network_on_components =
    comparisonPre.map MobusArrow.external_on_boundary
declarations.source:
/-- Arrow collapse: two distinct Mobus arrows map to the same Bunge path.
`network_on_components` (N → C) and `external_on_boundary` (G → B) both become
`struct_on_comp` (S → C) in the Bunge shape. -/
theorem arrow_collapse :
    comparisonPre.map MobusArrow.network_on_components =
    comparisonPre.map MobusArrow.external_on_boundary := rfl

declarations.name: arrow_annihilated
declarations.doc:
Arrow annihilation: `interfaces_in_components` (B → C) maps to the identity path.
Both source (boundary) and target (components) map to `composition`, so the dependency
arrow is absorbed into the identity.
declarations.signature: arrow_annihilated : comparisonPre.map MobusArrow.interfaces_in_components = Quiver.Path.nil
declarations.source:
/-- Arrow annihilation: `interfaces_in_components` (B → C) maps to the identity path.
Both source (boundary) and target (components) map to `composition`, so the dependency
arrow is absorbed into the identity. -/
theorem arrow_annihilated :
    comparisonPre.map MobusArrow.interfaces_in_components = Quiver.Path.nil := rfl

declarations.name: comparisonObj_not_injective
declarations.doc:
The comparison is not injective on objects. This is the categorical content of
information loss: the Bunge schema cannot distinguish fields that Mobus keeps separate.
declarations.signature: comparisonObj_not_injective : ¬Function.Injective comparisonObj
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison is not injective on objects. This is the categorical content of
information loss: the Bunge schema cannot distinguish fields that Mobus keeps separate. -/
theorem comparisonObj_not_injective : ¬ Function.Injective comparisonObj := by
  intro h
  exact absurd (h (show comparisonObj .internalNetwork = comparisonObj .externalFlows from rfl))
    (by exact MobusPosition.noConfusion)

declarations.name: fiber_composition
declarations.doc:
Fiber over `composition`: 5 Mobus positions collapse here.
Corresponds to Bridge.lean categories #3 (boundary), #4 (transforms), #5 (history), #6 (timeScale),
plus the canonical `components` mapping.
declarations.signature:
fiber_composition (p : MobusPosition) :
  comparisonObj p = BungePosition.composition ↔
    p = MobusPosition.components ∨
      p = MobusPosition.boundary ∨
        p = MobusPosition.transforms ∨ p = MobusPosition.history ∨ p = MobusPosition.timeScale
declarations.source:
/-- Fiber over `composition`: 5 Mobus positions collapse here.
Corresponds to Bridge.lean categories #3 (boundary), #4 (transforms), #5 (history), #6 (timeScale),
plus the canonical `components` mapping. -/
theorem fiber_composition (p : MobusPosition) :
    comparisonObj p = .composition ↔
    p = .components ∨ p = .boundary ∨ p = .transforms ∨
    p = .history ∨ p = .timeScale := by
  cases p <;> simp [comparisonObj]

declarations.name: fiber_environment
declarations.doc:
Fiber over `environment`: singleton (1:1 preservation).
Bridge.lean's info loss #1 (milieu μ) is invisible here — it occurs WITHIN the environment
position, not between positions.
declarations.signature:
fiber_environment (p : MobusPosition) :
  comparisonObj p = BungePosition.environment ↔ p = MobusPosition.environment
declarations.source:
/-- Fiber over `environment`: singleton (1:1 preservation).
Bridge.lean's info loss #1 (milieu μ) is invisible here — it occurs WITHIN the environment
position, not between positions. -/
theorem fiber_environment (p : MobusPosition) :
    comparisonObj p = .environment ↔ p = .environment := by
  cases p <;> simp [comparisonObj]

declarations.name: fiber_structure
declarations.doc:
Fiber over `structure'`: 2 Mobus positions collapse here.
Corresponds to the spatial factoring N + G → S. Bridge.lean's info loss #2 (capacity κ)
is invisible here — it occurs WITHIN the flow positions when `toRelation` discards κ.
declarations.signature:
fiber_structure (p : MobusPosition) :
  comparisonObj p = BungePosition.structure' ↔
    p = MobusPosition.internalNetwork ∨ p = MobusPosition.externalFlows
declarations.source:
/-- Fiber over `structure'`: 2 Mobus positions collapse here.
Corresponds to the spatial factoring N + G → S. Bridge.lean's info loss #2 (capacity κ)
is invisible here — it occurs WITHIN the flow positions when `toRelation` discards κ. -/
theorem fiber_structure (p : MobusPosition) :
    comparisonObj p = .structure' ↔
    p = .internalNetwork ∨ p = .externalFlows := by
  cases p <;> simp [comparisonObj]

declarations.name: generators_surjective
declarations.doc:
Every Bunge generating arrow has at least one Mobus preimage.
The comparison is surjective on generators (no Bunge dependency is "invented").
declarations.signature:
generators_surjective :
  (∃ f, comparisonPre.map f = Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_comp) ∧
    (∃ f, comparisonPre.map f = Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_env) ∧
      ∃ f, comparisonPre.map f = Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.env_acts_on_comp
declarations.source:
/-- Every Bunge generating arrow has at least one Mobus preimage.
The comparison is surjective on generators (no Bunge dependency is "invented"). -/
theorem generators_surjective :
    (∃ f : MobusArrow .internalNetwork .components,
      comparisonPre.map f = Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_comp) ∧
    (∃ f : MobusArrow .externalFlows .environment,
      comparisonPre.map f = Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_env) ∧
    (∃ f : MobusArrow .environment .components,
      comparisonPre.map f = Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.env_acts_on_comp) :=
  ⟨⟨.network_on_components, rfl⟩, ⟨.external_on_env, rfl⟩, ⟨.env_disjoint_comp, rfl⟩⟩

declarations.name: comparisonFunctor_not_full
declarations.doc:
The comparison functor is NOT full: there exist Bunge morphisms between image
objects with no Mobus preimage in the corresponding hom-set.

Witness: the composite path S → E → C (length 2) in I_Bunge lives in
Hom(structure', composition). But the only Mobus path from internalNetwork to
components is `network_on_components` (length 1), whose image is the direct
`struct_on_comp` (length 1). The length-2 path has no preimage from that hom-set.
declarations.signature:
comparisonFunctor_not_full :
  ∃ f,
    Quiver.Path.length f = 2 ∧
      Quiver.Path.length
          (comparisonFunctor.map (Quiver.Hom.toPath MobusArrow.network_on_components)) =
        1
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison functor is NOT full: there exist Bunge morphisms between image
objects with no Mobus preimage in the corresponding hom-set.

Witness: the composite path S → E → C (length 2) in I_Bunge lives in
Hom(structure', composition). But the only Mobus path from internalNetwork to
components is `network_on_components` (length 1), whose image is the direct
`struct_on_comp` (length 1). The length-2 path has no preimage from that hom-set. -/
theorem comparisonFunctor_not_full :
    ∃ (f : comparisonFunctor.obj (.internalNetwork : Paths MobusPosition) ⟶
           comparisonFunctor.obj (.components : Paths MobusPosition)),
      f.length = 2 ∧
      (comparisonFunctor.map (Quiver.Hom.toPath MobusArrow.network_on_components)).length = 1 := by
  exact ⟨(Quiver.Hom.toPath BungeArrow.struct_on_env).cons BungeArrow.env_acts_on_comp,
         rfl, rfl⟩

declarations.name: myersComparisonObj
declarations.doc:
Object-level comparison: Mobus positions projected into Myers's lens schema.

The mapping reflects the statics/dynamics split:
- `components → output`: composition is the OBSERVABLE aspect of a system
- All other positions → `state`: internal structure is opaque state
  from the lens perspective

Note: `environment` maps to `state` (not `input`) because Mobus's environment
participates in structural constraints (disjointness, flow endpoints) that are
all about characterizing the system's observable decomposition, not about
feeding it dynamic input.
declarations.signature: myersComparisonObj : MobusPosition → MyersPosition
declarations.source:
/-- Object-level comparison: Mobus positions projected into Myers's lens schema.

The mapping reflects the statics/dynamics split:
- `components → output`: composition is the OBSERVABLE aspect of a system
- All other positions → `state`: internal structure is opaque state
  from the lens perspective

Note: `environment` maps to `state` (not `input`) because Mobus's environment
participates in structural constraints (disjointness, flow endpoints) that are
all about characterizing the system's observable decomposition, not about
feeding it dynamic input. -/
def myersComparisonObj : MobusPosition → MyersPosition
  | .components       => .output
  | .internalNetwork  => .state
  | .environment      => .state
  | .externalFlows    => .state
  | .boundary         => .state
  | .transforms       => .state
  | .history          => .state
  | .timeScale        => .state

declarations.name: myersComparisonPre
declarations.doc:
The comparison as a prefunctor into the Myers path category.

Three Mobus arrows (N→C, B→C, E→C) map to `expose` — they all express
"internal structure produces/constrains the observable composition."
Two Mobus arrows (G→E, G→B) map to identity — they relate things within
the `state` abstraction.
declarations.signature: myersComparisonPre : MobusPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths MyersPosition
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison as a prefunctor into the Myers path category.

Three Mobus arrows (N→C, B→C, E→C) map to `expose` — they all express
"internal structure produces/constrains the observable composition."
Two Mobus arrows (G→E, G→B) map to identity — they relate things within
the `state` abstraction. -/
def myersComparisonPre : Prefunctor MobusPosition (Paths MyersPosition) where
  obj := myersComparisonObj
  map := fun
    | .network_on_components    => Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose
    | .interfaces_in_components => Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose
    | .external_on_env          => Quiver.Path.nil
    | .external_on_boundary     => Quiver.Path.nil
    | .env_disjoint_comp        => Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose

declarations.name: myersComparisonFunctor
declarations.doc: The comparison functor from I_Mobus to I_Myers.
declarations.signature:
myersComparisonFunctor :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Paths MobusPosition) (CategoryTheory.Paths MyersPosition)

declarations.name: myersComparisonFunctor_obj
declarations.signature: myersComparisonFunctor_obj (p : MobusPosition) : myersComparisonFunctor.obj p = myersComparisonObj p
declarations.source:
theorem myersComparisonFunctor_obj (p : MobusPosition) :
    myersComparisonFunctor.obj p = myersComparisonObj p := rfl

declarations.name: myers_fiber_state
declarations.doc: State absorbs 7 Mobus positions — everything except components.
declarations.signature:
myers_fiber_state (p : MobusPosition) :
  myersComparisonObj p = MyersPosition.state ↔
    p = MobusPosition.internalNetwork ∨
      p = MobusPosition.environment ∨
        p = MobusPosition.externalFlows ∨
          p = MobusPosition.boundary ∨
            p = MobusPosition.transforms ∨ p = MobusPosition.history ∨ p = MobusPosition.timeScale
declarations.source:
/-- State absorbs 7 Mobus positions — everything except components. -/
theorem myers_fiber_state (p : MobusPosition) :
    myersComparisonObj p = .state ↔
    p = .internalNetwork ∨ p = .environment ∨ p = .externalFlows ∨
    p = .boundary ∨ p = .transforms ∨ p = .history ∨ p = .timeScale := by
  cases p <;> simp [myersComparisonObj]

declarations.name: myers_fiber_output
declarations.doc: Output is a singleton fiber — components are what gets observed.
declarations.signature:
myers_fiber_output (p : MobusPosition) :
  myersComparisonObj p = MyersPosition.output ↔ p = MobusPosition.components
declarations.source:
/-- Output is a singleton fiber — components are what gets observed. -/
theorem myers_fiber_output (p : MobusPosition) :
    myersComparisonObj p = .output ↔ p = .components := by
  cases p <;> simp [myersComparisonObj]

declarations.name: myers_fiber_input
declarations.doc:
Input has an empty fiber — no Mobus position maps to Myers's input.
This is the categorical content of "Mobus has no dynamics concept."
declarations.signature: myers_fiber_input (p : MobusPosition) : myersComparisonObj p ≠ MyersPosition.input
declarations.source:
/-- Input has an empty fiber — no Mobus position maps to Myers's input.
This is the categorical content of "Mobus has no dynamics concept." -/
theorem myers_fiber_input (p : MobusPosition) :
    myersComparisonObj p ≠ .input := by
  cases p <;> simp [myersComparisonObj]

declarations.name: myers_expose_preimages
declarations.doc: Three Mobus arrows map to `expose` — all structural observation.
declarations.signature:
myers_expose_preimages :
  myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.network_on_components = Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose ∧
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.interfaces_in_components =
        Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose ∧
      myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.env_disjoint_comp = Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose
declarations.source:
/-- Three Mobus arrows map to `expose` — all structural observation. -/
theorem myers_expose_preimages :
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.network_on_components =
      Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose ∧
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.interfaces_in_components =
      Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose ∧
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.env_disjoint_comp =
      Quiver.Hom.toPath MyersArrow.expose :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

declarations.name: myers_arrows_annihilated
declarations.doc: Two Mobus arrows are annihilated (internal wiring).
declarations.signature:
myers_arrows_annihilated :
  myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.external_on_env = Quiver.Path.nil ∧
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.external_on_boundary = Quiver.Path.nil
declarations.source:
/-- Two Mobus arrows are annihilated (internal wiring). -/
theorem myers_arrows_annihilated :
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.external_on_env = Quiver.Path.nil ∧
    myersComparisonPre.map MobusArrow.external_on_boundary = Quiver.Path.nil :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

declarations.name: myers_update_unreachable
declarations.doc:
Myers's `update` arrow targets `input`, but no Mobus position maps to `input`.
Therefore `update` cannot appear in the image of any Mobus arrow under the comparison.

This is the formal content of "Mobus is structural, Myers is computational":
- Mobus captures what systems ARE (observation/decomposition → expose)
- Myers captures how systems BEHAVE (dynamics/transitions → update)
- The missing `update` is exactly what BERT's transform (T) is supposed to provide
  operationally — but T is isolated in I_Mobus (no generating arrows), so it cannot
  fill this gap at the shape level.
declarations.signature:
myers_update_unreachable (a b : MobusPosition) :
  ∀ (x : MobusArrow a b), myersComparisonObj b ≠ MyersPosition.input
declarations.source:
/-- Myers's `update` arrow targets `input`, but no Mobus position maps to `input`.
Therefore `update` cannot appear in the image of any Mobus arrow under the comparison.

This is the formal content of "Mobus is structural, Myers is computational":
- Mobus captures what systems ARE (observation/decomposition → expose)
- Myers captures how systems BEHAVE (dynamics/transitions → update)
- The missing `update` is exactly what BERT's transform (T) is supposed to provide
  operationally — but T is isolated in I_Mobus (no generating arrows), so it cannot
  fill this gap at the shape level. -/
theorem myers_update_unreachable :
    ∀ (a b : MobusPosition) (_ : MobusArrow a b),
      myersComparisonObj b ≠ .input := by
  intro a b f
  cases f <;> simp [myersComparisonObj]

declarations.name: myersComparisonObj_not_injective
declarations.signature: myersComparisonObj_not_injective : ¬Function.Injective myersComparisonObj
declarations.source:
theorem myersComparisonObj_not_injective : ¬ Function.Injective myersComparisonObj := by
  intro h
  exact absurd (h (show myersComparisonObj .internalNetwork = myersComparisonObj .environment from rfl))
    (by exact MobusPosition.noConfusion)

declarations.name: wymoreToMobusObj
declarations.doc: Object-level comparison: Wymore positions projected into Mobus's 8-tuple.
declarations.signature: wymoreToMobusObj : WymorePosition → MobusPosition
declarations.source:
/-- Object-level comparison: Wymore positions projected into Mobus's 8-tuple. -/
def wymoreToMobusObj : WymorePosition → MobusPosition
  | .state  => .externalFlows
  | .output => .environment
  | .input  => .boundary
  | .time   => .components

declarations.name: wymoreToMobusPre
declarations.doc:
The comparison as a prefunctor into the Mobus path category.

Two arrows map to length-1 paths (generating arrows); one maps to a length-2
composite path through boundary → components.
declarations.signature: wymoreToMobusPre : WymorePosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths MobusPosition
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison as a prefunctor into the Mobus path category.

Two arrows map to length-1 paths (generating arrows); one maps to a length-2
composite path through boundary → components. -/
def wymoreToMobusPre : Prefunctor WymorePosition (Paths MobusPosition) where
  obj := wymoreToMobusObj
  map := fun
    | .readout     => Quiver.Hom.toPath MobusArrow.external_on_env
    | .nextState   => Quiver.Hom.toPath MobusArrow.external_on_boundary
    | .stateOnTime =>
        (Quiver.Hom.toPath MobusArrow.external_on_boundary).cons
          MobusArrow.interfaces_in_components

declarations.name: wymoreToMobusFunctor
declarations.doc: The comparison functor from I_Wymore to I_Mobus.
declarations.signature:
wymoreToMobusFunctor :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Paths WymorePosition) (CategoryTheory.Paths MobusPosition)

declarations.name: wymoreToMobusFunctor_obj
declarations.signature: wymoreToMobusFunctor_obj (p : WymorePosition) : wymoreToMobusFunctor.obj p = wymoreToMobusObj p
declarations.source:
theorem wymoreToMobusFunctor_obj (p : WymorePosition) :
    wymoreToMobusFunctor.obj p = wymoreToMobusObj p := rfl

declarations.name: wymore_readout_length
declarations.doc: Readout maps to a length-1 path: direct correspondence.
declarations.signature: wymore_readout_length : Quiver.Path.length (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.readout) = 1
declarations.source:
/-- Readout maps to a length-1 path: direct correspondence. -/
theorem wymore_readout_length :
    (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.readout).length = 1 := rfl

declarations.name: wymore_nextState_length
declarations.doc: NextState maps to a length-1 path: direct correspondence.
declarations.signature: wymore_nextState_length : Quiver.Path.length (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.nextState) = 1
declarations.source:
/-- NextState maps to a length-1 path: direct correspondence. -/
theorem wymore_nextState_length :
    (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.nextState).length = 1 := rfl

declarations.name: wymore_stateOnTime_length
declarations.doc:
StateOnTime maps to a length-2 path: Mobus mediates time through boundary.
This is the structural content of their disagreement — Wymore allows state to be
directly time-indexed, while Mobus requires temporal grounding to pass through
the interface/boundary layer before reaching components.
declarations.signature: wymore_stateOnTime_length : Quiver.Path.length (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.stateOnTime) = 2
declarations.source:
/-- StateOnTime maps to a length-2 path: Mobus mediates time through boundary.
This is the structural content of their disagreement — Wymore allows state to be
directly time-indexed, while Mobus requires temporal grounding to pass through
the interface/boundary layer before reaching components. -/
theorem wymore_stateOnTime_length :
    (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.stateOnTime).length = 2 := rfl

declarations.name: wymore_time_mediated
declarations.doc:
The length asymmetry: stateOnTime requires strictly more structure in Mobus
than the other two arrows.
declarations.signature:
wymore_time_mediated :
  Quiver.Path.length (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.stateOnTime) >
    Quiver.Path.length (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.readout)
declarations.source:
/-- The length asymmetry: stateOnTime requires strictly more structure in Mobus
than the other two arrows. -/
theorem wymore_time_mediated :
    (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.stateOnTime).length >
    (wymoreToMobusPre.map WymoreArrow.readout).length := by
  decide

declarations.name: wymoreToMobusObj_injective
declarations.doc:
The comparison is injective on objects — no Wymore positions collapse.
This is stronger than the Mobus→Bunge or Mobus→Myers comparisons, where
multiple positions collapse. Wymore's 4-position structure fits cleanly
into Mobus's 8-position framework with room to spare.
declarations.signature: wymoreToMobusObj_injective : Function.Injective wymoreToMobusObj
declarations.source:
/-- The comparison is injective on objects — no Wymore positions collapse.
This is stronger than the Mobus→Bunge or Mobus→Myers comparisons, where
multiple positions collapse. Wymore's 4-position structure fits cleanly
into Mobus's 8-position framework with room to spare. -/
theorem wymoreToMobusObj_injective : Function.Injective wymoreToMobusObj := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [wymoreToMobusObj]

declarations.name: JoslynPosition
declarations.doc:
The three positions in Joslyn's control₂ system definition CS = (C, O_E, O_I).

- `controller`: C — the global environment (source of disturbances; hierarchically superior)
- `effector`: O_E — the external/efferent component (the regulator/effector; active part)
- `controlled`: O_I — the internal/afferent component (controlled variables; stable part)
declarations.signature: JoslynPosition : Type
declarations.source:
/-- The three positions in Joslyn's control₂ system definition CS = (C, O_E, O_I).

- `controller`: C — the global environment (source of disturbances; hierarchically superior)
- `effector`: O_E — the external/efferent component (the regulator/effector; active part)
- `controlled`: O_I — the internal/afferent component (controlled variables; stable part)
-/
inductive JoslynPosition
  | controller
  | effector
  | controlled
  deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited

declarations.name: instInhabitedJoslynPosition
declarations.signature: instInhabitedJoslynPosition : Inhabited JoslynPosition
declarations.source: deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited

declarations.name: instDecidableEqJoslynPosition
declarations.signature: instDecidableEqJoslynPosition : DecidableEq JoslynPosition
declarations.source: deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited

declarations.name: instInhabitedJoslynPosition.default
declarations.signature: instInhabitedJoslynPosition.default : JoslynPosition
declarations.source: deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited

declarations.name: JoslynArrow
declarations.doc:
Generating morphisms for the Joslyn shape quiver.

Each arrow encodes a functional relation from Joslyn (1995) Figure 1:
- `disturbance`: h — environmental disturbance acts on the regulator (C → O_E)
- `efferent`: g — regulator constrains controlled variables (O_E → O_I)
- `afferent`: f — feedback from controlled variables to regulator (O_I → O_E)

Note: the `efferent` and `afferent` arrows form a cycle, generating infinitely many
morphisms in the free category. This cyclic structure is unique among the shape
categories in this formalization and encodes the defining feedback loop of cybernetic
control systems.
declarations.signature: JoslynArrow : JoslynPosition → JoslynPosition → Type
declarations.source:
/-- Generating morphisms for the Joslyn shape quiver.

Each arrow encodes a functional relation from Joslyn (1995) Figure 1:
- `disturbance`: h — environmental disturbance acts on the regulator (C → O_E)
- `efferent`: g — regulator constrains controlled variables (O_E → O_I)
- `afferent`: f — feedback from controlled variables to regulator (O_I → O_E)

Note: the `efferent` and `afferent` arrows form a cycle, generating infinitely many
morphisms in the free category. This cyclic structure is unique among the shape
categories in this formalization and encodes the defining feedback loop of cybernetic
control systems.
-/
inductive JoslynArrow : JoslynPosition → JoslynPosition → Type
  | disturbance : JoslynArrow .controller .effector
  | efferent : JoslynArrow .effector .controlled

declarations.name: JoslynShape

functional-relation quiver.

has infinitely many morphisms between the cyclic vertices — each distinct path of
alternating efferent/afferent arrows is a genuinely different control trajectory.
This infinite morphism structure formally encodes the open-ended nature of feedback.

declarations.name: MesarovicArrow
declarations.doc:
Generating morphisms for the Mesarović global-state shape quiver.

Both arrows are projections of the response function R : C → V × Y:
- `response_input`: π₁ ∘ R : C → V (state determines the input component)
- `response_output`: π₂ ∘ R : C → Y (state determines the output component)

For each state c ∈ C, R(c) = (v, y) ∈ S specifies a consistent I/O pair. This is a
PASSIVE characterization: "what I/O behavior does this state produce?" There is no
dynamics — no arrow updates state from input.

declarations.name: MyersShape

This is the simplest shape category in the landscape: 3 objects, 2 arrows, no composable
chains (state is the only source, output and input are sinks). Every non-identity
morphism is a generating arrow — no composite paths exist.

The minimality of this shape is precisely Myers's design choice: he encodes ALL
compositional complexity in the lens/arena machinery rather than in the system definition
itself. The comparison functor `I_Mobus → I_Myers` will show what Mobus carries
structurally that Myers delegates to the categorical framework.
