declarations.name: rosen_observables_self
declarations.doc: Every self-path at `observables` is the identity: no arrow targets it.
declarations.signature:
rosen_observables_self (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.observables RosenPosition.observables) :
  p = Quiver.Path.nil
declarations.source:
/-- Every self-path at `observables` is the identity: no arrow targets it. -/
theorem rosen_observables_self
    (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.observables RosenPosition.observables) :
    p = Quiver.Path.nil := by
  cases p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons _ e => exact nomatch e

declarations.name: rosen_states_self
declarations.doc: Every self-path at `states` is the identity: `states` is a sink.
declarations.signature: rosen_states_self (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.states RosenPosition.states) : p = Quiver.Path.nil
declarations.source:
/-- Every self-path at `states` is the identity: `states` is a sink. -/
theorem rosen_states_self
    (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.states RosenPosition.states) :
    p = Quiver.Path.nil := by
  cases p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p e =>
    cases e with
    | defined_on =>
      cases p with
      | cons _ e' => exact nomatch e'

declarations.name: rosen_hom_unique
declarations.doc: Every path from `observables` to `states` is the generating arrow.
declarations.signature:
rosen_hom_unique (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.observables RosenPosition.states) :
  p = Quiver.Hom.toPath RosenArrow.defined_on
declarations.source:
/-- Every path from `observables` to `states` is the generating arrow. -/
theorem rosen_hom_unique
    (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.observables RosenPosition.states) :
    p = Quiver.Hom.toPath RosenArrow.defined_on := by
  cases p with
  | cons p e =>
    cases e with
    | defined_on =>
      have h := rosen_observables_self p
      subst h; rfl

declarations.name: rosen_no_path_states_observables
declarations.doc: There is no path from `states` to `observables`.
declarations.signature:
rosen_no_path_states_observables (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.states RosenPosition.observables) :
  False
declarations.source:
/-- There is no path from `states` to `observables`. -/
theorem rosen_no_path_states_observables
    (p : Quiver.Path RosenPosition.states RosenPosition.observables) : False := by
  cases p with
  | cons _ e => exact nomatch e

declarations.name: rosen_path_subsingleton
declarations.doc: Every hom-set of `I_Rosen` is a subsingleton.
declarations.signature: rosen_path_subsingleton (a b : RosenPosition) (p q : Quiver.Path a b) : p = q
declarations.source:
/-- Every hom-set of `I_Rosen` is a subsingleton. -/
theorem rosen_path_subsingleton :
    ∀ (a b : RosenPosition) (p q : Quiver.Path a b), p = q := by
  intro a b p q
  cases a <;> cases b
  · rw [rosen_states_self p, rosen_states_self q]
  · exact (rosen_no_path_states_observables p).elim
  · rw [rosen_hom_unique p, rosen_hom_unique q]
  · rw [rosen_observables_self p, rosen_observables_self q]

declarations.name: rosenHomSubsingleton
declarations.signature: rosenHomSubsingleton (X Y : CategoryTheory.Paths RosenPosition) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y)
declarations.source:
instance rosenHomSubsingleton (X Y : Paths RosenPosition) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
  ⟨rosen_path_subsingleton X Y⟩

- `expose`: f⁺ reads the parameter to produce output (identical to Myers's expose)
- `update`: the backward pass consumes input (identical to Myers's update)
- `potential_on_parameter`: the potential U reads Q
- `potential_on_input`: the potential U reads N⁻
- `drive`: the reaction ♯ turns dU into a parameter step — the new commitment

`drive` and `potential_on_parameter` form the value-feedback cycle
parameter ⇄ potential.
declarations.signature: SpivakArrow : SpivakPosition → SpivakPosition → Type
declarations.source:
/-- Generating morphisms for the Spivak shape quiver.

- `expose`: f⁺ reads the parameter to produce output (identical to Myers's expose)
- `update`: the backward pass consumes input (identical to Myers's update)
- `potential_on_parameter`: the potential U reads Q
- `potential_on_input`: the potential U reads N⁻
- `drive`: the reaction ♯ turns dU into a parameter step — the new commitment

`drive` and `potential_on_parameter` form the value-feedback cycle
parameter ⇄ potential.
-/
inductive SpivakArrow : SpivakPosition → SpivakPosition → Type
  | expose : SpivakArrow .parameter .output
  | update : SpivakArrow .parameter .input
  | potential_on_parameter : SpivakArrow .potential .parameter
  | potential_on_input : SpivakArrow .potential .input
  | drive : SpivakArrow .parameter .potential

instance : Quiver SpivakPosition where
  Hom := SpivakArrow

declarations.name: SpivakShape
declarations.doc:
The shape category for Spivak's adaptive arrangements: the free category on
the arrangement quiver.

Like `I_Joslyn`, this shape has a cycle — here between `parameter` and
`potential` — so the free category has infinitely many morphisms between the
cyclic vertices. Each distinct path of alternating drive/potential arrows is a
genuinely different adaptation trajectory: evaluate, step, re-evaluate. Where
Joslyn's cycle encodes feedback through observation, this one encodes feedback
through value.
declarations.signature: SpivakShape : Type
declarations.source:
/-- The shape category for Spivak's adaptive arrangements: the free category on
the arrangement quiver.

Like `I_Joslyn`, this shape has a cycle — here between `parameter` and
`potential` — so the free category has infinitely many morphisms between the
cyclic vertices. Each distinct path of alternating drive/potential arrows is a
genuinely different adaptation trajectory: evaluate, step, re-evaluate. Where
Joslyn's cycle encodes feedback through observation, this one encodes feedback
through value. -/
abbrev SpivakShape := Paths SpivakPosition

declarations.name: myersToSpivakPre
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of Myers's lens shape into the Spivak shape:
state ↦ parameter, output ↦ output, input ↦ input. Both generating arrows
map to their namesakes.
declarations.signature: myersToSpivakPre : MyersPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths SpivakPosition
declarations.source:
/-- The inclusion of Myers's lens shape into the Spivak shape:
state ↦ parameter, output ↦ output, input ↦ input. Both generating arrows
map to their namesakes. -/
def myersToSpivakPre : Prefunctor MyersPosition (Paths SpivakPosition) where
  obj | .state => .parameter | .output => .output | .input => .input
  map
    | .expose => Quiver.Hom.toPath SpivakArrow.expose
    | .update => Quiver.Hom.toPath SpivakArrow.update

declarations.name: myersToSpivak
declarations.doc:
The inclusion functor I_Myers → I_Spivak: the commitments ladder of
Remark 4.1.2 as a theorem. Spivak = Myers + potential + drive.
declarations.signature:
myersToSpivak :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Paths MyersPosition) (CategoryTheory.Paths SpivakPosition)
declarations.source:
/-- The inclusion functor I_Myers → I_Spivak: the commitments ladder of
Remark 4.1.2 as a theorem. Spivak = Myers + potential + drive. -/
def myersToSpivak : Paths MyersPosition ⥤ Paths SpivakPosition :=
  Paths.lift myersToSpivakPre

declarations.name: myersToSpivak_obj_injective
declarations.signature: myersToSpivak_obj_injective : Function.Injective myersToSpivakPre.obj
declarations.source:
theorem myersToSpivak_obj_injective : Function.Injective myersToSpivakPre.obj := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [myersToSpivakPre]

declarations.name: WillemsArrow
declarations.doc:
Generating morphisms for the Willems shape quiver, in the functional
direction (convention of Wymore/Spivak): a trajectory w ∈ B is a map T → W,
so behavior produces signal values and consumes time points.

- `evaluate`: behavior → signal — trajectories assign signal values
  (the predication of B on W: the kernel arrow)
- `indexed_by`: behavior → time — trajectories are indexed by the time axis

- `indexed_by`: behavior → time — trajectories are indexed by the time axis
-/

  | evaluate   : WillemsArrow .behavior .signal
  | indexed_by : WillemsArrow .behavior .time

declarations.name: WillemsShape
declarations.doc:
The shape category for Willems' behavioral triple: the free category on the
trajectory quiver.

3 objects, 2 arrows radiating outward from `behavior` — the span
time ← behavior → signal. No composable chains exist (behavior is the only
source; time and signal are sinks). Dropping `time` leaves the walking arrow:
Willems is the sparsest entry in the landscape, nearest the bare kernel.

declarations.name: klirToWillemsPre
declarations.doc:
Embedding I_Klir into I_Willems: things ↦ signal, relation ↦ behavior,
relation_on_things ↦ evaluate.

The tradition most hostile to I/O orientation still carries the predication
arrow — a behavior is a relation predicated on signal values. `dep_on` is
predication, not causation, so the behavioral stance has nothing to refuse.
declarations.signature: klirToWillemsPre : KlirPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths WillemsPosition
declarations.source:
/-- Embedding I_Klir into I_Willems: things ↦ signal, relation ↦ behavior,
relation_on_things ↦ evaluate.

The tradition most hostile to I/O orientation still carries the predication
arrow — a behavior is a relation predicated on signal values. `dep_on` is
predication, not causation, so the behavioral stance has nothing to refuse. -/
def klirToWillemsPre : Prefunctor KlirPosition (Paths WillemsPosition) where
  obj | .things => .signal | .relation => .behavior
  map | .relation_on_things => Quiver.Hom.toPath WillemsArrow.evaluate

declarations.doc:

klirToWillems :

declarations.source:
/-- The kernel embedding functor I_Klir ⥤ I_Willems. Faithfulness is free:
every functor out of I_Klir is faithful (CommonCore §Faithfulness). -/
def klirToWillems : Paths KlirPosition ⥤ Paths WillemsPosition :=
  Paths.lift klirToWillemsPre

declarations.name: willemsToMesarovicObj
declarations.doc:
Object-level comparison: Willems' span projected onto Mesarović's Shape 2 span.

The assignments `behavior ↦ globalState` and `time ↦ input` are forced by the
shapes and are semantically absurd — see the module docstring. The absurdity is
the finding.
declarations.signature: willemsToMesarovicObj : WillemsPosition → MesarovicPosition
declarations.source:
/-- Object-level comparison: Willems' span projected onto Mesarović's Shape 2 span.

The assignments `behavior ↦ globalState` and `time ↦ input` are forced by the
shapes and are semantically absurd — see the module docstring. The absurdity is
the finding. -/

  | .behavior => .globalState
  | .signal   => .output
  | .time     => .input

declarations.name: willemsToMesarovicPre
declarations.doc:
The forward comparison as a prefunctor into the Mesarović path category.
Both generating arrows map to generating arrows: the spans match leg for leg.
declarations.signature: willemsToMesarovicPre : WillemsPosition ⥤q CategoryTheory.Paths MesarovicPosition
declarations.source:
/-- The forward comparison as a prefunctor into the Mesarović path category.
Both generating arrows map to generating arrows: the spans match leg for leg. -/
def willemsToMesarovicPre : Prefunctor WillemsPosition (Paths MesarovicPosition) where
  obj := willemsToMesarovicObj
  map
    | .evaluate   => Quiver.Hom.toPath MesarovicArrow.response_output
    | .indexed_by => Quiver.Hom.toPath MesarovicArrow.response_input

  obj := mesarovicToWillemsObj

declarations.name: WymoreArrow
declarations.doc:
Generating morphisms for the Wymore shape quiver.

Each arrow encodes a functional dependency from the FSD definition:
- `nextState`: N_Z : S × I → S (state depends on input for transitions)
- `readout`: R_Z : S → O (output is produced from state, Moore-type)
- `stateOnTime`: state transitions are parameterized by TS_Z

These correspond to the two functions in the quintuple Z plus the FSD time-indexing:
- `N_Z : S_Z × I_Z → S_Z` (next-state)
- `R_Z : S_Z → O_Z` (readout)
- FSD temporal parameterization via TS_Z

declarations.name: WymoreShape

The shape category for Wymore's FSD: the free category on the system quiver.

State is the sole source; input, output, and time are sinks. Every non-identity
morphism is a generating arrow — no composite paths exist (same as Myers).

Without the `time` vertex, this is isomorphic to `MyersShape`, confirming that
Myers's lens-based deterministic system is Wymore's quintuple Z with the temporal
dimension abstracted away. The FSD time object is what distinguishes Wymore's
engineering-oriented framework from Myers's categorical one.

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.no_fork
declarations.doc: No fork. Two edges out of a common source have the same target.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.no_fork.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eJ : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition) {x y z : V} (e : x ⟶ y) (f : x ⟶ z) :
  y = z
declarations.source:
/-- No fork. Two edges out of a common source have the same target. -/
theorem no_fork (eJ : QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition) {x y z : V}
    (e : x ⟶ y) (f : x ⟶ z) : y = z :=
  eJ.obj_inj (joslyn_out_degree_le_one (eJ.toPre.map e) (eJ.toPre.map f))

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.no_cofork

declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.no_cofork.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y z : V} (e : x ⟶ z) (f : y ⟶ z) :
  x = y
declarations.source:
/-- No cofork. Two edges into a common target have the same source. -/
theorem no_cofork (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y z : V}
    (e : x ⟶ z) (f : y ⟶ z) : x = y :=
  eW.obj_inj (willems_in_degree_le_one (eW.toPre.map e) (eW.toPre.map f))

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.no_two_chain
declarations.doc: No two-chain.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.no_two_chain.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y z : V} (e : x ⟶ y) (f : y ⟶ z) :
  False
declarations.source:
/-- No two-chain. -/
theorem no_two_chain (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y z : V}
    (e : x ⟶ y) (f : y ⟶ z) : False :=
  willems_no_composable (eW.toPre.map e) (eW.toPre.map f)

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.no_loop
declarations.doc: No self-loop.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.no_loop.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x : V} (e : x ⟶ x) : False
declarations.source:
/-- No self-loop. -/
theorem no_loop (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x : V} (e : x ⟶ x) :

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.no_parallel
declarations.doc: No parallel edges.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.no_parallel.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y : V} (e f : x ⟶ y) : e = f
declarations.source:
/-- No parallel edges. -/
theorem no_parallel (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y : V}
    (e f : x ⟶ y) : e = f :=
  eW.map_inj (willems_no_parallel _ _)

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.edges_coincide_or_disjoint
declarations.doc:
In a quiver embedding into both the Joslyn and Willems shapes, any two edges
either have the same endpoints or share no vertex whatsoever.

A connected quiver with at least one edge therefore has exactly one edge, on two
vertices: it is `I_Klir`.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.edges_coincide_or_disjoint.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eJ : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition)
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y u v : V} (e : x ⟶ y) (f : u ⟶ v) :
  x = u ∧ y = v ∨ x ≠ u ∧ y ≠ v ∧ x ≠ v ∧ y ≠ u
declarations.source:
/-- In a quiver embedding into both the Joslyn and Willems shapes, any two edges
either have the same endpoints or share no vertex whatsoever.

A connected quiver with at least one edge therefore has exactly one edge, on two
vertices: it is `I_Klir`. -/
theorem edges_coincide_or_disjoint
    (eJ : QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition) (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition)
    {x y u v : V} (e : x ⟶ y) (f : u ⟶ v) :
    (x = u ∧ y = v) ∨ (x ≠ u ∧ y ≠ v ∧ x ≠ v ∧ y ≠ u) := by
  by_cases hxv : x = v
  · subst hxv; exact (no_two_chain eW f e).elim
  · by_cases hyu : y = u
    · subst hyu; exact (no_two_chain eW e f).elim
    · by_cases hxu : x = u
      · subst hxu; exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, no_fork eJ e f⟩
      · by_cases hyv : y = v
        · subst hyv; exact absurd (no_cofork eW e f) hxu
        · exact Or.inr ⟨hxu, hyv, hxv, hyu⟩

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.Zigzag
declarations.doc:
Weak connectivity for quivers: `x` and `y` are joined by a zigzag of edges,
traversed in either direction. This is the "connected" of the theorem statement.
declarations.signature: SharedPrimitive.Zigzag.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V] : V → V → Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Weak connectivity for quivers: `x` and `y` are joined by a zigzag of edges,
traversed in either direction. This is the "connected" of the theorem statement. -/
inductive Zigzag : V → V → Prop
  | refl (x : V) : Zigzag x x
  | fwd {x y z : V} : Zigzag x y → (y ⟶ z) → Zigzag x z
  | bwd {x y z : V} : Zigzag x y → (z ⟶ y) → Zigzag x z

constructors.name: SharedPrimitive.Zigzag.refl
constructors.type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Quiver V] (x : V), SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x x

constructors.name: SharedPrimitive.Zigzag.fwd
constructors.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Quiver V] {x y z : V},
  SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x y → ∀ (a : y ⟶ z), SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x z

constructors.name: SharedPrimitive.Zigzag.bwd
constructors.type:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Quiver V] {x y z : V},
  SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x y → ∀ (a : z ⟶ y), SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x z

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.zigzag_confined
declarations.doc:
Given an edge `x ⟶ y`, nothing outside `{x, y}` is reachable from `x`.

Each step is blocked by one of the obstructions: leaving `x` forwards is a fork,
leaving `y` forwards is a two-chain, entering `x` backwards is a two-chain, and
entering `y` backwards is a cofork.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.zigzag_confined.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eJ : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition)
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) {w : V} :
  SharedPrimitive.Zigzag x w → w = x ∨ w = y
declarations.source:
/-- Given an edge `x ⟶ y`, nothing outside `{x, y}` is reachable from `x`.

Each step is blocked by one of the obstructions: leaving `x` forwards is a fork,
leaving `y` forwards is a two-chain, entering `x` backwards is a two-chain, and
entering `y` backwards is a cofork. -/
theorem zigzag_confined (eJ : QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition)
    (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) :
    ∀ {w : V}, Zigzag x w → w = x ∨ w = y := by
  intro w hw
  induction hw with
  | refl => exact Or.inl rfl
  | fwd _ g ih =>
      rcases ih with rfl | rfl
      · exact Or.inr (no_fork eJ e g).symm
      · exact (no_two_chain eW e g).elim
  | bwd _ g ih =>
      rcases ih with rfl | rfl
      · exact (no_two_chain eW g e).elim
      · exact Or.inl (no_cofork eW e g).symm

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.connected_is_single_arrow
declarations.doc:
**The shared primitive is a single arrow.**

A connected quiver embedding into both the Joslyn and Willems shapes, and having at
least one edge, has exactly two vertices and exactly one edge. That quiver is
`I_Klir`, whose free category is the walking arrow **2**.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.connected_is_single_arrow.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} [Quiver V]
  (eJ : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition)
  (eW : SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition)
  (conn : ∀ (a b : V), SharedPrimitive.Zigzag a b) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) :
  x ≠ y ∧ (∀ (w : V), w = x ∨ w = y) ∧ ∀ (u v : V) (x_1 : u ⟶ v), u = x ∧ v = y
declarations.source:
/-- **The shared primitive is a single arrow.**

A connected quiver embedding into both the Joslyn and Willems shapes, and having at
least one edge, has exactly two vertices and exactly one edge. That quiver is
`I_Klir`, whose free category is the walking arrow **2**. -/
theorem connected_is_single_arrow
    (eJ : QuiverEmbedding V JoslynPosition) (eW : QuiverEmbedding V WillemsPosition)
    (conn : ∀ a b : V, Zigzag a b) {x y : V} (e : x ⟶ y) :
    x ≠ y ∧ (∀ w : V, w = x ∨ w = y) ∧ ∀ (u v : V) (_ : u ⟶ v), u = x ∧ v = y := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun w => zigzag_confined eJ eW e (conn x w), ?_⟩
  · rintro rfl; exact no_loop eW e
  · intro u v f
    rcases zigzag_confined eJ eW e (conn x u) with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨rfl, (no_fork eJ e f).symm⟩
    · exact (no_two_chain eW e f).elim

SharedPrimitive.v_src_left (p : Quiver.Path SharedPrimitive.VPos.src SharedPrimitive.VPos.left) :

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.v_path_subsingleton
declarations.doc: `V` is thin, so every functor out of it is faithful.
declarations.signature: SharedPrimitive.v_path_subsingleton (a b : SharedPrimitive.VPos) (p q : Quiver.Path a b) : p = q
declarations.source:
/-- `V` is thin, so every functor out of it is faithful. -/
theorem v_path_subsingleton : ∀ (a b : VPos) (p q : Quiver.Path a b), p = q := by
  intro a b p q
  cases a <;> cases b
  · rw [v_src_self p, v_src_self q]
  · rw [v_src_left p, v_src_left q]
  · rw [v_src_right p, v_src_right q]
  · exact (v_no_left_src p).elim
  · rw [v_left_self p, v_left_self q]
  · exact (v_no_left_right p).elim
  · exact (v_no_right_src p).elim
  · exact (v_no_right_left p).elim
  · rw [v_right_self p, v_right_self q]

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.vHomSubsingleton

SharedPrimitive.vHomSubsingleton (X Y : CategoryTheory.Paths SharedPrimitive.VPos) :
  Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y)
declarations.source:
instance vHomSubsingleton (X Y : Paths VPos) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
  ⟨v_path_subsingleton X Y⟩

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.free_category_maximality_fails
declarations.doc:
**The free-category maximality claim is false.** `V` has three objects where
`I_Klir` has two, is connected, and embeds into all eight shape categories
injectively on objects and faithfully.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.free_category_maximality_fails :
  Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToBungePre.obj ∧
    (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToBungePre).Faithful ∧
      Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToMobusPre.obj ∧
        (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToMobusPre).Faithful ∧
          Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToMyersPre.obj ∧
            (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToMyersPre).Faithful ∧
              Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToWymorePre.obj ∧
                (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToWymorePre).Faithful ∧
                  Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToMesarovicPre.obj ∧
                    (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToMesarovicPre).Faithful ∧
                      Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToSpivakPre.obj ∧
                        (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToSpivakPre).Faithful ∧
                          Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToWillemsPre.obj ∧
                            (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToWillemsPre).Faithful ∧
                              Function.Injective SharedPrimitive.vToJoslynPre.obj ∧
                                (CategoryTheory.Paths.lift SharedPrimitive.vToJoslynPre).Faithful
declarations.source:
/-- **The free-category maximality claim is false.** `V` has three objects where
`I_Klir` has two, is connected, and embeds into all eight shape categories
injectively on objects and faithfully. -/
theorem free_category_maximality_fails :
    Function.Injective vToBungePre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToBungePre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToMobusPre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToMobusPre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToMyersPre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToMyersPre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToWymorePre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToWymorePre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToMesarovicPre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToMesarovicPre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToSpivakPre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToSpivakPre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToWillemsPre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToWillemsPre).Faithful ∧
    Function.Injective vToJoslynPre.obj ∧ (Paths.lift vToJoslynPre).Faithful :=
  ⟨vToBunge_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToMobus_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToMyers_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToWymore_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToMesarovic_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToSpivak_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToWillems_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _,
   vToJoslyn_obj_injective, faithful_of_subsingleton_hom _⟩

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.v_has_three_objects
declarations.doc: And `V` is strictly larger: three objects, not two.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.v_has_three_objects (f : SharedPrimitive.VPos → KlirPosition) :
  ¬Function.Injective f
declarations.source:
/-- And `V` is strictly larger: three objects, not two. -/
theorem v_has_three_objects : ∀ (f : VPos → KlirPosition), ¬ Function.Injective f := by
  intro f hinj
  have h : f .src = f .left ∨ f .src = f .right ∨ f .left = f .right := by
    cases (f .src) <;> cases (f .left) <;> cases (f .right) <;> simp
  rcases h with h | h | h
  · exact absurd (hinj h) (by decide)
  · exact absurd (hinj h) (by decide)
  · exact absurd (hinj h) (by decide)

declarations.name: SharedPrimitive.v_no_quiver_embedding_into_joslyn
declarations.doc:
But `V` does **not** embed at the quiver level: Joslyn has no vertex of
out-degree two. This is the whole content of the level shift.
declarations.signature:
SharedPrimitive.v_no_quiver_embedding_into_joslyn :
  IsEmpty (SharedPrimitive.QuiverEmbedding SharedPrimitive.VPos JoslynPosition)
declarations.source:
/-- But `V` does **not** embed at the quiver level: Joslyn has no vertex of
out-degree two. This is the whole content of the level shift. -/
theorem v_no_quiver_embedding_into_joslyn :
    IsEmpty (QuiverEmbedding VPos JoslynPosition) := by
  constructor
  intro emb
  exact absurd (no_fork emb VArrow.toLeft VArrow.toRight) (by decide)

declarations.name: spivakLoop

The single drive ∘ potential_on_parameter value-feedback loop
`parameter ⟶ parameter` — the generating cycle of Spivak's shape. Length 2.
declarations.signature: spivakLoop : Quiver.Path SpivakPosition.parameter SpivakPosition.parameter
declarations.source:
/-- The single drive ∘ potential_on_parameter value-feedback loop
`parameter ⟶ parameter` — the generating cycle of Spivak's shape. Length 2. -/
def spivakLoop : Quiver.Path (SpivakPosition.parameter) (SpivakPosition.parameter) :=
  (Quiver.Path.nil.cons SpivakArrow.drive).cons SpivakArrow.potential_on_parameter

declarations.name: spivak_no_faithful_functor
declarations.doc:
**Spivak's value-feedback shape admits no faithful functor into any category
with finite hom-sets.** The `drive` / `potential_on_parameter` cycle makes
`parameter ⟶ parameter` infinite; faithfulness would inject it into the finite
hom-set of the target.
declarations.signature:
spivak_no_faithful_functor.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  [∀ (X Y : C), Finite (X ⟶ Y)] (F : CategoryTheory.Functor SpivakShape C) : ¬F.Faithful
declarations.source:
/-- **Spivak's value-feedback shape admits no faithful functor into any category
with finite hom-sets.** The `drive` / `potential_on_parameter` cycle makes
`parameter ⟶ parameter` infinite; faithfulness would inject it into the finite
hom-set of the target. -/
theorem spivak_no_faithful_functor
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [∀ X Y : C, Finite (X ⟶ Y)]
    (F : SpivakShape ⥤ C) : ¬ F.Faithful :=
  paths_no_faithful_functor_of_cycle spivakLoop (by simp [spivakLoop_length]) F

declarations.name: Systems.instPreorderConcreteSystem
declarations.doc:
The Bunge subsystem relation is a preorder on ConcreteSystem.
Reflexivity: `subsystem_refl` (System.lean).
Transitivity: `subsystem_trans` (System.lean).

Mathlib's `Preorder.smallCategory` then gives a thin category:
objects = concrete systems, a morphism σ₁ ⟶ σ₂ exists iff
Subsystem σ₁ σ₂ (i.e., C₁ ⊆ C₂, E₂ ⊆ E₁, S₁ ⊆ S₂).
declarations.signature:
Systems.instPreorderConcreteSystem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Preorder (Systems.ConcreteSystem α)
declarations.source:
/-- The Bunge subsystem relation is a preorder on ConcreteSystem.
    Reflexivity: `subsystem_refl` (System.lean).
    Transitivity: `subsystem_trans` (System.lean).

    Mathlib's `Preorder.smallCategory` then gives a thin category:
    objects = concrete systems, a morphism σ₁ ⟶ σ₂ exists iff
    Subsystem σ₁ σ₂ (i.e., C₁ ⊆ C₂, E₂ ⊆ E₁, S₁ ⊆ S₂). -/
instance instPreorderConcreteSystem {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    Preorder (ConcreteSystem α) where
  le := Subsystem
  le_refl := subsystem_refl
  le_trans := fun _ _ _ h₁₂ h₂₃ => subsystem_trans h₁₂ h₂₃

  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (hf : ∀ (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ), Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hg : ∀ (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ), sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
  Monotone fun sys => sys.toBunge ⋯ ⋯
declarations.source:
/-- The Mobus→Bunge projection is monotone: subsystem ordering is preserved. -/
theorem toBunge_monotone {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (hf : (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) → FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hg : (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) → sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    Monotone (fun sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ => sys.toBunge (hf sys) (hg sys)) :=
  fun _ _ hsub => ⟨hsub.1, hsub.2.1, hsub.2.2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Assembly
declarations.doc:
An assembly event: a thing x with initially no bonds assembles into a
system y with the same composition but nonempty bondage.
Bunge Def 1.12(i): x assembles into y at t' > t iff
C(y,t') = C(x,t) ∧ B(y,t') ≠ ∅ (while B(x,t) = ∅).
declarations.signature: Systems.Assembly.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [Systems.ActsOn α] : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- An assembly event: a thing x with initially no bonds assembles into a
    system y with the same composition but nonempty bondage.
    Bunge Def 1.12(i): x assembles into y at t' > t iff
    C(y,t') = C(x,t) ∧ B(y,t') ≠ ∅ (while B(x,t) = ∅). -/
structure Assembly (α : Type*) [ActsOn α] where
  /-- The initial thing (aggregate, no bonds) -/
  precursor : ConcreteSystem α
  /-- The resulting system (with bonds) -/
  result : ConcreteSystem α
  /-- Composition is preserved -/
  composition_preserved : result.composition = precursor.composition
  /-- The precursor had empty internal structure (no bonds) -/
  precursor_unbonded : precursor.internalStructure = ∅
  /-- The result has nonempty bondage (is a genuine system) -/
  result_bonded : result.internalStructure ≠ ∅

constructors.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Systems.ActsOn α] →
    (precursor result : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) →
      result.composition = precursor.composition →
        precursor.internalStructure = ∅ → result.internalStructure ≠ ∅ → Systems.Assembly α

Self-organization: self-assembly where the result contains subsystems
that did not exist before.
Bunge Def 1.12(iii): new subsystems come into being.
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfOrganization.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [Systems.ActsOn α] : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- Self-organization: self-assembly where the result contains subsystems
    that did not exist before.
    Bunge Def 1.12(iii): new subsystems come into being. -/
structure SelfOrganization (α : Type*) [ActsOn α] extends SelfAssembly α where
  /-- New subsystems that arise (not present in precursor) -/
  newSubsystems : Set (ConcreteSystem α)
  /-- The new subsystems are nonempty -/
  new_nonempty : newSubsystems.Nonempty

declarations.name: Systems.PropertySnapshot
declarations.doc:
Properties of a thing at a given time.
Bunge: p_x(t) is the collection of properties of thing x at time t.
We represent properties as a Set over an abstract property type.
declarations.signature: Systems.PropertySnapshot.{u_1} (P : Type u_1) : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- Properties of a thing at a given time.
    Bunge: p_x(t) is the collection of properties of thing x at time t.
    We represent properties as a Set over an abstract property type. -/
structure PropertySnapshot (P : Type*) where
  /-- The set of properties at this time -/
  properties : Set P

constructors.name: Systems.PropertySnapshot.mk
constructors.type: {P : Type u_1} → Set P → Systems.PropertySnapshot P

declarations.name: Systems.PropertySnapshot.properties
declarations.doc: The set of properties at this time
declarations.signature: Systems.PropertySnapshot.properties.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (self : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) : Set P
declarations.source: properties : Set P

declarations.name: Systems.qualitativeNovelty
declarations.doc:
Qualitative novelty: the symmetric difference of property sets.
Bunge Def 1.13(i): n_x(t,t') = p_x(t) △ ∪_{t<τ≤t'} p_x(τ)

We simplify to comparing two snapshots (before and after).
declarations.signature: Systems.qualitativeNovelty.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) : Set P
declarations.source:
/-- Qualitative novelty: the symmetric difference of property sets.
    Bunge Def 1.13(i): n_x(t,t') = p_x(t) △ ∪_{t<τ≤t'} p_x(τ)

    We simplify to comparing two snapshots (before and after). -/
def qualitativeNovelty {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) : Set P :=
  (before.properties \ after.properties) ∪ (after.properties \ before.properties)

declarations.name: Systems.emergentProperties
declarations.doc:
Emergent properties: new properties that appear.
Bunge Def 1.13(ii): e_x(t,t') = ∪_{t<τ≤t'} p_x(τ) - p_x(t)

Properties in the later state that were not in the earlier state.
declarations.signature: Systems.emergentProperties.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) : Set P
declarations.source:
/-- Emergent properties: new properties that appear.
    Bunge Def 1.13(ii): e_x(t,t') = ∪_{t<τ≤t'} p_x(τ) - p_x(t)

    Properties in the later state that were not in the earlier state. -/
def emergentProperties {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) : Set P :=
  after.properties \ before.properties

declarations.name: Systems.lostProperties
declarations.doc:
Lost properties: properties that disappear.
Complement of emergence within qualitative novelty.
declarations.signature: Systems.lostProperties.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) : Set P
declarations.source:
/-- Lost properties: properties that disappear.
    Complement of emergence within qualitative novelty. -/
def lostProperties {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) : Set P :=
  before.properties \ after.properties

declarations.name: Systems.novelty_eq_emergent_union_lost
declarations.doc:
Qualitative novelty is the union of emergent and lost properties.
This is the showcase: emergence is precisely set operations, not mystical.
declarations.signature:
Systems.novelty_eq_emergent_union_lost.{u_1} {P : Type u_1}
  (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) :
  Systems.qualitativeNovelty before after =
    Systems.lostProperties before after ∪ Systems.emergentProperties before after
declarations.source:
/-- Qualitative novelty is the union of emergent and lost properties.
    This is the showcase: emergence is precisely set operations, not mystical. -/
theorem novelty_eq_emergent_union_lost {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) :
    qualitativeNovelty before after =
      lostProperties before after ∪ emergentProperties before after := by
  simp [qualitativeNovelty, emergentProperties, lostProperties]

declarations.name: Systems.emergent_sub_novelty
declarations.doc: Emergence implies qualitative novelty (if anything emerged, there is novelty).
declarations.signature:
Systems.emergent_sub_novelty.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) :
  Systems.emergentProperties before after ⊆ Systems.qualitativeNovelty before after
declarations.source:
/-- Emergence implies qualitative novelty (if anything emerged, there is novelty). -/
theorem emergent_sub_novelty {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) :
    emergentProperties before after ⊆ qualitativeNovelty before after := by
  intro x hx
  simp [qualitativeNovelty, emergentProperties] at *
  exact Or.inr hx

declarations.name: Systems.absolutelyEmergent
declarations.doc:
Absolutely emergent properties: properties that have never appeared
in any thing before.
Bunge Def 1.14: e^a_x(t,t') = e_x(t,t') - ∪_{y∈Θ, τ≤t'} p_y(τ)
with y ≠ x.

Parametrized over a "prior properties" set representing all properties
ever observed in any other thing.
declarations.signature:
Systems.absolutelyEmergent.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P)
  (priorInUniverse : Set P) : Set P
declarations.source:
/-- Absolutely emergent properties: properties that have never appeared
    in any thing before.
    Bunge Def 1.14: e^a_x(t,t') = e_x(t,t') - ∪_{y∈Θ, τ≤t'} p_y(τ)
    with y ≠ x.

    Parametrized over a "prior properties" set representing all properties
    ever observed in any other thing. -/
def absolutelyEmergent {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) (priorInUniverse : Set P) : Set P :=
  emergentProperties before after \ priorInUniverse

declarations.name: Systems.absolutely_emergent_sub
declarations.doc: Absolutely emergent properties are a subset of emergent properties.
declarations.signature:
Systems.absolutely_emergent_sub.{u_1} {P : Type u_1} (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P)
  (prior : Set P) :
  Systems.absolutelyEmergent before after prior ⊆ Systems.emergentProperties before after
declarations.source:
/-- Absolutely emergent properties are a subset of emergent properties. -/
theorem absolutely_emergent_sub {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) (prior : Set P) :
    absolutelyEmergent before after prior ⊆ emergentProperties before after :=
  fun _ hx => hx.1

declarations.name: Systems.PostulateAssemblyEmergence
declarations.doc:
Bunge Postulate 1.5: Every assembly process is accompanied by the
emergence of some properties and the loss of others.
p_x(t) - p_x(t') ≠ ∅ and p_x(t') - p_x(t) ≠ ∅.
declarations.signature:
Systems.PostulateAssemblyEmergence.{u_1} {P : Type u_1}
  (before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Bunge Postulate 1.5: Every assembly process is accompanied by the
    emergence of some properties and the loss of others.
    p_x(t) - p_x(t') ≠ ∅ and p_x(t') - p_x(t) ≠ ∅. -/
structure PostulateAssemblyEmergence {P : Type*}
    (before after : PropertySnapshot P) where
  /-- Some properties are gained -/
  gains : (emergentProperties before after).Nonempty
  /-- Some properties are lost -/
  losses : (lostProperties before after).Nonempty

constructors.name: Systems.PostulateAssemblyEmergence.mk
constructors.type:
∀ {P : Type u_1} {before after : Systems.PropertySnapshot P},
  (Systems.emergentProperties before after).Nonempty →
    (Systems.lostProperties before after).Nonempty → Systems.PostulateAssemblyEmergence before after

declarations.name: Systems.PostulateAssemblyEmergence.gains
declarations.doc: Some properties are gained
declarations.source: gains : (emergentProperties before after).Nonempty

declarations.name: Systems.PostulateAssemblyEmergence.losses
declarations.doc: Some properties are lost
declarations.source: losses : (lostProperties before after).Nonempty

declarations.name: Systems.ActsOn
declarations.doc:
Thing a acts on thing b: a modifies b's behavior/trajectory/history.
Bunge §1.2: a ▷ b symbolizes the acting of thing a on thing b.
Bunge §2.2 item (x): A(x,y) = h(y|x) ∩ h̄(y), the difference
between forced and free trajectory.

This is abstract (Prop-valued) — concrete instances provide evidence.
declarations.signature: Systems.ActsOn.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- Thing a acts on thing b: a modifies b's behavior/trajectory/history.
    Bunge §1.2: a ▷ b symbolizes the acting of thing a on thing b.
    Bunge §2.2 item (x): A(x,y) = h(y|x) ∩ h̄(y), the difference
    between forced and free trajectory.

    This is abstract (Prop-valued) — concrete instances provide evidence. -/
class ActsOn (α : Type*) where
  actsOn : α → α → Prop

constructors.name: Systems.ActsOn.mk
constructors.type: {α : Type u_1} → (α → α → Prop) → Systems.ActsOn α

declarations.name: Systems.ActsOn.actsOn
declarations.signature: Systems.ActsOn.actsOn.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [self : Systems.ActsOn α] : α → α → Prop
declarations.source: actsOn : α → α → Prop

declarations.name: Systems.«term_▷_»
declarations.doc: Notation: a ▷ b for "a acts on b" (Bunge's symbol).
declarations.signature: Systems.«term_▷_» : Lean.TrailingParserDescr

/-- Notation: a ▷ b for "a acts on b" (Bunge's symbol). -/
scoped infixl:50 " ▷ " => actsOn

declarations.name: Systems.Bonded
declarations.doc:
Two things are bonded if at least one acts on the other.
Bunge §1.2: "two things are connected if at least one of them
acts on the other."
Note: bonding is symmetric but ActsOn is not — the asymmetry
(agent vs. patient) is important.
declarations.signature: Systems.Bonded.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a b : α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Two things are bonded if at least one acts on the other.
    Bunge §1.2: "two things are connected if at least one of them
    acts on the other."
    Note: bonding is symmetric but ActsOn is not — the asymmetry
    (agent vs. patient) is important. -/
def Bonded {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a b : α) : Prop :=
  a ▷ b ∨ b ▷ a

declarations.name: Systems.bonded_comm
declarations.doc: Bonded is symmetric by definition.
declarations.signature:
Systems.bonded_comm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a b : α) :
  Systems.Bonded a b ↔ Systems.Bonded b a
declarations.source:
/-- Bonded is symmetric by definition. -/
theorem bonded_comm {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a b : α) :
    Bonded a b ↔ Bonded b a := by
  simp [Bonded, or_comm]

declarations.name: Systems.Bondage
declarations.doc:
The bondage of a set X is the set of all bonded pairs within X.
Bunge §1.2: B_A is the set of bonds among the things in A.
declarations.signature: Systems.Bondage.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (X : Set α) : Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.NonBondingRelations
declarations.doc:
The set of non-bonding relations: complement of Bondage in the
total relation set on X.
Bunge §1.2: B̄_A, the nonbonding relations.
declarations.signature:
Systems.NonBondingRelations.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (X : Set α) (R : Set (α × α)) :
  Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.actsOn_mem_bondage
declarations.doc: If a acts on b and both are in X, then (a,b) is in the bondage of X.
declarations.signature:
Systems.actsOn_mem_bondage.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] {X : Set α} {a b : α}
  (ha : a ∈ X) (hb : b ∈ X) (hab : Systems.actsOn a b) : (a, b) ∈ Systems.Bondage X
declarations.source:
/-- If a acts on b and both are in X, then (a,b) is in the bondage of X. -/
theorem actsOn_mem_bondage {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] {X : Set α} {a b : α}
    (ha : a ∈ X) (hb : b ∈ X) (hab : a ▷ b) :
    (a, b) ∈ Bondage X :=
  ⟨ha, hb, Or.inl hab⟩

declarations.name: Systems.SameKind
declarations.doc:
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:233): "Systems exhibit various kinds and levels of complexity."
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:334): "Ultimately the complexity of any identified system is based on
the total number of components, number of kinds of components, and the attributes of
networks within a level and between levels (i.e., the degree of modularization)."
Encoding: "number of kinds of components"→the count of `SameKind` equivalence classes on
`composition` (kind = interaction profile under `▷`); "total number of components"→
`has_two_components` (lower bound); "attributes of networks"→`structure'` counts
(`compose_internalStructure_ge_*`); "between levels"→`RecursiveSystem.depth`.
Not encoded: "levels of complexity" as a graded scale (no single complexity measure is
defined); "degree of modularization" (Level.lean `NearDecomposable`); behavioral
complexity (Mobus defers it); kinds as intrinsic types — two physically different
components with identical interaction profiles count as one kind.

Two things are of the same kind iff they have identical interaction
profiles: they act on exactly the same things, and exactly the same
things act on them.

Source: ActsOn (Systemness #1). No new structure needed.

The number of SameKind equivalence classes in a system's composition
is its component-kind diversity — a complexity measure derivable
entirely from the ActsOn relation.
declarations.signature: Systems.SameKind.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a b : α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:233): "Systems exhibit various kinds and levels of complexity."
    Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:334): "Ultimately the complexity of any identified system is based on
    the total number of components, number of kinds of components, and the attributes of
    networks within a level and between levels (i.e., the degree of modularization)."
    Encoding: "number of kinds of components"→the count of `SameKind` equivalence classes on
    `composition` (kind = interaction profile under `▷`); "total number of components"→
    `has_two_components` (lower bound); "attributes of networks"→`structure'` counts
    (`compose_internalStructure_ge_*`); "between levels"→`RecursiveSystem.depth`.
    Not encoded: "levels of complexity" as a graded scale (no single complexity measure is
    defined); "degree of modularization" (Level.lean `NearDecomposable`); behavioral
    complexity (Mobus defers it); kinds as intrinsic types — two physically different
    components with identical interaction profiles count as one kind.

    Two things are of the same kind iff they have identical interaction
    profiles: they act on exactly the same things, and exactly the same
    things act on them.

    Source: ActsOn (Systemness #1). No new structure needed.

    The number of SameKind equivalence classes in a system's composition
    is its component-kind diversity — a complexity measure derivable
    entirely from the ActsOn relation. -/
def SameKind {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a b : α) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, a ▷ x ↔ b ▷ x) ∧ (∀ x, x ▷ a ↔ x ▷ b)

declarations.name: Systems.sameKind_refl
declarations.signature: Systems.sameKind_refl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a : α) : Systems.SameKind a a
declarations.source:
theorem sameKind_refl {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a : α) : SameKind a a :=
  ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sameKind_symm
declarations.signature:
Systems.sameKind_symm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] {a b : α} (h : Systems.SameKind a b) :
  Systems.SameKind b a

declarations.name: Systems.sameKind_trans
declarations.signature:
Systems.sameKind_trans.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] {a b c : α}
  (hab : Systems.SameKind a b) (hbc : Systems.SameKind b c) : Systems.SameKind a c

declarations.name: Systems.sameKind_equivalence
declarations.doc:
SameKind is an equivalence relation on any type with ActsOn.
This guarantees that component-kind diversity (the number of
equivalence classes) is well-defined.
declarations.signature: Systems.sameKind_equivalence.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] : Equivalence Systems.SameKind
declarations.source:
/-- SameKind is an equivalence relation on any type with ActsOn.
    This guarantees that component-kind diversity (the number of
    equivalence classes) is well-defined. -/
theorem sameKind_equivalence {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    Equivalence (@SameKind α _) :=
  ⟨sameKind_refl, fun h => sameKind_symm h, fun h₁ h₂ => sameKind_trans h₁ h₂⟩

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.has_two_components
declarations.doc:
Every system has at least 2 distinct components.
Immediate from bondage_nonempty: the CES constraint guarantees
non-trivial component complexity for every system.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.has_two_components.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : ∃ a ∈ σ.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ.composition, a ≠ b
declarations.source:
/-- Every system has at least 2 distinct components.
    Immediate from bondage_nonempty: the CES constraint guarantees
    non-trivial component complexity for every system. -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.has_two_components {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ : ConcreteSystem α) :
    ∃ a ∈ σ.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ.composition, a ≠ b := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hne, _⟩ := σ.bondage_nonempty
  exact ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hne⟩

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.compose_internalStructure_ge_left
declarations.doc:
Composition preserves internal structure: every bond internal to σ₁
remains internal in the composed system.

Bonds that were EXTERNAL to σ₁ (one endpoint in σ₁'s environment
that is a component of σ₂) become INTERNAL in the composed system.
Composition internalizes cross-boundary interaction — a qualitative
increase in structural complexity.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.compose_internalStructure_ge_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {σ₁ σ₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α} (h_disjoint : σ₁.composition ∩ σ₂.composition = ∅)
  (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ σ₁.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ₂.composition, Systems.Bonded a b) :
  σ₁.internalStructure ⊆ (σ₁.compose σ₂ h_disjoint h_interact).internalStructure
declarations.source:
/-- Composition preserves internal structure: every bond internal to σ₁
    remains internal in the composed system.

    Bonds that were EXTERNAL to σ₁ (one endpoint in σ₁'s environment
    that is a component of σ₂) become INTERNAL in the composed system.
    Composition internalizes cross-boundary interaction — a qualitative
    increase in structural complexity. -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.compose_internalStructure_ge_left {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {σ₁ σ₂ : ConcreteSystem α}
    (h_disjoint : σ₁.composition ∩ σ₂.composition = ∅)
    (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ σ₁.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ₂.composition, Bonded a b) :
    σ₁.internalStructure ⊆
      (σ₁.compose σ₂ h_disjoint h_interact).internalStructure := by
  intro p hp
  unfold ConcreteSystem.internalStructure at hp ⊢
  dsimp [ConcreteSystem.compose]
  obtain ⟨hs, hc1, hc2⟩ := hp
  exact ⟨Set.mem_union_left _ hs, Set.mem_union_left _ hc1, Set.mem_union_left _ hc2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.compose_internalStructure_ge_right
declarations.doc: Symmetric: composition preserves σ₂'s internal structure too.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.compose_internalStructure_ge_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {σ₁ σ₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α} (h_disjoint : σ₁.composition ∩ σ₂.composition = ∅)
  (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ σ₁.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ₂.composition, Systems.Bonded a b) :
  σ₂.internalStructure ⊆ (σ₁.compose σ₂ h_disjoint h_interact).internalStructure
declarations.source:
/-- Symmetric: composition preserves σ₂'s internal structure too. -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.compose_internalStructure_ge_right {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {σ₁ σ₂ : ConcreteSystem α}
    (h_disjoint : σ₁.composition ∩ σ₂.composition = ∅)
    (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ σ₁.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ₂.composition, Bonded a b) :
    σ₂.internalStructure ⊆
      (σ₁.compose σ₂ h_disjoint h_interact).internalStructure := by
  intro p hp
  unfold ConcreteSystem.internalStructure at hp ⊢
  dsimp [ConcreteSystem.compose]
  obtain ⟨hs, hc1, hc2⟩ := hp
  exact ⟨Set.mem_union_right _ hs, Set.mem_union_right _ hc1, Set.mem_union_right _ hc2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.inflows
declarations.doc: `in(c)`: parent internal-network edges flowing INTO the chosen component.

declarations.name: Systems.outflows
declarations.doc: `out(c)`: parent internal-network edges flowing OUT of the chosen component.

declarations.name: Systems.childSources
declarations.doc:
`Src′`: child external-flow edges inbound from the child's environment
(source ∈ O′). By the child's `bipartite` constraint the target of such an
edge is an interface component — the child-side terminal the contract lands on.

declarations.name: Systems.childSinks
declarations.doc:
`Snk′`: child external-flow edges outbound to the child's environment
(target ∈ O′). The source of such an edge is an interface component.

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition
declarations.doc:
A decomposition of component `comp` of `parent` into `child`, by reference.

The boundary contract `β : Src′ ⊎ Snk′ ≅ in(c) ⊎ out(c)` is carried as two
equivalences so that **direction-preservation holds by construction**:
`βsrc` bijects the child's sources with `c`'s inflows, `βsnk` the child's
sinks with `c`'s outflows. Substance-kind preservation and interface-landing
are the remaining `Prop` fields; the child's environment `E′` is derived
from the parent's interior neighborhood of `comp` (`derived_env`) — the
condition `RecursiveSystem` cannot state.

Parametric slots `T′, H′, Δt′` do not appear: they are level-local
(`H` = History, not hierarchy) or belong to the deferred dynamical face.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Decomposition.{u_9, u_10, u_11, u_12, u_13, u_14, u_15, u_16} (α : Type u_9) (κ : Type u_10)
  (μ : Type u_11) (π : Type u_12) (τ : Type u_13) (η : Type u_14) (δ : Type u_15) (σ : Type u_16) :
  Type (max (max (max (max (max (max (max u_10 u_11) u_12) u_13) u_14) u_15) u_16) u_9)
declarations.source:
/-- A decomposition of component `comp` of `parent` into `child`, by reference.

    The boundary contract `β : Src′ ⊎ Snk′ ≅ in(c) ⊎ out(c)` is carried as two
    equivalences so that **direction-preservation holds by construction**:
    `βsrc` bijects the child's sources with `c`'s inflows, `βsnk` the child's
    sinks with `c`'s outflows. Substance-kind preservation and interface-landing
    are the remaining `Prop` fields; the child's environment `E′` is derived
    from the parent's interior neighborhood of `comp` (`derived_env`) — the
    condition `RecursiveSystem` cannot state.

    Parametric slots `T′, H′, Δt′` do not appear: they are level-local
    (`H` = History, not hierarchy) or belong to the deferred dynamical face. -/
structure Decomposition (α κ μ π τ η δ σ : Type*) where
  /-- The parent flat 8-tuple (one level). -/
  parent : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ
  /-- The complex component being decomposed. -/
  comp : α
  /-- The child flat 8-tuple that replaces `comp`'s opacity. -/
  child : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ
  /-- Substance-kind label on flow edges (matter / energy / message).
      Introduced here because `FlowEdge` carries no substance slot. -/
  kind : FlowEdge α κ → σ
  /-- The decomposed component is a genuine parent component. -/
  comp_mem : comp ∈ parent.components
  /-- Contract, source half: child sources biject with `c`'s inflows. -/
  βsrc : childSources child ≃ inflows parent comp
  /-- Contract, sink half: child sinks biject with `c`'s outflows. -/
  βsnk : childSinks child ≃ outflows parent comp
  /-- (ii) `βsrc` preserves substance kind. -/
  src_preserves_kind :
    ∀ e : childSources child, kind (↑(βsrc e) : FlowEdge α κ) = kind (↑e : FlowEdge α κ)
  /-- (ii) `βsnk` preserves substance kind. -/
  snk_preserves_kind :
    ∀ e : childSinks child, kind (↑(βsnk e) : FlowEdge α κ) = kind (↑e : FlowEdge α κ)
  /-- (iii) each child source lands on a child interface component (its target). -/
  src_lands : ∀ e ∈ childSources child, e.target ∈ child.boundary.interfaces
  /-- (iii) each child sink lands on a child interface component (its source). -/
  snk_lands : ∀ e ∈ childSinks child, e.source ∈ child.boundary.interfaces
  /-- `E′` is DERIVED: the parent's interior neighborhood of `comp`
      (its predecessors and successors in `N`). Nothing else may appear in `E′`. -/
  derived_env : child.environment.objects =
    parent.internalNetwork.successors comp ∪ parent.internalNetwork.predecessors comp

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.seam
declarations.doc:
The seam bijection `β : Src′ ⊎ Snk′ ≅ in(c) ⊎ out(c)`, assembled from the
two direction-typed halves.
declarations.source:
/-- The seam bijection `β : Src′ ⊎ Snk′ ≅ in(c) ⊎ out(c)`, assembled from the
    two direction-typed halves. -/
def seam (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ) :
    (childSources d.child ⊕ childSinks d.child) ≃
      (inflows d.parent d.comp ⊕ outflows d.parent d.comp) :=
  Equiv.sumCongr d.βsrc d.βsnk

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.seam_inl
declarations.doc: Direction-preservation, source half: sources map to inflows (`inl ↦ inl`).
declarations.source:
/-- Direction-preservation, source half: sources map to inflows (`inl ↦ inl`). -/
@[simp] theorem seam_inl (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ)
    (e : childSources d.child) : d.seam (Sum.inl e) = Sum.inl (d.βsrc e) := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.seam_inr
declarations.doc: Direction-preservation, sink half: sinks map to outflows (`inr ↦ inr`).
declarations.source:
/-- Direction-preservation, sink half: sinks map to outflows (`inr ↦ inr`). -/
@[simp] theorem seam_inr (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ)
    (e : childSinks d.child) : d.seam (Sum.inr e) = Sum.inr (d.βsnk e) := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.seam_bijective
declarations.doc:
Flow conservation: the seam is a bijection (each parent flow at `comp`
corresponds to exactly one child boundary flow, and conversely).
declarations.source:
/-- Flow conservation: the seam is a bijection (each parent flow at `comp`
    corresponds to exactly one child boundary flow, and conversely). -/
theorem seam_bijective (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ) :
    Function.Bijective d.seam :=
  d.seam.bijective

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.inflow_continues
declarations.doc: Each parent inflow at `comp` continues into exactly one child source.
declarations.source:
/-- Each parent inflow at `comp` continues into exactly one child source. -/
theorem inflow_continues (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ)
    (p : inflows d.parent d.comp) : ∃! e : childSources d.child, d.βsrc e = p :=
  d.βsrc.bijective.existsUnique p

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.outflow_continues
declarations.doc: Each parent outflow at `comp` continues into exactly one child sink.
declarations.source:
/-- Each parent outflow at `comp` continues into exactly one child sink. -/
theorem outflow_continues (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ)
    (p : outflows d.parent d.comp) : ∃! e : childSinks d.child, d.βsnk e = p :=
  d.βsnk.bijective.existsUnique p

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.seam_preserves_kind
declarations.doc: Substance-kind preservation across the whole seam.
declarations.source:
/-- Substance-kind preservation across the whole seam. -/
theorem seam_preserves_kind (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ)
    (x : childSources d.child ⊕ childSinks d.child) :
    d.kind (edgeOf (d.seam x)) = d.kind (edgeOf x) := by
  cases x with
  | inl e => simp only [seam_inl, edgeOf, Sum.elim_inl]; exact d.src_preserves_kind e
  | inr e => simp only [seam_inr, edgeOf, Sum.elim_inr]; exact d.snk_preserves_kind e

declarations.name: Systems.Decomposition.substitution_sound
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3 (Eq. 4.3, structural).** Substituting the contracted child
for `comp` preserves the seam: `seam` is a bijection that preserves flow
direction (`inl`/`inr`) and substance kind. Purely structural — no `T`
composition, no `Δt`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Decomposition.substitution_sound.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8} {α : Type u_1}
  {κ : Type u_2} {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7}
  {σ : Type u_8} (d : Systems.Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ) :
  Function.Bijective ⇑d.seam ∧
    (∀ (e : ↑(Systems.childSources d.child)), d.seam (Sum.inl e) = Sum.inl (d.βsrc e)) ∧
      (∀ (e : ↑(Systems.childSinks d.child)), d.seam (Sum.inr e) = Sum.inr (d.βsnk e)) ∧
        ∀ (x : ↑(Systems.childSources d.child) ⊕ ↑(Systems.childSinks d.child)),
          d.kind (Systems.Decomposition.edgeOf✝ (d.seam x)) =
            d.kind (Systems.Decomposition.edgeOf✝¹ x)
declarations.source:
/-- **Statement 3 (Eq. 4.3, structural).** Substituting the contracted child
    for `comp` preserves the seam: `seam` is a bijection that preserves flow
    direction (`inl`/`inr`) and substance kind. Purely structural — no `T`
    composition, no `Δt`. -/
theorem substitution_sound (d : Decomposition α κ μ π τ η δ σ) :
    Function.Bijective d.seam ∧
      (∀ e : childSources d.child, d.seam (Sum.inl e) = Sum.inl (d.βsrc e)) ∧
      (∀ e : childSinks d.child, d.seam (Sum.inr e) = Sum.inr (d.βsnk e)) ∧
      (∀ x, d.kind (edgeOf (d.seam x)) = d.kind (edgeOf x)) :=
  ⟨d.seam.bijective, fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl, d.seam_preserves_kind⟩

declarations.name: Systems.assembleDepth1
declarations.doc:
Assemble a parent `ConcreteSystem` and a list of components (each mapped to
a child `RecursiveSystem`) into one in-place `RecursiveSystem` node.
declarations.signature:
Systems.assembleDepth1.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (t : α)
  (σ' : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) (comps : List α) (childOf : α → Systems.RecursiveSystem α) :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Assemble a parent `ConcreteSystem` and a list of components (each mapped to
    a child `RecursiveSystem`) into one in-place `RecursiveSystem` node. -/
def assembleDepth1 (t : α) (σ' : ConcreteSystem α) (comps : List α)
    (childOf : α → RecursiveSystem α) : RecursiveSystem α :=
  .composite t σ' (comps.map childOf)

declarations.name: Systems.assembleDepth1_wellFormed
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (depth 1).** If `comps` enumerates the parent's composition
and every child sits at its component's identity and is well-formed, the
assembled node is `WellFormed`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.assembleDepth1_wellFormed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (t : α)
  (σ' : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) (comps : List α) (childOf : α → Systems.RecursiveSystem α)
  (hcov : ∀ x ∈ σ'.composition, x ∈ comps) (hcomps : ∀ x ∈ comps, x ∈ σ'.composition)
  (hthing : ∀ x ∈ comps, (childOf x).thing = x) (hwf : ∀ x ∈ comps, (childOf x).WellFormed) :
  (Systems.assembleDepth1 t σ' comps childOf).WellFormed
declarations.source:
/-- **Statement 2 (depth 1).** If `comps` enumerates the parent's composition
    and every child sits at its component's identity and is well-formed, the
    assembled node is `WellFormed`. -/
theorem assembleDepth1_wellFormed (t : α) (σ' : ConcreteSystem α) (comps : List α)
    (childOf : α → RecursiveSystem α)
    (hcov : ∀ x ∈ σ'.composition, x ∈ comps)
    (hcomps : ∀ x ∈ comps, x ∈ σ'.composition)
    (hthing : ∀ x ∈ comps, (childOf x).thing = x)
    (hwf : ∀ x ∈ comps, (childOf x).WellFormed) :
    (assembleDepth1 t σ' comps childOf).WellFormed := by
  unfold assembleDepth1 RecursiveSystem.WellFormed
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    exact ⟨childOf x, List.mem_map.mpr ⟨x, hcov x hx, rfl⟩, hthing x (hcov x hx)⟩
  · intro c hc
    obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hc
    rw [hthing y hy]; exact hcomps y hy
  · intro c hc
    obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hc
    exact hwf y hy

declarations.name: Systems.decompose_one_wellFormed
declarations.doc:
Corollary: decomposing exactly ONE component `c` (expanded to any
well-formed `childRS`) while every other component stays a primitive
reference stub yields a `WellFormed` assembly. The proof is indifferent to
whether the `c` slot is expanded or a stub — the "same mathematics" claim,
made concrete.
declarations.signature:
Systems.decompose_one_wellFormed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] [DecidableEq α] (t c : α)
  (σ' : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) (comps : List α) (hcov : ∀ x ∈ σ'.composition, x ∈ comps)
  (hcomps : ∀ x ∈ comps, x ∈ σ'.composition) (childRS : Systems.RecursiveSystem α)
  (hchild_thing : childRS.thing = c) (hchild_wf : childRS.WellFormed) :
  (Systems.assembleDepth1 t σ' comps fun x =>
      if x = c then childRS else Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive x).WellFormed
declarations.source:
/-- Corollary: decomposing exactly ONE component `c` (expanded to any
    well-formed `childRS`) while every other component stays a primitive
    reference stub yields a `WellFormed` assembly. The proof is indifferent to
    whether the `c` slot is expanded or a stub — the "same mathematics" claim,
    made concrete. -/
theorem decompose_one_wellFormed [DecidableEq α]
    (t c : α) (σ' : ConcreteSystem α) (comps : List α)
    (hcov : ∀ x ∈ σ'.composition, x ∈ comps)
    (hcomps : ∀ x ∈ comps, x ∈ σ'.composition)
    (childRS : RecursiveSystem α)
    (hchild_thing : childRS.thing = c)
    (hchild_wf : childRS.WellFormed) :
    (assembleDepth1 t σ' comps
      (fun x => if x = c then childRS else .primitive x)).WellFormed := by
  refine assembleDepth1_wellFormed t σ' comps _ hcov hcomps ?_ ?_
  · intro x _
    by_cases h : x = c
    · simp only [if_pos h]; rw [hchild_thing]; exact h.symm
    · simp only [if_neg h]; rfl
  · intro x _
    by_cases h : x = c
    · simp only [if_pos h]; exact hchild_wf
    · simp only [if_neg h]; exact RecursiveSystem.primitive_wellFormed x

declarations.name: Systems.DynamicSystem
declarations.doc:
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:232): "Systems are dynamic on multiple time scales."
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:323): "Dynamics (or overt behavior) refers to how the processes operate
or change inputs into outputs over time."
Encoding: system→`system : ConcreteSystem α`; "dynamic ... over time"→`law : S → S` (one
tick of state change; iterated by `evolve`, recorded by `trajectory`); "multiple time
scales"→not in this structure: `TimeScaleSeparation` (Level.lean), `TimescaleDecomposition`
and `InteractionDynamicsBridge` (this file).
Not encoded: inputs and outputs (`law` is closed — no input argument); multiple time scales
in a single system (one law, one tick); continuous time (`Flow` below); spatial scales
(the section title pairs them with time scales); stochastic transitions.

A dynamic system: a ConcreteSystem with an associated state space
and a deterministic state-transition law.

The law captures "what happens next" — the core content of Dynamics
(#4) in its simplest form. Richer forms (time-parameterized flows,
stochastic transitions, input-dependent evolution) extend this;
the deterministic self-map is the foundation.

Bunge §2.2: a thing has a state function F mapping time to state.
The transition law is the generator of this trajectory.

    Not encoded: inputs and outputs (`law` is closed — no input argument); multiple time scales

    The law captures "what happens next" — the core content of Dynamics
    (#4) in its simplest form. Richer forms (time-parameterized flows,
    stochastic transitions, input-dependent evolution) extend this;

    Bunge §2.2: a thing has a state function F mapping time to state.

declarations.name: Systems.DynamicSystem.compose
declarations.doc:
Compose two dynamic systems with independent dynamics.

The composed state space is S₁ × S₂ (product). Each subsystem
evolves according to its own law, independently.

This is the "zeroth-order" dynamics of a near-decomposable system:
at the fast time scale, modules equilibrate independently. The
coupling corrections (slow inter-module dynamics) are what makes
near-decomposable systems nearly, not exactly, decomposable.
declarations.signature:
Systems.DynamicSystem.compose.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] {S₁ : Type u_2}
  {S₂ : Type u_3} (ds₁ : Systems.DynamicSystem α S₁) (ds₂ : Systems.DynamicSystem α S₂)
  (h_disjoint : ds₁.system.composition ∩ ds₂.system.composition = ∅)
  (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ ds₁.system.composition, ∃ b ∈ ds₂.system.composition, Systems.Bonded a b) :
  Systems.DynamicSystem α (S₁ × S₂)
declarations.source:
/-- Compose two dynamic systems with independent dynamics.

    The composed state space is S₁ × S₂ (product). Each subsystem
    evolves according to its own law, independently.

    This is the "zeroth-order" dynamics of a near-decomposable system:
    at the fast time scale, modules equilibrate independently. The
    coupling corrections (slow inter-module dynamics) are what makes
    near-decomposable systems nearly, not exactly, decomposable. -/
def DynamicSystem.compose {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] {S₁ S₂ : Type*}
    (ds₁ : DynamicSystem α S₁) (ds₂ : DynamicSystem α S₂)
    (h_disjoint : ds₁.system.composition ∩ ds₂.system.composition = ∅)
    (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ ds₁.system.composition,
      ∃ b ∈ ds₂.system.composition, Bonded a b) :
    DynamicSystem α (S₁ × S₂) where
  system := ds₁.system.compose ds₂.system h_disjoint h_interact
  law := fun (s₁, s₂) => (ds₁.law s₁, ds₂.law s₂)

declarations.name: Systems.DynamicSystem.compose_proj_left
declarations.doc:
The composed dynamics preserves σ₁'s state evolution:
projecting the composed state to S₁ and evolving equals
evolving in S₁ and then projecting.
declarations.signature:
Systems.DynamicSystem.compose_proj_left.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {S₁ : Type u_2} {S₂ : Type u_3} (ds₁ : Systems.DynamicSystem α S₁)
  (ds₂ : Systems.DynamicSystem α S₂)
  (h_disjoint : ds₁.system.composition ∩ ds₂.system.composition = ∅)
  (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ ds₁.system.composition, ∃ b ∈ ds₂.system.composition, Systems.Bonded a b)
  (s : S₁ × S₂) : ((ds₁.compose ds₂ h_disjoint h_interact).law s).1 = ds₁.law s.1
declarations.source:
/-- The composed dynamics preserves σ₁'s state evolution:
    projecting the composed state to S₁ and evolving equals
    evolving in S₁ and then projecting. -/
theorem DynamicSystem.compose_proj_left {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {S₁ S₂ : Type*}
    (ds₁ : DynamicSystem α S₁) (ds₂ : DynamicSystem α S₂)
    (h_disjoint : ds₁.system.composition ∩ ds₂.system.composition = ∅)
    (h_interact : ∃ a ∈ ds₁.system.composition,
      ∃ b ∈ ds₂.system.composition, Bonded a b)
    (s : S₁ × S₂) :
    ((ds₁.compose ds₂ h_disjoint h_interact).law s).1 = ds₁.law s.1 := by
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.DynamicSystem.compose_proj_right
declarations.doc: The composed dynamics preserves σ₂'s state evolution.
declarations.signature:
Systems.DynamicSystem.compose_proj_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {S₁ : Type u_2} {S₂ : Type u_3} (ds₁ : Systems.DynamicSystem α S₁)
  (ds₂ : Systems.DynamicSystem α S₂)

declarations.name: Systems.InteractionDynamicsBridge
declarations.doc:
The interaction-dynamics bridge: stronger interaction produces
faster characteristic dynamics.

This is the physical assumption Simon left implicit in his 1962
paper. It says: interaction strength (a structural property from
Hierarchy #2) monotonically determines time scale (a dynamical
property from Dynamics #4).

`toTimeScale` maps interaction strength to characteristic time.
`StrictAnti` means stronger interaction → shorter time scale
(faster dynamics).

  [Preorder S] : Type (max u_1 u_2)

/-- The interaction-dynamics bridge: stronger interaction produces
    faster characteristic dynamics.

    This is the physical assumption Simon left implicit in his 1962
    paper. It says: interaction strength (a structural property from
    Hierarchy #2) monotonically determines time scale (a dynamical
    property from Dynamics #4).

    `toTimeScale` maps interaction strength to characteristic time.
    `StrictAnti` means stronger interaction → shorter time scale
    (faster dynamics). -/
structure InteractionDynamicsBridge
    (T : Type*) [LinearOrder T]
    (S : Type*) [Preorder S] where
  toTimeScale : T → S
  strictAnti : StrictAnti toTimeScale

declarations.name: Systems.NearDecomposable.simon_from_bridge
declarations.doc:
Simon's conditional, instantiated from a dynamics-interaction bridge.

Given a near-decomposable system and evidence that its dynamics
respects its interaction structure, within-module dynamics are
strictly faster than between-module dynamics.

This is the COMPLETED form of Simon's argument: the conditional
from Level.lean supplies the logic; the bridge supplies the
dynamical assumption. Together they prove time-scale separation.
declarations.signature:
Systems.NearDecomposable.simon_from_bridge.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α} {T : Type u_2} [LinearOrder T] [Systems.InteractionStrength α T]
  (nd : Systems.NearDecomposable σ T) {S : Type u_3} [Preorder S]
  (bridge : Systems.InteractionDynamicsBridge T S) {m₁ m₂ : Set α} (hm₁ : m₁ ∈ nd.modules)
  (hm₂ : m₂ ∈ nd.modules) (hne : m₁ ≠ m₂) {a b : α} (ha : a ∈ m₁) (hb : b ∈ m₁) (hab : a ≠ b)
  {c : α} (hc : c ∈ m₂) :
  bridge.toTimeScale (Systems.strength a b) < bridge.toTimeScale (Systems.strength a c)
declarations.source:
/-- Simon's conditional, instantiated from a dynamics-interaction bridge.

    Given a near-decomposable system and evidence that its dynamics
    respects its interaction structure, within-module dynamics are
    strictly faster than between-module dynamics.

    This is the COMPLETED form of Simon's argument: the conditional
    from Level.lean supplies the logic; the bridge supplies the
    dynamical assumption. Together they prove time-scale separation. -/
theorem NearDecomposable.simon_from_bridge
    {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {σ : ConcreteSystem α} {T : Type*} [LinearOrder T]
    [InteractionStrength α T]
    (nd : NearDecomposable σ T)
    {S : Type*} [Preorder S]
    (bridge : InteractionDynamicsBridge T S)
    {m₁ m₂ : Set α} (hm₁ : m₁ ∈ nd.modules) (hm₂ : m₂ ∈ nd.modules)
    (hne : m₁ ≠ m₂)
    {a b : α} (ha : a ∈ m₁) (hb : b ∈ m₁) (hab : a ≠ b)
    {c : α} (hc : c ∈ m₂) :
    bridge.toTimeScale (@strength α T _ a b) <
      bridge.toTimeScale (@strength α T _ a c) :=
  nd.conditional_time_scale_separation bridge.toTimeScale bridge.strictAnti
    hm₁ hm₂ hne ha hb hab hc

declarations.doc:
A coupled dynamic system: two subsystems whose evolution depends
on each other's state.

`law₁ s₁ s₂` gives the next state of subsystem 1 given both
subsystems' current states. Similarly for `law₂`.

Independent dynamics is the special case where law₁ ignores s₂
and law₂ ignores s₁.

/-- A coupled dynamic system: two subsystems whose evolution depends
    on each other's state.

    `law₁ s₁ s₂` gives the next state of subsystem 1 given both
    subsystems' current states. Similarly for `law₂`.

    Independent dynamics is the special case where law₁ ignores s₂
    and law₂ ignores s₁. -/
structure CoupledDynamicSystem (α : Type*) [ActsOn α]
