declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.eliminated
declarations.doc:
The eliminated set: systems removed by selection.
Bunge Def 1.15(ii): Ā_E = S - A_E.
declarations.signature: Systems.SelectiveAction.eliminated.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (sel : Systems.SelectiveAction α) : Set α
declarations.source:
/-- The eliminated set: systems removed by selection.
    Bunge Def 1.15(ii): Ā_E = S - A_E. -/
def SelectiveAction.eliminated {α : Type*}
    (sel : SelectiveAction α) : Set α :=
  sel.population \ sel.adapted

declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.partition
declarations.doc:
The population is partitioned into adapted and eliminated.
adapted ∪ eliminated = population.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelectiveAction.partition.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (sel : Systems.SelectiveAction α) :
  sel.adapted ∪ sel.eliminated = sel.population
declarations.source:
/-- The population is partitioned into adapted and eliminated.
    adapted ∪ eliminated = population. -/
theorem SelectiveAction.partition {α : Type*}
    (sel : SelectiveAction α) :
    sel.adapted ∪ sel.eliminated = sel.population := by
  ext x
  simp [SelectiveAction.eliminated, Set.mem_diff]
  constructor
  · rintro (h | ⟨hp, _⟩) <;> [exact sel.adapted_sub h; exact hp]
  · intro hp
    by_cases ha : x ∈ sel.adapted
    · exact Or.inl ha
    · exact Or.inr ⟨hp, ha⟩

declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.adapted_eliminated_disjoint
declarations.doc: Adapted and eliminated are disjoint.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelectiveAction.adapted_eliminated_disjoint.{u_1} {α : Type u_1}
  (sel : Systems.SelectiveAction α) : sel.adapted ∩ sel.eliminated = ∅
declarations.source:
/-- Adapted and eliminated are disjoint. -/
theorem SelectiveAction.adapted_eliminated_disjoint {α : Type*}
    (sel : SelectiveAction α) :
    sel.adapted ∩ sel.eliminated = ∅ := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, SelectiveAction.eliminated, Set.mem_diff,
    Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_and, not_not]
  exact fun h _ => h

declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.compose
declarations.doc:
Compose two consecutive selective actions.
Bunge Thm 1.2: If E and E' are two different consecutive environments,
the resulting selective action is i_{EE'} = i_{E'} ∘ i_E.

The second environment acts on the survivors of the first.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelectiveAction.compose.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (sel₁ sel₂ : Systems.SelectiveAction α)
  (h : sel₂.population = sel₁.adapted) : Systems.SelectiveAction α
declarations.source:
/-- Compose two consecutive selective actions.
    Bunge Thm 1.2: If E and E' are two different consecutive environments,
    the resulting selective action is i_{EE'} = i_{E'} ∘ i_E.

    The second environment acts on the survivors of the first. -/
def SelectiveAction.compose {α : Type*}
    (sel₁ : SelectiveAction α) (sel₂ : SelectiveAction α)
    (h : sel₂.population = sel₁.adapted) : SelectiveAction α where
  population := sel₁.population
  adapted := sel₂.adapted
  adapted_sub := by
    intro x hx
    have h₂ := sel₂.adapted_sub hx
    rw [h] at h₂
    exact sel₁.adapted_sub h₂

declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.compose_adapted_sub
declarations.doc:
The adapted set of a composed selection is a subset of the first
environment's adapted set.
Consequence of Thm 1.2: A_{EE'} ⊆ A_E.
declarations.source:
/-- The adapted set of a composed selection is a subset of the first
    environment's adapted set.
    Consequence of Thm 1.2: A_{EE'} ⊆ A_E. -/
theorem SelectiveAction.compose_adapted_sub {α : Type*}
    (sel₁ : SelectiveAction α) (sel₂ : SelectiveAction α)
    (h : sel₂.population = sel₁.adapted) :
    (sel₁.compose sel₂ h).adapted ⊆ sel₁.adapted := by
  intro x hx
  have h₂ := sel₂.adapted_sub hx
  rw [h] at h₂
  exact h₂

declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.compose_adapted_eq
declarations.doc:
The composed adapted set is exactly the second selection's adapted set.
This is the core of Thm 1.2: composition of inclusion maps.
declarations.source:
/-- The composed adapted set is exactly the second selection's adapted set.
    This is the core of Thm 1.2: composition of inclusion maps. -/
theorem SelectiveAction.compose_adapted_eq {α : Type*}
    (sel₁ : SelectiveAction α) (sel₂ : SelectiveAction α)
    (h : sel₂.population = sel₁.adapted) :
    (sel₁.compose sel₂ h).adapted = sel₂.adapted :=
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.SelectiveAction.compose_assoc_adapted
declarations.doc:
Selection composition is associative.
Consequence of Thm 1.2: the adapted set of a triple composition
equals the adapted set of the third selection.
declarations.source:
/-- Selection composition is associative.
    Consequence of Thm 1.2: the adapted set of a triple composition
    equals the adapted set of the third selection. -/
theorem SelectiveAction.compose_assoc_adapted {α : Type*}
    (s₁ s₂ s₃ : SelectiveAction α)
    (h₁₂ : s₂.population = s₁.adapted)
    (h₂₃ : s₃.population = s₂.adapted) :
    ((s₁.compose s₂ h₁₂).compose s₃
      (by rw [compose_adapted_eq]; exact h₂₃)).adapted = s₃.adapted :=
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.UniversalSelection
declarations.doc:
Bunge Postulate 1.6: All systems are subject to environmental selection.
For every set S of any kind K and every environment E common to the
members of S, there is a selective action i_E : S → A_E with A_E ⊂ S.

We express this as: the adapted set is always a proper subset.
declarations.signature: Systems.UniversalSelection.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Bunge Postulate 1.6: All systems are subject to environmental selection.
    For every set S of any kind K and every environment E common to the
    members of S, there is a selective action i_E : S → A_E with A_E ⊂ S.

    We express this as: the adapted set is always a proper subset. -/
def UniversalSelection (α : Type*) : Prop :=
  ∀ (sel : SelectiveAction α),
    sel.population.Nonempty → sel.adapted ⊂ sel.population

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel
declarations.doc:
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:238): "Sufficiently complex, adaptive systems can contain
self-models."
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:368): "Creatures capable of having mentally mediated roles and
identities include models of themselves, and these likewise may involve greater or lesser
accuracy."
Encoding: the system→`dyn : S → S`; "models of themselves"→`selfModel : S → S` on the same
state space, tracking `dyn` via `self_simulates`; "greater or lesser accuracy"→`accurate`
(pointwise: `selfModel s = s`).
Not encoded: "sufficiently complex, adaptive" (no complexity or adaptivity precondition —
every system has `SelfModel.trivial`); "contain" as part–whole (model and modelled share
one state space); graded accuracy (exact-or-not, no metric); "mentally mediated roles and
identities".

A self-model: a system with dynamics `dyn : S → S` together with an internal
self-representation `selfModel : S → S` that simulates the system's OWN
dynamics one step at a time.

`self_simulates` is the self-simulation square — the diagonal instance of
`InternalModel.simulates` with the modelled system equal to the container.
It says: evolving the system then re-reading the self-model equals reading
the self-model then evolving — the self-model is a dynamics endomorphism
(`Function.Semiconj selfModel dyn dyn`).
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfModel.{u_2} (S : Type u_2) : Type u_2
declarations.source:
/-- Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:238): "Sufficiently complex, adaptive systems can contain
    self-models."
    Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:368): "Creatures capable of having mentally mediated roles and
    identities include models of themselves, and these likewise may involve greater or lesser
    accuracy."
    Encoding: the system→`dyn : S → S`; "models of themselves"→`selfModel : S → S` on the same
    state space, tracking `dyn` via `self_simulates`; "greater or lesser accuracy"→`accurate`
    (pointwise: `selfModel s = s`).
    Not encoded: "sufficiently complex, adaptive" (no complexity or adaptivity precondition —
    every system has `SelfModel.trivial`); "contain" as part–whole (model and modelled share
    one state space); graded accuracy (exact-or-not, no metric); "mentally mediated roles and
    identities".

    A self-model: a system with dynamics `dyn : S → S` together with an internal
    self-representation `selfModel : S → S` that simulates the system's OWN
    dynamics one step at a time.

    `self_simulates` is the self-simulation square — the diagonal instance of
    `InternalModel.simulates` with the modelled system equal to the container.
    It says: evolving the system then re-reading the self-model equals reading
    the self-model then evolving — the self-model is a dynamics endomorphism
    (`Function.Semiconj selfModel dyn dyn`). -/
structure SelfModel (S : Type*) where
  /-- The system's own dynamics. -/
  dyn : S → S
  /-- The system's internal model of itself. -/
  selfModel : S → S
  /-- One-step self-simulation: the self-model commutes with the dynamics. -/
  self_simulates : ∀ s, selfModel (dyn s) = dyn (selfModel s)

constructors.name: Systems.SelfModel.mk
constructors.type:
{S : Type u_2} →
  (dyn selfModel : S → S) → (∀ (s : S), selfModel (dyn s) = dyn (selfModel s)) → Systems.SelfModel S

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.dyn
declarations.doc: The system's own dynamics.
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfModel.dyn.{u_2} {S : Type u_2} (self : Systems.SelfModel S) : S → S
declarations.source: dyn : S → S

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.selfModel
declarations.doc: The system's internal model of itself.
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfModel.selfModel.{u_2} {S : Type u_2} (self : Systems.SelfModel S) : S → S
declarations.source: selfModel : S → S

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.self_simulates
declarations.doc: One-step self-simulation: the self-model commutes with the dynamics.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelfModel.self_simulates.{u_2} {S : Type u_2} (self : Systems.SelfModel S) (s : S) :
  self.selfModel (self.dyn s) = self.dyn (self.selfModel s)
declarations.source: self_simulates : ∀ s, selfModel (dyn s) = dyn (selfModel s)

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.toInternalModel
declarations.doc:
A self-model IS the diagonal internal model: an `InternalModel S S` whose
internal and system dynamics are the single shared `dyn`. This is the formal
content of "#10 is the S = R case of #9" — every Internal-Model result
transfers through this map.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelfModel.toInternalModel.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) :
  Systems.InternalModel S S
declarations.source:
/-- A self-model IS the diagonal internal model: an `InternalModel S S` whose
    internal and system dynamics are the single shared `dyn`. This is the formal
    content of "#10 is the S = R case of #9" — every Internal-Model result
    transfers through this map. -/
def SelfModel.toInternalModel (sm : SelfModel S) : InternalModel S S where
  model := sm.selfModel
  internalDyn := sm.dyn
  systemDyn := sm.dyn
  simulates := sm.self_simulates

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.tracks
declarations.doc:
A correct one-step self-model predicts the system's OWN future at every
horizon: reading the self-model after n internal steps equals the system's
actual n-step evolution of the represented state. This is anticipation
turned inward — the system foresees itself — and it is structural, free
from #9's induction.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelfModel.tracks.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
  sm.selfModel (sm.dyn^[n] s) = sm.dyn^[n] (sm.selfModel s)
declarations.source:
/-- A correct one-step self-model predicts the system's OWN future at every
    horizon: reading the self-model after n internal steps equals the system's
    actual n-step evolution of the represented state. This is anticipation
    turned inward — the system foresees itself — and it is structural, free
    from #9's induction. -/
theorem SelfModel.tracks (sm : SelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
    sm.selfModel (sm.dyn^[n] s) = sm.dyn^[n] (sm.selfModel s) :=
  sm.toInternalModel.tracks n s

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.predict
declarations.doc: The self-model's n-step self-prediction from a state.
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfModel.predict.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) : S

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.predict_correct
declarations.doc:
Anticipatory self-model: the n-step self-prediction equals the system's
actual n-step evolution of the represented state, at every horizon.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelfModel.predict_correct.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
  sm.predict n s = sm.dyn^[n] (sm.selfModel s)
declarations.source:
/-- Anticipatory self-model: the n-step self-prediction equals the system's
    actual n-step evolution of the represented state, at every horizon. -/
theorem SelfModel.predict_correct (sm : SelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
    sm.predict n s = sm.dyn^[n] (sm.selfModel s) :=
  sm.tracks n s

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.equilibrium_image
declarations.doc:
A self-modelled equilibrium stays an equilibrium: if a state is at rest
under the dynamics, so is the state its self-model represents. The
self-simulation square carries the system's fixed points through its own
model.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelfModel.equilibrium_image.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) {s : S}
  (h : Systems.IsEquilibrium sm.dyn s) : Systems.IsEquilibrium sm.dyn (sm.selfModel s)
declarations.source:
/-- A self-modelled equilibrium stays an equilibrium: if a state is at rest
    under the dynamics, so is the state its self-model represents. The
    self-simulation square carries the system's fixed points through its own
    model. -/
theorem SelfModel.equilibrium_image (sm : SelfModel S) {s : S}
    (h : IsEquilibrium sm.dyn s) :
    IsEquilibrium sm.dyn (sm.selfModel s) :=
  sm.toInternalModel.equilibrium_image h

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.trivial
declarations.doc:
The trivial self-model: the identity is always a self-model, since `id`
commutes with any dynamics. Hence EVERY system has a self-model — existence
is free, and the real question is faithfulness/non-triviality, not
existence.
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfModel.trivial.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (dyn : S → S) : Systems.SelfModel S
declarations.source:
/-- The trivial self-model: the identity is always a self-model, since `id`
    commutes with any dynamics. Hence EVERY system has a self-model — existence
    is free, and the real question is faithfulness/non-triviality, not
    existence. -/
def SelfModel.trivial (dyn : S → S) : SelfModel S where
  dyn := dyn
  selfModel := id
  self_simulates := fun _ => rfl

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.accurate
declarations.doc:
A state is accurately self-modelled when the self-model represents it as
itself: `selfModel s = s`. This is a self-consistent self-image — the model
and the modelled coincide on `s` (a fixed point of the model map).
declarations.signature: Systems.SelfModel.accurate.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) (s : S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A state is accurately self-modelled when the self-model represents it as
    itself: `selfModel s = s`. This is a self-consistent self-image — the model
    and the modelled coincide on `s` (a fixed point of the model map). -/
def SelfModel.accurate (sm : SelfModel S) (s : S) : Prop := sm.selfModel s = s

declarations.name: Systems.SelfModel.accurate_invariant
declarations.doc:
Self-consistency is preserved by the dynamics: if the self-model represents
`s` as itself, it represents `dyn s` as itself too. The accurate set is
invariant under evolution — the self-image, once correct, stays correct as
the system runs. This is the self-reference loop closing into itself
(`selfModel (dyn s) = dyn (selfModel s) = dyn s`) without Lawvere machinery.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SelfModel.accurate_invariant.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (sm : Systems.SelfModel S) {s : S}
  (h : sm.accurate s) : sm.accurate (sm.dyn s)
declarations.source:
/-- Self-consistency is preserved by the dynamics: if the self-model represents
    `s` as itself, it represents `dyn s` as itself too. The accurate set is
    invariant under evolution — the self-image, once correct, stays correct as
    the system runs. This is the self-reference loop closing into itself
    (`selfModel (dyn s) = dyn (selfModel s) = dyn s`) without Lawvere machinery. -/
theorem SelfModel.accurate_invariant (sm : SelfModel S) {s : S}
    (h : sm.accurate s) : sm.accurate (sm.dyn s) := by
  unfold SelfModel.accurate at *
  rw [sm.self_simulates, h]

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel
declarations.doc:
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:238): "Sufficiently complex, adaptive systems can contain
self-models."
Source: Rosen, Anticipatory Systems (1985) — verbatim not in vault.
Encoding: "self-models"→`selfModel : S → S` against the system's own `dyn`; anticipation→
`lead` steps of `dyn` per tick in `self_simulates`; accuracy→`accurate`.
Not encoded: "sufficiently complex, adaptive" (no precondition); "contain" as part–whole;
graded accuracy.

A fast self-model: the system's self-representation gains `lead` steps of
the system's own dynamics per tick — `AnticipatoryModel S S` with one
shared `dyn` (the diagonal), as `SelfModel` is the diagonal of
`InternalModel`.
declarations.signature: Systems.FastSelfModel.{u_2} (S : Type u_2) : Type u_2
declarations.source:
/-- Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:238): "Sufficiently complex, adaptive systems can contain
    self-models."
    Source: Rosen, Anticipatory Systems (1985) — verbatim not in vault.
    Encoding: "self-models"→`selfModel : S → S` against the system's own `dyn`; anticipation→
    `lead` steps of `dyn` per tick in `self_simulates`; accuracy→`accurate`.
    Not encoded: "sufficiently complex, adaptive" (no precondition); "contain" as part–whole;
    graded accuracy.

    A fast self-model: the system's self-representation gains `lead` steps of
    the system's own dynamics per tick — `AnticipatoryModel S S` with one
    shared `dyn` (the diagonal), as `SelfModel` is the diagonal of
    `InternalModel`. -/
structure FastSelfModel (S : Type*) where
  /-- The system's own dynamics. -/
  dyn : S → S
  /-- The system's internal model of itself. -/
  selfModel : S → S
  /-- System-steps of `dyn` gained per tick. -/
  lead : ℕ
  /-- One tick of the self-model simulates `lead` steps of the system. -/
  self_simulates : ∀ s, selfModel (dyn s) = dyn^[lead] (selfModel s)

  (dyn selfModel : S → S) →
    (lead : ℕ) → (∀ (s : S), selfModel (dyn s) = dyn^[lead] (selfModel s)) → Systems.FastSelfModel S

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.toAnticipatory
declarations.doc:
A fast self-model IS the diagonal anticipatory model: an
`AnticipatoryModel S S` whose internal and system dynamics are the single
shared `dyn`. Every `AnticipatoryModel` result transfers through this map.
declarations.signature:
Systems.FastSelfModel.toAnticipatory.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (fsm : Systems.FastSelfModel S) :
  Systems.AnticipatoryModel S S
declarations.source:
/-- A fast self-model IS the diagonal anticipatory model: an
    `AnticipatoryModel S S` whose internal and system dynamics are the single
    shared `dyn`. Every `AnticipatoryModel` result transfers through this map. -/
def FastSelfModel.toAnticipatory (fsm : FastSelfModel S) : AnticipatoryModel S S where
  model := fsm.selfModel
  internalDyn := fsm.dyn
  systemDyn := fsm.dyn
  lead := fsm.lead
  simulates := fsm.self_simulates

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.tracks
declarations.doc:
Fast self-prediction at every horizon: after n system steps the self-model
has raced `n * lead` steps ahead of the represented state — the compounding
lead of `AnticipatoryModel.tracks`, turned inward.
declarations.signature:
Systems.FastSelfModel.tracks.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (fsm : Systems.FastSelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
  fsm.selfModel (fsm.dyn^[n] s) = fsm.dyn^[n * fsm.lead] (fsm.selfModel s)
declarations.source:
/-- Fast self-prediction at every horizon: after n system steps the self-model
    has raced `n * lead` steps ahead of the represented state — the compounding
    lead of `AnticipatoryModel.tracks`, turned inward. -/
theorem FastSelfModel.tracks (fsm : FastSelfModel S) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
    fsm.selfModel (fsm.dyn^[n] s) = fsm.dyn^[n * fsm.lead] (fsm.selfModel s) :=
  fsm.toAnticipatory.tracks n s

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.accurate
declarations.doc:
A state is accurately self-modelled when the fast self-model represents it
as itself: `selfModel s = s` — same self-consistency as
`SelfModel.accurate`.
declarations.signature: Systems.FastSelfModel.accurate.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (fsm : Systems.FastSelfModel S) (s : S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A state is accurately self-modelled when the fast self-model represents it
    as itself: `selfModel s = s` — same self-consistency as
    `SelfModel.accurate`. -/
def FastSelfModel.accurate (fsm : FastSelfModel S) (s : S) : Prop :=
  fsm.selfModel s = s

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.accurate_collapse
declarations.source:
theorem FastSelfModel.accurate_collapse (fsm : FastSelfModel S) {s : S} {n : ℕ}
    (h1 : fsm.accurate s) (h2 : fsm.accurate (fsm.dyn^[n] s)) :
    fsm.dyn^[n * fsm.lead] s = fsm.dyn^[n] s := by
  unfold FastSelfModel.accurate at h1 h2
  rw [← h2, fsm.tracks, h1]

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.accurate_forces_periodic
declarations.signature:
Systems.FastSelfModel.accurate_forces_periodic.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (fsm : Systems.FastSelfModel S)
  {s : S} {n : ℕ} (h1 : fsm.accurate s) (h2 : fsm.accurate (fsm.dyn^[n] s)) :
  fsm.dyn^[n * (fsm.lead - 1)] (fsm.dyn^[n] s) = fsm.dyn^[n] s
declarations.source:
theorem FastSelfModel.accurate_forces_periodic (fsm : FastSelfModel S) {s : S}
    {n : ℕ} (h1 : fsm.accurate s) (h2 : fsm.accurate (fsm.dyn^[n] s)) :
    fsm.dyn^[n * (fsm.lead - 1)] (fsm.dyn^[n] s) = fsm.dyn^[n] s := by
  rw [← Function.iterate_add_apply]
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos fsm.lead with h0 | hpos
  · simp [h0]
  · have harith : n * (fsm.lead - 1) + n = n * fsm.lead := by
      -- why: succ_pred lemmas speak in Nat.pred while the goal has `- 1`;
      -- reduce to the linear index equation and close it arithmetically
      rw [← Nat.mul_succ]
      congr 1
      omega
    rw [harith]
    exact fsm.accurate_collapse h1 h2

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling
declarations.doc:
The doubling witness: `ℕ` under successor, self-modelled by doubling at
`lead = 2`. One tick of doubling gains two successor steps
(`2·(s+1) = (2·s) + 2`), so this is a genuinely fast self-model.
declarations.signature: Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling : Systems.FastSelfModel ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The doubling witness: `ℕ` under successor, self-modelled by doubling at
    `lead = 2`. One tick of doubling gains two successor steps
    (`2·(s+1) = (2·s) + 2`), so this is a genuinely fast self-model. -/
def FastSelfModel.doubling : FastSelfModel ℕ where
  dyn := Nat.succ
  selfModel := (2 * ·)
  lead := 2
  self_simulates := fun s => by
    simp [Function.iterate_succ_apply', Nat.mul_succ]

declarations.name: Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling_accurate_not_invariant
declarations.doc:
Accuracy is not invariant once the self-model genuinely outruns the system:
the doubling witness is accurate at 0 (`2·0 = 0`) but NOT at `dyn 0 = 1`
(`2·1 ≠ 1`). Contrast `SelfModel.accurate_invariant`, where lockstep
accuracy propagates unconditionally — the invariance of self-consistency is
a lockstep privilege, not a general fact about self-models.
declarations.signature:
Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling_accurate_not_invariant :
  Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling.accurate 0 ∧
    ¬Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling.accurate (Systems.FastSelfModel.doubling.dyn 0)
declarations.source:
/-- Accuracy is not invariant once the self-model genuinely outruns the system:
    the doubling witness is accurate at 0 (`2·0 = 0`) but NOT at `dyn 0 = 1`
    (`2·1 ≠ 1`). Contrast `SelfModel.accurate_invariant`, where lockstep
    accuracy propagates unconditionally — the invariance of self-consistency is
    a lockstep privilege, not a general fact about self-models. -/
theorem FastSelfModel.doubling_accurate_not_invariant :
    FastSelfModel.doubling.accurate 0 ∧
      ¬ FastSelfModel.doubling.accurate (FastSelfModel.doubling.dyn 0) := by
  constructor
  · rfl
  · intro h
    simp [FastSelfModel.accurate, FastSelfModel.doubling] at h

declarations.doc:
A state function for systems of kind K.
Bunge §2.2: F = ⟨F₁, F₂, ..., Fₙ⟩ : A → V₁ × V₂ × ... × Vₙ

We parametrize by:
- T: the time type
- S: the state space type (represents the product V₁ × ... × Vₙ)

/-- A state function for systems of kind K.

    - T: the time type

declarations.name: Systems.lawfulStateSpace
declarations.doc:
The lawful state space: a subset of the conceivable space satisfying laws.
Bunge §2.2: S_L(K) is a proper subset of S(K).
"Since the components of F are lawfully interrelated, and thus mutually
restricted, not every n-tuple represents a really possible state."

Parametrized by a law predicate.
declarations.signature:
Systems.lawfulStateSpace.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {T : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3}
  (F : Systems.StateFunction T S K) (law : S → Prop) : Set S
declarations.source:
/-- The lawful state space: a subset of the conceivable space satisfying laws.
    Bunge §2.2: S_L(K) is a proper subset of S(K).
    "Since the components of F are lawfully interrelated, and thus mutually
    restricted, not every n-tuple represents a really possible state."

    Parametrized by a law predicate. -/
def lawfulStateSpace {T : Type*} {S : Type*} {K : Type*}
    (F : StateFunction T S K) (law : S → Prop) : Set S :=
  {s ∈ conceivableStateSpace F | law s}

declarations.name: Systems.lawful_sub_conceivable
declarations.doc:
The lawful state space is a subset of the conceivable one.
Bunge §2.2: S_L(K) ⊂ S(K).
declarations.source:
/-- The lawful state space is a subset of the conceivable one.
    Bunge §2.2: S_L(K) ⊂ S(K). -/
theorem lawful_sub_conceivable {T : Type*} {S : Type*} {K : Type*}
    (F : StateFunction T S K) (law : S → Prop) :
    lawfulStateSpace F law ⊆ conceivableStateSpace F := by
  intro s hs
  exact hs.1

declarations.name: Systems.Event
declarations.doc:
An event is a state transition ⟨s, s', g⟩ where g is a lawful map.
Bunge §2.2(v): every event is representable by ⟨s, s', g⟩ where
s, s' ∈ S_L(K) and g : S_L(K) → S_L(K) is lawful.

The path g records how the transition occurs (different paths between
the same endpoints represent different processes).

declarations.name: Systems.totalAction
declarations.doc:
Total action of thing x on thing y: the difference between forced and
free trajectory.
Bunge 2.2(x): A(x,y) = h(y|x) minus h(y).

We represent this as the set of time-state pairs where the forced
and free trajectories differ.
declarations.signature:
Systems.totalAction.{u_1, u_2} {T : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2}
  (forcedHistory freeHistory : Set (T × S)) : Set (T × S)
declarations.source:
/-- Total action of thing x on thing y: the difference between forced and
    free trajectory.
    Bunge 2.2(x): A(x,y) = h(y|x) minus h(y).

    We represent this as the set of time-state pairs where the forced
    and free trajectories differ. -/
def totalAction {T : Type*} {S : Type*}
    (forcedHistory freeHistory : Set (T × S)) : Set (T × S) :=
  {p | p ∈ forcedHistory ∧ p ∉ freeHistory}

declarations.name: Systems.isAggregateUnion
declarations.doc:
RETIRED 2026-09-04: the union reading of Bunge 1979 p.640 misclassifies
Bunge's own three-neuron aggregate (1977, {0,1}^3); see
`JointState.union_misses_neuron_aggregate`. Replaced by
`IsProductAggregate`.

Retired definition: a composite state space is an aggregate iff the total
state space equals the union of the partial state spaces.
declarations.signature:
Systems.isAggregateUnion.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (totalSpace : Set S)
  (componentSpaces : List (Set S)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- RETIRED 2026-09-04: the union reading of Bunge 1979 p.640 misclassifies
    Bunge's own three-neuron aggregate (1977, {0,1}^3); see
    `JointState.union_misses_neuron_aggregate`. Replaced by
    `IsProductAggregate`.

    Retired definition: a composite state space is an aggregate iff the total
    state space equals the union of the partial state spaces. -/
def isAggregateUnion {S : Type*}
    (totalSpace : Set S) (componentSpaces : List (Set S)) : Prop :=
  totalSpace = componentSpaces.foldl (· ∪ ·) ∅

declarations.name: Systems.isSystemByStateSpace
declarations.doc:
ABOUT THE RETIRED READING. A composite is a system (not an aggregate)
iff the total state space strictly differs from the union of component
state spaces. "In the case of a system the state of every component is
determined, at least partly, by the states other system components are
in." Live form: `¬ IsProductAggregate`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.isSystemByStateSpace.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (totalSpace : Set S)
  (componentSpaces : List (Set S)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- ABOUT THE RETIRED READING. A composite is a system (not an aggregate)
    iff the total state space strictly differs from the union of component
    state spaces. "In the case of a system the state of every component is
    determined, at least partly, by the states other system components are
    in." Live form: `¬ IsProductAggregate`. -/
def isSystemByStateSpace {S : Type*}
    (totalSpace : Set S) (componentSpaces : List (Set S)) : Prop :=
  ¬isAggregateUnion totalSpace componentSpaces

declarations.name: Systems.aggregate_not_system
declarations.doc:
ABOUT THE RETIRED READING. If a thing is a union-aggregate, it is not a
union-system. Bunge p. 640: the two conditions are complementary. This
relates the criterion only to its own literal negation (SSF #48 vacuity);
the substantive bridge is `AggregateBridge.lean`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.aggregate_not_system.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (totalSpace : Set S)
  (componentSpaces : List (Set S)) (h : Systems.isAggregateUnion totalSpace componentSpaces) :
  ¬Systems.isSystemByStateSpace totalSpace componentSpaces
declarations.source:
/-- ABOUT THE RETIRED READING. If a thing is a union-aggregate, it is not a
    union-system. Bunge p. 640: the two conditions are complementary. This
    relates the criterion only to its own literal negation (SSF #48 vacuity);
    the substantive bridge is `AggregateBridge.lean`. -/
theorem aggregate_not_system {S : Type*}
    (totalSpace : Set S) (componentSpaces : List (Set S))
    (h : isAggregateUnion totalSpace componentSpaces) :
    ¬isSystemByStateSpace totalSpace componentSpaces :=
  fun hn => hn h

declarations.name: Systems.system_not_aggregate
declarations.doc:
ABOUT THE RETIRED READING. If a thing is a union-system, it is not a
union-aggregate. Same vacuity as `aggregate_not_system`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.system_not_aggregate.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (totalSpace : Set S)
  (componentSpaces : List (Set S)) (h : Systems.isSystemByStateSpace totalSpace componentSpaces) :
  ¬Systems.isAggregateUnion totalSpace componentSpaces
declarations.source:
/-- ABOUT THE RETIRED READING. If a thing is a union-system, it is not a
    union-aggregate. Same vacuity as `aggregate_not_system`. -/
theorem system_not_aggregate {S : Type*}
    (totalSpace : Set S) (componentSpaces : List (Set S))
    (h : isSystemByStateSpace totalSpace componentSpaces) :
    ¬isAggregateUnion totalSpace componentSpaces :=
  h

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem
declarations.doc:
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:229): "Systemness: Bounded networks of relations among
parts constitute a holistic unit. Systems interact with other systems, forming yet
larger systems. The Universe is composed of systems of systems."
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:273): "Systems of all kinds are found to be composed of
components, which may themselves be subsystems (i.e., systems in their own rights)."
Encoding: parts→`composition`; relations among parts→`structure'`; bounded→`disjoint`
(C ∩ E = ∅ fixes the boundary) with the outside as `environment`; "constitute a holistic
unit"→`bondage_nonempty` (at least one bonded pair, Bunge Def 1.1); "interact with other
systems, forming yet larger systems"→`ConcreteSystem.compose` (Systemness.lean);
"systems of systems"→`RecursiveSystem` (Systemness.lean).
Not encoded: "holistic unit" as anything beyond nonempty bondage (no emergence claim);
the Universe as a closed top-level system; time (the triple is a snapshot at t).

A concrete system is an ordered triple ⟨C, E, S⟩ where:
- C: composition (set of components)
- E: environment (set of external things bonded with components)
- S: structure (set of relations among components and environment)
The key constraints are:
- C ∩ E = ∅ (composition and environment are disjoint)
- There exist at least two different connected things in C (Def 1.1)

Bunge Def 1.2: s_A(σ,t) = ⟨C_A(σ,t), E_A(σ,t), S_A(σ,t)⟩

DESIGN: Time-parameterization is deferred — each ConcreteSystem represents
a snapshot at a given time t. This matches Bunge's "at time t" qualifier
while keeping types simple for Phase 1.
declarations.signature: Systems.ConcreteSystem.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [Systems.ActsOn α] : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:229): "Systemness: Bounded networks of relations among
    parts constitute a holistic unit. Systems interact with other systems, forming yet
    larger systems. The Universe is composed of systems of systems."
    Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:273): "Systems of all kinds are found to be composed of
    components, which may themselves be subsystems (i.e., systems in their own rights)."
    Encoding: parts→`composition`; relations among parts→`structure'`; bounded→`disjoint`
    (C ∩ E = ∅ fixes the boundary) with the outside as `environment`; "constitute a holistic
    unit"→`bondage_nonempty` (at least one bonded pair, Bunge Def 1.1); "interact with other
    systems, forming yet larger systems"→`ConcreteSystem.compose` (Systemness.lean);
    "systems of systems"→`RecursiveSystem` (Systemness.lean).
    Not encoded: "holistic unit" as anything beyond nonempty bondage (no emergence claim);
    the Universe as a closed top-level system; time (the triple is a snapshot at t).

    A concrete system is an ordered triple ⟨C, E, S⟩ where:
    - C: composition (set of components)
    - E: environment (set of external things bonded with components)
    - S: structure (set of relations among components and environment)
    The key constraints are:
    - C ∩ E = ∅ (composition and environment are disjoint)
    - There exist at least two different connected things in C (Def 1.1)

    Bunge Def 1.2: s_A(σ,t) = ⟨C_A(σ,t), E_A(σ,t), S_A(σ,t)⟩

    DESIGN: Time-parameterization is deferred — each ConcreteSystem represents
    a snapshot at a given time t. This matches Bunge's "at time t" qualifier
    while keeping types simple for Phase 1. -/
@[atlas "bunge-1979-def-1-1"]
structure ConcreteSystem (α : Type*) [ActsOn α] where
  /-- Composition: set of components -/
  composition : Set α
  /-- Environment: set of external things bonded with components -/
  environment : Set α
  /-- Structure: set of relations (as pairs) on C ∪ E -/
  structure' : Set (α × α)
  /-- Composition and environment are disjoint (Bunge §1.2: C ∩ E = ∅) -/
  disjoint : composition ∩ environment = ∅
  /-- Structure relations are defined on C ∪ E -/
  structure_on : ∀ p ∈ structure', p.1 ∈ composition ∪ environment ∧
    p.2 ∈ composition ∪ environment
  /-- Bondage is nonempty: at least one bonded pair exists in C (Def 1.1) -/
  bondage_nonempty : ∃ a ∈ composition, ∃ b ∈ composition, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b

constructors.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Systems.ActsOn α] →
    (composition environment : Set α) →
      (structure' : Set (α × α)) →
        composition ∩ environment = ∅ →
          (∀ p ∈ structure', p.1 ∈ composition ∪ environment ∧ p.2 ∈ composition ∪ environment) →
            (∃ a ∈ composition, ∃ b ∈ composition, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b) →
              Systems.ConcreteSystem α

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.isClosed
declarations.doc:
A system is closed at time t iff its environment is empty.
Bunge Def 1.3: σ is closed iff E(σ,t) = ∅.
"Since every thing but the universe interacts with some other things..."
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.isClosed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A system is closed at time t iff its environment is empty.
    Bunge Def 1.3: σ is closed iff E(σ,t) = ∅.
    "Since every thing but the universe interacts with some other things..." -/
def ConcreteSystem.isClosed {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (σ : ConcreteSystem α) : Prop :=
  σ.environment = ∅

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.isOpen
declarations.doc:
A system is open iff it is not closed.
Bunge Def 1.3: "otherwise σ is open."
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.isOpen.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A system is open iff it is not closed.
    Bunge Def 1.3: "otherwise σ is open." -/
def ConcreteSystem.isOpen {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (σ : ConcreteSystem α) : Prop :=
  ¬σ.isClosed

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.closed_or_open
declarations.doc:
Closed and open are complementary.
Bunge Def 1.3 immediate.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.closed_or_open.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : σ.isClosed ∨ σ.isOpen
declarations.source:
/-- Closed and open are complementary.
    Bunge Def 1.3 immediate. -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.closed_or_open {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (σ : ConcreteSystem α) :
    σ.isClosed ∨ σ.isOpen :=
  em σ.isClosed

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.isOpenWrt
declarations.doc:
A system is open with respect to a property P iff P relates to at least
one property of things in the environment.
Bunge Def 1.4: σ is open w.r.t. P at t iff P is related to at least one
property of things in E(σ,t).

DESIGN: We represent "property" abstractly as any predicate on α.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.isOpenWrt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) (P : α → Prop) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A system is open with respect to a property P iff P relates to at least
    one property of things in the environment.
    Bunge Def 1.4: σ is open w.r.t. P at t iff P is related to at least one
    property of things in E(σ,t).

    DESIGN: We represent "property" abstractly as any predicate on α. -/
def ConcreteSystem.isOpenWrt {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ : ConcreteSystem α) (P : α → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ x ∈ σ.environment, P x

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.closed_iff_closed_all
declarations.doc:
A system is closed iff it is closed in every respect.
Bunge: "a system is closed iff it is closed in every respect."
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.closed_iff_closed_all.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : σ.isClosed ↔ ∀ (P : α → Prop), ¬σ.isOpenWrt P
declarations.source:
/-- A system is closed iff it is closed in every respect.
    Bunge: "a system is closed iff it is closed in every respect." -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.closed_iff_closed_all {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ : ConcreteSystem α) :
    σ.isClosed ↔ ∀ P : α → Prop, ¬σ.isOpenWrt P := by
  constructor
  · intro hclosed P ⟨x, hx, _⟩
    rw [ConcreteSystem.isClosed, Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem] at hclosed
    exact hclosed x hx
  · intro h
    rw [ConcreteSystem.isClosed, Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    intro x hx
    exact h (fun _ => True) ⟨x, hx, trivial⟩

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.internalStructure
declarations.doc:
The internal structure of σ: relations among components only.
Bunge Def 1.5(i): subset of S_A composed of relations among A-parts.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.internalStructure.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Set (α × α)
declarations.source:
/-- The internal structure of σ: relations among components only.
    Bunge Def 1.5(i): subset of S_A composed of relations among A-parts. -/
def ConcreteSystem.internalStructure {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ : ConcreteSystem α) : Set (α × α) :=
  {p ∈ σ.structure' | p.1 ∈ σ.composition ∧ p.2 ∈ σ.composition}

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.externalStructure
declarations.doc:
The external structure: relations involving at least one environment thing.
Complement of internal structure within total structure.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.externalStructure.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Set (α × α)
declarations.source:
/-- The external structure: relations involving at least one environment thing.
    Complement of internal structure within total structure. -/
def ConcreteSystem.externalStructure {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ : ConcreteSystem α) : Set (α × α) :=
  {p ∈ σ.structure' | p.1 ∈ σ.environment ∨ p.2 ∈ σ.environment}

declarations.name: Systems.Subsystem
declarations.doc:
Subsystem relation: σ₁ is a subsystem of σ₂.
Bunge Def 1.6: x ≺ σ iff
(i) x is a system, and
(ii) C(x) ⊆ C(σ) ∧ E(x) ⊇ E(σ) ∧ S(x) ⊆ S(σ)

Note the asymmetry: a subsystem has MORE environment (it sees
the rest of the supersystem as part of its environment) but
LESS composition and structure.
declarations.signature: Systems.Subsystem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (σ₁ σ₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Subsystem relation: σ₁ is a subsystem of σ₂.
    Bunge Def 1.6: x ≺ σ iff
    (i) x is a system, and
    (ii) C(x) ⊆ C(σ) ∧ E(x) ⊇ E(σ) ∧ S(x) ⊆ S(σ)

    Note the asymmetry: a subsystem has MORE environment (it sees
    the rest of the supersystem as part of its environment) but
    LESS composition and structure. -/
def Subsystem {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ₁ σ₂ : ConcreteSystem α) : Prop :=
  σ₁.composition ⊆ σ₂.composition ∧
  σ₂.environment ⊆ σ₁.environment ∧
  σ₁.structure' ⊆ σ₂.structure'

declarations.name: Systems.subsystem_refl
declarations.doc:
Subsystem is reflexive.
Every system is a subsystem of itself.
declarations.signature:
Systems.subsystem_refl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) :
  Systems.Subsystem σ σ
declarations.source:
/-- Subsystem is reflexive.
    Every system is a subsystem of itself. -/
theorem subsystem_refl {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (σ : ConcreteSystem α) :
    Subsystem σ σ :=
  ⟨Set.Subset.refl _, Set.Subset.refl _, Set.Subset.refl _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.subsystem_trans
declarations.doc:
Subsystem is transitive.
If σ₁ ≺ σ₂ and σ₂ ≺ σ₃, then σ₁ ≺ σ₃.
declarations.signature:
Systems.subsystem_trans.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {σ₁ σ₂ σ₃ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α} (h₁₂ : Systems.Subsystem σ₁ σ₂)
  (h₂₃ : Systems.Subsystem σ₂ σ₃) : Systems.Subsystem σ₁ σ₃
declarations.source:
/-- Subsystem is transitive.
    If σ₁ ≺ σ₂ and σ₂ ≺ σ₃, then σ₁ ≺ σ₃. -/
theorem subsystem_trans {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {σ₁ σ₂ σ₃ : ConcreteSystem α}
    (h₁₂ : Subsystem σ₁ σ₂) (h₂₃ : Subsystem σ₂ σ₃) :
    Subsystem σ₁ σ₃ :=
  ⟨Set.Subset.trans h₁₂.1 h₂₃.1,
   Set.Subset.trans h₂₃.2.1 h₁₂.2.1,
   Set.Subset.trans h₁₂.2.2 h₂₃.2.2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.subsystem_antisymm_components
declarations.doc:
Subsystem is antisymmetric (on the CES triple).
If σ₁ ≺ σ₂ and σ₂ ≺ σ₁, then their CES triples are equal.
This is the key property making subsystem a partial order.
declarations.signature:
Systems.subsystem_antisymm_components.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {σ₁ σ₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α} (h₁₂ : Systems.Subsystem σ₁ σ₂)
  (h₂₁ : Systems.Subsystem σ₂ σ₁) :
  σ₁.composition = σ₂.composition ∧ σ₁.environment = σ₂.environment ∧ σ₁.structure' = σ₂.structure'
declarations.source:
/-- Subsystem is antisymmetric (on the CES triple).
    If σ₁ ≺ σ₂ and σ₂ ≺ σ₁, then their CES triples are equal.
    This is the key property making subsystem a partial order. -/
theorem subsystem_antisymm_components {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {σ₁ σ₂ : ConcreteSystem α}
    (h₁₂ : Subsystem σ₁ σ₂) (h₂₁ : Subsystem σ₂ σ₁) :
    σ₁.composition = σ₂.composition ∧
    σ₁.environment = σ₂.environment ∧
    σ₁.structure' = σ₂.structure' :=
  ⟨Set.Subset.antisymm h₁₂.1 h₂₁.1,
   Set.Subset.antisymm h₂₁.2.1 h₁₂.2.1,
   Set.Subset.antisymm h₁₂.2.2 h₂₁.2.2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.universe_only_closed
declarations.doc:
Corollary 1.1: The universe is the only closed system.
Bunge: "The universe is the only system closed at all times."
We state a weaker version: if σ is closed, its environment is empty.
declarations.signature:
Systems.universe_only_closed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : σ.isClosed ↔ σ.environment = ∅
declarations.source:
/-- Corollary 1.1: The universe is the only closed system.
    Bunge: "The universe is the only system closed at all times."
    We state a weaker version: if σ is closed, its environment is empty. -/
theorem universe_only_closed {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (σ : ConcreteSystem α) :
    σ.isClosed ↔ σ.environment = ∅ :=
  Iff.rfl

declarations.name: Systems.NestedSystems
declarations.doc:
A system of nested systems: a collection of supersystems of σ
partially ordered by the subsystem relation.
Bunge Def 1.7(i): N_σ = {σ_i ∈ Σ | σ ≺ σ_i}.
declarations.signature:
Systems.NestedSystems.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (core : Systems.ConcreteSystem α)
  (chain : List (Systems.ConcreteSystem α)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A system of nested systems: a collection of supersystems of σ
    partially ordered by the subsystem relation.
    Bunge Def 1.7(i): N_σ = {σ_i ∈ Σ | σ ≺ σ_i}. -/
def NestedSystems {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (core : ConcreteSystem α) (chain : List (ConcreteSystem α)) : Prop :=
  (∀ σ ∈ chain, Subsystem core σ) ∧
  chain.Pairwise (fun σ₁ σ₂ => Subsystem σ₁ σ₂)

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem
declarations.doc:
A recursive system: Mobus Eq. 4.3 enriched with Bunge's CES constraints.

Each node is either:
- `primitive`: a process primitive (atomic work process, terminal)
- `composite`: a system with full CES constraints whose components
  are themselves RecursiveSystem nodes

The existing `RecursiveComponent` captures the tree shape without
system semantics. `RecursiveSystem` adds the CES constraints that
make each composite level a genuine system, not just a tree node.

Constraints linking children to composition are in `WellFormed`
(Lean 4's kernel requires separating existential proof fields from
the inductive type definition).

Decomposition terminates by Lean's structural recursion on the
inductive type — no explicit well-foundedness proof needed.
declarations.signature: Systems.RecursiveSystem.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [Systems.ActsOn α] : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- A recursive system: Mobus Eq. 4.3 enriched with Bunge's CES constraints.

    Each node is either:
    - `primitive`: a process primitive (atomic work process, terminal)
    - `composite`: a system with full CES constraints whose components
      are themselves RecursiveSystem nodes

    The existing `RecursiveComponent` captures the tree shape without
    system semantics. `RecursiveSystem` adds the CES constraints that
    make each composite level a genuine system, not just a tree node.

    Constraints linking children to composition are in `WellFormed`
    (Lean 4's kernel requires separating existential proof fields from
    the inductive type definition).

    Decomposition terminates by Lean's structural recursion on the
    inductive type — no explicit well-foundedness proof needed. -/
inductive RecursiveSystem (α : Type*) [ActsOn α] where
  /-- A process primitive: terminal component, no further decomposition.
      These are the atomic work processes at the bottom of every
      decomposition hierarchy. -/
  | primitive (thing : α) : RecursiveSystem α
  /-- A composite system: carries a full ConcreteSystem with CES
      constraints, whose components are themselves RecursiveSystem nodes.
      The `thing` field is this system's identity when viewed as a
      component in its parent's composition. -/
  | composite
      (thing : α)
      (system : ConcreteSystem α)
      (children : List (RecursiveSystem α))
      : RecursiveSystem α

constructors.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive
constructors.doc:
A process primitive: terminal component, no further decomposition.
These are the atomic work processes at the bottom of every
decomposition hierarchy.
constructors.type: {α : Type u_1} → [inst : Systems.ActsOn α] → α → Systems.RecursiveSystem α

constructors.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.composite
constructors.doc:
A composite system: carries a full ConcreteSystem with CES
constraints, whose components are themselves RecursiveSystem nodes.
The `thing` field is this system's identity when viewed as a
component in its parent's composition.
constructors.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Systems.ActsOn α] →
    α → Systems.ConcreteSystem α → List (Systems.RecursiveSystem α) → Systems.RecursiveSystem α

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.thing
declarations.doc: The thing represented by a recursive system node.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.thing.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α → α
declarations.source:
/-- The thing represented by a recursive system node. -/
def RecursiveSystem.thing {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] : RecursiveSystem α → α
  | .primitive a => a
  | .composite a _ _ => a

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.isPrimitive
declarations.doc: Whether a node is a process primitive (leaf).
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.isPrimitive.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α → Bool
declarations.source:
/-- Whether a node is a process primitive (leaf). -/
def RecursiveSystem.isPrimitive {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    RecursiveSystem α → Bool
  | .primitive _ => true
  | .composite _ _ _ => false

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.isComposite
declarations.doc: Whether a node is composite (has internal structure).
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.isComposite.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α → Bool
declarations.source:
/-- Whether a node is composite (has internal structure). -/
def RecursiveSystem.isComposite {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    RecursiveSystem α → Bool
  | .primitive _ => false
  | .composite _ _ _ => true

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.depth
declarations.doc:
The depth of a recursive system (height of the decomposition tree).
Process primitives have depth 0.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.depth.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α → ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The depth of a recursive system (height of the decomposition tree).
    Process primitives have depth 0. -/
def RecursiveSystem.depth {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    RecursiveSystem α → Nat
  | .primitive _ => 0
  | .composite _ _ children =>
      1 + children.foldl (fun acc c => max acc c.depth) 0

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitiveCount
declarations.doc: Count the total number of process primitives (leaf nodes).
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitiveCount.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α → ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- Count the total number of process primitives (leaf nodes). -/
def RecursiveSystem.primitiveCount {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    RecursiveSystem α → Nat
  | .primitive _ => 1
  | .composite _ _ children =>
      children.foldl (fun acc c => acc + c.primitiveCount) 0

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.WellFormed
declarations.doc:
A RecursiveSystem is well-formed iff at every composite level:
- Every component in the system's composition is some child's thing
- Every child's thing belongs to the system's composition
- All children are themselves well-formed

Process primitives are trivially well-formed.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.WellFormed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] :
  Systems.RecursiveSystem α → Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A RecursiveSystem is well-formed iff at every composite level:
    - Every component in the system's composition is some child's thing
    - Every child's thing belongs to the system's composition
    - All children are themselves well-formed

    Process primitives are trivially well-formed. -/
def RecursiveSystem.WellFormed {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] :
    RecursiveSystem α → Prop
  | .primitive _ => True
  | .composite _ sys children =>
      (∀ x ∈ sys.composition, ∃ c ∈ children, c.thing = x) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ children, c.thing ∈ sys.composition) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ children, c.WellFormed)

declarations.name: Systems.IsOrganized
declarations.doc:
A collection of things is organized iff it has nonempty internal bonds.
This is the formal content of Mobus's "organized vs. heaped" distinction.

An organized set has at least two distinct members that are bonded —
there is genuine interaction, not just co-location. This predicate
works on any set of things; ConcreteSystem.bondage_nonempty guarantees
that every system's composition satisfies it.
declarations.signature: Systems.IsOrganized.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (S : Set α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A collection of things is organized iff it has nonempty internal bonds.
    This is the formal content of Mobus's "organized vs. heaped" distinction.

    An organized set has at least two distinct members that are bonded —
    there is genuine interaction, not just co-location. This predicate
    works on any set of things; ConcreteSystem.bondage_nonempty guarantees
    that every system's composition satisfies it. -/
def IsOrganized {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (S : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b

declarations.name: Systems.IsAggregate
declarations.doc:
A collection is an aggregate iff it has no internal bonds.
Mobus: an aggregate is "heaped" — components are co-located but
do not interact. Assembly (Assembly.lean) is the transition from
aggregate to organized.
declarations.signature: Systems.IsAggregate.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (S : Set α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A collection is an aggregate iff it has no internal bonds.
    Mobus: an aggregate is "heaped" — components are co-located but
    do not interact. Assembly (Assembly.lean) is the transition from
    aggregate to organized. -/
def IsAggregate {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (S : Set α) : Prop :=
  ¬IsOrganized S

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.composition_organized
declarations.doc:
Every ConcreteSystem's composition is organized.
Immediate from bondage_nonempty — the defining constraint
that separates systems from mere collections.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.composition_organized.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Systems.IsOrganized σ.composition
declarations.source:
/-- Every ConcreteSystem's composition is organized.
    Immediate from bondage_nonempty — the defining constraint
    that separates systems from mere collections. -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.composition_organized {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ : ConcreteSystem α) : IsOrganized σ.composition := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hne, hbond⟩ := σ.bondage_nonempty
  exact ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hne, hbond⟩

declarations.name: Systems.organized_of_bond
declarations.doc:
An aggregate that gains bonds becomes organized.
This connects to Assembly.lean: assembly is the process by which
an aggregate becomes a system.
declarations.signature:
Systems.organized_of_bond.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] {S : Set α} {a b : α} (ha : a ∈ S)
  (hb : b ∈ S) (hne : a ≠ b) (hbond : Systems.Bonded a b) : Systems.IsOrganized S
declarations.source:
/-- An aggregate that gains bonds becomes organized.
    This connects to Assembly.lean: assembly is the process by which
    an aggregate becomes a system. -/
theorem organized_of_bond {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] {S : Set α}
    {a b : α} (ha : a ∈ S) (hb : b ∈ S) (hne : a ≠ b)
    (hbond : Bonded a b) : IsOrganized S :=
  ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hne, hbond⟩

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_depth
declarations.doc: A process primitive has depth 0.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_depth.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a : α) :
  (Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive a).depth = 0
declarations.source:
/-- A process primitive has depth 0. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.primitive_depth {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a : α) :
    (RecursiveSystem.primitive a : RecursiveSystem α).depth = 0 := by
  unfold RecursiveSystem.depth
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_count
declarations.doc: A process primitive counts as exactly 1.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_count.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a : α) :
  (Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive a).primitiveCount = 1
declarations.source:
/-- A process primitive counts as exactly 1. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.primitive_count {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a : α) :
    (RecursiveSystem.primitive a : RecursiveSystem α).primitiveCount = 1 := by
  unfold RecursiveSystem.primitiveCount
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_or_composite
declarations.doc: Every node is either a primitive or composite.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_or_composite.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (rs : Systems.RecursiveSystem α) : rs.isPrimitive = true ∨ rs.isComposite = true
declarations.source:
/-- Every node is either a primitive or composite. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.primitive_or_composite {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (rs : RecursiveSystem α) :
    rs.isPrimitive = true ∨ rs.isComposite = true := by
  cases rs with
  | primitive _ => exact Or.inl rfl
  | composite _ _ _ => exact Or.inr rfl

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_wellFormed
declarations.doc: A process primitive is well-formed.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive_wellFormed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (a : α) :
  (Systems.RecursiveSystem.primitive a).WellFormed
declarations.source:
/-- A process primitive is well-formed. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.primitive_wellFormed {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (a : α) :
    (RecursiveSystem.primitive a : RecursiveSystem α).WellFormed := by
  unfold RecursiveSystem.WellFormed
  trivial

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.child_wellFormed
declarations.doc:
Well-formedness propagates to children: every child of a well-formed
composite is itself well-formed.
This is closure under decomposition — the defining property of
Systemness as a principle.
declarations.source:
/-- Well-formedness propagates to children: every child of a well-formed
    composite is itself well-formed.
    This is closure under decomposition — the defining property of
    Systemness as a principle. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.child_wellFormed {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {t : α} {sys : ConcreteSystem α}
    {children : List (RecursiveSystem α)}
    (hwf : (RecursiveSystem.composite t sys children).WellFormed)
    {child : RecursiveSystem α} (hmem : child ∈ children) :
    child.WellFormed := by
  unfold RecursiveSystem.WellFormed at hwf
  exact hwf.2.2 child hmem

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.child_thing_in_composition
declarations.doc:
In a well-formed composite, every child's thing belongs to the
parent's composition.
declarations.source:
/-- In a well-formed composite, every child's thing belongs to the
    parent's composition. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.child_thing_in_composition {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {t : α} {sys : ConcreteSystem α}
    {children : List (RecursiveSystem α)}
    (hwf : (RecursiveSystem.composite t sys children).WellFormed)
    {child : RecursiveSystem α} (hmem : child ∈ children) :
    child.thing ∈ sys.composition := by
  unfold RecursiveSystem.WellFormed at hwf
  exact hwf.2.1 child hmem

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.composition_covered
declarations.doc:
In a well-formed composite, every component in the composition
is represented by some child.
declarations.source:
/-- In a well-formed composite, every component in the composition
    is represented by some child. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.composition_covered {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {t : α} {sys : ConcreteSystem α}
    {children : List (RecursiveSystem α)}
    (hwf : (RecursiveSystem.composite t sys children).WellFormed)
    {x : α} (hx : x ∈ sys.composition) :
    ∃ c ∈ children, c.thing = x := by
  unfold RecursiveSystem.WellFormed at hwf
  exact hwf.1 x hx

declarations.name: Systems.RecursiveSystem.every_level_organized
declarations.doc:
The composition of every composite level is organized (not aggregate).
Every composite node carries a ConcreteSystem, which by definition has
nonempty bondage. Therefore no level in the decomposition tree is a
mere aggregate — systemness holds at every level.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RecursiveSystem.every_level_organized.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Systems.IsOrganized sys.composition
declarations.source:
/-- The composition of every composite level is organized (not aggregate).
    Every composite node carries a ConcreteSystem, which by definition has
    nonempty bondage. Therefore no level in the decomposition tree is a
    mere aggregate — systemness holds at every level. -/
theorem RecursiveSystem.every_level_organized {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : ConcreteSystem α) :
    IsOrganized sys.composition :=
  sys.composition_organized

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.compose
declarations.doc:
Compose two interacting systems into a supersystem.

Given σ₁ and σ₂ with disjoint compositions and at least one bond
between their components, produce a ConcreteSystem whose composition
is the union, whose environment is the minimal set satisfying
structure_on, and whose structure combines both systems' relations.

Mobus §2.3.1: "Systems interact with other systems, forming yet
larger systems."

The environment formula (E₁ ∪ E₂) \ (C₁ ∪ C₂) is the unique
minimal environment: intersection would break structure_on
(environmental things referenced by one system's structure but
unknown to the other would have no home in C ∪ E).

FINDING: Neither hypothesis is needed for the coherence proofs.
The CES construction is unconditionally valid — any two systems
can be combined. The hypotheses add physical content: disjointness
ensures distinct systems, interaction ensures meaningful composition
(not just disjoint union).
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.compose.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (σ₁ σ₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) (_h_disjoint : σ₁.composition ∩ σ₂.composition = ∅)
  (_h_interact : ∃ a ∈ σ₁.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ₂.composition, Systems.Bonded a b) :
  Systems.ConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Compose two interacting systems into a supersystem.

    Given σ₁ and σ₂ with disjoint compositions and at least one bond
    between their components, produce a ConcreteSystem whose composition
    is the union, whose environment is the minimal set satisfying
    structure_on, and whose structure combines both systems' relations.

    Mobus §2.3.1: "Systems interact with other systems, forming yet
    larger systems."

    The environment formula (E₁ ∪ E₂) \ (C₁ ∪ C₂) is the unique
    minimal environment: intersection would break structure_on
    (environmental things referenced by one system's structure but
    unknown to the other would have no home in C ∪ E).

    FINDING: Neither hypothesis is needed for the coherence proofs.
    The CES construction is unconditionally valid — any two systems
    can be combined. The hypotheses add physical content: disjointness
    ensures distinct systems, interaction ensures meaningful composition
    (not just disjoint union). -/
def ConcreteSystem.compose {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (σ₁ σ₂ : ConcreteSystem α)
    (_h_disjoint : σ₁.composition ∩ σ₂.composition = ∅)
    (_h_interact : ∃ a ∈ σ₁.composition, ∃ b ∈ σ₂.composition, Bonded a b)
    : ConcreteSystem α where
  composition := σ₁.composition ∪ σ₂.composition
  environment := (σ₁.environment ∪ σ₂.environment) \ (σ₁.composition ∪ σ₂.composition)
  structure' := σ₁.structure' ∪ σ₂.structure'
  disjoint := by
    ext x
    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_diff, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_empty_iff_false,
               iff_false]
    rintro ⟨hc, -, hnc⟩
    exact hnc hc
  structure_on := by
    intro p hp
    rcases hp with hp₁ | hp₂
    · obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := σ₁.structure_on p hp₁
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rcases h1 with hc | he
        · exact Or.inl (Or.inl hc)
        · by_cases hc2 : p.1 ∈ σ₂.composition
          · exact Or.inl (Or.inr hc2)
          · have hc1 : p.1 ∉ σ₁.composition :=
              fun h => Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp σ₁.disjoint p.1 ⟨h, he⟩
            exact Or.inr ⟨Or.inl he, fun hcu => hcu.elim hc1 hc2⟩
      · rcases h2 with hc | he
        · exact Or.inl (Or.inl hc)
        · by_cases hc2 : p.2 ∈ σ₂.composition
          · exact Or.inl (Or.inr hc2)
          · have hc1 : p.2 ∉ σ₁.composition :=
              fun h => Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp σ₁.disjoint p.2 ⟨h, he⟩
            exact Or.inr ⟨Or.inl he, fun hcu => hcu.elim hc1 hc2⟩
    · obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := σ₂.structure_on p hp₂
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rcases h1 with hc | he
        · exact Or.inl (Or.inr hc)
        · by_cases hc1 : p.1 ∈ σ₁.composition
          · exact Or.inl (Or.inl hc1)
          · have hc2 : p.1 ∉ σ₂.composition :=
              fun h => Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp σ₂.disjoint p.1 ⟨h, he⟩
            exact Or.inr ⟨Or.inr he, fun hcu => hcu.elim hc1 hc2⟩
      · rcases h2 with hc | he
        · exact Or.inl (Or.inr hc)
        · by_cases hc1 : p.2 ∈ σ₁.composition
          · exact Or.inl (Or.inl hc1)
          · have hc2 : p.2 ∉ σ₂.composition :=
              fun h => Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp σ₂.disjoint p.2 ⟨h, he⟩
            exact Or.inr ⟨Or.inr he, fun hcu => hcu.elim hc1 hc2⟩
  bondage_nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hne, hbond⟩ := σ₁.bondage_nonempty
    exact ⟨a, Set.mem_union_left _ ha, b, Set.mem_union_left _ hb, hne, hbond⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Composition
declarations.doc:
The composition of a thing x is the set of all its parts.
Bunge §1.2: C(x) = {y ∈ Θ | y ⊑ x} where ⊑ is parthood.
Here, parthood is the ≤ relation of the Preorder on α.
declarations.signature: Systems.Composition.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] (x : α) : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.AComposition
declarations.doc:
The A-composition of a thing x is the set of its parts that belong to A.
Bunge §1.2: C_A(x) = C(x) ∩ A = {y ∈ A | y ⊑ x}.
declarations.signature: Systems.AComposition.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] (A : Set α) (x : α) : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.aComposition_eq_inter
declarations.doc:
A-composition equals the intersection of Composition with A.
Bunge §1.2: C_A(x) = C(x) ∩ A.
declarations.signature:
Systems.aComposition_eq_inter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] (A : Set α) (x : α) :
  Systems.AComposition A x = Systems.Composition x ∩ A
declarations.source:
/-- A-composition equals the intersection of Composition with A.
    Bunge §1.2: C_A(x) = C(x) ∩ A. -/
theorem aComposition_eq_inter {α : Type*} [Preorder α] (A : Set α) (x : α) :
    AComposition A x = Composition x ∩ A := by
  ext y
  simp [AComposition, Composition, Set.mem_inter_iff]
  exact ⟨fun ⟨ha, hle⟩ => ⟨hle, ha⟩, fun ⟨hle, ha⟩ => ⟨ha, hle⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.self_mem_composition
declarations.doc:
Every thing is part of itself (reflexivity of parthood).
Immediate from Preorder.
declarations.signature: Systems.self_mem_composition.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] (x : α) : x ∈ Systems.Composition x
declarations.source:
/-- Every thing is part of itself (reflexivity of parthood).
    Immediate from Preorder. -/
theorem self_mem_composition {α : Type*} [Preorder α] (x : α) :
    x ∈ Composition x :=
  le_refl x

declarations.name: Systems.composition_trans
declarations.doc:
If y is part of x and z is part of y, then z is part of x (transitivity).
Immediate from Preorder.
declarations.signature:
Systems.composition_trans.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Preorder α] {x y z : α}
  (hzy : z ∈ Systems.Composition y) (hyx : y ∈ Systems.Composition x) : z ∈ Systems.Composition x
declarations.source:
/-- If y is part of x and z is part of y, then z is part of x (transitivity).
    Immediate from Preorder. -/
theorem composition_trans {α : Type*} [Preorder α] {x y z : α}
    (hzy : z ∈ Composition y) (hyx : y ∈ Composition x) :
    z ∈ Composition x :=
  le_trans hzy hyx

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding
declarations.doc:
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:239): "Systems can be understood (a corollary of #9)-Science."
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:374): "When you understand you can make predictions, or at least
project scenarios that can then be tested."
Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:378): "When we say that systems can be understood, then, we are
referring to our ability to function successfully through the guidance of models in the
mind that correlate with relevant features of systems in the world. A model is not
identical with the object it models, so our understanding of a system is not identical
with the system itself, and therefore is never final."
Encoding: "models in the mind"→`M` with `modelDyn`; "correlate with relevant features of
systems in the world"→`abstract : S → M` and `abstracts` (one-step commuting square);
"relevant" (no junk model states)→`surjective`; "not identical with the object it models"→
`compresses` (not injective) together with `nontrivial`; "make predictions"→`predict` /
`predict_correct`.
Not encoded: "never final" (a single fixed understanding — no refinement order over models);
"function successfully" (no agent or action — that is `DirectedAgent`, #12); "a corollary
of #9" (this file argues the opposite: `modeling_does_not_imply_understanding`); science as
a social process; approximate or erroneous models (the square is exact).

An `Understanding` of a system with dynamics `systemDyn : S → S`: a coarse-graining
`abstract : S → M` onto a model space `M`, with model dynamics `modelDyn : M → M`
that commute with the system one step at a time (`abstracts`), where the
coarse-graining is **onto** (`surjective`), **lossy** (`compresses`: not injective),
and the model is **non-degenerate** (`nontrivial`: at least two distinguishable
model states, ruling out the useless total collapse to a point).

The `compresses` field is the content #9 lacks; the `nontrivial` field keeps the
compression honest — a proper quotient, not the everything-to-one-point map.
declarations.signature: Systems.Understanding.{u_1, u_2} (S : Type u_1) (M : Type u_2) : Type (max u_1 u_2)
declarations.source:
/-- Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:239): "Systems can be understood (a corollary of #9)-Science."
    Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:374): "When you understand you can make predictions, or at least
    project scenarios that can then be tested."
    Mobus (2022, 2-principles-of-systems-science.md:378): "When we say that systems can be understood, then, we are
    referring to our ability to function successfully through the guidance of models in the
    mind that correlate with relevant features of systems in the world. A model is not
    identical with the object it models, so our understanding of a system is not identical
    with the system itself, and therefore is never final."
    Encoding: "models in the mind"→`M` with `modelDyn`; "correlate with relevant features of
    systems in the world"→`abstract : S → M` and `abstracts` (one-step commuting square);
    "relevant" (no junk model states)→`surjective`; "not identical with the object it models"→
    `compresses` (not injective) together with `nontrivial`; "make predictions"→`predict` /
    `predict_correct`.
    Not encoded: "never final" (a single fixed understanding — no refinement order over models);
    "function successfully" (no agent or action — that is `DirectedAgent`, #12); "a corollary
    of #9" (this file argues the opposite: `modeling_does_not_imply_understanding`); science as
    a social process; approximate or erroneous models (the square is exact).

    An `Understanding` of a system with dynamics `systemDyn : S → S`: a coarse-graining
    `abstract : S → M` onto a model space `M`, with model dynamics `modelDyn : M → M`
    that commute with the system one step at a time (`abstracts`), where the
    coarse-graining is **onto** (`surjective`), **lossy** (`compresses`: not injective),
    and the model is **non-degenerate** (`nontrivial`: at least two distinguishable
    model states, ruling out the useless total collapse to a point).

    The `compresses` field is the content #9 lacks; the `nontrivial` field keeps the
    compression honest — a proper quotient, not the everything-to-one-point map. -/
structure Understanding (S M : Type*) where
  /-- The coarse-graining of system states to model states (Rosen's encoding). -/
  abstract : S → M
  /-- The actual dynamics of the system. -/
  systemDyn : S → S
  /-- The induced dynamics on the model space. -/
  modelDyn : M → M
  /-- One-step commuting square: abstracting then stepping the model equals
      stepping the system then abstracting. -/
  abstracts : ∀ s, abstract (systemDyn s) = modelDyn (abstract s)
  /-- The model space is a genuine quotient: every model state is realised. -/
  surjective : Function.Surjective abstract
  /-- Strict simplification: distinct system states share a model state. -/
  compresses : ¬ Function.Injective abstract
  /-- Non-degenerate: the model retains at least one distinction (excludes the
      total collapse to a single point, which would "understand" everything). -/
  nontrivial : Nontrivial M

  {M : Type u_2} →
    (abstract : S → M) →
      (systemDyn : S → S) →
        (modelDyn : M → M) →
          (∀ (s : S), abstract (systemDyn s) = modelDyn (abstract s)) →
            Function.Surjective abstract →
              ¬Function.Injective abstract → Nontrivial M → Systems.Understanding S M

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.tracks
declarations.source:
theorem Understanding.tracks {S M : Type*} (u : Understanding S M) (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
    u.abstract (u.systemDyn^[n] s) = u.modelDyn^[n] (u.abstract s) := by
  induction n generalizing s with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, ih (u.systemDyn s), u.abstracts,
        ← Function.iterate_succ_apply]
