declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.predict_correct
declarations.doc:
Anticipation through compression: running the simple model forward n steps from
a coarse-grained state equals the system's true n-step future, coarse-grained.
Understanding the comprehensible law (`modelDyn`) is enough to predict the
incomprehensibly detailed system.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Understanding.predict_correct.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2}
  (u : Systems.Understanding S M) (n : ℕ) (s : S) : u.predict n s = u.abstract (u.systemDyn^[n] s)
declarations.source:
/-- Anticipation through compression: running the simple model forward n steps from
    a coarse-grained state equals the system's true n-step future, coarse-grained.
    Understanding the comprehensible law (`modelDyn`) is enough to predict the
    incomprehensibly detailed system. -/
theorem Understanding.predict_correct {S M : Type*} (u : Understanding S M)
    (n : ℕ) (s : S) :
    u.predict n s = u.abstract (u.systemDyn^[n] s) :=
  (u.tracks n s).symm

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.equilibrium_image
declarations.doc:
Understanding preserves rest: a system equilibrium coarse-grains to a model
equilibrium. The simple model agrees with the system about what stands still.
declarations.source:
/-- Understanding preserves rest: a system equilibrium coarse-grains to a model
    equilibrium. The simple model agrees with the system about what stands still. -/
theorem Understanding.equilibrium_image {S M : Type*} (u : Understanding S M)
    {s : S} (h : IsEquilibrium u.systemDyn s) :
    IsEquilibrium u.modelDyn (u.abstract s) := by
  unfold IsEquilibrium at *
  rw [← u.abstracts, h]

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.card_lt
declarations.doc:
An understanding's model space has strictly fewer states than the system: a
surjection that is not injective drops cardinality.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Understanding.card_lt.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Fintype S] [Fintype M]
  (u : Systems.Understanding S M) : Fintype.card M < Fintype.card S
declarations.source:
/-- An understanding's model space has strictly fewer states than the system: a
    surjection that is not injective drops cardinality. -/
theorem Understanding.card_lt {S M : Type*} [Fintype S] [Fintype M]
    (u : Understanding S M) : Fintype.card M < Fintype.card S := by
  rcases lt_or_eq_of_le (Fintype.card_le_of_surjective _ u.surjective) with h | h
  · exact h
  · exact absurd
      ((Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card u.abstract).mpr ⟨u.surjective, h.symm⟩).injective
      u.compresses

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.hartley_lt
declarations.doc:
Understanding strictly lowers Hartley nonspecificity (#7): the model resolves
strictly fewer distinguishable states than the system. This is the information-
theoretic statement of "the model is simpler" — `hartley = log (card)`, and the
card drops, so the log drops. The compression of #11 is the Hartley drop of #7.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Understanding.hartley_lt.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Fintype S] [Fintype M]
  (u : Systems.Understanding S M) : Systems.hartley Finset.univ < Systems.hartley Finset.univ
declarations.source:
/-- Understanding strictly lowers Hartley nonspecificity (#7): the model resolves
    strictly fewer distinguishable states than the system. This is the information-
    theoretic statement of "the model is simpler" — `hartley = log (card)`, and the
    card drops, so the log drops. The compression of #11 is the Hartley drop of #7. -/
theorem Understanding.hartley_lt {S M : Type*} [Fintype S] [Fintype M]
    (u : Understanding S M) :
    hartley (Finset.univ : Finset M) < hartley (Finset.univ : Finset S) := by
  rw [hartley, hartley, Finset.card_univ, Finset.card_univ]
  apply Real.log_lt_log
  · haveI := u.nontrivial
    haveI : Nonempty M := ⟨(exists_pair_ne M).choose⟩
    exact_mod_cast (Fintype.card_pos : 0 < Fintype.card M)
  · exact_mod_cast u.card_lt

declarations.name: Systems.InternalModel.refl
declarations.doc:
The trivial self-model: every system with dynamics `f` is an InternalModel of
itself, with the identity as the modelling map. Witnesses that #9 is always
satisfiable — modeling, in the bare sense, costs nothing.
declarations.signature: Systems.InternalModel.refl.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Systems.InternalModel S S
declarations.source:
/-- The trivial self-model: every system with dynamics `f` is an InternalModel of
    itself, with the identity as the modelling map. Witnesses that #9 is always
    satisfiable — modeling, in the bare sense, costs nothing. -/
def InternalModel.refl {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : InternalModel S S where
  model := id
  internalDyn := f
  systemDyn := f
  simulates := fun _ => rfl

declarations.name: Systems.no_trivial_understanding
declarations.doc:
The identity map is not an understanding. The model that duplicates the system
state-for-state simplifies nothing, so it cannot satisfy `compresses`: even a
perfect, full-resolution model of a system is not yet an understanding of it.
declarations.signature:
Systems.no_trivial_understanding.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (u : Systems.Understanding S S)
  (h : u.abstract = id) : False
declarations.source:
/-- The identity map is not an understanding. The model that duplicates the system
    state-for-state simplifies nothing, so it cannot satisfy `compresses`: even a
    perfect, full-resolution model of a system is not yet an understanding of it. -/
theorem no_trivial_understanding {S : Type*} (u : Understanding S S)
    (h : u.abstract = id) : False := by
  apply u.compresses
  rw [h]
  exact Function.injective_id

declarations.name: Systems.no_understanding_of_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
No subsingleton system can be understood: with at most one state there is nothing
to collapse, so every abstraction out of it is injective and fails `compresses`.
Understanding needs something to throw away.
declarations.signature:
Systems.no_understanding_of_subsingleton.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Subsingleton S]
  (u : Systems.Understanding S M) : False
declarations.source:
/-- No subsingleton system can be understood: with at most one state there is nothing
    to collapse, so every abstraction out of it is injective and fails `compresses`.
    Understanding needs something to throw away. -/
theorem no_understanding_of_subsingleton {S M : Type*} [Subsingleton S]
    (u : Understanding S M) : False :=
  u.compresses (fun a b _ => Subsingleton.elim a b)

declarations.name: Systems.modeling_does_not_imply_understanding
declarations.doc:
**Independence witness I (minimal): #9 ⇏ #11.** A one-state system has an internal
model (every system does — `InternalModel.refl`) yet admits NO understanding for any
model space (`no_understanding_of_subsingleton`, since `Unit` is a subsingleton).
"Has a model" is satisfied while "is understood" is impossible.
declarations.signature:
Systems.modeling_does_not_imply_understanding.{u_1} :
  (∃ x, True) ∧ ∀ (M : Type u_1) (a : Systems.Understanding Unit M), False
declarations.source:
/-- **Independence witness I (minimal): #9 ⇏ #11.** A one-state system has an internal
    model (every system does — `InternalModel.refl`) yet admits NO understanding for any
    model space (`no_understanding_of_subsingleton`, since `Unit` is a subsingleton).
    "Has a model" is satisfied while "is understood" is impossible. -/
theorem modeling_does_not_imply_understanding :
    (∃ _ : InternalModel Unit Unit, True) ∧ (∀ M, Understanding Unit M → False) :=
  ⟨⟨InternalModel.refl id, trivial⟩, fun _ u => no_understanding_of_subsingleton u⟩

declarations.name: Systems.cyclic3_no_understanding
declarations.doc:
A three-state system with the 3-cycle as its dynamics cannot be understood. Any
abstraction respecting the dynamics that identifies two of the three states is
forced (because the cycle visits all three) to identify all three, collapsing the
model to a point and violating `nontrivial`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.cyclic3_no_understanding.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} (u : Systems.Understanding (Fin 3) M)
  (h : ∀ (x : Fin 3), u.systemDyn x = x + 1) : False
declarations.source:
/-- A three-state system with the 3-cycle as its dynamics cannot be understood. Any
    abstraction respecting the dynamics that identifies two of the three states is
    forced (because the cycle visits all three) to identify all three, collapsing the
    model to a point and violating `nontrivial`. -/
theorem cyclic3_no_understanding {M : Type*} (u : Understanding (Fin 3) M)
    (h : ∀ x : Fin 3, u.systemDyn x = x + 1) : False := by
  -- the kernel of `abstract` is a congruence for the +1 dynamics
  have hstep : ∀ a b : Fin 3, u.abstract a = u.abstract b →
      u.abstract (a + 1) = u.abstract (b + 1) := by
    intro a b hab
    have ea : u.abstract (a + 1) = u.modelDyn (u.abstract a) := by
      have e := u.abstracts a; rw [h a] at e; exact e
    have eb : u.abstract (b + 1) = u.modelDyn (u.abstract b) := by
      have e := u.abstracts b; rw [h b] at e; exact e
    rw [ea, eb, hab]
  -- a genuine identification from compression
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab, hne⟩ := Function.not_injective_iff.mp u.compresses
  -- closed decidable arithmetic over Fin 3
  have hd : ∀ x y : Fin 3, x ≠ y → (y = x + 1 ∨ y = x + 2) := by decide
  have c1 : ∀ x : Fin 3, x + 2 + 1 = x := by decide
  have c2 : ∀ x : Fin 3, x + 1 + 1 = x + 2 := by decide
  have cover : ∀ x y : Fin 3, y = x ∨ y = x + 1 ∨ y = x + 2 := by decide
  -- one generator edge: abstract a = abstract (a+1)
  have g : u.abstract a = u.abstract (a + 1) := by
    rcases hd a b hne with hb | hb
    · rw [hb] at hab; exact hab
    · have e := hstep a b hab
      rw [hb, c1 a] at e
      exact e.symm
  -- second edge: abstract (a+1) = abstract (a+2)
  have g2 : u.abstract (a + 1) = u.abstract (a + 2) := by
    have e := hstep a (a + 1) g
    rw [c2 a] at e
    exact e
  -- abstract is constant — every state maps to abstract a
  have alleq : ∀ x : Fin 3, u.abstract x = u.abstract a := by
    intro x
    rcases cover a x with hx | hx | hx
    · rw [hx]
    · rw [hx]; exact g.symm
    · rw [hx]; exact g2.symm.trans g.symm
  -- constant abstract contradicts surjectivity onto a nontrivial M
  haveI := u.nontrivial
  obtain ⟨m₁, m₂, hm⟩ := exists_pair_ne M
  obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁⟩ := u.surjective m₁
  obtain ⟨x₂, hx₂⟩ := u.surjective m₂
  exact hm (by rw [← hx₁, ← hx₂, alleq x₁, alleq x₂])

declarations.name: Systems.cyclic3_modeling_not_understanding
declarations.doc:
**Independence witness II (strong): #9 ⇏ #11 even for richly dynamic systems.** The
3-cycle on three states has an internal model yet admits no understanding. Modeling
is free; understanding can be impossible even when there is plenty to compress —
the obstruction is the dynamics, not the cardinality.
declarations.signature:
Systems.cyclic3_modeling_not_understanding :
  (∃ x, True) ∧
    ∀ (M : Type) (u : Systems.Understanding (Fin 3) M),
      (∀ (x : Fin 3), u.systemDyn x = x + 1) → False
declarations.source:
/-- **Independence witness II (strong): #9 ⇏ #11 even for richly dynamic systems.** The
    3-cycle on three states has an internal model yet admits no understanding. Modeling
    is free; understanding can be impossible even when there is plenty to compress —
    the obstruction is the dynamics, not the cardinality. -/
theorem cyclic3_modeling_not_understanding :
    (∃ _ : InternalModel (Fin 3) (Fin 3), True) ∧
      (∀ (M : Type) (u : Understanding (Fin 3) M),
        (∀ x : Fin 3, u.systemDyn x = x + 1) → False) :=
  ⟨⟨InternalModel.refl (fun x => x + 1), trivial⟩,
    fun _ u h => cyclic3_no_understanding u h⟩

declarations.name: Systems.noisyPairUnderstanding
declarations.doc:
A system with a conserved coordinate and a noisy one. `abstract = fst` throws away
the noise; the resulting one-state-dynamics `id` captures the law "the invariant is
invariant." Surjective, strictly lossy, and the model `Bool` is non-degenerate, so a
genuine Understanding exists.
declarations.signature: Systems.noisyPairUnderstanding : Systems.Understanding (Bool × Bool) Bool
declarations.source:
/-- A system with a conserved coordinate and a noisy one. `abstract = fst` throws away
    the noise; the resulting one-state-dynamics `id` captures the law "the invariant is
    invariant." Surjective, strictly lossy, and the model `Bool` is non-degenerate, so a
    genuine Understanding exists. -/
def noisyPairUnderstanding : Understanding (Bool × Bool) Bool where
  abstract := Prod.fst
  systemDyn := fun p => (p.1, !p.2)
  modelDyn := id
  abstracts := fun _ => rfl
  surjective := fun b => ⟨(b, false), rfl⟩
  compresses := by
    intro hinj
    have h : ((true, true) : Bool × Bool) = (true, false) :=
      hinj (show ((true, true) : Bool × Bool).1 = ((true, false) : Bool × Bool).1 from rfl)
    exact absurd h (by decide)
  nontrivial := inferInstance

declarations.name: Systems.AgentLayer
declarations.doc:
An agent layer over stocks `S` with memory `M` and commands `C`: the three
maps of Mobus's Fig. 11.1 as bert-compose runs them.
declarations.signature: Systems.AgentLayer (S M C : Type) : Type
declarations.source:
/-- An agent layer over stocks `S` with memory `M` and commands `C`: the three
    maps of Mobus's Fig. 11.1 as bert-compose runs them. -/
structure AgentLayer (S M C : Type) where
  /-- The decision model: observation and memory to a command. -/
  decide : S → M → C
  /-- The memory update (H); `fun _ m => m` at the purely reactive rung. -/
  remember : S → M → M
  /-- The work processes under the command: one tick of the stocks. -/
  stepWith : C → S → S

declarations.name: Systems.AgentLayer.step
declarations.doc:
One tick, read-before-write: the command comes from the pre-tick state,
the stocks step under it, the memory updates from the pre-tick state.
declarations.signature: Systems.AgentLayer.step {S M C : Type} (al : Systems.AgentLayer S M C) : S × M → S × M
declarations.source:
/-- One tick, read-before-write: the command comes from the pre-tick state,
    the stocks step under it, the memory updates from the pre-tick state. -/
def step (al : AgentLayer S M C) : S × M → S × M :=
  fun (s, m) => (al.stepWith (al.decide s m) s, al.remember s m)

declarations.name: Systems.AgentLayer.transition
declarations.doc:
The layer as a typed transition: the DETERMINISTIC coalgebra on the product
carrier. That this definition elaborates is the obligation's first half —
the step with agents has the `Id` kind, nothing more.
declarations.signature:
Systems.AgentLayer.transition {S M C : Type} (al : Systems.AgentLayer S M C) :
  Systems.Transition (Systems.Dynamics.conservationExample (S × M))
declarations.source:
/-- The layer as a typed transition: the DETERMINISTIC coalgebra on the product
    carrier. That this definition elaborates is the obligation's first half —
    the step with agents has the `Id` kind, nothing more. -/
def transition (al : AgentLayer S M C) :
    Transition (Dynamics.conservationExample (S × M)) :=
  Transition.deterministicClosed al.step

declarations.name: Systems.AgentLayer.agent_step_is_product
declarations.doc:
ADR 0008 D6, `agent_step_is_product`: the typed transition's step IS the
product step, definitionally. No new functor, no new state shape — the
stocks' coordinates and the agents' memory coordinates, and the kind stays
deterministic.
declarations.signature:
Systems.AgentLayer.agent_step_is_product {S M C : Type} (al : Systems.AgentLayer S M C) (s : S)
  (m : M) : al.transition.step ((), s, m) = ((), al.step (s, m))
declarations.source:
/-- ADR 0008 D6, `agent_step_is_product`: the typed transition's step IS the
    product step, definitionally. No new functor, no new state shape — the
    stocks' coordinates and the agents' memory coordinates, and the kind stays
    deterministic. -/
theorem agent_step_is_product (al : AgentLayer S M C) (s : S) (m : M) :
    (al.transition).step ((), (s, m)) = ((), al.step (s, m)) := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.AgentLayer.reactive
declarations.doc:
The purely reactive rung (ADR 0008 D4: Threshold, Proportional, Table): no
memory, so `M = Unit` and the decision reads the stocks alone.
declarations.signature:
Systems.AgentLayer.reactive {S C : Type} (decide : S → C) (stepWith : C → S → S) :
  Systems.AgentLayer S Unit C
declarations.source:
/-- The purely reactive rung (ADR 0008 D4: Threshold, Proportional, Table): no
    memory, so `M = Unit` and the decision reads the stocks alone. -/
def reactive (decide : S → C) (stepWith : C → S → S) : AgentLayer S Unit C where
  decide := fun s _ => decide s
  remember := fun _ m => m
  stepWith := stepWith

declarations.name: Systems.AgentLayer.reactive_step
declarations.doc:
A reactive layer's step on the stocks is the stocks under the decision,
and the memory coordinate is inert.
declarations.signature:
Systems.AgentLayer.reactive_step {S C : Type} (decide : S → C) (stepWith : C → S → S) (s : S) :
  (Systems.AgentLayer.reactive decide stepWith).step (s, ()) = (stepWith (decide s) s, ())
declarations.source:
/-- A reactive layer's step on the stocks is the stocks under the decision,
    and the memory coordinate is inert. -/
theorem reactive_step (decide : S → C) (stepWith : C → S → S) (s : S) :
    (reactive decide stepWith).step (s, ()) = (stepWith (decide s) s, ()) := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.markov_codomain_ne_deterministic
declarations.doc:
The two kinds have different codomains, so a sampling agent has no
deterministic typing and a run mixing the two has no single kind: the
constraint of ADR 0008 D2 bites. Proof: `Unit` is a subsingleton and
`List (Unit × Nat)` is not (`[]` and `[((), 0)]` differ), so the types
cannot be equal.
declarations.signature:
Systems.markov_codomain_ne_deterministic :
  Systems.kindCodomain Systems.DynamicsKind.markov Unit ≠
    Systems.kindCodomain Systems.DynamicsKind.deterministic Unit
declarations.source:
/-- The two kinds have different codomains, so a sampling agent has no
    deterministic typing and a run mixing the two has no single kind: the
    constraint of ADR 0008 D2 bites. Proof: `Unit` is a subsingleton and
    `List (Unit × Nat)` is not (`[]` and `[((), 0)]` differ), so the types
    cannot be equal. -/
theorem markov_codomain_ne_deterministic :
    kindCodomain .markov Unit ≠ kindCodomain .deterministic Unit := by
  intro h
  have hsub : Subsingleton (kindCodomain .markov Unit) := by
    rw [h]
    exact ⟨fun _ _ => rfl⟩
  have this : ([] : List (Unit × Nat)) = [((), 0)] := @Subsingleton.elim _ hsub _ _
  exact List.cons_ne_nil _ _ this.symm

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier
declarations.doc:
The per-node fields `step_dt` actually reads AND writes each tick
(`circuit.rs:477-519`, restricted to `storage`/`activity`). `ι` stands in
for the circuit's fixed node index set (topology is a *parameter*, not
state — §1.2). `V` stands in for the numeric type `storage`/`activity`/
`time`/the ledger totals actually carry (`f32` in Rust) — left abstract
because none of this file's theorems depend on which ordered field it
is; `f32` is not itself a Lean/Mathlib type, so a real instantiation
would pick `ℝ` or `ℚ` at the point this connects to executable code, not
here.
declarations.signature: Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier (ι V : Type) : Type
declarations.source:
/-- The per-node fields `step_dt` actually reads AND writes each tick
    (`circuit.rs:477-519`, restricted to `storage`/`activity`). `ι` stands in
    for the circuit's fixed node index set (topology is a *parameter*, not
    state — §1.2). `V` stands in for the numeric type `storage`/`activity`/
    `time`/the ledger totals actually carry (`f32` in Rust) — left abstract
    because none of this file's theorems depend on which ordered field it
    is; `f32` is not itself a Lean/Mathlib type, so a real instantiation
    would pick `ℝ` or `ℚ` at the point this connects to executable code, not
    here. -/
structure Carrier (ι V : Type) where
  /-- Per-node stock level. -/
  storage : ι → V
  /-- Per-node this-tick activity (flow computed by the one-tick map). -/
  activity : ι → V
  /-- Ticks stepped so far. -/
  tick : ℕ
  /-- Accumulated model time (Σ dt), what forced-series lookups index by
      (§1.4). -/
  time : V
  /-- Circuit-level ledger accumulators (`circuit.rs:477-519`). Included
      because they are genuinely mutated by `step_dt`'s write phase
      (`circuit.rs:1383-1384`, the `dissipated` residual at
      `circuit.rs:1331-1352`) — they are accumulators, like the excluded
      per-node `total`, but the target text (proposal §4) names them
      explicitly as part of the carrier ("storage, activity, tick, time,
      ledger totals"), so they are kept and the asymmetry with `total` is
      flagged, not silently resolved. -/
  emitted : V
  sunk : V
  dissipated : V

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory
declarations.doc:
The internal-trajectory reading of a recorded run (issue #97's
ratified reading, "process = sequence of states"): the state after each
of the first `n` ticks, starting from `x0`, INCLUDING `x0` itself at
index 0. In the engine that is `RecordedRun.start` followed by the `n`
rows of `RecordedRun.history`: `history` holds one row per tick and no
starting row, and `start` carries `x0` (facets `run.rs`, `record`;
`start` since facets walk row 47, 2026-11-04). An earlier version of
this docstring said `history` itself held the starting row; it never
did (facets walk row 41).
declarations.source:
/-- The internal-trajectory reading of a recorded run (issue #97's
    ratified reading, "process = sequence of states"): the state after each
    of the first `n` ticks, starting from `x0`, INCLUDING `x0` itself at
    index 0. In the engine that is `RecordedRun.start` followed by the `n`
    rows of `RecordedRun.history`: `history` holds one row per tick and no
    starting row, and `start` carries `x0` (facets `run.rs`, `record`;
    `start` since facets walk row 47, 2026-11-04). An earlier version of
    this docstring said `history` itself held the starting row; it never
    did (facets walk row 41). -/
def recordedHistory (f : Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V) (x0 : Carrier ι V) (n : ℕ) :
    List (Carrier ι V) :=
  (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun i => f^[i] x0)

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.orbit
declarations.doc:
The orbit of `f` from `x0` — Bunge's "a process is a sequence of
states," read internally (ported verbatim from the probe, §2).
declarations.source:
/-- The orbit of `f` from `x0` — Bunge's "a process is a sequence of
    states," read internally (ported verbatim from the probe, §2). -/
def orbit (f : Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V) (x0 : Carrier ι V) : ℕ → Carrier ι V :=
  fun n => f^[n] x0

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory_eq_orbit_prefix
declarations.doc:
`recordedHistory` is definitionally the finite prefix of `orbit` — the
engineering-naming bridge between `RecordedRun.history` (a `Vec`, in
Rust) and the coalgebraic `orbit` (a stream, in Lean). This direction of
the claim needs no coalgebra machinery; it is true by how `history` is
built (append one `orbit`-step per tick).
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory_eq_orbit_prefix {ι V : Type}
  (f : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V → Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V)
  (x0 : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V) (n : ℕ) :
  Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory f x0 n =
    List.map (Systems.CircuitHistory.orbit f x0) (List.range (n + 1))
declarations.source:
/-- `recordedHistory` is definitionally the finite prefix of `orbit` — the
    engineering-naming bridge between `RecordedRun.history` (a `Vec`, in
    Rust) and the coalgebraic `orbit` (a stream, in Lean). This direction of
    the claim needs no coalgebra machinery; it is true by how `history` is
    built (append one `orbit`-step per tick). -/
theorem recordedHistory_eq_orbit_prefix (f : Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V)
    (x0 : Carrier ι V) (n : ℕ) :
    recordedHistory f x0 n = (List.range (n + 1)).map (orbit f x0) := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal
declarations.doc:
A word of `Unit`-inputs plus one more, mapping to a `Carrier ι V` output
— the closed, `Carrier`-observed final-coalgebra carrier before the
stream-collapse identification.
declarations.signature: Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal (ι V : Type) : Type
declarations.source:
/-- A word of `Unit`-inputs plus one more, mapping to a `Carrier ι V` output
    — the closed, `Carrier`-observed final-coalgebra carrier before the
    stream-collapse identification. -/
def Causal (ι V : Type) : Type := List Unit → Unit → Carrier ι V

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal.step
declarations.doc:
The final coalgebra's own structure map: next output, plus the
derivative (ported verbatim from the probe).
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal.step {ι V : Type} (f : Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal ι V) :
  Unit → Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V × Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal ι V
declarations.source:
/-- The final coalgebra's own structure map: next output, plus the
    derivative (ported verbatim from the probe). -/
def Causal.step (f : Causal ι V) : Unit → Carrier ι V × Causal ι V :=
  fun a => (f [] a, fun w a' => f (a :: w) a')

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh
declarations.doc:
The behaviour map out of an arbitrary closed-deterministic coalgebra
(ported verbatim from the probe, generalized only in the output type).
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh {ι V : Type}
  (step :
    Unit →
      Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V →
        Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V × Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V) :
  Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V → Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal ι V
declarations.source:
/-- The behaviour map out of an arbitrary closed-deterministic coalgebra
    (ported verbatim from the probe, generalized only in the output type). -/
def cbeh (step : Unit → Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V × Carrier ι V) :
    Carrier ι V → Causal ι V :=
  fun s w a =>
    match w with
    | []      => (step a s).1
    | x :: xs => cbeh step (step x s).2 xs a

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh_morphism
declarations.doc: `cbeh` is a coalgebra morphism (ported verbatim).
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh_morphism {ι V : Type}
  (step :
    Unit →
      Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V →
        Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V × Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V)
  (s : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V) :
  (Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh step s).step = fun a =>
    ((step a s).1, Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh step (step a s).2)
declarations.source:
/-- `cbeh` is a coalgebra morphism (ported verbatim). -/
theorem cbeh_morphism
    (step : Unit → Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V × Carrier ι V) (s : Carrier ι V) :
    Causal.step (cbeh step s)
      = fun a => ((step a s).1, cbeh step (step a s).2) := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh_unique
declarations.doc:
**Finality**, ported verbatim: any coalgebra morphism into `Causal ι V`
equals `cbeh`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh_unique {ι V : Type}
  (step :
    Unit →
      Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V →
        Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V × Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V)
  (g : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V → Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal ι V)
  (hyp :
    ∀ (s : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V),
      (g s).step = fun a => ((step a s).1, g (step a s).2)) :
  g = Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh step
declarations.source:
/-- **Finality**, ported verbatim: any coalgebra morphism into `Causal ι V`
    equals `cbeh`. -/
theorem cbeh_unique
    (step : Unit → Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V × Carrier ι V)
    (g : Carrier ι V → Causal ι V)
    (hyp : ∀ s, Causal.step (g s)
      = fun a => ((step a s).1, g (step a s).2)) :
    g = cbeh step := by
  funext s w
  induction w generalizing s with
  | nil =>
      funext a
      have := congrFun (hyp s) a
      exact congrArg Prod.fst this
  | cons x xs ih =>
      funext a
      have h := congrFun (hyp s) x
      have h2 : (fun w a' => g s (x :: w) a') = g (step x s).2 :=
        congrArg Prod.snd h
      calc g s (x :: xs) a = (fun w a' => g s (x :: w) a') xs a := rfl
        _ = g (step x s).2 xs a := by rw [h2]
        _ = cbeh step (step x s).2 xs a := by rw [ih]
        _ = cbeh step s (x :: xs) a := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.replicate_length_unit
declarations.signature: Systems.CircuitHistory.replicate_length_unit (w : List Unit) : List.replicate w.length () = w
declarations.source:
theorem replicate_length_unit : ∀ w : List Unit, List.replicate w.length () = w
  | []       => rfl
  | () :: xs => congrArg (fun l => () :: l) (replicate_length_unit xs)

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.causalOutputOnly
declarations.doc:
With a `Carrier`-valued output port and no live input port, `H` (the
final coalgebra, `Causal ι V`) is exactly the output STREAM `ℕ →
Carrier ι V` (ported verbatim from the probe).
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.causalOutputOnly {ι V : Type} :
  Systems.CircuitHistory.Causal ι V ≃ (ℕ → Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V)
declarations.source:
/-- With a `Carrier`-valued output port and no live input port, `H` (the
    final coalgebra, `Causal ι V`) is exactly the output STREAM `ℕ →
    Carrier ι V` (ported verbatim from the probe). -/
def causalOutputOnly : Causal ι V ≃ (ℕ → Carrier ι V) where
  toFun f := fun n => f (List.replicate n ()) ()
  invFun g := fun w _ => g w.length
  left_inv f := by
    funext w a
    cases a
    show f (List.replicate w.length ()) () = f w ()
    exact congrArg (fun l => f l ()) (replicate_length_unit w)
  right_inv g := by
    funext n
    exact congrArg g (List.length_replicate ..)

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.history_is_final_coalgebra_behaviour
declarations.doc:
**The target theorem.** Declaring the state itself as the observable
(`outputType := Carrier ι V`, `inputType := Unit` — the identity-
observer fix the 2026-07-25 comment names as what avoids the closed-
deterministic degeneracy), the observable behaviour of `x0` under the
final Id-Mealy-coalgebra reading — `cbeh`, transported along
`causalOutputOnly` — IS `orbit f x0`. Nothing about the descriptor
changes but the choice of port; this is `Transition.deterministicClosed`
read through the finality argument above, not a new construction.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.history_is_final_coalgebra_behaviour {ι V : Type}
  (f : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V → Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V)
  (x0 : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V) :
  Systems.CircuitHistory.causalOutputOnly (Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh (fun x t => (t, f t)) x0) =
    Systems.CircuitHistory.orbit f x0
declarations.source:
/-- **The target theorem.** Declaring the state itself as the observable
    (`outputType := Carrier ι V`, `inputType := Unit` — the identity-
    observer fix the 2026-07-25 comment names as what avoids the closed-
    deterministic degeneracy), the observable behaviour of `x0` under the
    final Id-Mealy-coalgebra reading — `cbeh`, transported along
    `causalOutputOnly` — IS `orbit f x0`. Nothing about the descriptor
    changes but the choice of port; this is `Transition.deterministicClosed`
    read through the finality argument above, not a new construction. -/
theorem history_is_final_coalgebra_behaviour (f : Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V)
    (x0 : Carrier ι V) :
    causalOutputOnly (cbeh (fun (_ : Unit) (t : Carrier ι V) => (t, f t)) x0)
      = orbit f x0 := by
  funext n
  show cbeh (fun (_ : Unit) (t : Carrier ι V) => (t, f t)) x0
        (List.replicate n ()) () = f^[n] x0
  induction n generalizing x0 with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ m ih =>
      show cbeh (fun (_ : Unit) (t : Carrier ι V) => (t, f t)) (f x0)
            (List.replicate m ()) () = f^[m + 1] x0
      rw [ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply]

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory_is_coalgebra_prefix
declarations.doc:
Chaining the two theorems: `RecordedRun.history`, for the abstracted
`Circuit` carrier and one-tick map `f`, is a finite prefix of the
Carrier-observed final-Id-coalgebra's behaviour map at `x0`. This is the
top-level claim this file was built to state.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory_is_coalgebra_prefix {ι V : Type}
  (f : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V → Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V)
  (x0 : Systems.CircuitHistory.Carrier ι V) (n : ℕ) :
  Systems.CircuitHistory.recordedHistory f x0 n =
    List.map
      (Systems.CircuitHistory.causalOutputOnly
        (Systems.CircuitHistory.cbeh (fun x t => (t, f t)) x0))
      (List.range (n + 1))
declarations.source:
/-- Chaining the two theorems: `RecordedRun.history`, for the abstracted
    `Circuit` carrier and one-tick map `f`, is a finite prefix of the
    Carrier-observed final-Id-coalgebra's behaviour map at `x0`. This is the
    top-level claim this file was built to state. -/
theorem recordedHistory_is_coalgebra_prefix (f : Carrier ι V → Carrier ι V)
    (x0 : Carrier ι V) (n : ℕ) :
    recordedHistory f x0 n
      = (List.range (n + 1)).map
          (causalOutputOnly
            (cbeh (fun (_ : Unit) (t : Carrier ι V) => (t, f t)) x0)) := by
  rw [recordedHistory_eq_orbit_prefix, history_is_final_coalgebra_behaviour]

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichStep
declarations.doc: One step of a stoichiometric system: the state moves by `N *ᵥ r`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichStep {σ ρ R : Type} [Fintype ρ] [CommRing R] (N : Matrix σ ρ R)
  (x : σ → R) (r : ρ → R) : σ → R

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichRun
declarations.doc:
A run: at tick `n` the rates are `rates n x`, read from the opening
state `x` of that tick.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichRun {σ ρ R : Type} [Fintype ρ] [CommRing R] (N : Matrix σ ρ R)
  (rates : ℕ → (σ → R) → ρ → R) (x0 : σ → R) : ℕ → σ → R
declarations.source:
/-- A run: at tick `n` the rates are `rates n x`, read from the opening
    state `x` of that tick. -/
def stoichRun (N : Matrix σ ρ R) (rates : ℕ → (σ → R) → (ρ → R))
    (x0 : σ → R) : ℕ → σ → R
  | 0 => x0
  | n + 1 => stoichStep N (stoichRun N rates x0 n) (rates n (stoichRun N rates x0 n))

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichStep_conserves
declarations.doc:
A left null vector of `N` gives a quantity one step conserves, for any
rates.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichStep_conserves {σ ρ R : Type} [Fintype σ] [Fintype ρ] [CommRing R]
  (N : Matrix σ ρ R) (ℓ : σ → R) (h : Matrix.vecMul ℓ N = 0) (x : σ → R) (r : ρ → R) :
  ℓ ⬝ᵥ Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichStep N x r = ℓ ⬝ᵥ x
declarations.source:
/-- A left null vector of `N` gives a quantity one step conserves, for any
    rates. -/
theorem stoichStep_conserves (N : Matrix σ ρ R) (ℓ : σ → R) (h : ℓ ᵥ* N = 0)
    (x : σ → R) (r : ρ → R) :
    ℓ ⬝ᵥ stoichStep N x r = ℓ ⬝ᵥ x := by
  rw [stoichStep, dotProduct_add, Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec, h, zero_dotProduct,
    add_zero]

declarations.name: Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichRun_conserves
declarations.doc: And so every tick of a run conserves it, whatever the rate law.
declarations.signature:
Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichRun_conserves {σ ρ R : Type} [Fintype σ] [Fintype ρ] [CommRing R]
  (N : Matrix σ ρ R) (ℓ : σ → R) (h : Matrix.vecMul ℓ N = 0) (rates : ℕ → (σ → R) → ρ → R)
  (x0 : σ → R) (n : ℕ) : ℓ ⬝ᵥ Systems.CircuitHistory.stoichRun N rates x0 n = ℓ ⬝ᵥ x0
declarations.source:
/-- And so every tick of a run conserves it, whatever the rate law. -/
theorem stoichRun_conserves (N : Matrix σ ρ R) (ℓ : σ → R) (h : ℓ ᵥ* N = 0)
    (rates : ℕ → (σ → R) → (ρ → R)) (x0 : σ → R) (n : ℕ) :
    ℓ ⬝ᵥ stoichRun N rates x0 n = ℓ ⬝ᵥ x0 := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ m ih => rw [stoichRun, stoichStep_conserves N ℓ h, ih]

declarations.name: Systems.Kingdom
declarations.doc:
Bunge's two (exhaustive, exclusive) system kingdoms (§1.2). Asserted on the
MODELED OBJECT'S nature — a theory/number is `conceptual`; an animal, an
organization, a machine is `concrete`. NOT derived from carrier contents, and NOT
a property of the model artifact: it is what the modeler declares the object to be.
See `docs/reference/system-type-typologies.md` (bert-lenses#71).
declarations.signature: Systems.Kingdom : Type
declarations.source:
/-- Bunge's two (exhaustive, exclusive) system kingdoms (§1.2). Asserted on the
    MODELED OBJECT'S nature — a theory/number is `conceptual`; an animal, an
    organization, a machine is `concrete`. NOT derived from carrier contents, and NOT
    a property of the model artifact: it is what the modeler declares the object to be.
    See `docs/reference/system-type-typologies.md` (bert-lenses#71). -/
inductive Kingdom
  | conceptual   -- theories, numbers: undergo no material process (M = ∅)
  | concrete     -- animals, organizations, machines: may bear a mechanism

declarations.name: Systems.MechanismSpec
declarations.doc:
The honest Increment-1 surrogate for Bunge's mechanism coordinate: the declared
dynamics descriptor together with its typed transition — the coalgebra GENERATOR of
the behavior set, not the behavior set itself. Attach it to a system as a named
auxiliary; it is deliberately NOT threaded into `MobusSystem.toBunge` (Bridge.lean),
whose proven output is the CES triple. Full M(σ) requires unfolding `transition` to
the behavior set H (Increment 2).
declarations.signature: Systems.MechanismSpec (S : Type) : Type 1
declarations.source:
/-- The honest Increment-1 surrogate for Bunge's mechanism coordinate: the declared
    dynamics descriptor together with its typed transition — the coalgebra GENERATOR of
    the behavior set, not the behavior set itself. Attach it to a system as a named
    auxiliary; it is deliberately NOT threaded into `MobusSystem.toBunge` (Bridge.lean),
    whose proven output is the CES triple. Full M(σ) requires unfolding `transition` to
    the behavior set H (Increment 2). -/
structure MechanismSpec (S : Type) where
  /-- The declared dynamics descriptor (kind, support, ports, invariants). -/
  descriptor : Dynamics S
  /-- The typed transition of that descriptor — the coalgebra structure map `S → F(S)`,
      Mealy-shaped over the ports. This is the generator; unfolding it yields H. -/
  transition : Transition descriptor

declarations.name: Systems.wellKinded
declarations.doc:
Bunge's coherence constraint, machine-checkable now: a system whose MODELED OBJECT
is of the Conceptual kingdom bears NO mechanism (M(σ) = ∅). Scoped to `k` — the
kingdom of the modeled object — so a concrete system that merely *processes*
conceptual objects (kingdom = `concrete`) is unaffected. Forward-compatible: when H
is typed (Increment 2), this refusal of a generator upgrades to `M(σ) = ∅` on H.
declarations.signature: Systems.wellKinded {S : Type} (k : Systems.Kingdom) (m : Option (Systems.MechanismSpec S)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Bunge's coherence constraint, machine-checkable now: a system whose MODELED OBJECT
    is of the Conceptual kingdom bears NO mechanism (M(σ) = ∅). Scoped to `k` — the
    kingdom of the modeled object — so a concrete system that merely *processes*
    conceptual objects (kingdom = `concrete`) is unaffected. Forward-compatible: when H
    is typed (Increment 2), this refusal of a generator upgrades to `M(σ) = ∅` on H. -/
def wellKinded {S : Type} (k : Kingdom) (m : Option (MechanismSpec S)) : Prop :=
  k = Kingdom.conceptual → m.isNone = true

A concrete MechanismSpec built from a closed deterministic transition (a
conservation-flow step, TYPED as the deterministic coalgebra).
declarations.signature: Systems.proofAssistantMechanism (S : Type) (step : S → S) : Systems.MechanismSpec S

/-- A concrete MechanismSpec built from a closed deterministic transition (a
    conservation-flow step, TYPED as the deterministic coalgebra). -/
def proofAssistantMechanism (S : Type) (step : S → S) : MechanismSpec S where

  transition := Transition.deterministicClosed step

declarations.signature: Systems.Invariant : Type
declarations.source:
/-- A conserved quantity is DECLARED, never assumed by the engine (axis D). At this
    layer it is named; DERIVING it from structure (as a CRN derives conservation from
    its stoichiometry, `ker Nᵀ`) is a deeper design question, not this record's.
    Conservation is ONE optional declaration — `invariants = []` is honest for a kind
    that conserves nothing (e.g. a Markov chain). -/

  name : String
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

declarations.name: Systems.Dynamics
declarations.doc:
The declared Dynamics descriptor over a carrier (state space): a checkable
refinement of Mobus's opaque `τ`. It declares WHAT KIND of dynamics, at WHAT
support, across WHAT boundary interface, preserving WHICH invariants — not the
transition function itself (that is the typed, per-kind object of bert-lenses#112,
indexed by this descriptor).
declarations.signature: Systems.Dynamics (Carrier : Type) : Type 1
declarations.source:
/-- The declared Dynamics descriptor over a carrier (state space): a checkable
    refinement of Mobus's opaque `τ`. It declares WHAT KIND of dynamics, at WHAT
    support, across WHAT boundary interface, preserving WHICH invariants — not the
    transition function itself (that is the typed, per-kind object of bert-lenses#112,
    indexed by this descriptor). -/
structure Dynamics (Carrier : Type) where
  /-- The declared index shape. -/
  support : Support
  /-- The transition-functor family, by name. -/
  kind : DynamicsKind
  /-- The boundary interface, input side. `Unit` = closed (no environment coupling). -/
  inputType : Type := Unit
  /-- The boundary interface, output side. `Unit` = closed. -/
  outputType : Type := Unit
  /-- The declared conserved quantities (possibly none). -/
  invariants : List Invariant

declarations.name: Systems.kindCodomain
declarations.doc:
The endofunctor a kind names, as BERT's own definition:
- `deterministic` ↝ `Id`  (— Rutten `F X = X`)
- `markov`        ↝ Nat-weighted finite successors (— Rutten `F X = Dist X`,
  here the finite, weight-counted form of bert-lenses#67; no Mathlib `PMF`)
- `nondeterministic` ↝ finite successor list (— Rutten `F X = 𝒫 X`, the
  life-cycle `ΔS ∈ F(S)` in its finite form).

The finiteness is not a convenience, and Rutten's `Dist`/`𝒫` are the
citation, never the type. Wrapped over the descriptor's ports these are
polynomial (container) functors, so a final coalgebra always exists and `H`
is well defined; **unrestricted `𝒫` has no final coalgebra in `Set`**
(Adámek–Milius–Velebil, MSCS 15 (2005), Ex. 3.14), so a kernel typed on it
could not carry `H`-as-behaviour at all. Do not "generalise" these to
`Dist`/`𝒫`. Settled 2026-07-25, with a compiled `#print axioms` probe:
vault `operations/sessions/2026-07-25/references/final-coalgebra-existence.md`.
declarations.signature: Systems.kindCodomain (k : Systems.DynamicsKind) (X : Type) : Type
declarations.source:
/-- The endofunctor a kind names, as BERT's own definition:
    - `deterministic` ↝ `Id`  (— Rutten `F X = X`)
    - `markov`        ↝ Nat-weighted finite successors (— Rutten `F X = Dist X`,
      here the finite, weight-counted form of bert-lenses#67; no Mathlib `PMF`)
    - `nondeterministic` ↝ finite successor list (— Rutten `F X = 𝒫 X`, the
      life-cycle `ΔS ∈ F(S)` in its finite form).

    The finiteness is not a convenience, and Rutten's `Dist`/`𝒫` are the
    citation, never the type. Wrapped over the descriptor's ports these are
    polynomial (container) functors, so a final coalgebra always exists and `H`
    is well defined; **unrestricted `𝒫` has no final coalgebra in `Set`**
    (Adámek–Milius–Velebil, MSCS 15 (2005), Ex. 3.14), so a kernel typed on it
    could not carry `H`-as-behaviour at all. Do not "generalise" these to
    `Dist`/`𝒫`. Settled 2026-07-25, with a compiled `#print axioms` probe:
    vault `operations/sessions/2026-07-25/references/final-coalgebra-existence.md`. -/
def kindCodomain (k : DynamicsKind) (X : Type) : Type :=
  match k with
  | .deterministic    => X
  | .markov           => List (X × Nat)
  | .nondeterministic => List X

declarations.name: Systems.Transition
declarations.doc:
The typed transition over a descriptor: the coalgebra structure map, Mealy-
shaped over the ports. For a closed descriptor (`inputType = outputType =
Unit`) the field type reduces to `Unit × S → kindCodomain kind (Unit × S)`,
i.e. essentially `S → F(S)`.
declarations.signature: Systems.Transition {S : Type} (d : Systems.Dynamics S) : Type
declarations.source:
/-- The typed transition over a descriptor: the coalgebra structure map, Mealy-
    shaped over the ports. For a closed descriptor (`inputType = outputType =
    Unit`) the field type reduces to `Unit × S → kindCodomain kind (Unit × S)`,
    i.e. essentially `S → F(S)`. -/
structure Transition {S : Type} (d : Dynamics S) where
  step : d.inputType × S → kindCodomain d.kind (d.outputType × S)

constructors.type:
{S : Type} →
  {d : Systems.Dynamics S} →
    (d.inputType × S → Systems.kindCodomain d.kind (d.outputType × S)) → Systems.Transition d

Systems.Transition.step {S : Type} {d : Systems.Dynamics S} (self : Systems.Transition d) :

declarations.source: step : d.inputType × S → kindCodomain d.kind (d.outputType × S)

declarations.name: Systems.Transition.deterministicClosed
declarations.doc:
A deterministic closed transition is exactly a self-map `S → S` — the shape of
a conservation-flow step (Euler-stepped), now TYPED as the deterministic
coalgebra.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Transition.deterministicClosed {S : Type} (f : S → S) :
  Systems.Transition (Systems.Dynamics.conservationExample S)
declarations.source:
/-- A deterministic closed transition is exactly a self-map `S → S` — the shape of
    a conservation-flow step (Euler-stepped), now TYPED as the deterministic
    coalgebra. -/
def deterministicClosed {S : Type} (f : S → S) :
    Transition (Dynamics.conservationExample S) where
  step := fun (_, s) => ((), f s)

declarations.name: Systems.Transition.markovClosed
declarations.doc:
A Markov closed transition maps a state to its Nat-weighted successors — the
absorbing chain of bert-lenses#67, TYPED as the markov coalgebra.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Transition.markovClosed {S : Type} (succ : S → List (S × ℕ)) :
  Systems.Transition (Systems.Dynamics.billMarkovDescriptor S)
declarations.source:
/-- A Markov closed transition maps a state to its Nat-weighted successors — the
    absorbing chain of bert-lenses#67, TYPED as the markov coalgebra. -/
def markovClosed {S : Type} (succ : S → List (S × Nat)) :
    Transition (Dynamics.billMarkovDescriptor S) where
  step := fun (_, s) => (succ s).map (fun p => (((), p.1), p.2))

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.support
declarations.doc:
The support of a binary Joslyn system: elements appearing in some
constrained state. This is the composition of any Bunge image — the
things the distinction is actually about.
declarations.signature: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.support.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α) : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.support_mono
declarations.doc: Support is monotone in the constrained states.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.support_mono.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {J₁ J₂ : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α}
  (h : J₁.states ⊆ J₂.states) : J₁.support ⊆ J₂.support
declarations.source:
/-- Support is monotone in the constrained states. -/
theorem JoslynSystem₂.support_mono {α : Type*} {J₁ J₂ : JoslynSystem₂ α}
    (h : J₁.states ⊆ J₂.states) : J₁.support ⊆ J₂.support := by
  rintro a ⟨b, hab | hba⟩
  · exact ⟨b, Or.inl (h hab)⟩
  · exact ⟨b, Or.inr (h hba)⟩

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBunge
declarations.doc:
The Joslyn→Bunge partial map (roadmap §4.4). NOT a functor: beyond the
Joslyn system itself it requires TWO externally supplied pieces of data,
one per ontological seam:

* `env` + `hdisj` — Bunge's environment is PRIMITIVE; Joslyn's is derived
  from the distinction. No canonical choice exists (see
  `joslyn_toBunge_not_canonical`), so E must be given.
* `hbond` — Bunge Def 1.1 requires at least two distinct bonded
  components; Joslyn's relational states carry no action semantics, so
  bondage evidence must be given.

The composition is the support, the structure is the constrained states
themselves.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBunge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α)
  (env : Set α) (hdisj : J.support ∩ env = ∅)
  (hbond : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b) : Systems.ConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- The Joslyn→Bunge partial map (roadmap §4.4). NOT a functor: beyond the
    Joslyn system itself it requires TWO externally supplied pieces of data,
    one per ontological seam:

    * `env` + `hdisj` — Bunge's environment is PRIMITIVE; Joslyn's is derived
      from the distinction. No canonical choice exists (see
      `joslyn_toBunge_not_canonical`), so E must be given.
    * `hbond` — Bunge Def 1.1 requires at least two distinct bonded
      components; Joslyn's relational states carry no action semantics, so
      bondage evidence must be given.

    The composition is the support, the structure is the constrained states
    themselves. -/
def JoslynSystem₂.toBunge {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (J : JoslynSystem₂ α)
    (env : Set α)
    (hdisj : J.support ∩ env = ∅)
    (hbond : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b) :
    ConcreteSystem α where
  composition := J.support
  environment := env
  structure' := J.states
  disjoint := hdisj
  structure_on := fun p hp =>
    ⟨Or.inl ⟨p.2, Or.inl hp⟩, Or.inl ⟨p.1, Or.inr hp⟩⟩
  bondage_nonempty := hbond

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBunge_ne_of_env_ne
declarations.doc:
Different environment choices give DIFFERENT Bunge systems from the same
Joslyn system — the map is not a function of `J` alone.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBunge_ne_of_env_ne.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α) {env₁ env₂ : Set α} (h₁ : J.support ∩ env₁ = ∅)
  (h₂ : J.support ∩ env₂ = ∅) (b₁ b₂ : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b)
  (hne : env₁ ≠ env₂) : J.toBunge env₁ h₁ b₁ ≠ J.toBunge env₂ h₂ b₂
declarations.source:
/-- Different environment choices give DIFFERENT Bunge systems from the same
    Joslyn system — the map is not a function of `J` alone. -/
theorem JoslynSystem₂.toBunge_ne_of_env_ne {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (J : JoslynSystem₂ α) {env₁ env₂ : Set α}
    (h₁ : J.support ∩ env₁ = ∅) (h₂ : J.support ∩ env₂ = ∅)
    (b₁ : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b)
    (b₂ : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b)
    (hne : env₁ ≠ env₂) :
    J.toBunge env₁ h₁ b₁ ≠ J.toBunge env₂ h₂ b₂ := by
  intro h
  exact hne (congrArg ConcreteSystem.environment h)

declarations.name: Systems.instActsOnFinOfNatNat
declarations.doc:
Action evidence for the witness carrier: everything acts on everything.
Local to this section — the witness needs SOME `ActsOn`, and the
obstruction being exhibited is environmental, not action-theoretic.
declarations.signature: Systems.instActsOnFinOfNatNat : Systems.ActsOn (Fin 3)
declarations.source:
/-- Action evidence for the witness carrier: everything acts on everything.
    Local to this section — the witness needs SOME `ActsOn`, and the
    obstruction being exhibited is environmental, not action-theoretic. -/
local instance : ActsOn (Fin 3) := ⟨fun _ _ => True⟩

declarations.name: Systems.joslyn_toBunge_not_canonical
declarations.doc:
THE NON-FUNCTORIALITY WITNESS (roadmap §4.6 item 3): a single Joslyn
system admitting two environments — the empty one and `{2}` — whose Bunge
images differ. Environment-as-derived vs environment-as-primitive is a
genuine ontological disagreement: no assignment of Bunge systems to
Joslyn systems can be canonical in the environment.
declarations.signature:
Systems.joslyn_toBunge_not_canonical :
  ∃ J env₁ env₂,
    ∃ (h₁ : J.support ∩ env₁ = ∅) (h₂ : J.support ∩ env₂ = ∅) (hb :
      ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b),
      J.toBunge env₁ h₁ hb ≠ J.toBunge env₂ h₂ hb
declarations.source:
/-- THE NON-FUNCTORIALITY WITNESS (roadmap §4.6 item 3): a single Joslyn
    system admitting two environments — the empty one and `{2}` — whose Bunge
    images differ. Environment-as-derived vs environment-as-primitive is a
    genuine ontological disagreement: no assignment of Bunge systems to
    Joslyn systems can be canonical in the environment. -/
theorem joslyn_toBunge_not_canonical :
    ∃ (J : JoslynSystem₂ (Fin 3)) (env₁ env₂ : Set (Fin 3))
      (h₁ : J.support ∩ env₁ = ∅) (h₂ : J.support ∩ env₂ = ∅)
      (hb : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b),
      J.toBunge env₁ h₁ hb ≠ J.toBunge env₂ h₂ hb := by
  have hdisj₂ : witnessJ.support ∩ {2} = ∅ := by
    rw [witnessJ_support]
    ext a
    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
      Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_and]
    rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> decide
  have hb : ∃ a ∈ witnessJ.support, ∃ b ∈ witnessJ.support,
      a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b := by
    refine ⟨0, ?_, 1, ?_, ?_, Or.inl trivial⟩
    · rw [witnessJ_support]; exact Or.inl rfl
    · rw [witnessJ_support]; exact Or.inr rfl
    · decide
  -- ∅ ≠ {2} proved at the membership level: Set.Nonempty.ne_empty routes
  -- through Classical.choice in Mathlib (incidental, run-4 pattern)
  have henv : (∅ : Set (Fin 3)) ≠ ({2} : Set (Fin 3)) := by
    intro h
    have h2 : (2 : Fin 3) ∈ ({2} : Set (Fin 3)) := rfl
    rw [← h] at h2
    exact h2
  exact ⟨witnessJ, ∅, {2}, Set.inter_empty _, hdisj₂, hb,
    witnessJ.toBunge_ne_of_env_ne _ _ hb hb henv⟩

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.support_inter_compl
declarations.doc:
`support ∩ supportᶜ = ∅`, proved at the membership level.
Mathlib's `Set.inter_compl_self` routes through `Classical.choice`
(incidental, run-4 pattern); the fact itself is constructive.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.support_inter_compl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α) :
  J.support ∩ J.supportᶜ = ∅
declarations.source:
/-- `support ∩ supportᶜ = ∅`, proved at the membership level.
    Mathlib's `Set.inter_compl_self` routes through `Classical.choice`
    (incidental, run-4 pattern); the fact itself is constructive. -/
theorem JoslynSystem₂.support_inter_compl {α : Type*} (J : JoslynSystem₂ α) :
    J.support ∩ J.supportᶜ = ∅ :=
  Set.ext fun _ => ⟨fun h => (h.2 h.1).elim, False.elim⟩

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBungeDerived
declarations.doc:
The canonical map obtained by DERIVING the environment Joslyn-style:
`env := supportᶜ`. Only the bondage seam remains as an input.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBungeDerived.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α)
  (hbond : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b) : Systems.ConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- The canonical map obtained by DERIVING the environment Joslyn-style:
    `env := supportᶜ`. Only the bondage seam remains as an input. -/
def JoslynSystem₂.toBungeDerived {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (J : JoslynSystem₂ α)
    (hbond : ∃ a ∈ J.support, ∃ b ∈ J.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b) :
    ConcreteSystem α :=
  J.toBunge J.supportᶜ J.support_inter_compl hbond

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBungeDerived_subsystem
declarations.doc:
CONDITIONAL FUNCTORIALITY: with the environment derived, the assignment
is monotone from states-inclusion into Bunge's Subsystem order — larger
distinction, larger composition, SMALLER environment (the complement),
larger structure. Exactly the C ⊆ / E ⊇ / S ⊆ shape of Def 1.6.

Note the environment leg is the CONSTRUCTIVE complement direction
(`a ∉ support₂ → a ∉ support₁`), not double-negation elimination — unlike
Def 21's `compl_constraint`, this theorem is expected axiom-free.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toBungeDerived_subsystem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {J₁ J₂ : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α} (h : J₁.states ⊆ J₂.states)
  (b₁ : ∃ a ∈ J₁.support, ∃ b ∈ J₁.support, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b)
  (b₂ : ∃ a ∈ J₂.support, ∃ b ∈ J₂.support, a ≠ b ∧ Systems.Bonded a b) :
  Systems.Subsystem (J₁.toBungeDerived b₁) (J₂.toBungeDerived b₂)
declarations.source:
/-- CONDITIONAL FUNCTORIALITY: with the environment derived, the assignment
    is monotone from states-inclusion into Bunge's Subsystem order — larger
    distinction, larger composition, SMALLER environment (the complement),
    larger structure. Exactly the C ⊆ / E ⊇ / S ⊆ shape of Def 1.6.

    Note the environment leg is the CONSTRUCTIVE complement direction
    (`a ∉ support₂ → a ∉ support₁`), not double-negation elimination — unlike
    Def 21's `compl_constraint`, this theorem is expected axiom-free. -/
theorem JoslynSystem₂.toBungeDerived_subsystem {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {J₁ J₂ : JoslynSystem₂ α} (h : J₁.states ⊆ J₂.states)
    (b₁ : ∃ a ∈ J₁.support, ∃ b ∈ J₁.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b)
    (b₂ : ∃ a ∈ J₂.support, ∃ b ∈ J₂.support, a ≠ b ∧ Bonded a b) :
    Subsystem (J₁.toBungeDerived b₁) (J₂.toBungeDerived b₂) :=
  ⟨JoslynSystem₂.support_mono h,
   fun _ ha hmem => ha (JoslynSystem₂.support_mono h hmem),
   h⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Control₁
declarations.doc:
Joslyn's control₁ (1995, Def 25): each controller state induces a
constraint₁ — an envelope — on the object's states, and the constraint
is genuine: nonempty (overconstraint guard, §3.3.2) and a proper
reduction of variety (dissociation guard, §3.3.1).
declarations.signature: Systems.Control₁.{u_1, u_2} (C : Type u_1) (O : Type u_2) : Type (max u_1 u_2)
declarations.source:
/-- Joslyn's control₁ (1995, Def 25): each controller state induces a
    constraint₁ — an envelope — on the object's states, and the constraint
    is genuine: nonempty (overconstraint guard, §3.3.2) and a proper
    reduction of variety (dissociation guard, §3.3.1). -/
structure Control₁ (C O : Type*) where
  /-- The constraint₁ that each controller state places on O. -/
  envelope : C → Set O
  /-- Overconstraint guard (§3.3.2): the envelope never collapses to ∅. -/
  envelope_nonempty : ∀ c, (envelope c).Nonempty
  /-- Genuine variety reduction (Def 24/25; dissociation guard §3.3.1). -/
  constrains : ∀ c, envelope c ≠ Set.univ

constructors.name: Systems.Control₁.mk
constructors.type:
{C : Type u_1} →
  {O : Type u_2} →
    (envelope : C → Set O) →
      (∀ (c : C), (envelope c).Nonempty) → (∀ (c : C), envelope c ≠ Set.univ) → Systems.Control₁ C O

declarations.name: Systems.Control₁.envelope

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂
declarations.doc:
Joslyn's control₂ (1995, Def 28): a control₁ system where the
second-order variation — the variation of the envelope induced by C's
variation — is itself constrained₂: a nonempty region `stable` (O*)
survives inside EVERY induced envelope. Marken's Def 27 is the
descriptive face: the variable stays in O* despite factors (C's
variation) that should move it.
declarations.signature: Systems.Control₂.{u_1, u_2} (C : Type u_1) (O : Type u_2) : Type (max u_1 u_2)

/-- Joslyn's control₂ (1995, Def 28): a control₁ system where the
    second-order variation — the variation of the envelope induced by C's
    variation — is itself constrained₂: a nonempty region `stable` (O*)
    survives inside EVERY induced envelope. Marken's Def 27 is the
    descriptive face: the variable stays in O* despite factors (C's
    variation) that should move it. -/
structure Control₂ (C O : Type*) extends Control₁ C O where
  /-- O*: the maintained region. -/
  stable : Set O
  /-- O* is a genuine region. -/
  stable_nonempty : stable.Nonempty
  /-- Def 28: O* survives C's variation — second-order constraint₂. -/
  maintained : ∀ c, stable ⊆ envelope c

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂Realized
declarations.doc:
A realized control₂ system (Prop 29's decomposition as data):
`CS = ⟨C, O = ⟨O_E, O_I⟩⟩`. `disturb` is Joslyn's h (the global
environment's variation hitting the effector), `effect` is g (the
effector's constraint₁ on the controlled variables), and `compensates`
is the cancellation: however C varies, the composite constraint on the
controlled variables is the SAME stable region — "the variation of C
and the variation of O_E cancel." The existence direction (every
control₂ admits such a realization) is deferred on Mesarovic 1964.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂Realized.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (C : Type u_1) (E : Type u_2) (I : Type u_3) :
  Type (max (max u_1 u_2) u_3)
declarations.source:
/-- A realized control₂ system (Prop 29's decomposition as data):
    `CS = ⟨C, O = ⟨O_E, O_I⟩⟩`. `disturb` is Joslyn's h (the global
    environment's variation hitting the effector), `effect` is g (the
    effector's constraint₁ on the controlled variables), and `compensates`
    is the cancellation: however C varies, the composite constraint on the
    controlled variables is the SAME stable region — "the variation of C
    and the variation of O_E cancel." The existence direction (every
    control₂ admits such a realization) is deferred on Mesarovic 1964. -/
structure Control₂Realized (C E I : Type*) where
  /-- h: the envelope C's variation imposes on the effector. -/
  disturb : C → Set E
  /-- g: the constraint each effector state places on the controlled
      variables. -/
  effect : E → Set I
  /-- The disturbance envelope is never empty. -/
  disturb_nonempty : ∀ c, (disturb c).Nonempty
  /-- The effector's constraint is never empty. -/
  effect_nonempty : ∀ e, (effect e).Nonempty
  /-- The effector genuinely constrains the controlled variables. -/
  effect_constrains : ∀ e, effect e ≠ Set.univ
  /-- O*_I: the maintained region of the controlled variables. -/
  stableI : Set I
  /-- The maintained region is a genuine constraint. -/
  stableI_ne_univ : stableI ≠ Set.univ
  /-- The cancellation (Prop 29): the composite constraint on the
      controlled variables is invariant under C's variation. -/
  compensates : ∀ c, (⋃ e ∈ disturb c, effect e) = stableI

constructors.name: Systems.Control₂Realized.mk
constructors.type:
{C : Type u_1} →
  {E : Type u_2} →
    {I : Type u_3} →
      (disturb : C → Set E) →
        (effect : E → Set I) →
          (∀ (c : C), (disturb c).Nonempty) →
            (∀ (e : E), (effect e).Nonempty) →
              (∀ (e : E), effect e ≠ Set.univ) →
                (stableI : Set I) →
                  stableI ≠ Set.univ →
                    (∀ (c : C), ⋃ e ∈ disturb c, effect e = stableI) →
                      Systems.Control₂Realized C E I

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂Realized.stableI_nonempty
declarations.doc:
The maintained region is nonempty: any controller state's disturbance
admits an effector state, whose effect is nonempty and lands inside
the (invariant) composite constraint.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂Realized.stableI_nonempty.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {C : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2}
  {I : Type u_3} (R : Systems.Control₂Realized C E I) [Nonempty C] : R.stableI.Nonempty
declarations.source:
/-- The maintained region is nonempty: any controller state's disturbance
    admits an effector state, whose effect is nonempty and lands inside
    the (invariant) composite constraint. -/
theorem stableI_nonempty [Nonempty C] : R.stableI.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨c⟩ := ‹Nonempty C›
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := R.disturb_nonempty c
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := R.effect_nonempty e
  rw [← R.compensates c]
  exact ⟨i, Set.mem_biUnion he hi⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂Realized.cancellation
declarations.doc:
Prop 29's cancellation, stated as invariance: the composite constraint
the effector transmits to the controlled variables does not depend on
the controller's state — "the variation of C and the variation of O_E
cancel."
declarations.source:
/-- Prop 29's cancellation, stated as invariance: the composite constraint
    the effector transmits to the controlled variables does not depend on
    the controller's state — "the variation of C and the variation of O_E
    cancel." -/
theorem cancellation (c c' : C) :
    (⋃ e ∈ R.disturb c, R.effect e) = ⋃ e ∈ R.disturb c', R.effect e := by
  rw [R.compensates c, R.compensates c']

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂Realized.toControl₂
declarations.doc:
Prop 29 coherence, outer face: a realized control₂ system IS a control₂
system over the controlled variables (the Marken face — his "controlled
event" is O_I; the product E × I misrepresents the compensation since
the effector's role is to vary). The envelope is the composite
constraint; the maintained region is O*_I.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂Realized.toControl₂.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {C : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {I : Type u_3}
  (R : Systems.Control₂Realized C E I) [Nonempty C] : Systems.Control₂ C I
declarations.source:
/-- Prop 29 coherence, outer face: a realized control₂ system IS a control₂
    system over the controlled variables (the Marken face — his "controlled
    event" is O_I; the product E × I misrepresents the compensation since
    the effector's role is to vary). The envelope is the composite
    constraint; the maintained region is O*_I. -/
def toControl₂ [Nonempty C] : Control₂ C I where
  envelope := fun c => ⋃ e ∈ R.disturb c, R.effect e
  envelope_nonempty := fun c => by
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := R.disturb_nonempty c
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := R.effect_nonempty e
    exact ⟨i, Set.mem_biUnion he hi⟩
  constrains := fun c => by
    rw [R.compensates c]
    exact R.stableI_ne_univ
  stable := R.stableI
  stable_nonempty := R.stableI_nonempty
  -- why: (compensates c).ge routes through the classical Set order instance;
  -- direct membership transport keeps the construction axiom-free
  maintained := fun c => fun _ hi => (R.compensates c).symm ▸ hi

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂Realized.toControl₁
declarations.doc:
Prop 29's inner claim: the realized object is ITSELF a control₁ system
O = ⟨O_E, O_I⟩ — the effector controls₁ the controlled variables.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂Realized.toControl₁.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {C : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {I : Type u_3}
  (R : Systems.Control₂Realized C E I) : Systems.Control₁ E I
declarations.source:
/-- Prop 29's inner claim: the realized object is ITSELF a control₁ system
    O = ⟨O_E, O_I⟩ — the effector controls₁ the controlled variables. -/
def toControl₁ : Control₁ E I where
  envelope := R.effect
  envelope_nonempty := R.effect_nonempty
  constrains := R.effect_constrains

declarations.name: Systems.singleton_ne_univ'
declarations.doc:
A singleton is never the whole of a nontrivial type — constructive
replacement for Mathlib's `Set.singleton_ne_univ`, which pulls
`Classical.choice`; this proof pulls no axioms at all.
declarations.signature: Systems.singleton_ne_univ'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Nontrivial α] (a : α) : {a} ≠ Set.univ
declarations.source:
/-- A singleton is never the whole of a nontrivial type — constructive
    replacement for Mathlib's `Set.singleton_ne_univ`, which pulls
    `Classical.choice`; this proof pulls no axioms at all. -/
theorem singleton_ne_univ' {α : Type*} [Nontrivial α] (a : α) :
    ({a} : Set α) ≠ Set.univ := by
  intro heq
  obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := ‹Nontrivial α›
  have hx : x ∈ ({a} : Set α) := heq ▸ Set.mem_univ x
  have hy : y ∈ ({a} : Set α) := heq ▸ Set.mem_univ y
  exact hxy (hx.trans hy.symm)

declarations.name: Systems.Homeostat.toControl₂Realized
declarations.doc:
Every PERFECT homeostat — one whose feedback law reaches the set point
in one tick (`hreach`) — realizes Joslyn's control₂: disturbed states
force the compensating action (h), the sensor reads out the controlled
variable (g), and the composite readout is pinned to the set point —
the cancellation. This machine-checks the roadmap's claim that the
Joslyn formalization IS the Governance formalization, for perfect
regulators; the asymptotic version (set point reached in the limit)
needs dynamics and is deferred.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Homeostat.toControl₂Realized.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [Nontrivial O]
  (h : Systems.Homeostat S O) (hreach : ∀ (s : S), h.sensor (h.feedbackLaw s) = h.setPoint) :
  Systems.Control₂Realized S S O
declarations.source:
/-- Every PERFECT homeostat — one whose feedback law reaches the set point
    in one tick (`hreach`) — realizes Joslyn's control₂: disturbed states
    force the compensating action (h), the sensor reads out the controlled
    variable (g), and the composite readout is pinned to the set point —
    the cancellation. This machine-checks the roadmap's claim that the
    Joslyn formalization IS the Governance formalization, for perfect
    regulators; the asymptotic version (set point reached in the limit)
    needs dynamics and is deferred. -/
def Homeostat.toControl₂Realized {S O : Type*} [Nontrivial O]
    (h : Homeostat S O)
    (hreach : ∀ s, h.sensor (h.feedbackLaw s) = h.setPoint) :
    Control₂Realized S S O where
  disturb := fun s => {h.feedbackLaw s}
  effect := fun s' => {h.sensor s'}
  disturb_nonempty := fun s => Set.singleton_nonempty _
  effect_nonempty := fun s' => Set.singleton_nonempty _
  effect_constrains := fun s' => singleton_ne_univ' _
  stableI := {h.setPoint}
  stableI_ne_univ := singleton_ne_univ' _
  -- why: simp / Set.biUnion_singleton route through classical lemmas; the
  -- elementary two-inclusion proof keeps the bridge choice-free
  compensates := fun s => by
    apply Set.Subset.antisymm
    · intro o ho
      obtain ⟨s', hs', ho'⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp ho
      rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hs' ho' ⊢
      rw [ho', hs', hreach s]
    · intro o ho
      rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ho
      refine Set.mem_biUnion (Set.mem_singleton _) ?_
      rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff, ho, hreach s]

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂.stable_ne_univ
declarations.doc:
The stable region of a control₂ system is a genuine constraint:
it sits inside some envelope, and envelopes never fill the space.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂.stable_ne_univ.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [Nonempty C]
  (ct : Systems.Control₂ C O) : ct.stable ≠ Set.univ
declarations.source:
/-- The stable region of a control₂ system is a genuine constraint:
    it sits inside some envelope, and envelopes never fill the space. -/
theorem Control₂.stable_ne_univ {C O : Type*} [Nonempty C]
    (ct : Control₂ C O) : ct.stable ≠ Set.univ := by
  intro heq
  obtain ⟨c₀⟩ := ‹Nonempty C›
  apply ct.constrains c₀
  ext x
  exact ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => ct.maintained c₀ (by rw [heq]; trivial)⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂.trivialRealization
declarations.doc:
The trivial realization: effector := the controller itself, effect :=
constantly the stable region. Every `Control₂Realized` field is
satisfied — including the cancellation, which holds because the
effect never varied in the first place. Cancellation by IGNORING the
disturbance: formally admissible, semantically empty. This is the
degeneracy that shows the set tier cannot distinguish compensation
from ignorance.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂.trivialRealization.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [Nonempty C]
  (ct : Systems.Control₂ C O) : Systems.Control₂Realized C C O
declarations.source:
/-- The trivial realization: effector := the controller itself, effect :=
    constantly the stable region. Every `Control₂Realized` field is
    satisfied — including the cancellation, which holds because the
    effect never varied in the first place. Cancellation by IGNORING the
    disturbance: formally admissible, semantically empty. This is the
    degeneracy that shows the set tier cannot distinguish compensation
    from ignorance. -/
def Control₂.trivialRealization {C O : Type*} [Nonempty C]
    (ct : Control₂ C O) : Control₂Realized C C O where
  disturb := fun c => {c}
  effect := fun _ => ct.stable
  disturb_nonempty := fun c => Set.singleton_nonempty c
  effect_nonempty := fun _ => ct.stable_nonempty
  effect_constrains := fun _ => ct.stable_ne_univ
  stableI := ct.stable
  stableI_ne_univ := ct.stable_ne_univ
  -- why: elementary two-inclusion proof keeps the construction axiom-free
  -- (Set.biUnion_singleton routes through Classical.choice, run-4 lesson)
  compensates := fun c => by
    apply Set.Subset.antisymm
    · intro i hi
      obtain ⟨e, _, hie⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp hi
      exact hie
    · intro i hi
      exact Set.mem_biUnion rfl hi

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂.exists_realization
declarations.doc:
PROP 29, EXISTENCE DIRECTION (set-tier form): every control₂ system
admits a realization with the same maintained region. TRIVIALLY true
via `trivialRealization` — and that triviality IS the finding. Joslyn
derived Prop 29 from Mesarovic's decomposition theorem as "O must
have internal states that vary to compensate"; at the set tier the
quantifier over realizations is satisfied by one that does not vary
at all. The semantic content of Prop 29 lives one tier up, where
variation is a real notion. Pair with `toControl₂_envelope_const`
for the obstruction half.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Control₂.exists_realization.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [Nonempty C]
  (ct : Systems.Control₂ C O) : ∃ R, R.stableI = ct.stable
declarations.source:
/-- PROP 29, EXISTENCE DIRECTION (set-tier form): every control₂ system
    admits a realization with the same maintained region. TRIVIALLY true
    via `trivialRealization` — and that triviality IS the finding. Joslyn
    derived Prop 29 from Mesarovic's decomposition theorem as "O must
    have internal states that vary to compensate"; at the set tier the
    quantifier over realizations is satisfied by one that does not vary
    at all. The semantic content of Prop 29 lives one tier up, where
    variation is a real notion. Pair with `toControl₂_envelope_const`
    for the obstruction half. -/
theorem Control₂.exists_realization {C O : Type*} [Nonempty C]
    (ct : Control₂ C O) :
    ∃ R : Control₂Realized C C O, R.stableI = ct.stable :=
  ⟨ct.trivialRealization, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Control₂Realized.toControl₂_envelope_const
declarations.doc:
THE OBSTRUCTION: the outer control₂ extracted from ANY realization
has constant envelopes — `compensates` pins every composite to the
same maintained region. So envelope-faithful recovery of a control₂
with genuinely varying envelopes is impossible through
`toControl₂`: Prop 29's existence direction is trivial in its
stable-region form and false in its envelope-faithful form.
declarations.source:
/-- THE OBSTRUCTION: the outer control₂ extracted from ANY realization
    has constant envelopes — `compensates` pins every composite to the
    same maintained region. So envelope-faithful recovery of a control₂
    with genuinely varying envelopes is impossible through
    `toControl₂`: Prop 29's existence direction is trivial in its
    stable-region form and false in its envelope-faithful form. -/
theorem Control₂Realized.toControl₂_envelope_const {C E I : Type*}
    [Nonempty C] (R : Control₂Realized C E I) (c c' : C) :
    R.toControl₂.envelope c = R.toControl₂.envelope c' :=
  R.cancellation c c'

declarations.name: Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.levelRealizes
declarations.doc:
Each level of the HCGS, at any coordination state, is a homeostat
(`opsHomeostat`) — and a PERFECT level (one whose feedback law reaches
the fed-down set point in one tick) realizes Joslyn's control₂ through
run 4's Governance bridge. "HCGS level = homeostat = realized
control₂", as a composite.
declarations.signature:
Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.levelRealizes.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {S_ops : Type u_2} {S_coord : Type u_3} {O : Type u_4} [Nontrivial O]
  (tlg : Systems.TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) (sc : S_coord)
  (hreach :
    ∀ (so : S_ops),
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).sensor ((tlg.opsHomeostat sc).feedbackLaw so) =
        (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint) :
  Systems.Control₂Realized S_ops S_ops O
declarations.source:
/-- Each level of the HCGS, at any coordination state, is a homeostat
    (`opsHomeostat`) — and a PERFECT level (one whose feedback law reaches
    the fed-down set point in one tick) realizes Joslyn's control₂ through
    run 4's Governance bridge. "HCGS level = homeostat = realized
    control₂", as a composite. -/
def TwoLevelGovernance.levelRealizes [Nontrivial O]
    (tlg : TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) (sc : S_coord)
    (hreach : ∀ so, (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).sensor
        ((tlg.opsHomeostat sc).feedbackLaw so) =
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint) :
    Control₂Realized S_ops S_ops O :=
  (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).toControl₂Realized hreach
