declarations.name: Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.toCoupled
declarations.doc:
The HCGS as coupled dynamics: coordination (slow slot) and operations
(fast slot) as a `CoupledDynamicSystem`. The laws are read off
`TwoLevelGovernance.combinedLaw`'s let-bindings exactly — see
`toCoupled_combinedLaw` for the coherence.
declarations.signature:
Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.toCoupled.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {S_ops : Type u_2} {S_coord : Type u_3} {O : Type u_4}
  (tlg : Systems.TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) :
  Systems.CoupledDynamicSystem α S_coord S_ops
declarations.source:
/-- The HCGS as coupled dynamics: coordination (slow slot) and operations
    (fast slot) as a `CoupledDynamicSystem`. The laws are read off
    `TwoLevelGovernance.combinedLaw`'s let-bindings exactly — see
    `toCoupled_combinedLaw` for the coherence. -/
def TwoLevelGovernance.toCoupled
    (tlg : TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) :
    CoupledDynamicSystem α S_coord S_ops where
  system := tlg.system
  law₁ := fun sc so =>
    tlg.coordLaw sc (tlg.opsError (tlg.opsSensor so) tlg.opsSetPoint)
  law₂ := fun sc so =>
    tlg.opsCorrect
      (tlg.opsError (tlg.opsSensor so)
        (tlg.setPointUpdate sc (tlg.opsError tlg.opsSetPoint tlg.opsSetPoint)))
      so

declarations.name: Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.toCoupled_combinedLaw
declarations.doc:
Coherence: the coupled packaging has the SAME combined dynamics as the
two-level governance it came from. The packaging forgets nothing.
declarations.source:
/-- Coherence: the coupled packaging has the SAME combined dynamics as the
    two-level governance it came from. The packaging forgets nothing. -/
theorem TwoLevelGovernance.toCoupled_combinedLaw
    (tlg : TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) :
    tlg.toCoupled.combinedLaw = tlg.combinedLaw :=
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.fast_ops_is_level_homeostat
declarations.doc:
JOSLYN DEF 28 ≡ TIMESCALE DECOMPOSITION, machine-checked: at any
coupled equilibrium, the HCGS decomposes into fast/slow dynamics, and
the fast operational dynamics — the coordinator frozen at its
equilibrium value — IS the level homeostat's feedback law. Joslyn's
"second-order variation at a hierarchically distinct level, on a
slower time scale" (§3.3, citing Auger/Salthe) and Mobus's
timescale-separated HCGS make the same structural claim; once both are
packaged, the identification is definitional.
declarations.source:
/-- JOSLYN DEF 28 ≡ TIMESCALE DECOMPOSITION, machine-checked: at any
    coupled equilibrium, the HCGS decomposes into fast/slow dynamics, and
    the fast operational dynamics — the coordinator frozen at its
    equilibrium value — IS the level homeostat's feedback law. Joslyn's
    "second-order variation at a hierarchically distinct level, on a
    slower time scale" (§3.3, citing Auger/Salthe) and Mobus's
    timescale-separated HCGS make the same structural claim; once both are
    packaged, the identification is definitional. -/
theorem TwoLevelGovernance.fast_ops_is_level_homeostat
    (tlg : TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) (sc₀ : S_coord) (so₀ : S_ops)
    (heq : CoupledEquilibrium tlg.toCoupled.law₁ tlg.toCoupled.law₂ sc₀ so₀) :
    (tlg.toCoupled.decompose sc₀ so₀ heq).fast₂ =
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc₀).feedbackLaw :=
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.feedDownward_moves_stable
declarations.doc:
THE DIVERGENCE THEOREM (new in the sketch; not in the roadmap): if two
coordination states issue different set points, the corresponding level
realizations maintain DIFFERENT regions. Joslyn's Prop 29 cancellation
demands the maintained region be invariant under the upper level's
variation; Mobus's feed-downward exists to violate exactly that — the
coordinator's variation MOVES O*. The upper level of the HCGS is an
authority that retunes, not a disturbance that is cancelled: Joslyn's C
maps to strategic CONTEXT, never to the coordinator.
declarations.signature:
Systems.TwoLevelGovernance.feedDownward_moves_stable.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1}
  [Systems.ActsOn α] {S_ops : Type u_2} {S_coord : Type u_3} {O : Type u_4} [Nontrivial O]
  (tlg : Systems.TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) {sc sc' : S_coord}
  (hreach :
    ∀ (so : S_ops),
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).sensor ((tlg.opsHomeostat sc).feedbackLaw so) =
        (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint)
  (hreach' :
    ∀ (so : S_ops),
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc').sensor ((tlg.opsHomeostat sc').feedbackLaw so) =
        (tlg.opsHomeostat sc').setPoint)
  (hne : (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint ≠ (tlg.opsHomeostat sc').setPoint) :
  (tlg.levelRealizes sc hreach).stableI ≠ (tlg.levelRealizes sc' hreach').stableI
declarations.source:
/-- THE DIVERGENCE THEOREM (new in the sketch; not in the roadmap): if two
    coordination states issue different set points, the corresponding level
    realizations maintain DIFFERENT regions. Joslyn's Prop 29 cancellation
    demands the maintained region be invariant under the upper level's
    variation; Mobus's feed-downward exists to violate exactly that — the
    coordinator's variation MOVES O*. The upper level of the HCGS is an
    authority that retunes, not a disturbance that is cancelled: Joslyn's C
    maps to strategic CONTEXT, never to the coordinator. -/
theorem TwoLevelGovernance.feedDownward_moves_stable [Nontrivial O]
    (tlg : TwoLevelGovernance α S_ops S_coord O) {sc sc' : S_coord}
    (hreach : ∀ so, (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).sensor
        ((tlg.opsHomeostat sc).feedbackLaw so) =
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint)
    (hreach' : ∀ so, (tlg.opsHomeostat sc').sensor
        ((tlg.opsHomeostat sc').feedbackLaw so) =
      (tlg.opsHomeostat sc').setPoint)
    (hne : (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint ≠ (tlg.opsHomeostat sc').setPoint) :
    (tlg.levelRealizes sc hreach).stableI ≠
      (tlg.levelRealizes sc' hreach').stableI := by
  intro heq
  have hmem : (tlg.opsHomeostat sc).setPoint ∈
      (tlg.levelRealizes sc hreach).stableI := rfl
  rw [heq, tlg.levelRealizes_stableI sc' hreach'] at hmem
  exact hne hmem

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem
declarations.doc:
Joslyn's System₁ (1995, Def 5): a nonempty constrained subset of a
product of dimensional distinctions, `S ⊆ ∏ᵢ Xᵢ`, `S ≠ ∅`.
Mesarovic's relational system; `ι` indexes the dimensional variety,
`X i` the distinctions along dimension `i`. Nonemptiness is
definitional — a system with no admitted states draws no distinction.
declarations.signature: Systems.JoslynSystem.{u_1, u_2} (ι : Type u_1) (X : ι → Type u_2) : Type (max u_1 u_2)
declarations.source:
/-- Joslyn's System₁ (1995, Def 5): a nonempty constrained subset of a
    product of dimensional distinctions, `S ⊆ ∏ᵢ Xᵢ`, `S ≠ ∅`.
    Mesarovic's relational system; `ι` indexes the dimensional variety,
    `X i` the distinctions along dimension `i`. Nonemptiness is
    definitional — a system with no admitted states draws no distinction. -/
structure JoslynSystem (ι : Type*) (X : ι → Type*) where
  /-- S: the constrained (admitted) states within the product space. -/
  states : Set (∀ i, X i)
  /-- Def 5's S ≠ ∅ — an empty system draws no cardinal distinction. -/
  nonempty : states.Nonempty

    to Klir): a nonempty relation on a single carrier. -/

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem.constraint
declarations.doc:
The constraint of a Joslyn system: `C = X − S`, everything the system
excludes (Def 21). The environment is DERIVED from the distinction,
not primitive — the ontological seam with Bunge's CES triple, where E
is a given (Phase 4.4, out of scope here).
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem.constraint.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {X : ι → Type u_2}
  (J : Systems.JoslynSystem ι X) : Set ((i : ι) → X i)
declarations.source:
/-- The constraint of a Joslyn system: `C = X − S`, everything the system
    excludes (Def 21). The environment is DERIVED from the distinction,
    not primitive — the ontological seam with Bunge's CES triple, where E
    is a given (Phase 4.4, out of scope here). -/
@[atlas "joslyn-1995-system"]
def JoslynSystem.constraint {ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*}
    (J : JoslynSystem ι X) : Set (∀ i, X i) :=
  J.statesᶜ

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.constraint
declarations.doc: Binary version of the Def 21 constraint.
declarations.signature: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.constraint.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α) : Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem.compl_constraint
declarations.doc:
The system is recoverable from its constraint: `Cᶜ = S`. Def 21's
synthetic reading is faithful — specifying what is excluded specifies
the system.

FOUNDATIONAL NOTE: this theorem is essentially CLASSICAL
(`#print axioms` shows `Classical.choice`, via LEM). Double complement
`Sᶜᶜ = S` is double-negation elimination on membership, unprovable
constructively — so Joslyn's synthetic definition ("a system IS its
constraint") is a theorem of classical set theory only. A constructivist
can pass from system to constraint but not faithfully back. The
projection theorems below, by contrast, are axiom-free.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem.compl_constraint.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {X : ι → Type u_2}
  (J : Systems.JoslynSystem ι X) : J.constraintᶜ = J.states
declarations.source:
/-- The system is recoverable from its constraint: `Cᶜ = S`. Def 21's
    synthetic reading is faithful — specifying what is excluded specifies
    the system.

    FOUNDATIONAL NOTE: this theorem is essentially CLASSICAL
    (`#print axioms` shows `Classical.choice`, via LEM). Double complement
    `Sᶜᶜ = S` is double-negation elimination on membership, unprovable
    constructively — so Joslyn's synthetic definition ("a system IS its
    constraint") is a theorem of classical set theory only. A constructivist
    can pass from system to constraint but not faithfully back. The
    projection theorems below, by contrast, are axiom-free. -/
theorem JoslynSystem.compl_constraint {ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*}
    (J : JoslynSystem ι X) : J.constraintᶜ = J.states :=
  compl_compl J.states

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.compl_constraint
declarations.doc: Binary version: the system is recoverable from its constraint.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.compl_constraint.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α) :
  J.constraintᶜ = J.states
declarations.source:
/-- Binary version: the system is recoverable from its constraint. -/
theorem JoslynSystem₂.compl_constraint {α : Type*} (J : JoslynSystem₂ α) :
    J.constraintᶜ = J.states :=
  compl_compl J.states

declarations.name: Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toKlir
declarations.doc:
The Joslyn→Klir projection (roadmap §4.3): the thing-set is the full
carrier (`⋃ᵢ Xᵢ` read at the binary tier as `univ`), the relation is
the constrained states. Forgets the constraint's derived-environment
reading and the nonemptiness — the information loss is characterized
by `mem_range_toKlir_iff`.
declarations.signature:
Systems.JoslynSystem₂.toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (J : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α) :
  Systems.KlirSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- The Joslyn→Klir projection (roadmap §4.3): the thing-set is the full
    carrier (`⋃ᵢ Xᵢ` read at the binary tier as `univ`), the relation is
    the constrained states. Forgets the constraint's derived-environment
    reading and the nonemptiness — the information loss is characterized
    by `mem_range_toKlir_iff`. -/
def JoslynSystem₂.toKlir {α : Type*} (J : JoslynSystem₂ α) : KlirSystem α where
  things := Set.univ
  relation := J.states

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.toJoslyn₂
declarations.doc:
The partial section: a Klir system lifts to Joslyn exactly when its
relation is nonempty — Def 5 demands a witness Klir does not.
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.toJoslyn₂.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (K : Systems.KlirSystem α)
  (h : K.relation.Nonempty) : Systems.JoslynSystem₂ α
declarations.source:
/-- The partial section: a Klir system lifts to Joslyn exactly when its
    relation is nonempty — Def 5 demands a witness Klir does not. -/
def KlirSystem.toJoslyn₂ {α : Type*} (K : KlirSystem α)
    (h : K.relation.Nonempty) : JoslynSystem₂ α where
  states := K.relation
  nonempty := h

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.toJoslyn₂_toKlir_relation
declarations.doc:
The lift is a section on relations: lifting a Klir system to Joslyn
and projecting back preserves the relation exactly.
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.toJoslyn₂_toKlir_relation.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (K : Systems.KlirSystem α)
  (h : K.relation.Nonempty) : (K.toJoslyn₂ h).toKlir.relation = K.relation
declarations.source:
/-- The lift is a section on relations: lifting a Klir system to Joslyn
    and projecting back preserves the relation exactly. -/
theorem KlirSystem.toJoslyn₂_toKlir_relation {α : Type*} (K : KlirSystem α)
    (h : K.relation.Nonempty) : ((K.toJoslyn₂ h).toKlir).relation = K.relation :=
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.mem_range_toKlir_iff
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.mem_range_toKlir_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (K : Systems.KlirSystem α) :
  (∃ J, J.toKlir = K) ↔ K.relation.Nonempty ∧ K.things = Set.univ
declarations.source:
theorem KlirSystem.mem_range_toKlir_iff {α : Type*} (K : KlirSystem α) :
    (∃ J : JoslynSystem₂ α, J.toKlir = K) ↔
      K.relation.Nonempty ∧ K.things = Set.univ := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨J, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨J.nonempty, rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, huniv⟩
    refine ⟨K.toJoslyn₂ hne, ?_⟩
    apply KlirSystem.ext
    · exact huniv.symm
    · rfl

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.hasBondB
declarations.doc:
Structural gate: the dependency contains a distinct pair. Under the total
action pinning this is exactly `Kernel.HasBond` (see `hasBondB_iff`).
declarations.signature: Systems.GatesTruthTable.hasBondB.{u} {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (D : List (α × α)) : Bool
declarations.source:
/-- Structural gate: the dependency contains a distinct pair. Under the total
    action pinning this is exactly `Kernel.HasBond` (see `hasBondB_iff`). -/
def hasBondB {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (D : List (α × α)) : Bool :=
  D.any fun p => decide (p.1 ≠ p.2)

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.irreflexiveB
declarations.doc:
Operational gate: no pair depends on itself. Exactly `Kernel.Irreflexive`
(see `irreflexiveB_iff`).
declarations.signature: Systems.GatesTruthTable.irreflexiveB.{u} {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (D : List (α × α)) : Bool
declarations.source:
/-- Operational gate: no pair depends on itself. Exactly `Kernel.Irreflexive`
    (see `irreflexiveB_iff`). -/
def irreflexiveB {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (D : List (α × α)) : Bool :=
  D.all fun p => decide (p.1 ≠ p.2)

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.kernelOf
declarations.doc:
The kernel on `Fin n` whose dependency is the pairs in `D` (things are all of
`Fin n`, so the arrow constraint is immediate).
declarations.signature: Systems.GatesTruthTable.kernelOf {n : ℕ} (D : List (Fin n × Fin n)) : Systems.Kernel (Fin n)
declarations.source:
/-- The kernel on `Fin n` whose dependency is the pairs in `D` (things are all of
    `Fin n`, so the arrow constraint is immediate). -/
def kernelOf {n : ℕ} (D : List (Fin n × Fin n)) : Kernel (Fin n) where
  things := Set.univ
  dep := {p | p ∈ D}
  dep_on := fun p _ => ⟨Set.mem_univ p.1, Set.mem_univ p.2⟩

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.powerlist
declarations.doc: Every sublist of `l`, deterministically ordered — the powerlist.
declarations.signature: Systems.GatesTruthTable.powerlist.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : List α → List (List α)
declarations.source:
/-- Every sublist of `l`, deterministically ordered — the powerlist. -/
def powerlist {α : Type*} : List α → List (List α)
  | [] => [[]]
  | a :: rest => let s := powerlist rest; s.map (a :: ·) ++ s

/-- Every dependency `R ⊆ Fin n × Fin n`, deterministically ordered so the
    emitted fixture is byte-stable across regenerations. -/
def subsets (n : ℕ) : List (List (Fin n × Fin n)) :=
  powerlist (allPairs n)

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.totalActsOn
declarations.doc:
The total action instance: every thing acts on every thing, so `Bonded`
holds for every pair. This is the semantics `check_bond` computes.
declarations.signature: Systems.GatesTruthTable.totalActsOn (n : ℕ) : Systems.ActsOn (Fin n)
declarations.source:
/-- The total action instance: every thing acts on every thing, so `Bonded`
    holds for every pair. This is the semantics `check_bond` computes. -/
local instance totalActsOn (n : ℕ) : ActsOn (Fin n) := ⟨fun _ _ => True⟩

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.irreflexiveB_iff
declarations.signature:
Systems.GatesTruthTable.irreflexiveB_iff {n : ℕ} (D : List (Fin n × Fin n)) :
  Systems.GatesTruthTable.irreflexiveB D = true ↔ (Systems.GatesTruthTable.kernelOf D).Irreflexive
declarations.source:
theorem irreflexiveB_iff {n : ℕ} (D : List (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    irreflexiveB D = true ↔ (kernelOf D).Irreflexive := by
  simp [irreflexiveB, Kernel.Irreflexive, kernelOf, List.all_eq_true]

declarations.name: Systems.GatesTruthTable.hasBondB_iff
declarations.signature:
Systems.GatesTruthTable.hasBondB_iff {n : ℕ} (D : List (Fin n × Fin n)) :
  Systems.GatesTruthTable.hasBondB D = true ↔ (Systems.GatesTruthTable.kernelOf D).HasBond
declarations.source:
theorem hasBondB_iff {n : ℕ} (D : List (Fin n × Fin n)) :
    hasBondB D = true ↔ (kernelOf D).HasBond := by
  simp only [hasBondB, Kernel.HasBond, kernelOf, List.any_eq_true,
    Set.mem_setOf_eq, decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨p, hp, hne⟩
    exact ⟨p, hp, hne, Or.inl trivial⟩
  · rintro ⟨p, hp, hne, _⟩
    exact ⟨p, hp, hne⟩

declarations.signature: Systems.GatesTruthTable.allRows : List String

/-- Every row, small `n` first, dependency subsets in `subsets` order. The bound

def fixtureJson : String :=
  let rows := String.intercalate ",\n    " allRows
  String.intercalate "" [
    "{\n",
    "  \"_generator\": {\n",
    "    \"source\": \"systems-science-foundations/Systems/Klir/GatesTruthTable.lean\",\n",
    "    \"command\": \"lake env lean --run Systems/Klir/GatesTruthTable.lean > ../bert-lenses/fixtures/gates_truth_table.json\",\n",
    "    \"lean_decls\": {\"has_bond\": \"Systems.Kernel.HasBond\", \"irreflexive\": \"Systems.Kernel.Irreflexive\", \"klir_view\": \"Systems.Kernel.toKlir\"},\n",
    "    \"acts_on_pinning\": \"HasBond is computed under the total action instance, where every distinct pair is bonded; this is the syntactic semantics bert-core::check_bond implements. See hasBondB_iff.\",\n",
    "    \"bound\": \"all (T, R) kernels over Fin n for n <= 2, with T = univ\",\n",
    "    \"row_count\": ", toString allRows.length, "\n",
    "  },\n",
    "  \"rows\": [\n    ", rows, "\n  ]\n",
    "}"
  ]

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem
declarations.doc:
A Klir system: the common-sense definition S = (T, R).
Klir, Facets of Systems Science (2001), Eq. 1.1.

- T (things): the set of entities that constitute the system
- R (relation): the set of pairs encoding systemhood — which things
  are related to which

This is the mathematical common ancestor of Bunge's CES triple
and Mobus's 8-tuple. Both frameworks elaborate this pair in
different directions while preserving T and R as Set α and
Set (α × α) respectively.
declarations.signature: Systems.KlirSystem.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- A Klir system: the common-sense definition S = (T, R).
    Klir, Facets of Systems Science (2001), Eq. 1.1.

    - T (things): the set of entities that constitute the system
    - R (relation): the set of pairs encoding systemhood — which things
      are related to which

    This is the mathematical common ancestor of Bunge's CES triple
    and Mobus's 8-tuple. Both frameworks elaborate this pair in
    different directions while preserving T and R as Set α and
    Set (α × α) respectively. -/
@[ext]
structure KlirSystem (α : Type*) where
  /-- T: the set of things (thinghood). -/
  things : Set α
  /-- R: the relation on things (systemhood). -/
  relation : Set (α × α)

constructors.name: Systems.KlirSystem.mk
constructors.type: {α : Type u_1} → Set α → Set (α × α) → Systems.KlirSystem α

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.ext
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.ext.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {x y : Systems.KlirSystem α}

declarations.source: @[ext]

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.ext_iff
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.ext_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {x y : Systems.KlirSystem α} :
  x = y ↔ x.things = y.things ∧ x.relation = y.relation

declarations.source: things : Set α

declarations.doc: R: the relation on things (systemhood).

declarations.source: relation : Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.toKlir
declarations.doc:
Every Bunge CES triple projects to a Klir system by forgetting
environment. What remains is exactly Klir's (T, R): composition
becomes the thing-set, structure becomes the relation.
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (s : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) : Systems.KlirSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Every Bunge CES triple projects to a Klir system by forgetting
    environment. What remains is exactly Klir's (T, R): composition
    becomes the thing-set, structure becomes the relation. -/
def ConcreteSystem.toKlir {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (s : ConcreteSystem α) : KlirSystem α where
  things := s.composition
  relation := s.structure'

declarations.name: Systems.MobusSystem.toKlir
declarations.doc:
Every Mobus 8-tuple projects to a Klir system by forgetting
everything except (T, R): components become the thing-set, the
total relation (union of internal and external flow relations,
with capacity discarded) becomes the relation.

This projection discards eight categories of information:
environment (objects and milieu), internal/external network
structure, boundary, transforms, history, and time scale.
declarations.source:
/-- Every Mobus 8-tuple projects to a Klir system by forgetting
    everything except (T, R): components become the thing-set, the
    total relation (union of internal and external flow relations,
    with capacity discarded) becomes the relation.

    This projection discards eight categories of information:
    environment (objects and milieu), internal/external network
    structure, boundary, transforms, history, and time scale. -/
def MobusSystem.toKlir {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*}
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) : KlirSystem α where
  things := sys.components
  relation := sys.totalRelation

declarations.name: Systems.triangle_commutes
declarations.doc:
SHOWCASE THEOREM: The diagram commutes.

```
      toBunge
Mobus -------→ Bunge
  \              |
   \  toKlir    | toKlir
    \           |
     ↘          ↓
       Klir
```

Going Mobus → Bunge → Klir (forget Mobus-specific structure, then
forget environment) gives the same (T, R) as going Mobus → Klir
directly (forget everything at once).

The `rfl` proof says: these paths are not merely equal — they are
*definitionally* identical. The type-checker confirms this without
any proof search. This traces to both Bunge and Mobus inheriting
T = Set α and R = Set (α × α) from Klir's common-sense definition
without changing the mathematical type.
declarations.signature:
Systems.triangle_commutes.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hflow : Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hedge : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) : (sys.toBunge hflow hedge).toKlir = sys.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- SHOWCASE THEOREM: The diagram commutes.

    ```
          toBunge
    Mobus -------→ Bunge
      \              |
       \  toKlir    | toKlir
        \           |
         ↘          ↓
           Klir
    ```

    Going Mobus → Bunge → Klir (forget Mobus-specific structure, then
    forget environment) gives the same (T, R) as going Mobus → Klir
    directly (forget everything at once).

    The `rfl` proof says: these paths are not merely equal — they are
    *definitionally* identical. The type-checker confirms this without
    any proof search. This traces to both Bunge and Mobus inheriting
    T = Set α and R = Set (α × α) from Klir's common-sense definition
    without changing the mathematical type. -/
theorem triangle_commutes {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hflow : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hedge : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    (sys.toBunge hflow hedge).toKlir = sys.toKlir := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.toKlir_eq_of_composition_structure_eq
declarations.doc:
What Bunge adds to Klir: environment. Two CES triples with the
same composition and structure project to the same Klir system —
they can differ only in their environment.

Bunge's contribution to Klir's (T, R) was recognizing that a
system exists *within* something: the environment E is a third
first-class component alongside T and R.
declarations.signature:
Systems.toKlir_eq_of_composition_structure_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (s₁ s₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α) (hc : s₁.composition = s₂.composition)
  (hs : s₁.structure' = s₂.structure') : s₁.toKlir = s₂.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- What Bunge adds to Klir: environment. Two CES triples with the
    same composition and structure project to the same Klir system —
    they can differ only in their environment.

    Bunge's contribution to Klir's (T, R) was recognizing that a
    system exists *within* something: the environment E is a third
    first-class component alongside T and R. -/
theorem toKlir_eq_of_composition_structure_eq {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (s₁ s₂ : ConcreteSystem α)
    (hc : s₁.composition = s₂.composition)
    (hs : s₁.structure' = s₂.structure') :
    s₁.toKlir = s₂.toKlir := by
  exact KlirSystem.ext hc hs

declarations.name: Systems.toBunge_eq_iff_toKlir_eq
declarations.doc:
What Mobus adds beyond Bunge: milieu, capacity, boundary
properties, transforms, history, and time scale. Two Mobus
8-tuples with the same components, environment objects, and
total relation project to the same Bunge CES triple —
they can differ in six categories of engineering detail.

Combined with `toKlir_eq_of_composition_structure_eq`, this
establishes the full information loss chain:
Mobus →[lose 6 categories]→ Bunge →[lose environment]→ Klir
declarations.signature:
Systems.toBunge_eq_iff_toKlir_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (s₁ s₂ : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
  (_hflow₁ : Systems.FlowInducesAction s₁.internalNetwork)
  (_hedge₁ : s₁.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty)
  (_hflow₂ : Systems.FlowInducesAction s₂.internalNetwork)
  (_hedge₂ : s₂.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) (hc : s₁.components = s₂.components)
  (he : s₁.environment.objects = s₂.environment.objects)
  (hs : s₁.totalRelation = s₂.totalRelation) : s₁.toKlir = s₂.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- What Mobus adds beyond Bunge: milieu, capacity, boundary
    properties, transforms, history, and time scale. Two Mobus
    8-tuples with the same components, environment objects, and
    total relation project to the same Bunge CES triple —
    they can differ in six categories of engineering detail.

    Combined with `toKlir_eq_of_composition_structure_eq`, this
    establishes the full information loss chain:
    Mobus →[lose 6 categories]→ Bunge →[lose environment]→ Klir -/
theorem toBunge_eq_iff_toKlir_eq {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (s₁ s₂ : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (_hflow₁ : FlowInducesAction s₁.internalNetwork)
    (_hedge₁ : s₁.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty)
    (_hflow₂ : FlowInducesAction s₂.internalNetwork)
    (_hedge₂ : s₂.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty)
    (hc : s₁.components = s₂.components)
    (he : s₁.environment.objects = s₂.environment.objects)
    (hs : s₁.totalRelation = s₂.totalRelation) :
    s₁.toKlir = s₂.toKlir := by
  exact KlirSystem.ext hc hs

declarations.doc: Two things; `false` acts on `true`, nothing acts on `false`.

declarations.source:
/-- Two things; `false` acts on `true`, nothing acts on `false`. -/
scoped instance : ActsOn Bool := ⟨fun a b => a = false ∧ b = true⟩

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair
declarations.doc: Witness (1): Bunge concrete system with a single directed bond.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair : Systems.ConcreteSystem Bool
declarations.source:
/-- Witness (1): Bunge concrete system with a single directed bond. -/
def directedPair : ConcreteSystem Bool where
  composition := Set.univ
  environment := ∅
  structure' := {(false, true)}
  disjoint := Set.inter_empty _
  structure_on := by
    rintro p hp
    exact ⟨Or.inl (Set.mem_univ _), Or.inl (Set.mem_univ _)⟩
  bondage_nonempty :=
    ⟨false, Set.mem_univ _, true, Set.mem_univ _, Bool.false_ne_true, Or.inl false_acts_true⟩
