declarations.doc: The directed pair as a kernel (its (T, R) with the arrow proof).
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.directedKernel : Systems.Kernel Bool
declarations.source:
/-- The directed pair as a kernel (its (T, R) with the arrow proof). -/
def directedKernel : Kernel Bool where
  things := Set.univ
  dep := {(false, true)}
  dep_on := fun _ _ => ⟨Set.mem_univ _, Set.mem_univ _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair_toKlir
declarations.signature:
Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair_toKlir :
  Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair.toKlir = Systems.RosenWitness.directedKernel.toKlir
declarations.source: theorem directedPair_toKlir : directedPair.toKlir = directedKernel.toKlir := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair_has_no_rosen_view
declarations.doc:
CLAIM 3, DIRECTED FACE: no Rosen pair projects to the bonded pair's
(T, R). The bond `false ▷ true` is unrecoverable because it is
one-way and every R_F is symmetric.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair_has_no_rosen_view (V : Systems.RosenSystem Bool) :
  V.toKlir ≠ Systems.RosenWitness.directedPair.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- CLAIM 3, DIRECTED FACE: no Rosen pair projects to the bonded pair's
    (T, R). The bond `false ▷ true` is unrecoverable because it is
    one-way and every R_F is symmetric. -/
theorem directedPair_has_no_rosen_view :
    ∀ V : RosenSystem Bool, V.toKlir ≠ directedPair.toKlir := by
  rw [directedPair_toKlir]
  apply rosen_no_view_of_asymmetric
  refine ⟨(false, true), rfl, ?_⟩
  simp [directedKernel]

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel
declarations.doc: Witness (2): the mutually bonded pair as a kernel — the full relation.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel : Systems.Kernel Bool
declarations.source:
/-- Witness (2): the mutually bonded pair as a kernel — the full relation. -/
def mutualKernel : Kernel Bool where
  things := Set.univ
  dep := Set.univ
  dep_on := fun _ _ => ⟨Set.mem_univ _, Set.mem_univ _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel_isIndist
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel_isIndist : Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel.IsIndist
declarations.source:
theorem mutualKernel_isIndist : mutualKernel.IsIndist where
  refl := fun _ _ => Set.mem_univ _
  symm := fun _ _ => Set.mem_univ _
  trans := fun _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel_hasBond
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel_hasBond : Systems.RosenWitness.mutualKernel.HasBond
declarations.source:
theorem mutualKernel_hasBond : mutualKernel.HasBond :=
  ⟨(false, true), Set.mem_univ _, Bool.false_ne_true, Or.inl false_acts_true⟩

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualBunge
declarations.doc: The Bunge view of the mutual pair exists (two bonded components).
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualBunge : Systems.ConcreteSystem Bool
declarations.source:
/-- The Bunge view of the mutual pair exists (two bonded components). -/
noncomputable def mutualBunge : ConcreteSystem Bool :=
  mutualKernel.toBunge mutualKernel_hasBond

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen
declarations.doc: The Rosen view of the same kernel exists.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen : Systems.RosenSystem Bool
declarations.source:
/-- The Rosen view of the same kernel exists. -/
noncomputable def mutualRosen : RosenSystem Bool :=
  mutualKernel.toRosen mutualKernel_isIndist

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen_observables
declarations.doc:
CLAIM 3, MUTUAL FACE (i): the Rosen view has exactly one observable,
the constant 1 — "a single state set with observables".
declarations.signature:
Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen_observables :
  Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen.observables = {fun x => 1}
declarations.source:
/-- CLAIM 3, MUTUAL FACE (i): the Rosen view has exactly one observable,
    the constant 1 — "a single state set with observables". -/
theorem mutualRosen_observables : mutualRosen.observables = {fun _ => (1 : ℝ)} := by
  ext f
  simp only [mutualRosen, Kernel.toRosen, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, -, rfl⟩
    funext x
    exact mutualKernel.classIndicator_eq_one (Set.mem_univ _)
  · rintro rfl
    refine ⟨false, Set.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    funext x
    exact (mutualKernel.classIndicator_eq_one (Set.mem_univ _)).symm

declarations.name: Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen_indist_false_true
declarations.doc:
CLAIM 3, MUTUAL FACE (ii): the two bonded things are one reduced
state — no observable separates them. Bunge's a ≠ b is invisible.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen_indist_false_true :
  (false, true) ∈ Systems.RosenWitness.mutualRosen.indist
declarations.source:
/-- CLAIM 3, MUTUAL FACE (ii): the two bonded things are one reduced
    state — no observable separates them. Bunge's a ≠ b is invisible. -/
theorem mutualRosen_indist_false_true : (false, true) ∈ mutualRosen.indist := by
  refine ⟨Set.mem_univ _, Set.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
  intro f hf
  rw [mutualRosen_observables, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hf
  subst hf
  rfl

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem
declarations.doc:
An open energy-driven system at the data level (CLS24 Def 7): exposed
relata, a reactive state, a potential valuing states per input, and a
reaction converting valuations into motion. The step is not a free
field — `step_drives` forces it to factor through the potential, and
`reaction_const` pins the reaction's zero-covector behavior. Together
they make "value drives motion" structural: motion cannot bypass
value.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (α : Type u_1) (In : Type u_2) (V : Type u_3) :
  Type (max (max u_1 u_2) u_3)
declarations.source:
/-- An open energy-driven system at the data level (CLS24 Def 7): exposed
    relata, a reactive state, a potential valuing states per input, and a
    reaction converting valuations into motion. The step is not a free
    field — `step_drives` forces it to factor through the potential, and
    `reaction_const` pins the reaction's zero-covector behavior. Together
    they make "value drives motion" structural: motion cannot bypass
    value. -/
structure SpivakSystem (α In V : Type*) where
  /-- N⁺: the exposed relata. -/
  output : Set α
  /-- Q: the reactive state — the dependency cast in the state role. -/
  parameter : Set (α × α)
  /-- State pairs lie among the exposed relata. -/
  exposes : ∀ p ∈ parameter, p.1 ∈ output ∧ p.2 ∈ output
  /-- U: inputs parameterize a valuation of states. -/
  potential : In → (α × α) → V
  /-- ♯: the reaction, converting a valuation into motion. The
      nomological slot — conservative vs dissipative physics is a choice
      of reaction with the potential held fixed. -/
  reaction : ((α × α) → V) → (α × α) → (α × α)
  /-- The zero-covector law: a constant valuation has no gradient, so the
      reaction induces no motion. Set-level shadow of the reaction being
      a bundle map over the state space. -/
  reaction_const : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), reaction (fun _ => c) p = p
  /-- The dynamics induced by each input. -/
  step : In → (α × α) → (α × α)
  /-- The factorization law: every step routes through the potential. -/
  step_drives : ∀ i, step i = reaction (potential i)

constructors.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.mk
constructors.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  {In : Type u_2} →
    {V : Type u_3} →
      (output : Set α) →
        (parameter : Set (α × α)) →
          (∀ p ∈ parameter, p.1 ∈ output ∧ p.2 ∈ output) →
            (potential : In → α × α → V) →
              (reaction : (α × α → V) → α × α → α × α) →
                (∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), reaction (fun x => c) p = p) →
                  (step : In → α × α → α × α) →
                    (∀ (i : In), step i = reaction (potential i)) → Systems.SpivakSystem α In V

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.output
declarations.doc: N⁺: the exposed relata.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.output.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Set α
declarations.source: output : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.parameter
declarations.doc: Q: the reactive state — the dependency cast in the state role.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.parameter.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Set (α × α)
declarations.source: parameter : Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.exposes
declarations.doc: State pairs lie among the exposed relata.
declarations.source: exposes : ∀ p ∈ parameter, p.1 ∈ output ∧ p.2 ∈ output

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.potential
declarations.doc: U: inputs parameterize a valuation of states.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.potential.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : In → α × α → V
declarations.source: potential : In → (α × α) → V

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.reaction
declarations.doc:
♯: the reaction, converting a valuation into motion. The
nomological slot — conservative vs dissipative physics is a choice
of reaction with the potential held fixed.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.reaction.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : (α × α → V) → α × α → α × α
declarations.source: reaction : ((α × α) → V) → (α × α) → (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.reaction_const
declarations.doc:
The zero-covector law: a constant valuation has no gradient, so the
reaction induces no motion. Set-level shadow of the reaction being
a bundle map over the state space.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.reaction_const.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) (c : V) (p : α × α) : self.reaction (fun x => c) p = p
declarations.source: reaction_const : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), reaction (fun _ => c) p = p

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.step
declarations.doc: The dynamics induced by each input.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.step.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : In → α × α → α × α
declarations.source: step : In → (α × α) → (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.step_drives
declarations.doc: The factorization law: every step routes through the potential.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.step_drives.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (self : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) (i : In) : self.step i = self.reaction (self.potential i)
declarations.source: step_drives : ∀ i, step i = reaction (potential i)

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.PotentialFree
declarations.doc:
Potential-free (Def 5.3.2): every input's valuation is constant in
the state — value distinguishes nothing.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.PotentialFree.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Potential-free (Def 5.3.2): every input's valuation is constant in
    the state — value distinguishes nothing. -/
def SpivakSystem.PotentialFree {α In V : Type*} (S : SpivakSystem α In V) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : In) (p q : α × α), S.potential i p = S.potential i q

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.Static
declarations.doc: Static (Def 5.3.2): no input moves the state.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.Static.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Prop

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.Stateless
declarations.doc: Stateless (Def 5.3.2): the state space is trivial (Q ≅ 1).
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.Stateless.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Prop

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.Driven
declarations.doc:
Driven: some input actually moves the state — the system escapes the
static stratum.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.Driven.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Driven: some input actually moves the state — the system escapes the
    static stratum. -/
def SpivakSystem.Driven {α In V : Type*} (S : SpivakSystem α In V) : Prop :=
  ¬S.Static

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.potentialFree_static
declarations.doc:
THE CLASSIFIER BITE: a potential-free system is static. The
factorization law leaves motion nowhere to come from once value
distinguishes nothing. This is what a bare tuple could not prove —
with independent fields, a do-nothing potential coexists with
arbitrary dynamics.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.potentialFree_static.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2}
  {V : Type u_3} (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) (h : S.PotentialFree) : S.Static
declarations.source:
/-- THE CLASSIFIER BITE: a potential-free system is static. The
    factorization law leaves motion nowhere to come from once value
    distinguishes nothing. This is what a bare tuple could not prove —
    with independent fields, a do-nothing potential coexists with
    arbitrary dynamics. -/
theorem SpivakSystem.potentialFree_static {α In V : Type*}
    (S : SpivakSystem α In V) (h : S.PotentialFree) : S.Static := by
  intro i
  funext p
  have hconst : S.potential i = fun _ => S.potential i p :=
    funext fun q => h i q p
  rw [S.step_drives i, hconst]
  exact S.reaction_const _ p

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.driven_not_potentialFree
declarations.doc:
The cost, gate-flavored: dynamics costs value. A driven system cannot
be potential-free.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.driven_not_potentialFree.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2}
  {V : Type u_3} (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) (hd : S.Driven) : ¬S.PotentialFree
declarations.source:
/-- The cost, gate-flavored: dynamics costs value. A driven system cannot
    be potential-free. -/
theorem SpivakSystem.driven_not_potentialFree {α In V : Type*}
    (S : SpivakSystem α In V) (hd : S.Driven) : ¬S.PotentialFree :=
  fun hp => hd (S.potentialFree_static hp)

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_potentialFree
declarations.doc:
A trivial value type cannot distinguish states: every Spivak system whose
value type is a subsingleton is potential-free.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_potentialFree.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2}
  {V : Type u_3} [Subsingleton V] (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : S.PotentialFree
declarations.source:
/-- A trivial value type cannot distinguish states: every Spivak system whose
    value type is a subsingleton is potential-free. -/
theorem SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_potentialFree {α In V : Type*}
    [Subsingleton V] (S : SpivakSystem α In V) : S.PotentialFree :=
  fun _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_static
declarations.doc:
Hence static: value that distinguishes nothing leaves motion nowhere to
come from (via the factorization law).
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_static.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2}
  {V : Type u_3} [Subsingleton V] (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : S.Static
declarations.source:
/-- Hence static: value that distinguishes nothing leaves motion nowhere to
    come from (via the factorization law). -/
theorem SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_static {α In V : Type*}
    [Subsingleton V] (S : SpivakSystem α In V) : S.Static :=
  S.potentialFree_static S.subsingleton_value_potentialFree

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_not_driven
declarations.doc:
**Drivenness requires a non-trivial value type, which the kernel does not
carry.** Over a subsingleton value type — all the kernel alone supplies —
no Spivak system is driven. `Kernel.toSpivak` (`V = PUnit`) is the instance:
the kernel always enters Spivak's world, but only its static stratum;
escaping it needs value data from outside (`toSpivakWith`). This is the
value elaboration's cost stated as a theorem, in kind distinct from the
(T, R)-conditions charged by Bunge and Mobus.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_not_driven.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2}
  {V : Type u_3} [Subsingleton V] (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : ¬S.Driven
declarations.source:
/-- **Drivenness requires a non-trivial value type, which the kernel does not
    carry.** Over a subsingleton value type — all the kernel alone supplies —
    no Spivak system is driven. `Kernel.toSpivak` (`V = PUnit`) is the instance:
    the kernel always enters Spivak's world, but only its static stratum;
    escaping it needs value data from outside (`toSpivakWith`). This is the
    value elaboration's cost stated as a theorem, in kind distinct from the
    (T, R)-conditions charged by Bunge and Mobus. -/
theorem SpivakSystem.subsingleton_value_not_driven {α In V : Type*}
    [Subsingleton V] (S : SpivakSystem α In V) : ¬S.Driven :=
  fun hd => hd S.subsingleton_value_static

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivak
declarations.doc:
Generate the Spivak view: the kernel as an energy-driven system with
the minimal value channel. Unconditional — the kernel always enters
Spivak's world, but only into its degenerate stratum.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivak.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) :
  Systems.SpivakSystem α PUnit.{u_2 + 1} PUnit.{u_3 + 1}
declarations.source:
/-- Generate the Spivak view: the kernel as an energy-driven system with
    the minimal value channel. Unconditional — the kernel always enters
    Spivak's world, but only into its degenerate stratum. -/
def Kernel.toSpivak {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) : SpivakSystem α PUnit PUnit where
  output := k.things
  parameter := k.dep
  exposes := k.dep_on
  potential := fun _ _ => PUnit.unit
  reaction := fun _ p => p
  reaction_const := fun _ _ => rfl
  step := fun _ p => p
  step_drives := fun _ => rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_potentialFree
declarations.doc:
COST (stratum form, part one): the generated view is potential-free.
A value channel is data (T, R) cannot supply — contrast the Bunge and
Mobus costs, which are conditions the kernel may already satisfy.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_potentialFree.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) :
  k.toSpivak.PotentialFree
declarations.source:
/-- COST (stratum form, part one): the generated view is potential-free.
    A value channel is data (T, R) cannot supply — contrast the Bunge and
    Mobus costs, which are conditions the kernel may already satisfy. -/
theorem Kernel.toSpivak_potentialFree {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) :
    k.toSpivak.PotentialFree :=
  fun _ _ _ => rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_static
declarations.doc:
COST (stratum form, part two): the generated view is static. The
kernel is pure exposed structure — all how-it-is, no why-it-moves.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_static.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) :
  k.toSpivak.Static
declarations.source:
/-- COST (stratum form, part two): the generated view is static. The
    kernel is pure exposed structure — all how-it-is, no why-it-moves. -/
theorem Kernel.toSpivak_static {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) :
    k.toSpivak.Static :=
  fun _ => rfl

declarations.name: Systems.SpivakSystem.toKlir
declarations.doc:
Project a Spivak system to its Klir content: exposed relata and state
pairs — the (T, R) it elaborates.
declarations.signature:
Systems.SpivakSystem.toKlir.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3}
  (S : Systems.SpivakSystem α In V) : Systems.KlirSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Project a Spivak system to its Klir content: exposed relata and state
    pairs — the (T, R) it elaborates. -/
def SpivakSystem.toKlir {α In V : Type*} (S : SpivakSystem α In V) : KlirSystem α where
  things := S.output
  relation := S.parameter

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_toKlir
declarations.doc:
Round trip (Spivak): the generated view projects back to the kernel's
(T, R) — the value elaboration adds a channel but loses nothing.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_toKlir.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) :
  k.toSpivak.toKlir = k.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- Round trip (Spivak): the generated view projects back to the kernel's
    (T, R) — the value elaboration adds a channel but loses nothing. -/
theorem Kernel.toSpivak_toKlir {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) :
    k.toSpivak.toKlir = k.toKlir := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_injective
declarations.doc: Faithfulness (Spivak): distinct kernels generate distinct views.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivak_injective.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} :
  Function.Injective Systems.Kernel.toSpivak
declarations.source:
/-- Faithfulness (Spivak): distinct kernels generate distinct views. -/
theorem Kernel.toSpivak_injective {α : Type*} :
    Function.Injective (Kernel.toSpivak (α := α)) := by
  intro k₁ k₂ h
  apply Kernel.toKlir_injective
  rw [← Kernel.toSpivak_toKlir k₁, ← Kernel.toSpivak_toKlir k₂, h]

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivakWith
declarations.doc:
Generate a Spivak view with a supplied value channel. The step is
derived, never free: the factorization law holds by construction.
declarations.source:
/-- Generate a Spivak view with a supplied value channel. The step is
    derived, never free: the factorization law holds by construction. -/
def Kernel.toSpivakWith {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) {In V : Type*}
    (U : In → (α × α) → V)
    (r : ((α × α) → V) → (α × α) → (α × α))
    (hr : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), r (fun _ => c) p = p) :
    SpivakSystem α In V where
  output := k.things
  parameter := k.dep
  exposes := k.dep_on
  potential := U
  reaction := r
  reaction_const := hr
  step := fun i => r (U i)
  step_drives := fun _ => rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivakWith_toKlir
declarations.doc: The enriched view still fixes the kernel: same round trip.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivakWith_toKlir.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} (U : In → α × α → V) (r : (α × α → V) → α × α → α × α)
  (hr : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), r (fun x => c) p = p) : (k.toSpivakWith U r hr).toKlir = k.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- The enriched view still fixes the kernel: same round trip. -/
theorem Kernel.toSpivakWith_toKlir {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) {In V : Type*}
    (U : In → (α × α) → V) (r : ((α × α) → V) → (α × α) → (α × α))
    (hr : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), r (fun _ => c) p = p) :
    (k.toSpivakWith U r hr).toKlir = k.toKlir := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toSpivakWith_driven
declarations.doc:
Supplied value data escapes the stratum: if the reaction moves any
state under some input's potential, the enriched view is driven. With
`driven_not_potentialFree`, such a view provably carries a nontrivial
potential — value earned, not decorated.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toSpivakWith_driven.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  {In : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} (U : In → α × α → V) (r : (α × α → V) → α × α → α × α)
  (hr : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), r (fun x => c) p = p) (h : ∃ i p, r (U i) p ≠ p) :
  (k.toSpivakWith U r hr).Driven
declarations.source:
/-- Supplied value data escapes the stratum: if the reaction moves any
    state under some input's potential, the enriched view is driven. With
    `driven_not_potentialFree`, such a view provably carries a nontrivial
    potential — value earned, not decorated. -/
theorem Kernel.toSpivakWith_driven {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) {In V : Type*}
    (U : In → (α × α) → V) (r : ((α × α) → V) → (α × α) → (α × α))
    (hr : ∀ (c : V) (p : α × α), r (fun _ => c) p = p)
    (h : ∃ (i : In) (p : α × α), r (U i) p ≠ p) :
    (k.toSpivakWith U r hr).Driven := by
  intro hstatic
  obtain ⟨i, p, hne⟩ := h
  exact hne (congrFun (hstatic i) p)

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel
declarations.doc:
The K ≅ 2 kernel at the data level: a system IS a morphism.

`things` and `dep` are Klir's (T, R); `dep_on` is the walking
arrow — the structural commitment that relations depend on things.
This Prop is what distinguishes the kernel from a bare KlirSystem,
whose relation is unconstrained.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- The K ≅ 2 kernel at the data level: a system IS a morphism.

    `things` and `dep` are Klir's (T, R); `dep_on` is the walking
    arrow — the structural commitment that relations depend on things.
    This Prop is what distinguishes the kernel from a bare KlirSystem,
    whose relation is unconstrained. -/
structure Kernel (α : Type*) where
  /-- T: the relata. -/
  things : Set α
  /-- R: the dependency relation — the morphism's graph. -/
  dep : Set (α × α)
  /-- The walking arrow: R is ON T. -/
  dep_on : ∀ p ∈ dep, p.1 ∈ things ∧ p.2 ∈ things

constructors.name: Systems.Kernel.mk
constructors.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  (things : Set α) →
    (dep : Set (α × α)) → (∀ p ∈ dep, p.1 ∈ things ∧ p.2 ∈ things) → Systems.Kernel α

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.things
declarations.doc: T: the relata.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.things.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (self : Systems.Kernel α) : Set α
declarations.source: things : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.dep
declarations.doc: R: the dependency relation — the morphism's graph.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.dep.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (self : Systems.Kernel α) : Set (α × α)
declarations.source: dep : Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.dep_on
declarations.doc: The walking arrow: R is ON T.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.dep_on.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (self : Systems.Kernel α) (p : α × α) :
  p ∈ self.dep → p.1 ∈ self.things ∧ p.2 ∈ self.things
declarations.source: dep_on : ∀ p ∈ dep, p.1 ∈ things ∧ p.2 ∈ things

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.ext
declarations.doc:
Two kernels with the same things and dependency are equal
(the arrow constraint is propositional).
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.ext.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {k₁ k₂ : Systems.Kernel α} (ht : k₁.things = k₂.things)
  (hd : k₁.dep = k₂.dep) : k₁ = k₂
declarations.source:
/-- Two kernels with the same things and dependency are equal
    (the arrow constraint is propositional). -/
theorem Kernel.ext {α : Type*} {k₁ k₂ : Kernel α}
    (ht : k₁.things = k₂.things) (hd : k₁.dep = k₂.dep) : k₁ = k₂ := by
  cases k₁; cases k₂
  simp_all

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toKlir
declarations.doc: Generate the Klir view: forget the arrow, keep (T, R).
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) : Systems.KlirSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Generate the Klir view: forget the arrow, keep (T, R). -/
def Kernel.toKlir {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) : KlirSystem α where
  things := k.things
  relation := k.dep

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.toKernel
declarations.doc: Lift a dependency-respecting KlirSystem back to the kernel.
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.toKernel.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (S : Systems.KlirSystem α)
  (h : ∀ p ∈ S.relation, p.1 ∈ S.things ∧ p.2 ∈ S.things) : Systems.Kernel α
declarations.source:
/-- Lift a dependency-respecting KlirSystem back to the kernel. -/
def KlirSystem.toKernel {α : Type*} (S : KlirSystem α)
    (h : ∀ p ∈ S.relation, p.1 ∈ S.things ∧ p.2 ∈ S.things) : Kernel α where
  things := S.things
  dep := S.relation
  dep_on := h

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toKlir_toKernel
declarations.doc: Round trip (Klir): generating the view and lifting back is the identity.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.toKlir_toKernel.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) : k.toKlir.toKernel ⋯ = k
declarations.source:
/-- Round trip (Klir): generating the view and lifting back is the identity. -/
theorem Kernel.toKlir_toKernel {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) :
    k.toKlir.toKernel k.dep_on = k := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.KlirSystem.toKernel_toKlir
declarations.doc: Round trip (Klir, other direction): lifting and regenerating is the identity.
declarations.signature:
Systems.KlirSystem.toKernel_toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (S : Systems.KlirSystem α)
  (h : ∀ p ∈ S.relation, p.1 ∈ S.things ∧ p.2 ∈ S.things) : (S.toKernel h).toKlir = S
declarations.source:
/-- Round trip (Klir, other direction): lifting and regenerating is the identity. -/
theorem KlirSystem.toKernel_toKlir {α : Type*} (S : KlirSystem α)
    (h : ∀ p ∈ S.relation, p.1 ∈ S.things ∧ p.2 ∈ S.things) :
    (S.toKernel h).toKlir = S := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toKlir_injective
declarations.doc: Faithfulness (Klir): distinct kernels generate distinct Klir views.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.toKlir_injective.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : Function.Injective Systems.Kernel.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- Faithfulness (Klir): distinct kernels generate distinct Klir views. -/
theorem Kernel.toKlir_injective {α : Type*} :
    Function.Injective (Kernel.toKlir (α := α)) := by
  intro k₁ k₂ h
  exact Kernel.ext (congrArg KlirSystem.things h) (congrArg KlirSystem.relation h)

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.HasBond
declarations.doc:
A kernel has a bond iff its dependency contains a pair of distinct,
bonded relata. This is the price of the Bunge view: Def 1.1's
bondage condition imposed back on the kernel.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.HasBond.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (k : Systems.Kernel α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A kernel has a bond iff its dependency contains a pair of distinct,
    bonded relata. This is the price of the Bunge view: Def 1.1's
    bondage condition imposed back on the kernel. -/
def Kernel.HasBond {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (k : Kernel α) : Prop :=
  ∃ p ∈ k.dep, p.1 ≠ p.2 ∧ Bonded p.1 p.2

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toBunge
declarations.doc: Generate the Bunge view: the kernel as a closed CES triple.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toBunge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  (hb : k.HasBond) : Systems.ConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Generate the Bunge view: the kernel as a closed CES triple. -/
def Kernel.toBunge {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (k : Kernel α) (hb : k.HasBond) :
    ConcreteSystem α where
  composition := k.things
  environment := ∅
  structure' := k.dep
  disjoint := Set.inter_empty _
  structure_on := fun p hp =>
    ⟨Or.inl (k.dep_on p hp).1, Or.inl (k.dep_on p hp).2⟩
  bondage_nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hne, hbond⟩ := hb
    exact ⟨p.1, (k.dep_on p hp).1, p.2, (k.dep_on p hp).2, hne, hbond⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toBunge_isClosed
declarations.doc:
The generated Bunge view is closed: the kernel makes no
environmental commitment, so the minimal view has E = ∅.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toBunge_isClosed.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  (hb : k.HasBond) : (k.toBunge hb).isClosed
declarations.source:
/-- The generated Bunge view is closed: the kernel makes no
    environmental commitment, so the minimal view has E = ∅. -/
theorem Kernel.toBunge_isClosed {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (k : Kernel α) (hb : k.HasBond) : (k.toBunge hb).isClosed := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toBunge_toKlir
declarations.doc:
Round trip (Bunge): the generated view projects back to the kernel's
(T, R) — Bunge's elaboration adds environment but loses nothing.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toBunge_toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  (hb : k.HasBond) : (k.toBunge hb).toKlir = k.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- Round trip (Bunge): the generated view projects back to the kernel's
    (T, R) — Bunge's elaboration adds environment but loses nothing. -/
theorem Kernel.toBunge_toKlir {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (k : Kernel α) (hb : k.HasBond) :
    (k.toBunge hb).toKlir = k.toKlir := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toBunge_injective
declarations.doc: Faithfulness (Bunge): distinct kernels generate distinct Bunge views.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toBunge_injective.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] {k₁ k₂ : Systems.Kernel α}
  {h₁ : k₁.HasBond} {h₂ : k₂.HasBond} (h : k₁.toBunge h₁ = k₂.toBunge h₂) : k₁ = k₂
declarations.source:
/-- Faithfulness (Bunge): distinct kernels generate distinct Bunge views. -/
theorem Kernel.toBunge_injective {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    {k₁ k₂ : Kernel α} {h₁ : k₁.HasBond} {h₂ : k₂.HasBond}
    (h : k₁.toBunge h₁ = k₂.toBunge h₂) : k₁ = k₂ :=
  Kernel.toKlir_injective <| by
    rw [← Kernel.toBunge_toKlir k₁ h₁, ← Kernel.toBunge_toKlir k₂ h₂, h]

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.Irreflexive
declarations.doc:
A kernel is irreflexive iff no thing depends on itself.
The price of the Mobus view.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.Irreflexive.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A kernel is irreflexive iff no thing depends on itself.
    The price of the Mobus view. -/
def Kernel.Irreflexive {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ k.dep, p.1 ≠ p.2

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork
declarations.doc:
The kernel's dependency as a flow network: nodes = things,
edges = dependency pairs with trivial capacity.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) :
  Systems.FlowNetwork α PUnit.{u_2 + 1}
declarations.source:
/-- The kernel's dependency as a flow network: nodes = things,
    edges = dependency pairs with trivial capacity. -/
def Kernel.toFlowNetwork {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) :
    FlowNetwork α PUnit where
  nodes := k.things
  edges := {e | e.toPair ∈ k.dep}
  edges_on := fun e he => k.dep_on e.toPair he
  no_self_loops := fun e he => hi e.toPair he

declarations.name: Systems.FlowNetwork.empty
declarations.doc:
The empty flow network: no nodes, no edges. The minimal witness
for the external-flow slot of a generated Mobus view.
declarations.signature: Systems.FlowNetwork.empty.{u_1, u_2} (α : Type u_1) (κ : Type u_2) : Systems.FlowNetwork α κ
declarations.source:
/-- The empty flow network: no nodes, no edges. The minimal witness
    for the external-flow slot of a generated Mobus view. -/
def FlowNetwork.empty (α : Type*) (κ : Type*) : FlowNetwork α κ where
  nodes := ∅
  edges := ∅
  edges_on := fun e he => absurd he (Set.notMem_empty e)
  no_self_loops := fun e he => absurd he (Set.notMem_empty e)

declarations.name: Systems.FlowNetwork.empty_toRelation
declarations.doc: The empty network's relation is empty.
declarations.signature:
Systems.FlowNetwork.empty_toRelation.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} :
  (Systems.FlowNetwork.empty α κ).toRelation = ∅
declarations.source:
/-- The empty network's relation is empty. -/
theorem FlowNetwork.empty_toRelation {α κ : Type*} :
    (FlowNetwork.empty α κ).toRelation = ∅ := by
  ext p
  simp [FlowNetwork.toRelation, FlowNetwork.empty]

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork_toRelation
declarations.doc:
The generated network's relation is exactly the kernel's dependency:
flows recover R with nothing added and nothing lost.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork_toRelation.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  (hi : k.Irreflexive) : (k.toFlowNetwork hi).toRelation = k.dep
declarations.source:
/-- The generated network's relation is exactly the kernel's dependency:
    flows recover R with nothing added and nothing lost. -/
theorem Kernel.toFlowNetwork_toRelation {α : Type*}
    (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) :
    (k.toFlowNetwork hi).toRelation = k.dep := by
  ext p
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨e, he, rfl⟩
    exact he
  · intro hp
    exact ⟨⟨p.1, p.2, PUnit.unit⟩, hp, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toMobus
declarations.doc:
Generate the Mobus view: the kernel as an 8-tuple with minimal
elaboration slots.
declarations.source:
/-- Generate the Mobus view: the kernel as an 8-tuple with minimal
    elaboration slots. -/
def Kernel.toMobus {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) :
    MobusSystem α PUnit PUnit PUnit PUnit PUnit PUnit where
  components := k.things
  internalNetwork := k.toFlowNetwork hi
  environment := ⟨∅, PUnit.unit⟩
  externalFlows := FlowNetwork.empty α PUnit
  boundary := ⟨PUnit.unit, ∅⟩
  transforms := PUnit.unit
  history := PUnit.unit
  timeScale := PUnit.unit
  network_components := rfl
  disjoint := Set.inter_empty _
  interfaces_sub := Set.empty_subset _
  bipartite := fun e he => absurd he (Set.notMem_empty e)
  externalFlows_nodes := Set.empty_subset _
  interfaces_carry_flow := interfacesCarryFlow_empty _

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toMobus_totalRelation
declarations.doc:
The generated 8-tuple's total relation is exactly the kernel's
dependency: internal flows recover R, external flows are empty.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toMobus_totalRelation.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1}
  (k : Systems.Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) : (k.toMobus hi).totalRelation = k.dep
declarations.source:
/-- The generated 8-tuple's total relation is exactly the kernel's
    dependency: internal flows recover R, external flows are empty. -/
theorem Kernel.toMobus_totalRelation {α : Type*}
    (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) :
    (k.toMobus hi).totalRelation = k.dep := by
  unfold MobusSystem.totalRelation
  rw [show (k.toMobus hi).internalNetwork = k.toFlowNetwork hi from rfl,
      show (k.toMobus hi).externalFlows = FlowNetwork.empty α PUnit from rfl,
      Kernel.toFlowNetwork_toRelation, FlowNetwork.empty_toRelation,
      Set.union_empty]

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toMobus_toKlir
declarations.doc:
Round trip (Mobus): the generated 8-tuple projects back to the
kernel's (T, R) — the six engineering elaborations add slots but
lose nothing of the kernel.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toMobus_toKlir.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1}
  (k : Systems.Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) : (k.toMobus hi).toKlir = k.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- Round trip (Mobus): the generated 8-tuple projects back to the
    kernel's (T, R) — the six engineering elaborations add slots but
    lose nothing of the kernel. -/
theorem Kernel.toMobus_toKlir {α : Type*}
    (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) :
    (k.toMobus hi).toKlir = k.toKlir :=
  KlirSystem.ext rfl (k.toMobus_totalRelation hi)

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toMobus_injective
declarations.doc: Faithfulness (Mobus): distinct kernels generate distinct 8-tuples.

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.DepActs
declarations.doc:
A kernel's dependency induces action: every dependent pair is an
action pair. Required to run the existing Mobus → Bunge bridge on
a generated view.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.DepActs.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α] (k : Systems.Kernel α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A kernel's dependency induces action: every dependent pair is an
    action pair. Required to run the existing Mobus → Bunge bridge on
    a generated view. -/
def Kernel.DepActs {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] (k : Kernel α) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ k.dep, actsOn p.1 p.2

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork_inducesAction
declarations.doc:
The generated flow network induces action when the kernel's
dependency does.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork_inducesAction.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (k : Systems.Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) (ha : k.DepActs) :
  Systems.FlowInducesAction (k.toFlowNetwork hi)
declarations.source:
/-- The generated flow network induces action when the kernel's
    dependency does. -/
theorem Kernel.toFlowNetwork_inducesAction {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) (ha : k.DepActs) :
    FlowInducesAction (k.toFlowNetwork hi) :=
  fun e he => ha e.toPair he

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork_edges_nonempty
declarations.doc: A bonded kernel's generated network has at least one edge.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toFlowNetwork_edges_nonempty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (k : Systems.Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) (hb : k.HasBond) : (k.toFlowNetwork hi).edges.Nonempty
declarations.source:
/-- A bonded kernel's generated network has at least one edge. -/
theorem Kernel.toFlowNetwork_edges_nonempty {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) (hb : k.HasBond) :
    (k.toFlowNetwork hi).edges.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, -, -⟩ := hb
  exact ⟨⟨p.1, p.2, PUnit.unit⟩, hp⟩

declarations.name: Systems.ConcreteSystem.ext'
declarations.doc:
Two concrete systems with the same C, E, S are equal
(the coherence constraints are propositional).
declarations.signature:
Systems.ConcreteSystem.ext'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  {σ₁ σ₂ : Systems.ConcreteSystem α} (hc : σ₁.composition = σ₂.composition)
  (he : σ₁.environment = σ₂.environment) (hs : σ₁.structure' = σ₂.structure') : σ₁ = σ₂
declarations.source:
/-- Two concrete systems with the same C, E, S are equal
    (the coherence constraints are propositional). -/
theorem ConcreteSystem.ext' {α : Type*} [ActsOn α] {σ₁ σ₂ : ConcreteSystem α}
    (hc : σ₁.composition = σ₂.composition)
    (he : σ₁.environment = σ₂.environment)
    (hs : σ₁.structure' = σ₂.structure') : σ₁ = σ₂ := by
  cases σ₁; cases σ₂
  simp_all

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toMobus_toBunge
declarations.doc:
VIEW COHERENCE: generating Mobus and projecting to Bunge equals
generating Bunge directly. The kernel sits at the apex of the
commuting triangle: every path between views fixes the kernel.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toMobus_toBunge.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (k : Systems.Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) (hb : k.HasBond) (ha : k.DepActs) :
  (k.toMobus hi).toBunge ⋯ ⋯ = k.toBunge hb
declarations.source:
/-- VIEW COHERENCE: generating Mobus and projecting to Bunge equals
    generating Bunge directly. The kernel sits at the apex of the
    commuting triangle: every path between views fixes the kernel. -/
theorem Kernel.toMobus_toBunge {α : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (k : Kernel α) (hi : k.Irreflexive) (hb : k.HasBond) (ha : k.DepActs) :
    (k.toMobus hi).toBunge (k.toFlowNetwork_inducesAction hi ha)
      (k.toFlowNetwork_edges_nonempty hi hb) = k.toBunge hb :=
  ConcreteSystem.ext' rfl rfl (k.toMobus_totalRelation hi)

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem
declarations.doc: Rosen's formal system (S, F) at the data level.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenSystem.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) : Type u_1
declarations.source:
/-- Rosen's formal system (S, F) at the data level. -/
structure RosenSystem (α : Type*) where
  /-- S: the set of states. -/
  states : Set α
  /-- F: the family of real-valued observables. -/
  observables : Set (α → ℝ)
  /-- "defined on S": an observable carries no value off S. The walking
      arrow, F depends on S, as a Prop. -/
  defined_on : ∀ f ∈ observables, ∀ x, x ∉ states → f x = 0

constructors.name: Systems.RosenSystem.mk
constructors.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  (states : Set α) →
    (observables : Set (α → ℝ)) → (∀ f ∈ observables, ∀ x ∉ states, f x = 0) → Systems.RosenSystem α

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem.states
declarations.doc: S: the set of states.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenSystem.states.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (self : Systems.RosenSystem α) : Set α
declarations.source: states : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem.observables
declarations.doc: F: the family of real-valued observables.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenSystem.observables.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (self : Systems.RosenSystem α) : Set (α → ℝ)
declarations.source: observables : Set (α → ℝ)

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem.defined_on
declarations.doc:
"defined on S": an observable carries no value off S. The walking
arrow, F depends on S, as a Prop.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RosenSystem.defined_on.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (self : Systems.RosenSystem α) (f : α → ℝ) :
  f ∈ self.observables → ∀ x ∉ self.states, f x = 0
declarations.source: defined_on : ∀ f ∈ observables, ∀ x, x ∉ states → f x = 0

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem.indist
declarations.doc:
Rosen's R_F: two states are indistinguishable when every observable
agrees on them (the relation whose quotient is S/R_F, p. 54).
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenSystem.indist.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (V : Systems.RosenSystem α) : Set (α × α)

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem.toKlir
declarations.doc: Rosen's own projection to (T, R): states, and the relation R_F.
declarations.signature: Systems.RosenSystem.toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (V : Systems.RosenSystem α) : Systems.KlirSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Rosen's own projection to (T, R): states, and the relation R_F. -/
def RosenSystem.toKlir {α : Type*} (V : RosenSystem α) : KlirSystem α where
  things := V.states
  relation := V.indist

declarations.name: Systems.RosenSystem.indist_symm
declarations.doc: R_F is symmetric — the fact that bounds what a Rosen view can carry.
declarations.signature:
Systems.RosenSystem.indist_symm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (V : Systems.RosenSystem α) {p : α × α}
  (hp : p ∈ V.indist) : (p.2, p.1) ∈ V.indist
declarations.source:
/-- R_F is symmetric — the fact that bounds what a Rosen view can carry. -/
theorem RosenSystem.indist_symm {α : Type*} (V : RosenSystem α)
    {p : α × α} (hp : p ∈ V.indist) : (p.2, p.1) ∈ V.indist :=
  ⟨hp.2.1, hp.1, fun f hf => (hp.2.2 f hf).symm⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.IsIndist
declarations.doc:
The price of the Rosen view: the dependency is an equivalence
relation on the things.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- The price of the Rosen view: the dependency is an equivalence
    relation on the things. -/
structure Kernel.IsIndist {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) : Prop where
  refl : ∀ a ∈ k.things, (a, a) ∈ k.dep
  symm : ∀ p ∈ k.dep, (p.2, p.1) ∈ k.dep
  trans : ∀ a b c, (a, b) ∈ k.dep → (b, c) ∈ k.dep → (a, c) ∈ k.dep

constructors.name: Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.mk
constructors.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {k : Systems.Kernel α},
  (∀ a ∈ k.things, (a, a) ∈ k.dep) →
    (∀ p ∈ k.dep, (p.2, p.1) ∈ k.dep) →
      (∀ (a b c : α), (a, b) ∈ k.dep → (b, c) ∈ k.dep → (a, c) ∈ k.dep) → k.IsIndist

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.refl
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.refl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {k : Systems.Kernel α} (self : k.IsIndist)
  (a : α) : a ∈ k.things → (a, a) ∈ k.dep
declarations.source: refl : ∀ a ∈ k.things, (a, a) ∈ k.dep

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.symm
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.symm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {k : Systems.Kernel α} (self : k.IsIndist)
  (p : α × α) : p ∈ k.dep → (p.2, p.1) ∈ k.dep
declarations.source: symm : ∀ p ∈ k.dep, (p.2, p.1) ∈ k.dep

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.trans
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.IsIndist.trans.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {k : Systems.Kernel α} (self : k.IsIndist)
  (a b c : α) : (a, b) ∈ k.dep → (b, c) ∈ k.dep → (a, c) ∈ k.dep
declarations.source: trans : ∀ a b c, (a, b) ∈ k.dep → (b, c) ∈ k.dep → (a, c) ∈ k.dep

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.classIndicator
declarations.doc:
The indicator of a thing's dependency class: 1 on the things related
to `a`, 0 elsewhere. The canonical real-valued witness.
declarations.signature: Systems.Kernel.classIndicator.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) (a : α) : α → ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The indicator of a thing's dependency class: 1 on the things related
    to `a`, 0 elsewhere. The canonical real-valued witness. -/
noncomputable def Kernel.classIndicator {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) (a : α) : α → ℝ :=
  fun x => if (x, a) ∈ k.dep then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.classIndicator_eq_one
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.classIndicator_eq_one.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) {a x : α}
  (h : (x, a) ∈ k.dep) : k.classIndicator a x = 1

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.classIndicator_eq_zero
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.classIndicator_eq_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) {a x : α}
  (h : (x, a) ∉ k.dep) : k.classIndicator a x = 0

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toRosen
declarations.doc:
Generate the Rosen view: the things as states, one observable per
dependency class.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toRosen.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) (_h : k.IsIndist) :
  Systems.RosenSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- Generate the Rosen view: the things as states, one observable per
    dependency class. -/
noncomputable def Kernel.toRosen {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) (_h : k.IsIndist) :
    RosenSystem α where
  states := k.things
  observables := {f | ∃ a ∈ k.things, f = k.classIndicator a}
  defined_on := by
    rintro f ⟨a, -, rfl⟩ x hx
    apply k.classIndicator_eq_zero
    intro hxa
    exact hx (k.dep_on _ hxa).1

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toRosen_indist
declarations.doc: R_F of the generated view is exactly the kernel's dependency.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toRosen_indist.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) (h : k.IsIndist) :
  (k.toRosen h).indist = k.dep
declarations.source:
/-- R_F of the generated view is exactly the kernel's dependency. -/
theorem Kernel.toRosen_indist {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) (h : k.IsIndist) :
    (k.toRosen h).indist = k.dep := by
  ext ⟨s, t⟩
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hs, ht, hf⟩
    have h1 := hf (k.classIndicator s) ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
    rw [k.classIndicator_eq_one (h.refl s hs)] at h1
    by_contra hst
    have := k.classIndicator_eq_zero (a := s) (x := t)
      (fun hts => hst (h.symm _ hts))
    simp only at h1 this
    rw [this] at h1
    exact one_ne_zero h1
  · intro hst
    refine ⟨(k.dep_on _ hst).1, (k.dep_on _ hst).2, ?_⟩
    rintro f ⟨a, -, rfl⟩
    by_cases hsa : (s, a) ∈ k.dep
    · have hta : (t, a) ∈ k.dep := h.trans t s a (h.symm _ hst) hsa
      rw [k.classIndicator_eq_one hsa, k.classIndicator_eq_one hta]
    · have hta : (t, a) ∉ k.dep := fun hta => hsa (h.trans s t a hst hta)
      rw [k.classIndicator_eq_zero hsa, k.classIndicator_eq_zero hta]

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toRosen_toKlir
declarations.doc:
Round trip (Rosen): the generated pair projects back, through Rosen's
own S/R_F construction, to the kernel's (T, R).
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toRosen_toKlir.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α) (h : k.IsIndist) :
  (k.toRosen h).toKlir = k.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- Round trip (Rosen): the generated pair projects back, through Rosen's
    own S/R_F construction, to the kernel's (T, R). -/
theorem Kernel.toRosen_toKlir {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α) (h : k.IsIndist) :
    (k.toRosen h).toKlir = k.toKlir :=
  KlirSystem.ext rfl (k.toRosen_indist h)

declarations.name: Systems.Kernel.toRosen_injective
declarations.doc: Faithfulness (Rosen): distinct kernels generate distinct Rosen views.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Kernel.toRosen_injective.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {k₁ k₂ : Systems.Kernel α} {h₁ : k₁.IsIndist}
  {h₂ : k₂.IsIndist} (h : k₁.toRosen h₁ = k₂.toRosen h₂) : k₁ = k₂

declarations.name: Systems.rosen_no_view_of_asymmetric
declarations.doc:
WHAT THE ROSEN VIEW CANNOT CARRY. A kernel in which some thing depends
on another without the converse has NO Rosen view at all: no pair
(S, F) projects, through R_F, to its (T, R). The cost of the view is
not a slot left empty but a relation with no home.
declarations.signature:
Systems.rosen_no_view_of_asymmetric.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (k : Systems.Kernel α)
  (hasym : ∃ p ∈ k.dep, (p.2, p.1) ∉ k.dep) (V : Systems.RosenSystem α) : V.toKlir ≠ k.toKlir
declarations.source:
/-- WHAT THE ROSEN VIEW CANNOT CARRY. A kernel in which some thing depends
    on another without the converse has NO Rosen view at all: no pair
    (S, F) projects, through R_F, to its (T, R). The cost of the view is
    not a slot left empty but a relation with no home. -/
theorem rosen_no_view_of_asymmetric {α : Type*} (k : Kernel α)
    (hasym : ∃ p ∈ k.dep, (p.2, p.1) ∉ k.dep) :
    ∀ V : RosenSystem α, V.toKlir ≠ k.toKlir := by
  intro V hV
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hnp⟩ := hasym
  have hrel : V.indist = k.dep := congrArg KlirSystem.relation hV
  apply hnp
  rw [← hrel] at hp ⊢
  exact V.indist_symm hp

declarations.name: Systems.pairingGraph
declarations.doc:
The triadic factor the peel produces: the graph of pairing — the
connecting term IS the pair of the two coordinates consumed.
Mesarovic p. 16: the connecting term "embodies the entire past
history of the system".
declarations.signature: Systems.pairingGraph.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) : Set (A × B × A × B)

declarations.name: Systems.Set.peel
declarations.doc:
THE PEEL LEMMA (Mesarovic eq. 19, one step, modern form): any relation
on A × B × C is the relative product of the triadic pairing graph and
a remainder relation through the fresh state Z := A × B. Since C may
itself be a product (the whole tail), iterating this step is exactly
part 1 of the p. 14 theorem: (n - 2) triadic factors, unconditionally.
Fully constructive — the witness is the prefix pair itself.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Set.peel.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} {C : Type u_3} (S : Set (A × B × C))
  (p : A × B × C) :
  p ∈ S ↔
    ∃ z, (p.1, p.2.1, z) ∈ Systems.pairingGraph A B ∧ (z, p.2.2) ∈ {q | (q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2) ∈ S}
declarations.source:
/-- THE PEEL LEMMA (Mesarovic eq. 19, one step, modern form): any relation
    on A × B × C is the relative product of the triadic pairing graph and
    a remainder relation through the fresh state Z := A × B. Since C may
    itself be a product (the whole tail), iterating this step is exactly
    part 1 of the p. 14 theorem: (n - 2) triadic factors, unconditionally.
    Fully constructive — the witness is the prefix pair itself. -/
theorem Set.peel {A B C : Type*} (S : Set (A × B × C)) :
    ∀ p : A × B × C, p ∈ S ↔
      ∃ z : A × B, (p.1, p.2.1, z) ∈ pairingGraph A B ∧
        (z, p.2.2) ∈ {q : (A × B) × C | (q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2) ∈ S} := by
  intro p
  constructor
  · intro hp
    exact ⟨(p.1, p.2.1), rfl, hp⟩
  · rintro ⟨z, hz, hS⟩
    rw [pairingGraph] at hz
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hz hS
    rw [hz] at hS
    exact hS

declarations.name: Systems.Set.quaternary_two_triadic
declarations.doc:
One full crank at n = 4: a quaternary relation decomposes into
2 = (4 - 2) triadic relations through the prefix state A × B.
The general count is this construction iterated.
declarations.source:
/-- One full crank at n = 4: a quaternary relation decomposes into
    2 = (4 - 2) triadic relations through the prefix state A × B.
    The general count is this construction iterated. -/
theorem Set.quaternary_two_triadic {A B C D : Type*} (S : Set (A × B × C × D)) :
    ∃ (T₁ : Set (A × B × (A × B))) (T₂ : Set ((A × B) × C × D)),
      ∀ p : A × B × C × D, p ∈ S ↔
        ∃ z : A × B, (p.1, p.2.1, z) ∈ T₁ ∧ (z, p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2) ∈ T₂ := by
  refine ⟨pairingGraph A B, {q | (q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2.1, q.2.2) ∈ S}, fun p => ?_⟩
  constructor
  · intro hp
    exact ⟨(p.1, p.2.1), rfl, hp⟩
  · rintro ⟨z, hz, hS⟩
    rw [pairingGraph] at hz
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hz hS
    rw [hz] at hS
    exact hS

declarations.name: Systems.parityRel
declarations.doc:
Parity: the third coordinate is determined by (and genuinely depends
on) BOTH of the first two.
declarations.signature: Systems.parityRel : Set (Bool × Bool × Bool)

declarations.name: Systems.binaryJoin
declarations.doc:
The join of a ternary relation's three binary shadows: everything the
dyadic projections jointly admit. Reconstruction from dyadic data can
do no better than this.
declarations.signature: Systems.binaryJoin (S : Set (Bool × Bool × Bool)) : Set (Bool × Bool × Bool)

declarations.name: Systems.parityRel_subset_binaryJoin
declarations.doc: Any relation sits inside the join of its own shadows.
declarations.signature: Systems.parityRel_subset_binaryJoin : Systems.parityRel ⊆ Systems.binaryJoin Systems.parityRel
declarations.source:
/-- Any relation sits inside the join of its own shadows. -/
theorem parityRel_subset_binaryJoin : parityRel ⊆ binaryJoin parityRel :=
  fun p hp => ⟨⟨p.2.2, hp⟩, ⟨p.1, hp⟩, ⟨p.2.1, hp⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.binaryJoin_parityRel_ne
declarations.doc:
THE DYADIC FLOOR: the join of parity's binary shadows strictly exceeds
parity — witness (true, true, true), admitted by every shadow but
violating parity (xor true true = false). Binary data cannot pin down
a triadic relation; the third dimension is invisible to dyadic
shadows.
declarations.signature: Systems.binaryJoin_parityRel_ne : Systems.binaryJoin Systems.parityRel ≠ Systems.parityRel
declarations.source:
/-- THE DYADIC FLOOR: the join of parity's binary shadows strictly exceeds
    parity — witness (true, true, true), admitted by every shadow but
    violating parity (xor true true = false). Binary data cannot pin down
    a triadic relation; the third dimension is invisible to dyadic
    shadows. -/
theorem binaryJoin_parityRel_ne : binaryJoin parityRel ≠ parityRel := by
  intro h
  have hmem : ((true, true, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ binaryJoin parityRel := by
    refine ⟨⟨false, rfl⟩, ⟨false, rfl⟩, ⟨false, rfl⟩⟩
  rw [h] at hmem
  exact Bool.noConfusion hmem

declarations.name: Systems.MiddleFactorizable
declarations.doc:
Dyadic factorizability through the MIDDLE coordinate: the two factors
share only Y. This is eq. 18's shape with the medium term drawn from
the existing terms (condition (b)) rather than fresh.
declarations.signature:
Systems.MiddleFactorizable.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3}
  (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Dyadic factorizability through the MIDDLE coordinate: the two factors
    share only Y. This is eq. 18's shape with the medium term drawn from
    the existing terms (condition (b)) rather than fresh. -/
def MiddleFactorizable {X Y W : Type*} (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (R₁ : Set (X × Y)) (R₂ : Set (Y × W)),
    ∀ p : X × Y × W, p ∈ R ↔ (p.1, p.2.1) ∈ R₁ ∧ (p.2.1, p.2.2) ∈ R₂

declarations.name: Systems.LeftFactorizable
declarations.doc: Dyadic factorizability through the FIRST coordinate (pivot = X).
declarations.signature:
Systems.LeftFactorizable.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3}
  (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Dyadic factorizability through the FIRST coordinate (pivot = X). -/
def LeftFactorizable {X Y W : Type*} (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (R₁ : Set (X × Y)) (R₂ : Set (X × W)),
    ∀ p : X × Y × W, p ∈ R ↔ (p.1, p.2.1) ∈ R₁ ∧ (p.1, p.2.2) ∈ R₂

declarations.name: Systems.RightFactorizable
declarations.doc: Dyadic factorizability through the THIRD coordinate (pivot = W).
declarations.signature:
Systems.RightFactorizable.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3}
  (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Dyadic factorizability through the THIRD coordinate (pivot = W). -/
def RightFactorizable {X Y W : Type*} (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (R₁ : Set (X × W)) (R₂ : Set (Y × W)),
    ∀ p : X × Y × W, p ∈ R ↔ (p.1, p.2.2) ∈ R₁ ∧ (p.2.1, p.2.2) ∈ R₂

declarations.name: Systems.middleJoin
declarations.doc:
The join of R's own two shadows through the middle coordinate: the
best any middle-pivot dyadic reconstruction can do.
declarations.signature:
Systems.middleJoin.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3}
  (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Set (X × Y × W)

declarations.name: Systems.middleFactorizable_iff_eq_middleJoin
declarations.doc:
THE CHARACTERIZATION (part 2's iff, modernized — and the closure of
the "any splitting" gap): R is middle-factorizable, by ANY pair of
dyadic relations, iff R equals the join of its own two shadows.
Forward is the mixing argument: witnesses (x, y, w') ∈ R and
(x', y, w) ∈ R yield R₁(x, y) and R₂(y, w), which the factorization
recombines into (x, y, w) ∈ R. Backward: the shadows themselves
factorize. So non-factorizability never depends on which splitting
was tried — exactly what Mesarovic's canonical-splitting proof left
open.
declarations.signature:
Systems.middleFactorizable_iff_eq_middleJoin.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2}
  {W : Type u_3} (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : Systems.MiddleFactorizable R ↔ R = Systems.middleJoin R
declarations.source:
/-- THE CHARACTERIZATION (part 2's iff, modernized — and the closure of
    the "any splitting" gap): R is middle-factorizable, by ANY pair of
    dyadic relations, iff R equals the join of its own two shadows.
    Forward is the mixing argument: witnesses (x, y, w') ∈ R and
    (x', y, w) ∈ R yield R₁(x, y) and R₂(y, w), which the factorization
    recombines into (x, y, w) ∈ R. Backward: the shadows themselves
    factorize. So non-factorizability never depends on which splitting
    was tried — exactly what Mesarovic's canonical-splitting proof left
    open. -/
theorem middleFactorizable_iff_eq_middleJoin {X Y W : Type*}
    (R : Set (X × Y × W)) : MiddleFactorizable R ↔ R = middleJoin R := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨R₁, R₂, h⟩
    ext p
    constructor
    · intro hp
      exact ⟨⟨p.2.2, hp⟩, ⟨p.1, hp⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨⟨w', hw⟩, ⟨x', hx⟩⟩
      exact (h p).mpr ⟨((h _).mp hw).1, ((h _).mp hx).2⟩
  · intro heq
    refine ⟨{q | ∃ w', (q.1, q.2, w') ∈ R}, {q | ∃ x', (x', q.1, q.2) ∈ R},
      fun p => ⟨fun hp => ⟨⟨p.2.2, hp⟩, ⟨p.1, hp⟩⟩, ?_⟩⟩
    rintro ⟨⟨w', hw⟩, ⟨x', hx⟩⟩
    rw [heq]
    exact ⟨⟨w', hw⟩, ⟨x', hx⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.parityRel_not_middleFactorizable
declarations.doc:
Parity refuses middle-pivot factorization: (t,t,f) and (f,t,t) are in
parity, so any factorization admits (t,t) into both factors — but
(t,t,t) violates parity.
declarations.signature: Systems.parityRel_not_middleFactorizable : ¬Systems.MiddleFactorizable Systems.parityRel
declarations.source:
/-- Parity refuses middle-pivot factorization: (t,t,f) and (f,t,t) are in
    parity, so any factorization admits (t,t) into both factors — but
    (t,t,t) violates parity. -/
theorem parityRel_not_middleFactorizable : ¬ MiddleFactorizable parityRel := by
  rintro ⟨R₁, R₂, h⟩
  have h₁ : ((true, true, false) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel := rfl
  have h₂ : ((false, true, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel := rfl
  have : ((true, true, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel :=
    (h _).mpr ⟨((h _).mp h₁).1, ((h _).mp h₂).2⟩
  exact Bool.noConfusion this

declarations.name: Systems.parityRel_not_leftFactorizable
declarations.doc: Parity refuses left-pivot factorization (same witness class).
declarations.signature: Systems.parityRel_not_leftFactorizable : ¬Systems.LeftFactorizable Systems.parityRel
declarations.source:
/-- Parity refuses left-pivot factorization (same witness class). -/
theorem parityRel_not_leftFactorizable : ¬ LeftFactorizable parityRel := by
  rintro ⟨R₁, R₂, h⟩
  have h₁ : ((true, true, false) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel := rfl
  have h₂ : ((true, false, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel := rfl
  have : ((true, true, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel :=
    (h _).mpr ⟨((h _).mp h₁).1, ((h _).mp h₂).2⟩
  exact Bool.noConfusion this

declarations.name: Systems.parityRel_not_rightFactorizable
declarations.doc:
Parity refuses right-pivot factorization (same witness class). With
the middle and left cases: NO pivot admits a dyadic factorization of
parity — the full necessity face of the p. 14 theorem at n = 3.
declarations.signature: Systems.parityRel_not_rightFactorizable : ¬Systems.RightFactorizable Systems.parityRel
declarations.source:
/-- Parity refuses right-pivot factorization (same witness class). With
    the middle and left cases: NO pivot admits a dyadic factorization of
    parity — the full necessity face of the p. 14 theorem at n = 3. -/
theorem parityRel_not_rightFactorizable : ¬ RightFactorizable parityRel := by
  rintro ⟨R₁, R₂, h⟩
  have h₁ : ((true, false, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel := rfl
  have h₂ : ((false, true, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel := rfl
  have : ((true, true, true) : Bool × Bool × Bool) ∈ parityRel :=
    (h _).mpr ⟨((h _).mp h₁).1, ((h _).mp h₂).2⟩
  exact Bool.noConfusion this

declarations.name: Systems.MobusBoundary
declarations.doc:
The boundary of a Mobus system: properties and interfaces.
Mobus Eq. 4.6: B_{i,l} = ⟨P_{i,l}, I_{i,l}⟩

- P: boundary properties (parametric — Mobus defers their exact form)
- I: interface components that mediate flows across the boundary

Parametrized by:
- α: node type (interfaces are components, sharing the type)
- π: boundary property type (domain-supplied, opaque)
declarations.signature: Systems.MobusBoundary.{u_1, u_2} (α : Type u_1) (π : Type u_2) : Type (max u_1 u_2)
declarations.source:
/-- The boundary of a Mobus system: properties and interfaces.
    Mobus Eq. 4.6: B_{i,l} = ⟨P_{i,l}, I_{i,l}⟩

    - P: boundary properties (parametric — Mobus defers their exact form)
    - I: interface components that mediate flows across the boundary

    Parametrized by:
    - α: node type (interfaces are components, sharing the type)
    - π: boundary property type (domain-supplied, opaque) -/
structure MobusBoundary (α : Type*) (π : Type*) where
  /-- Boundary properties.
      Mobus: "The exact form of P is still an object of research." -/
  properties : π
  /-- Interface components: the subset of components that transport
      flows across the boundary. Every external flow edge has its
      component-side endpoint in this set. -/
  interfaces : Set α

constructors.name: Systems.MobusBoundary.mk
constructors.type: {α : Type u_1} → {π : Type u_2} → π → Set α → Systems.MobusBoundary α π

declarations.name: Systems.MobusBoundary.properties
declarations.doc:
Boundary properties.
Mobus: "The exact form of P is still an object of research."
declarations.signature:
Systems.MobusBoundary.properties.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {π : Type u_2}
  (self : Systems.MobusBoundary α π) : π
declarations.source: properties : π

declarations.name: Systems.MobusBoundary.interfaces
declarations.doc:
Interface components: the subset of components that transport
flows across the boundary. Every external flow edge has its
component-side endpoint in this set.
declarations.signature:
Systems.MobusBoundary.interfaces.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {π : Type u_2}
  (self : Systems.MobusBoundary α π) : Set α
declarations.source: interfaces : Set α

declarations.name: Systems.BoundaryComplete
declarations.doc:
Boundary completeness: every external flow edge passes through an
interface. If an edge endpoint is not an environmental object, it
must be an interface component.

This is the formal statement of the boundary principle: non-interface
components are "shielded" from the environment by the boundary.
declarations.source:
/-- Boundary completeness: every external flow edge passes through an
    interface. If an edge endpoint is not an environmental object, it
    must be an interface component.

    This is the formal statement of the boundary principle: non-interface
    components are "shielded" from the environment by the boundary. -/
def BoundaryComplete {α : Type*} {κ : Type*} {π : Type*}
    (boundary : MobusBoundary α π)
    (externalFlows : FlowNetwork α κ)
    (envObjects : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ externalFlows.edges,
    (e.source ∉ envObjects → e.source ∈ boundary.interfaces) ∧
    (e.target ∉ envObjects → e.target ∈ boundary.interfaces)

declarations.name: Systems.boundary_complete_endpoints
declarations.doc:
SHOWCASE THEOREM #3: If the boundary is complete, then every external
flow edge has both endpoints in the union of interfaces and environment
objects. No flow reaches a non-interface component directly.

This is what systems theorists mean by "the boundary mediates all
interaction with the environment."
declarations.signature:
Systems.boundary_complete_endpoints.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {π : Type u_3}
  (boundary : Systems.MobusBoundary α π) (flows : Systems.FlowNetwork α κ) (envObjects : Set α)
  (hbc : Systems.BoundaryComplete boundary flows envObjects) (e : Systems.FlowEdge α κ) :
  e ∈ flows.edges →
    e.source ∈ boundary.interfaces ∪ envObjects ∧ e.target ∈ boundary.interfaces ∪ envObjects
declarations.source:
/-- SHOWCASE THEOREM #3: If the boundary is complete, then every external
    flow edge has both endpoints in the union of interfaces and environment
    objects. No flow reaches a non-interface component directly.

    This is what systems theorists mean by "the boundary mediates all
    interaction with the environment." -/
theorem boundary_complete_endpoints {α : Type*} {κ : Type*} {π : Type*}
    (boundary : MobusBoundary α π)
    (flows : FlowNetwork α κ)
    (envObjects : Set α)
    (hbc : BoundaryComplete boundary flows envObjects) :
    ∀ e ∈ flows.edges,
      e.source ∈ boundary.interfaces ∪ envObjects ∧
      e.target ∈ boundary.interfaces ∪ envObjects := by
  intro e he
  have ⟨hs, ht⟩ := hbc e he
  constructor
  · by_cases h : e.source ∈ envObjects
    · exact Set.mem_union_right _ h
    · exact Set.mem_union_left _ (hs h)
  · by_cases h : e.target ∈ envObjects
    · exact Set.mem_union_right _ h
    · exact Set.mem_union_left _ (ht h)

declarations.name: Systems.non_interface_shielded
declarations.doc:
Contrapositive of boundary completeness: a component that is neither
an interface nor an environmental object does not appear as an
endpoint in any external flow edge.

This is the "shielding" property — internal (non-interface) components
are invisible to the environment.
declarations.signature:
Systems.non_interface_shielded.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {π : Type u_3}
  (boundary : Systems.MobusBoundary α π) (flows : Systems.FlowNetwork α κ) (envObjects : Set α)
  (hbc : Systems.BoundaryComplete boundary flows envObjects) (a : α) (hni : a ∉ boundary.interfaces)
  (hne : a ∉ envObjects) (e : Systems.FlowEdge α κ) : e ∈ flows.edges → e.source ≠ a ∧ e.target ≠ a
declarations.source:
/-- Contrapositive of boundary completeness: a component that is neither
    an interface nor an environmental object does not appear as an
    endpoint in any external flow edge.

    This is the "shielding" property — internal (non-interface) components
    are invisible to the environment. -/
theorem non_interface_shielded {α : Type*} {κ : Type*} {π : Type*}
    (boundary : MobusBoundary α π)
    (flows : FlowNetwork α κ)
    (envObjects : Set α)
    (hbc : BoundaryComplete boundary flows envObjects)
    (a : α) (hni : a ∉ boundary.interfaces) (hne : a ∉ envObjects) :
    ∀ e ∈ flows.edges, e.source ≠ a ∧ e.target ≠ a := by
  intro e he
  have ⟨hs, ht⟩ := hbc e he
  constructor
  · intro ha
    have : e.source ∉ envObjects := by rw [ha]; exact hne
    have := hs this
    rw [ha] at this
    exact absurd this hni
  · intro ha
    have : e.target ∉ envObjects := by rw [ha]; exact hne
    have := ht this
    rw [ha] at this
    exact absurd this hni

declarations.name: Systems.FlowInducesAction
declarations.doc:
Flow edges induce action: if there is a flow from a to b in the
internal network, then a acts on b in Bunge's sense.

This connects Mobus's graph-theoretic representation (flow edges)
to Bunge's relation-theoretic one (ActsOn). The consistency
assumption is necessary because ActsOn is abstract (Prop-valued)
while FlowNetwork is concrete (edge-set-valued).
declarations.signature:
Systems.FlowInducesAction.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (net : Systems.FlowNetwork α κ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Flow edges induce action: if there is a flow from a to b in the
    internal network, then a acts on b in Bunge's sense.

    This connects Mobus's graph-theoretic representation (flow edges)
    to Bunge's relation-theoretic one (ActsOn). The consistency
    assumption is necessary because ActsOn is abstract (Prop-valued)
    while FlowNetwork is concrete (edge-set-valued). -/
def FlowInducesAction {α : Type*} {κ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (net : FlowNetwork α κ) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ net.edges, e.source ▷ e.target

declarations.name: Systems.MobusSystem.toBunge
declarations.doc:
SHOWCASE THEOREM #1: Every well-formed Mobus 8-tuple induces a
Bunge CES triple.

The map:
  composition  := components           (exact)
  environment  := environment.objects   (milieu discarded)
  structure'   := totalRelation         (capacity discarded)

Requires:
- [ActsOn α]: Bunge's action relation in scope
- FlowInducesAction: flow edges → action (connects the two frameworks)
- At least one internal edge (for Bunge's bondage_nonempty)

Information projected away (no Bunge counterpart):
  milieu M, boundary properties π, transforms τ,
  history η, time scale δ, capacity labels κ
declarations.signature:
Systems.MobusSystem.toBunge.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  {μ : Type u_3} {π : Type u_4} {τ : Type u_5} {η : Type u_6} {δ : Type u_7} [Systems.ActsOn α]
  (sys : Systems.MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hflow : Systems.FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
  (hedge : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) : Systems.ConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- SHOWCASE THEOREM #1: Every well-formed Mobus 8-tuple induces a
    Bunge CES triple.

    The map:
      composition  := components           (exact)
      environment  := environment.objects   (milieu discarded)
      structure'   := totalRelation         (capacity discarded)

    Requires:
    - [ActsOn α]: Bunge's action relation in scope
    - FlowInducesAction: flow edges → action (connects the two frameworks)
    - At least one internal edge (for Bunge's bondage_nonempty)

    Information projected away (no Bunge counterpart):
      milieu M, boundary properties π, transforms τ,
      history η, time scale δ, capacity labels κ -/
def MobusSystem.toBunge {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ)
    (hflow : FlowInducesAction sys.internalNetwork)
    (hedge : sys.internalNetwork.edges.Nonempty) :
    ConcreteSystem α where
  composition := sys.components
  environment := sys.environment.objects
  structure' := sys.totalRelation
  disjoint := sys.disjoint
  structure_on := sys.totalRelation_on
  bondage_nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hedge
    have hon := sys.internalNetwork.edges_on e he
    rw [sys.network_components] at hon
    exact ⟨e.source, hon.1, e.target, hon.2,
           sys.internalNetwork.no_self_loops e he,
           Or.inl (hflow e he)⟩

declarations.name: Systems.MobusSystem.toBunge_composition
declarations.doc: The bridge maps components to composition exactly.
declarations.source:
/-- The bridge maps components to composition exactly. -/
theorem MobusSystem.toBunge_composition {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hf hg) :
    (sys.toBunge hf hg).composition = sys.components :=
  rfl

theorem MobusSystem.toBunge_environment {α κ μ π τ η δ : Type*} [ActsOn α]
    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hf hg) :
    (sys.toBunge hf hg).environment = sys.environment.objects :=

declarations.name: Systems.MobusSystem.toBunge_structure
declarations.doc: The bridge maps totalRelation to structure (capacity lost).
declarations.source:

    (sys : MobusSystem α κ μ π τ η δ) (hf hg) :
    (sys.toBunge hf hg).structure' = sys.totalRelation :=
