declarations.name: Systems.sep_hierarchy_networks
declarations.doc:
**#2 ⇏ #3** (`sep_hierarchy_networks`). A one-thing world with the reflexive ancestry
admits no flow network with an edge, for any capacity type: `no_self_loops` needs two
distinct nodes. The witness is a cardinality one and, like `sep_hierarchy_systemness_unit`,
dies if #2 is required to be acyclic; under that requirement #2 ⇒ #3 by
`ImmediateAncestor.toFlowNetwork`.

`#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_hierarchy_networks :
  (∃ x y, Systems.immediateAncestor x y) ∧
    ∀ (κ : Type) (net : Systems.FlowNetwork Unit κ), net.edges = ∅
declarations.source:
/-- **#2 ⇏ #3** (`sep_hierarchy_networks`). A one-thing world with the reflexive ancestry
    admits no flow network with an edge, for any capacity type: `no_self_loops` needs two
    distinct nodes. The witness is a cardinality one and, like `sep_hierarchy_systemness_unit`,
    dies if #2 is required to be acyclic; under that requirement #2 ⇒ #3 by
    `ImmediateAncestor.toFlowNetwork`.

    `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_hierarchy_networks :
    (∃ x y : Unit, @ImmediateAncestor.immediateAncestor Unit ⟨fun _ _ => True⟩ x y) ∧
      (∀ (κ : Type) (net : FlowNetwork Unit κ), net.edges = ∅) := by
  refine ⟨⟨(), (), trivial⟩, fun κ net => Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr fun e he => ?_⟩
  exact net.no_self_loops e he (Subsingleton.elim _ _)

declarations.name: Systems.ImmediateAncestor.toFlowNetwork
declarations.doc:
The derivation that survives acyclicity: an ancestry relation with an off-diagonal pair
is a flow network on the whole carrier (edges = off-diagonal ancestry pairs, constant
capacity `c`).
declarations.signature:
Systems.ImmediateAncestor.toFlowNetwork.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  (inst : Systems.ImmediateAncestor α) (c : κ) : Systems.FlowNetwork α κ
declarations.source:
/-- The derivation that survives acyclicity: an ancestry relation with an off-diagonal pair
    is a flow network on the whole carrier (edges = off-diagonal ancestry pairs, constant
    capacity `c`). -/
def ImmediateAncestor.toFlowNetwork {α κ : Type*} (inst : ImmediateAncestor α) (c : κ) :
    FlowNetwork α κ where
  nodes := Set.univ
  edges := {e | inst.immediateAncestor e.source e.target ∧ e.source ≠ e.target ∧
    e.capacity = c}
  edges_on := fun _ _ => ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
  no_self_loops := fun _ he => he.2.1

declarations.name: Systems.oneFlow
declarations.doc: A single flow `false → true` on `Bool`, unit capacity.
declarations.signature: Systems.oneFlow : Systems.FlowNetwork Bool Unit
declarations.source:
/-- A single flow `false → true` on `Bool`, unit capacity. -/
def oneFlow : FlowNetwork Bool Unit where
  nodes := Set.univ
  edges := {⟨false, true, ()⟩}
  edges_on := fun _ _ => ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
  no_self_loops := fun e he => by
    rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at he
    subst he
    exact Bool.false_ne_true

declarations.name: Systems.sep_networks_systemness
declarations.doc:
**#3 ⇏ #1** (`sep_networks_systemness`). A network with a flow, under the empty action
relation, is not a system. This separation exists only because `FlowNetwork` never
mentions `ActsOn`: the two vocabularies are disconnected, and one can be filled while the
other is left empty. Read with the action relation the network itself induces, the
separation fails — see `FlowNetwork.toConcreteSystem`.

`#print axioms`: propext.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_networks_systemness :
  Systems.oneFlow.edges.Nonempty ∧ ∀ (a : Systems.ConcreteSystem Bool), False
declarations.source:
/-- **#3 ⇏ #1** (`sep_networks_systemness`). A network with a flow, under the empty action
    relation, is not a system. This separation exists only because `FlowNetwork` never
    mentions `ActsOn`: the two vocabularies are disconnected, and one can be filled while the
    other is left empty. Read with the action relation the network itself induces, the
    separation fails — see `FlowNetwork.toConcreteSystem`.

    `#print axioms`: propext. -/
theorem sep_networks_systemness :
    oneFlow.edges.Nonempty ∧ (@ConcreteSystem Bool (noAction Bool) → False) := by
  refine ⟨⟨⟨false, true, ()⟩, rfl⟩, fun σ => ?_⟩
  letI := noAction Bool
  obtain ⟨_, -, _, -, -, hbond⟩ := σ.bondage_nonempty
  exact hbond.elim (fun h => h) (fun h => h)

declarations.name: Systems.FlowNetwork.toConcreteSystem
declarations.doc:
NOT SEPARABLE under the induced action (#3 ⇒ #1): a flow network with at least one edge
is a concrete system under the action relation it induces — composition = nodes,
environment empty, structure = the underlying relation, and `no_self_loops` is exactly
the `a ≠ b` that `bondage_nonempty` needs. A FINDING: the flow network's only content
beyond CES is the capacity label; as a directed graph it and #1's bondage are the same
datum read in two directions (`ConcreteSystem.toFlowNetwork` is the other).
declarations.signature:
Systems.FlowNetwork.toConcreteSystem.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2}
  (net : Systems.FlowNetwork α κ) (h : net.edges.Nonempty) : Systems.ConcreteSystem α
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE under the induced action (#3 ⇒ #1): a flow network with at least one edge
    is a concrete system under the action relation it induces — composition = nodes,
    environment empty, structure = the underlying relation, and `no_self_loops` is exactly
    the `a ≠ b` that `bondage_nonempty` needs. A FINDING: the flow network's only content
    beyond CES is the capacity label; as a directed graph it and #1's bondage are the same
    datum read in two directions (`ConcreteSystem.toFlowNetwork` is the other). -/
def FlowNetwork.toConcreteSystem {α κ : Type*} (net : FlowNetwork α κ)
    (h : net.edges.Nonempty) : @ConcreteSystem α net.toActsOn := by
  letI := net.toActsOn
  exact
    { composition := net.nodes
      environment := ∅
      structure' := net.toRelation
      disjoint := by simp
      structure_on := fun p hp => by
        have := net.toRelation_on p hp
        simpa using this
      bondage_nonempty := by
        obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := h
        exact ⟨e.source, (net.edges_on e he).1, e.target, (net.edges_on e he).2,
          net.no_self_loops e he, Or.inl ⟨e, he, rfl⟩⟩ }

declarations.name: Systems.Moving
declarations.doc:
#4, tied and non-degenerate: some state moves. (`DynamicSystem` itself is always
inhabited for any law — `DynamicSystem.ofLaw` below — so this is the whole content.)
declarations.signature: Systems.Moving.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #4, tied and non-degenerate: some state moves. (`DynamicSystem` itself is always
    inhabited for any law — `DynamicSystem.ofLaw` below — so this is the whole content.) -/
def Moving {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop := ∃ s, f s ≠ s

declarations.name: Systems.EvolvesBy
declarations.doc:
#6, tied and non-degenerate: `f` is the step of an `Evolution` for some fitness preorder
on `S`, and climbs strictly somewhere.
declarations.signature: Systems.EvolvesBy.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #6, tied and non-degenerate: `f` is the step of an `Evolution` for some fitness preorder
    on `S`, and climbs strictly somewhere. -/
def EvolvesBy {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (inst : Preorder S) (e : @Evolution S inst), @Evolution.step S inst e = f ∧
    ∃ s, @LT.lt S (@Preorder.toLT S inst) s (f s)

declarations.name: Systems.Governs
declarations.doc:
#8, tied and non-degenerate: `f` is the feedback law of a homeostat that is neutral at
its set point (the two hypotheses of `Homeostat.target_is_equilibrium`) and effective
(some off-target state is corrected onto target in one tick).
declarations.signature: Systems.Governs.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #8, tied and non-degenerate: `f` is the feedback law of a homeostat that is neutral at
    its set point (the two hypotheses of `Homeostat.target_is_equilibrium`) and effective
    (some off-target state is corrected onto target in one tick). -/
def Governs {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (O : Type) (h : Homeostat S O), h.feedbackLaw = f ∧
    (∀ o, h.error o o = h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint) ∧
    (∀ s', h.correct (h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint) s' = s') ∧
    ∃ s, ¬ h.atTarget s ∧ h.atTarget (f s)

declarations.name: Systems.Understood
declarations.doc:
#11, tied: some understanding has `f` as its system dynamics. (`Understanding` carries
its own non-degeneracy: `compresses` and `nontrivial`.)
declarations.signature: Systems.Understood.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #11, tied: some understanding has `f` as its system dynamics. (`Understanding` carries
    its own non-degeneracy: `compresses` and `nontrivial`.) -/
def Understood {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Type) (u : Understanding S M), u.systemDyn = f

declarations.name: Systems.Improved
declarations.doc: #12 (bare), tied: some `Improvement` has `f` as its native dynamics.
declarations.signature: Systems.Improved.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #12 (bare), tied: some `Improvement` has `f` as its native dynamics. -/
def Improved {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop := ∃ imp : Improvement S, imp.dyn = f

declarations.name: Systems.Directed
declarations.doc: #12 (full), tied: some `DirectedAgent` acts on a system whose dynamics is `f`.
declarations.signature: Systems.Directed.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop

declarations.name: Systems.allAction
declarations.doc: Stock component side, so `DynamicSystem` can be instantiated inside the state block.
declarations.signature: Systems.allAction.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) : Systems.ActsOn α
declarations.source:
/-- Stock component side, so `DynamicSystem` can be instantiated inside the state block. -/
def allAction (α : Type*) : ActsOn α := ⟨fun _ _ => True⟩

declarations.name: Systems.stockSystem
declarations.signature: Systems.stockSystem : Systems.ConcreteSystem Bool
declarations.source:
def stockSystem : @ConcreteSystem Bool (allAction Bool) := by
  letI := allAction Bool
  exact
    { composition := Set.univ
      environment := ∅
      structure' := ∅
      disjoint := by simp
      structure_on := fun _ h => h.elim
      bondage_nonempty := ⟨false, trivial, true, trivial, Bool.false_ne_true, Or.inl trivial⟩ }

declarations.name: Systems.DynamicSystem.ofLaw
declarations.doc: VACUITY (#4): every law on every state type is the law of a `DynamicSystem`.
declarations.signature: Systems.DynamicSystem.ofLaw.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Systems.DynamicSystem Bool S
declarations.source:
/-- VACUITY (#4): every law on every state type is the law of a `DynamicSystem`. -/
def DynamicSystem.ofLaw {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : @DynamicSystem Bool (allAction Bool) S := by
  letI := allAction Bool
  exact ⟨stockSystem, f⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Evolution.trivial
declarations.doc:
VACUITY (#6): the identity is an `Evolution` for every preorder (nothing gets less fit
because nothing changes).
declarations.signature: Systems.Evolution.trivial.{u_1} (S : Type u_1) [Preorder S] : Systems.Evolution S
declarations.source:
/-- VACUITY (#6): the identity is an `Evolution` for every preorder (nothing gets less fit
    because nothing changes). -/
def Evolution.trivial (S : Type*) [Preorder S] : Evolution S := ⟨id, fun _ => le_refl _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.evolvable_iff_exists_lt'
declarations.doc:
VACUITY (#6, sharper): `Evolvable S` is a property of the fitness preorder alone. It holds
iff the order has a strict pair, whatever the dynamics: the step "jump `s` to `t`, fix
everything else" is an Evolution. So the `Evolvable (Fin 3)` half of
`evolvable_but_not_improvable` is the statement `0 < 1` in `Fin 3`; `fin3climb` plays no
role in it. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.evolvable_iff_exists_lt'.{u_1} (S : Type u_1) [Preorder S] :
  Systems.Evolvable S ↔ ∃ s t, s < t
declarations.source:
/-- VACUITY (#6, sharper): `Evolvable S` is a property of the fitness preorder alone. It holds
    iff the order has a strict pair, whatever the dynamics: the step "jump `s` to `t`, fix
    everything else" is an Evolution. So the `Evolvable (Fin 3)` half of
    `evolvable_but_not_improvable` is the statement `0 < 1` in `Fin 3`; `fin3climb` plays no
    role in it. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem evolvable_iff_exists_lt' (S : Type*) [Preorder S] : Evolvable S ↔ ∃ s t : S, s < t := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨e, s, hs⟩
    exact ⟨s, e.step s, hs⟩
  · rintro ⟨s, t, hst⟩
    classical
    refine ⟨⟨fun u => if u = s then t else u, fun u => ?_⟩, s, ?_⟩
    · by_cases hu : u = s
      · subst hu; simp [le_of_lt hst]
      · simp [hu]
    · simpa using hst

declarations.name: Systems.Homeostat.ofLawAt
declarations.doc:
VACUITY (#8): every law is the feedback law of a homeostat — sensor the identity, set point
ignored, correction the law. The set point is data the feedback law need not read. The
neutrality and effectiveness conditions in `Governs` are what make #8 non-degenerate.
declarations.signature: Systems.Homeostat.ofLawAt.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (s₀ : S) (f : S → S) : Systems.Homeostat S S
declarations.source:
/-- VACUITY (#8): every law is the feedback law of a homeostat — sensor the identity, set point
    ignored, correction the law. The set point is data the feedback law need not read. The
    neutrality and effectiveness conditions in `Governs` are what make #8 non-degenerate. -/
def Homeostat.ofLawAt {S : Type*} (s₀ : S) (f : S → S) : Homeostat S S :=
  ⟨s₀, id, fun o _ => o, fun o _ => f o⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Homeostat.ofLawAt_feedbackLaw
declarations.signature:
Systems.Homeostat.ofLawAt_feedbackLaw.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (s₀ : S) (f : S → S) :
  (Systems.Homeostat.ofLawAt s₀ f).feedbackLaw = f
declarations.source:
theorem Homeostat.ofLawAt_feedbackLaw {S : Type*} (s₀ : S) (f : S → S) :
    (Homeostat.ofLawAt s₀ f).feedbackLaw = f := rfl

declarations.name: Systems.improved_iff_moving
declarations.doc:
VACUITY (#12, bare): a law admits an `Improvement` iff some state moves. The `intervene`
field is unconstrained, so "drive straight to the goal" always works; `improves` and
`genuine` then say only that the goal was not already at rest. Bare #12 coincides with
non-degenerate #4. `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature: Systems.improved_iff_moving.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Systems.Improved f ↔ Systems.Moving f
declarations.source:
/-- VACUITY (#12, bare): a law admits an `Improvement` iff some state moves. The `intervene`
    field is unconstrained, so "drive straight to the goal" always works; `improves` and
    `genuine` then say only that the goal was not already at rest. Bare #12 coincides with
    non-degenerate #4. `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem improved_iff_moving {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Improved f ↔ Moving f := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨imp, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨imp.goal, imp.genuine⟩
  · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
    exact ⟨⟨f, s, fun _ => Function.const S s, rfl, hs⟩, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Nonperiodic
declarations.doc: Non-periodic point: `s` never returns to itself.
declarations.signature: Systems.Nonperiodic.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) (s : S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Non-periodic point: `s` never returns to itself. -/
def Nonperiodic {S : Type*} (f : S → S) (s : S) : Prop := ∀ n, f^[n + 1] s ≠ s

declarations.name: Systems.reachPreorder
declarations.doc: The reachability preorder of a law: `t ≤ u` iff `u` is reached from `t`.
declarations.signature: Systems.reachPreorder.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Preorder S
declarations.source:
/-- The reachability preorder of a law: `t ≤ u` iff `u` is reached from `t`. -/
def reachPreorder {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Preorder S where
  le t u := ∃ n, f^[n] t = u
  le_refl _ := ⟨0, rfl⟩
  le_trans _ _ _ := fun ⟨m, hm⟩ ⟨n, hn⟩ => ⟨n + m, by rw [Function.iterate_add_apply, hm, hn]⟩

declarations.name: Systems.evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic
declarations.doc:
A law is a non-degenerate blind evolution for some fitness order iff it has a
non-periodic point. (⇒) A strict climb `s < f s` forbids returning, since every iterate is
at least as fit. (⇐) Reachability is a fitness order under which `f` climbs.
`#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) :
  Systems.EvolvesBy f ↔ ∃ s, Systems.Nonperiodic f s
declarations.source:
/-- A law is a non-degenerate blind evolution for some fitness order iff it has a
    non-periodic point. (⇒) A strict climb `s < f s` forbids returning, since every iterate is
    at least as fit. (⇐) Reachability is a fitness order under which `f` climbs.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic {S : Type*} (f : S → S) :
    EvolvesBy f ↔ ∃ s, Nonperiodic f s := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨inst, e, rfl, s, hs⟩
    refine ⟨s, fun n hn => ?_⟩
    have h1 : e.step s ≤ e.step^[n] (e.step s) := e.adapts n (e.step s)
    rw [← Function.iterate_succ_apply, hn] at h1
    exact (lt_iff_le_not_ge.mp hs).2 h1
  · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
    letI := reachPreorder f
    refine ⟨reachPreorder f, ⟨f, fun t => ⟨1, rfl⟩⟩, rfl, s, ?_⟩
    refine ⟨⟨1, rfl⟩, fun ⟨n, hn⟩ => hs n ?_⟩
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    exact hn

declarations.name: Systems.Governs.exists_fixed
declarations.doc:
A governing law has a fixed point reached in one tick from a non-fixed state.
`#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Governs.exists_fixed.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.Governs f) :
  ∃ s p, s ≠ p ∧ f s = p ∧ f p = p
declarations.source:
/-- A governing law has a fixed point reached in one tick from a non-fixed state.
    `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem Governs.exists_fixed {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Governs f) :
    ∃ s p, s ≠ p ∧ f s = p ∧ f p = p := by
  obtain ⟨O, h, hlaw, hz, hn, s, hs, hfs⟩ := h
  have hp : f (f s) = f s := by
    have := h.target_is_equilibrium (f s) hfs hz hn
    rwa [hlaw] at this
  exact ⟨s, f s, fun heq => hs (by rw [heq]; exact hfs), rfl, hp⟩

declarations.name: Systems.governs_of_fixed
declarations.doc:
Conversely, a law with a fixed point `p` reached in one tick from some `s ≠ p` governs:
observe "am I at `p`", correct by `f` when not. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.governs_of_fixed.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} {s p : S} (hsp : s ≠ p) (hs : f s = p)
  (hp : f p = p) : Systems.Governs f
declarations.source:
/-- Conversely, a law with a fixed point `p` reached in one tick from some `s ≠ p` governs:
    observe "am I at `p`", correct by `f` when not. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem governs_of_fixed {S : Type*} {f : S → S} {s p : S} (hsp : s ≠ p) (hs : f s = p)
    (hp : f p = p) : Governs f := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Bool, ⟨true, fun t => decide (t = p), fun o o' => decide (o = o'),
    fun b t => if b then t else f t⟩, ?_, ?_, ?_, s, ?_, ?_⟩
  · funext t
    by_cases ht : t = p
    · subst ht; simp [Homeostat.feedbackLaw, hp]
    · simp [Homeostat.feedbackLaw, ht]
  · intro o; simp
  · intro t; simp
  · simp [Homeostat.atTarget, hsp]
  · simp [Homeostat.atTarget, hs]

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.ofMissingPoint
declarations.doc:
A point outside the range of `f`, plus two other distinct points, gives an understanding
of `f` with the two-state model "am I at the unreachable point?" whose model dynamics is
the constant `false`. This is a legitimate `Understanding` per the encoding and it
predicts nothing that changes — the md proposes a non-degeneracy condition (non-constant
`modelDyn`) that would exclude it.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Understanding.ofMissingPoint.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) (c : S)
  (hc : ∀ (s : S), f s ≠ c) (a b : S) (ha : a ≠ c) (hb : b ≠ c) (hab : a ≠ b) :
  Systems.Understanding S Bool
declarations.source:
/-- A point outside the range of `f`, plus two other distinct points, gives an understanding
    of `f` with the two-state model "am I at the unreachable point?" whose model dynamics is
    the constant `false`. This is a legitimate `Understanding` per the encoding and it
    predicts nothing that changes — the md proposes a non-degeneracy condition (non-constant
    `modelDyn`) that would exclude it. -/
noncomputable def Understanding.ofMissingPoint {S : Type*} (f : S → S) (c : S) (hc : ∀ s, f s ≠ c)
    (a b : S) (ha : a ≠ c) (hb : b ≠ c) (hab : a ≠ b) : Understanding S Bool :=
  { abstract := fun s => @decide (s = c) (Classical.propDecidable _)
    systemDyn := f
    modelDyn := fun _ => false
    abstracts := fun s => by simp [hc s]
    surjective := fun m => by
      cases m
      · exact ⟨a, by simp [ha]⟩
      · exact ⟨c, by simp⟩
    compresses := fun hinj => hab (hinj (by simp [ha, hb]))
    nontrivial := inferInstance }

declarations.name: Systems.understood_of_not_surjective
declarations.doc:
On a finite carrier with at least three states, every law that is not surjective is
understood. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.understood_of_not_surjective.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
  (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (hf : ¬Function.Surjective f) : Systems.Understood f
declarations.source:
/-- On a finite carrier with at least three states, every law that is not surjective is
    understood. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem understood_of_not_surjective {S : Type*} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
    (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (hf : ¬ Function.Surjective f) : Understood f := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, ∀ s, f s ≠ c := by
    by_contra hcon
    push_neg at hcon
    exact hf fun c => hcon c
  obtain ⟨x, y, z, hxy, hxz, hyz⟩ := Fintype.two_lt_card_iff.mp h3
  by_cases hx : x = c
  · subst hx
    exact ⟨Bool, Understanding.ofMissingPoint f x hc y z (Ne.symm hxy) (Ne.symm hxz) hyz, rfl⟩
  · by_cases hy : y = c
    · subst hy
      exact ⟨Bool, Understanding.ofMissingPoint f y hc x z hx (Ne.symm hyz) hxz, rfl⟩
    · exact ⟨Bool, Understanding.ofMissingPoint f c hc x y hx hy hxy, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.exists_iterate_eq_self_of_bijective
declarations.doc: A bijection of a finite type has every point periodic. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.exists_iterate_eq_self_of_bijective.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [Fintype S] {f : S → S}
  (hf : Function.Bijective f) (s : S) : ∃ n, f^[n + 1] s = s
declarations.source:
/-- A bijection of a finite type has every point periodic. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem exists_iterate_eq_self_of_bijective {S : Type*} [Fintype S] {f : S → S}
    (hf : Function.Bijective f) (s : S) : ∃ n, f^[n + 1] s = s := by
  classical
  let σ : Equiv.Perm S := Equiv.ofBijective f hf
  have hpos : 0 < orderOf σ := orderOf_pos σ
  refine ⟨orderOf σ - 1, ?_⟩
  have hk : (σ ^ orderOf σ) s = s := by rw [pow_orderOf_eq_one]; rfl
  rw [Equiv.Perm.coe_pow] at hk
  rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel hpos]
  exact hk

declarations.name: Systems.understood_of_evolvesBy_finite
declarations.doc:
On a finite carrier with at least three states, a non-degenerate blind evolution is
understood: a strict climb means a non-periodic point, so `f` is not a bijection, so (finite)
not surjective, so some state is never revisited, so the two-state "unreachable point"
model is an understanding. **#6 ⇒ #11 on finite carriers with ≥ 3 states.**
`#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.understood_of_evolvesBy_finite.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
  (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (h : Systems.EvolvesBy f) : Systems.Understood f
declarations.source:
/-- On a finite carrier with at least three states, a non-degenerate blind evolution is
    understood: a strict climb means a non-periodic point, so `f` is not a bijection, so (finite)
    not surjective, so some state is never revisited, so the two-state "unreachable point"
    model is an understanding. **#6 ⇒ #11 on finite carriers with ≥ 3 states.**
    `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem understood_of_evolvesBy_finite {S : Type*} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
    (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (h : EvolvesBy f) : Understood f := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic f).mp h
  refine understood_of_not_surjective f h3 fun hsurj => ?_
  have hbij : Function.Bijective f := ⟨(Finite.injective_iff_surjective).mpr hsurj, hsurj⟩
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_iterate_eq_self_of_bijective hbij s
  exact hs n hn

declarations.name: Systems.DirectedAgent.ofUnderstanding
declarations.doc:
Understanding plus a moving state gives a directed agent: the agent's goal is a moving
state and its intervention pins it. **#11 ∧ #4 ⇒ #12 (full).**
declarations.signature:
Systems.DirectedAgent.ofUnderstanding.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2}
  (u : Systems.Understanding S M) (s : S) (hs : u.systemDyn s ≠ s) : Systems.DirectedAgent S M
declarations.source:
/-- Understanding plus a moving state gives a directed agent: the agent's goal is a moving
    state and its intervention pins it. **#11 ∧ #4 ⇒ #12 (full).** -/
def DirectedAgent.ofUnderstanding {S M : Type*} (u : Understanding S M) (s : S)
    (hs : u.systemDyn s ≠ s) : DirectedAgent S M :=
  { understanding := u
    goal := s
    intervene := fun _ => Function.const S s
    improves := rfl
    genuine := hs }

declarations.name: Systems.directed_of_understood_moving
declarations.signature:
Systems.directed_of_understood_moving.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (hu : Systems.Understood f)
  (hm : Systems.Moving f) : Systems.Directed f
declarations.source:
theorem directed_of_understood_moving {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (hu : Understood f)
    (hm : Moving f) : Directed f := by
  obtain ⟨M, u, rfl⟩ := hu
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := hm
  exact ⟨M, DirectedAgent.ofUnderstanding u s hs, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.moving_of_evolvesBy
declarations.doc: NOT SEPARABLE (#6 ⇒ #4): a strict climb moves. `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.moving_of_evolvesBy.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.EvolvesBy f) :
  Systems.Moving f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE (#6 ⇒ #4): a strict climb moves. `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem moving_of_evolvesBy {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : EvolvesBy f) : Moving f := by
  obtain ⟨_, _, rfl, s, hs⟩ := h
  exact ⟨s, fun heq => (lt_iff_le_not_ge.mp hs).2 (le_of_eq heq)⟩

declarations.name: Systems.moving_of_governs
declarations.doc: NOT SEPARABLE (#8 ⇒ #4): an effective correction moves. `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.moving_of_governs.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.Governs f) :
  Systems.Moving f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE (#8 ⇒ #4): an effective correction moves. `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem moving_of_governs {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Governs f) : Moving f := by
  obtain ⟨s, p, hsp, hs, _⟩ := h.exists_fixed
  exact ⟨s, by rw [hs]; exact Ne.symm hsp⟩

declarations.name: Systems.evolvesBy_of_governs
declarations.doc:
NOT SEPARABLE (#8 ⇒ #6): a governing law is a non-degenerate blind evolution — the
corrected state `s` never returns (it sits at the fixed point `p ≠ s` forever), so
reachability is a fitness order along which `f` climbs. Semantically: fitness = "reached
the set point", selection = the feedback law. A FINDING: as encoded, governance is a
special case of evolution rather than an alternative to it.
`#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.evolvesBy_of_governs.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.Governs f) :
  Systems.EvolvesBy f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE (#8 ⇒ #6): a governing law is a non-degenerate blind evolution — the
    corrected state `s` never returns (it sits at the fixed point `p ≠ s` forever), so
    reachability is a fitness order along which `f` climbs. Semantically: fitness = "reached
    the set point", selection = the feedback law. A FINDING: as encoded, governance is a
    special case of evolution rather than an alternative to it.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem evolvesBy_of_governs {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Governs f) : EvolvesBy f := by
  obtain ⟨s, p, hsp, hs, hp⟩ := h.exists_fixed
  refine (evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic f).mpr ⟨s, fun n hn => hsp ?_⟩
  rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, hs, equilibrium_iterate hp n] at hn
  exact hn.symm

declarations.name: Systems.moving_of_directed
declarations.doc: NOT SEPARABLE (#12 ⇒ #4): a genuine improvement has a moving goal. `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.moving_of_directed.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.Directed f) :
  Systems.Moving f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE (#12 ⇒ #4): a genuine improvement has a moving goal. `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem moving_of_directed {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Directed f) : Moving f := by
  obtain ⟨_, a, rfl⟩ := h
  exact ⟨a.goal, a.genuine⟩

declarations.name: Systems.understood_of_directed
declarations.doc:
NOT SEPARABLE (#12 ⇒ #11): by construction, `DirectedAgent.toUnderstanding`.
`#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.understood_of_directed.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.Directed f) :
  Systems.Understood f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE (#12 ⇒ #11): by construction, `DirectedAgent.toUnderstanding`.
    `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem understood_of_directed {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Directed f) : Understood f := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, ha⟩ := h
  exact ⟨M, a.understanding, ha⟩

declarations.name: Systems.improved_of_moving
declarations.doc:
NOT SEPARABLE (#4 ⇒ #12 bare, #6 ⇒ #12 bare, #8 ⇒ #12 bare): anything that moves is
improvable in the bare sense, by `improved_iff_moving`. `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.improved_of_moving.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.Moving f) :
  Systems.Improved f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE (#4 ⇒ #12 bare, #6 ⇒ #12 bare, #8 ⇒ #12 bare): anything that moves is
    improvable in the bare sense, by `improved_iff_moving`. `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem improved_of_moving {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Moving f) : Improved f :=
  (improved_iff_moving f).mpr h

declarations.name: Systems.directed_of_evolvesBy_finite
declarations.doc:
NOT SEPARABLE on finite carriers with ≥ 3 states (#6 ⇒ #12 full, #8 ⇒ #12 full): a
non-degenerate blind evolution is understood and moves, hence admits a directed agent.
The `Bool` witnesses below are therefore the only kind possible for #6 ⇏ #12 and
#8 ⇏ #12 on finite carriers: the separation is by cardinality, not by dynamics.
`#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.directed_of_evolvesBy_finite.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
  (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (h : Systems.EvolvesBy f) : Systems.Directed f
declarations.source:
/-- NOT SEPARABLE on finite carriers with ≥ 3 states (#6 ⇒ #12 full, #8 ⇒ #12 full): a
    non-degenerate blind evolution is understood and moves, hence admits a directed agent.
    The `Bool` witnesses below are therefore the only kind possible for #6 ⇏ #12 and
    #8 ⇏ #12 on finite carriers: the separation is by cardinality, not by dynamics.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem directed_of_evolvesBy_finite {S : Type*} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
    (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (h : EvolvesBy f) : Directed f :=
  directed_of_understood_moving (understood_of_evolvesBy_finite f h3 h) (moving_of_evolvesBy h)

declarations.name: Systems.directed_of_governs_finite
declarations.signature:
Systems.directed_of_governs_finite.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
  (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (h : Systems.Governs f) : Systems.Directed f
declarations.source:
theorem directed_of_governs_finite {S : Type*} [Fintype S] (f : S → S)
    (h3 : 2 < Fintype.card S) (h : Governs f) : Directed f :=
  directed_of_evolvesBy_finite f h3 (evolvesBy_of_governs h)

declarations.name: Systems.no_understanding_of_bool'
declarations.doc:
No two-state system is understood, for any dynamics: an onto map from `Bool` to a
nontrivial type is injective. (`Understanding.card_lt` gives the general
`card S ≤ 2` form; the direct proof avoids a `Fintype M`.) `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature: Systems.no_understanding_of_bool'.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} (u : Systems.Understanding Bool M) : False
declarations.source:
/-- No two-state system is understood, for any dynamics: an onto map from `Bool` to a
    nontrivial type is injective. (`Understanding.card_lt` gives the general
    `card S ≤ 2` form; the direct proof avoids a `Fintype M`.) `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem no_understanding_of_bool' {M : Type*} (u : Understanding Bool M) : False := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab, hne⟩ := Function.not_injective_iff.mp u.compresses
  have hconst : ∀ x, u.abstract x = u.abstract a := by
    intro x
    cases a <;> cases b <;> cases x <;> first | rfl | exact hab.symm | exact hab | exact absurd rfl hne
  haveI := u.nontrivial
  obtain ⟨m₁, m₂, hm⟩ := exists_pair_ne M
  obtain ⟨x₁, rfl⟩ := u.surjective m₁
  obtain ⟨x₂, rfl⟩ := u.surjective m₂
  exact hm ((hconst x₁).trans (hconst x₂).symm)

declarations.name: Systems.not_understood_bool
declarations.signature: Systems.not_understood_bool (f : Bool → Bool) : ¬Systems.Understood f
declarations.source:
theorem not_understood_bool (f : Bool → Bool) : ¬ Understood f :=
  fun ⟨_, u, _⟩ => no_understanding_of_bool' u

declarations.name: Systems.not_directed_bool
declarations.signature: Systems.not_directed_bool (f : Bool → Bool) : ¬Systems.Directed f
declarations.source:
theorem not_directed_bool (f : Bool → Bool) : ¬ Directed f :=
  fun h => not_understood_bool f (understood_of_directed h)

declarations.name: Systems.not_governs_of_no_fixed
declarations.doc: A law with no fixed point does not govern. `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.not_governs_of_no_fixed.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : ∀ (s : S), f s ≠ s) :
  ¬Systems.Governs f
declarations.source:
/-- A law with no fixed point does not govern. `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem not_governs_of_no_fixed {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : ∀ s, f s ≠ s) : ¬ Governs f :=
  fun hg => by
    obtain ⟨_, p, _, _, hp⟩ := hg.exists_fixed
    exact h p hp

declarations.name: Systems.not_evolvesBy_of_periodic
declarations.doc:
A law all of whose points are periodic is not a blind evolution for any fitness order.
`#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.not_evolvesBy_of_periodic.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S}
  (h : ∀ (s : S), ∃ n, f^[n + 1] s = s) : ¬Systems.EvolvesBy f
declarations.source:
/-- A law all of whose points are periodic is not a blind evolution for any fitness order.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem not_evolvesBy_of_periodic {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : ∀ s, ∃ n, f^[n + 1] s = s) :
    ¬ EvolvesBy f := fun he => by
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic f).mp he
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := h s
  exact hs n hn

declarations.name: Systems.sep_dynamics_evolution
declarations.doc:
**#4 ⇏ #6** (`sep_dynamics_evolution`). The toggle moves every state and is periodic at
every state, so under no fitness order is it a non-degenerate evolution: blind selection
cannot climb a cycle. `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature: Systems.sep_dynamics_evolution : Systems.Moving not ∧ ¬Systems.EvolvesBy not
declarations.source:
/-- **#4 ⇏ #6** (`sep_dynamics_evolution`). The toggle moves every state and is periodic at
    every state, so under no fitness order is it a non-degenerate evolution: blind selection
    cannot climb a cycle. `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_dynamics_evolution : Moving not ∧ ¬ EvolvesBy not :=
  ⟨⟨true, by decide⟩, not_evolvesBy_of_periodic fun s => ⟨1, by cases s <;> rfl⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_dynamics_governance
declarations.doc:
**#4 ⇏ #8** (`sep_dynamics_governance`). The toggle has no fixed point, so no neutral
effective homeostat has it as feedback law: a dynamics with no rest state has nothing to
hold. (Contrast `Homeostat.ofLawAt`: without neutrality any law, the toggle included, is a
feedback law.) `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature: Systems.sep_dynamics_governance : Systems.Moving not ∧ ¬Systems.Governs not
declarations.source:
/-- **#4 ⇏ #8** (`sep_dynamics_governance`). The toggle has no fixed point, so no neutral
    effective homeostat has it as feedback law: a dynamics with no rest state has nothing to
    hold. (Contrast `Homeostat.ofLawAt`: without neutrality any law, the toggle included, is a
    feedback law.) `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem sep_dynamics_governance : Moving not ∧ ¬ Governs not :=
  ⟨⟨true, by decide⟩, not_governs_of_no_fixed fun s => by cases s <;> decide⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_dynamics_understanding
declarations.doc:
**#4 ⇏ #11** (`sep_dynamics_understanding`). The toggle is not understood — two states
cannot compress. The library's `cyclic3_modeling_not_understanding` is the sharper form
(three states, obstruction from the dynamics). `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature: Systems.sep_dynamics_understanding : Systems.Moving not ∧ ¬Systems.Understood not
declarations.source:
/-- **#4 ⇏ #11** (`sep_dynamics_understanding`). The toggle is not understood — two states
    cannot compress. The library's `cyclic3_modeling_not_understanding` is the sharper form
    (three states, obstruction from the dynamics). `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_dynamics_understanding : Moving not ∧ ¬ Understood not :=
  ⟨⟨true, by decide⟩, not_understood_bool not⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_dynamics_directed
declarations.doc:
**#4 ⇏ #12 (full)** (`sep_dynamics_directed`). The toggle admits no directed agent (no
understanding to carry); it does admit a bare `Improvement` (`boolImprovement`), so the
bare form is NOT separated from #4 — see `improved_iff_moving`. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature: Systems.sep_dynamics_directed : Systems.Moving not ∧ ¬Systems.Directed not ∧ Systems.Improved not
declarations.source:
/-- **#4 ⇏ #12 (full)** (`sep_dynamics_directed`). The toggle admits no directed agent (no
    understanding to carry); it does admit a bare `Improvement` (`boolImprovement`), so the
    bare form is NOT separated from #4 — see `improved_iff_moving`. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_dynamics_directed : Moving not ∧ ¬ Directed not ∧ Improved not :=
  ⟨⟨true, by decide⟩, not_directed_bool not, ⟨boolImprovement true, rfl⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_evolution_governance
declarations.doc:
**#6 ⇏ #8** (`sep_evolution_governance`). Successor is a blind evolution (reachability is
the usual order on ℕ, `0` never returns) with no fixed point, so it governs nothing: an
unbounded climb has no set point. `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature: Systems.sep_evolution_governance : Systems.EvolvesBy Nat.succ ∧ ¬Systems.Governs Nat.succ
declarations.source:
/-- **#6 ⇏ #8** (`sep_evolution_governance`). Successor is a blind evolution (reachability is
    the usual order on ℕ, `0` never returns) with no fixed point, so it governs nothing: an
    unbounded climb has no set point. `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_evolution_governance : EvolvesBy Nat.succ ∧ ¬ Governs Nat.succ :=
  ⟨(evolvesBy_iff_nonperiodic _).mpr ⟨0, fun n => by simp [Function.iterate_succ_apply']⟩,
    not_governs_of_no_fixed fun n => Nat.succ_ne_self n⟩

declarations.name: Systems.governs_collapse
declarations.doc: The collapse governs: `true` is fixed and reached from `false`. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature: Systems.governs_collapse : Systems.Governs fun x => true
declarations.source:
/-- The collapse governs: `true` is fixed and reached from `false`. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem governs_collapse : Governs (fun _ : Bool => true) :=
  governs_of_fixed (s := false) (p := true) Bool.false_ne_true rfl rfl

declarations.name: Systems.evolvesBy_collapse
declarations.signature: Systems.evolvesBy_collapse : Systems.EvolvesBy fun x => true
declarations.source:
theorem evolvesBy_collapse : EvolvesBy (fun _ : Bool => true) :=
  evolvesBy_of_governs governs_collapse

declarations.name: Systems.sep_evolution_understanding
declarations.doc:
**#6 ⇏ #11** (`sep_evolution_understanding`). The collapse to `true` is a blind evolution
on two states, and two states are never understood. The separation is by cardinality and
must be: `understood_of_evolvesBy_finite` shows that on any finite carrier with three or
more states a blind evolution IS understood. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_evolution_understanding :
  (Systems.EvolvesBy fun x => true) ∧ ¬Systems.Understood fun x => true
declarations.source:
/-- **#6 ⇏ #11** (`sep_evolution_understanding`). The collapse to `true` is a blind evolution
    on two states, and two states are never understood. The separation is by cardinality and
    must be: `understood_of_evolvesBy_finite` shows that on any finite carrier with three or
    more states a blind evolution IS understood. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_evolution_understanding :
    EvolvesBy (fun _ : Bool => true) ∧ ¬ Understood (fun _ : Bool => true) :=
  ⟨evolvesBy_collapse, not_understood_bool _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_evolution_directed
declarations.doc:
**#6 ⇏ #12 (full)** (`sep_evolution_directed`). Same carrier: evolvable, not directed —
by cardinality only (`directed_of_evolvesBy_finite`). Bare #12 holds. Note the library's
`evolvable_but_not_improvable` is NOT a tied witness: its `Evolvable` half is the order on
`Fin 3` (`evolvable_iff_exists_lt'`) and its un-improvable half is a different law, the
3-cycle. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_evolution_directed :
  (Systems.EvolvesBy fun x => true) ∧
    (¬Systems.Directed fun x => true) ∧ Systems.Improved fun x => true
declarations.source:
/-- **#6 ⇏ #12 (full)** (`sep_evolution_directed`). Same carrier: evolvable, not directed —
    by cardinality only (`directed_of_evolvesBy_finite`). Bare #12 holds. Note the library's
    `evolvable_but_not_improvable` is NOT a tied witness: its `Evolvable` half is the order on
    `Fin 3` (`evolvable_iff_exists_lt'`) and its un-improvable half is a different law, the
    3-cycle. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_evolution_directed :
    EvolvesBy (fun _ : Bool => true) ∧ ¬ Directed (fun _ : Bool => true) ∧
      Improved (fun _ : Bool => true) :=
  ⟨evolvesBy_collapse, not_directed_bool _, improved_of_moving ⟨false, by decide⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_governance_understanding
declarations.doc:
**#8 ⇏ #11** (`sep_governance_understanding`). The collapse governs and is not
understood — by cardinality only (`directed_of_governs_finite` covers ≥ 3 states).
`#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_governance_understanding :
  (Systems.Governs fun x => true) ∧ ¬Systems.Understood fun x => true
declarations.source:
/-- **#8 ⇏ #11** (`sep_governance_understanding`). The collapse governs and is not
    understood — by cardinality only (`directed_of_governs_finite` covers ≥ 3 states).
    `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_governance_understanding :
    Governs (fun _ : Bool => true) ∧ ¬ Understood (fun _ : Bool => true) :=
  ⟨governs_collapse, not_understood_bool _⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_governance_directed
declarations.doc:
**#8 ⇏ #12 (full)** (`sep_governance_directed`). Same carrier, same caveat. Bare #12
holds, as `Homeostat.toImprovement` already showed in general.
`#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_governance_directed :
  (Systems.Governs fun x => true) ∧
    (¬Systems.Directed fun x => true) ∧ Systems.Improved fun x => true
declarations.source:
/-- **#8 ⇏ #12 (full)** (`sep_governance_directed`). Same carrier, same caveat. Bare #12
    holds, as `Homeostat.toImprovement` already showed in general.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_governance_directed :
    Governs (fun _ : Bool => true) ∧ ¬ Directed (fun _ : Bool => true) ∧
      Improved (fun _ : Bool => true) :=
  ⟨governs_collapse, not_directed_bool _, improved_of_moving ⟨false, by decide⟩⟩

declarations.name: Systems.staticUnderstanding
declarations.doc:
The static three-state system is understood: "is it state 0?" is a proper coarse-graining
whose model dynamics is the identity.
declarations.signature: Systems.staticUnderstanding : Systems.Understanding (Fin 3) Bool
declarations.source:
/-- The static three-state system is understood: "is it state 0?" is a proper coarse-graining
    whose model dynamics is the identity. -/
def staticUnderstanding : Understanding (Fin 3) Bool where
  abstract := fun s => decide (s = 0)
  systemDyn := id
  modelDyn := id
  abstracts := fun _ => rfl
  surjective := fun m => by cases m <;> [exact ⟨1, by decide⟩; exact ⟨0, by decide⟩]
  compresses := fun hinj => absurd (hinj (show decide ((1 : Fin 3) = 0) = decide ((2 : Fin 3) = 0) by decide)) (by decide)
  nontrivial := inferInstance

declarations.name: Systems.sep_understanding_dynamics
declarations.doc:
**#11 ⇏ #4** (`sep_understanding_dynamics`). The static system is understood and nothing
moves: understanding does not require motion. `#print axioms`: propext.
declarations.signature: Systems.sep_understanding_dynamics : Systems.Understood id ∧ ¬Systems.Moving id
declarations.source:
/-- **#11 ⇏ #4** (`sep_understanding_dynamics`). The static system is understood and nothing
    moves: understanding does not require motion. `#print axioms`: propext. -/
theorem sep_understanding_dynamics : Understood (id : Fin 3 → Fin 3) ∧ ¬ Moving (id : Fin 3 → Fin 3) :=
  ⟨⟨Bool, staticUnderstanding, rfl⟩, fun ⟨_, hs⟩ => hs rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_understanding_improvability
declarations.doc:
**#11 ⇏ #12 (bare and full)** (`sep_understanding_improvability`). The static system is
understood and admits no improvement of either kind: every state is already at rest, so
no goal is `genuine`. The already-perfect is un-improvable. `#print axioms`: propext.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_understanding_improvability :
  Systems.Understood id ∧ ¬Systems.Improved id ∧ ¬Systems.Directed id
declarations.source:
/-- **#11 ⇏ #12 (bare and full)** (`sep_understanding_improvability`). The static system is
    understood and admits no improvement of either kind: every state is already at rest, so
    no goal is `genuine`. The already-perfect is un-improvable. `#print axioms`: propext. -/
theorem sep_understanding_improvability :
    Understood (id : Fin 3 → Fin 3) ∧ ¬ Improved (id : Fin 3 → Fin 3) ∧
      ¬ Directed (id : Fin 3 → Fin 3) :=
  ⟨⟨Bool, staticUnderstanding, rfl⟩,
    fun h => ((improved_iff_moving _).mp h).elim fun _ hs => hs rfl,
    fun h => (moving_of_directed h).elim fun _ hs => hs rfl⟩

declarations.name: Systems.rotationUnderstanding
declarations.doc:
The 4-cycle is understood: parity is a proper coarse-graining and the model dynamics is
the toggle. Unlike the 3-cycle, 4 is composite, so an informative quotient exists.
declarations.signature: Systems.rotationUnderstanding : Systems.Understanding (Fin 4) Bool
declarations.source:
/-- The 4-cycle is understood: parity is a proper coarse-graining and the model dynamics is
    the toggle. Unlike the 3-cycle, 4 is composite, so an informative quotient exists. -/
def rotationUnderstanding : Understanding (Fin 4) Bool where
  abstract := fun s => decide (s.val % 2 = 0)
  systemDyn := fun s => s + 1
  modelDyn := not
  abstracts := by decide
  surjective := fun m => by cases m <;> [exact ⟨1, by decide⟩; exact ⟨0, by decide⟩]
  compresses := fun hinj => absurd (hinj (show decide ((0 : Fin 4).val % 2 = 0) = decide ((2 : Fin 4).val % 2 = 0) by decide)) (by decide)
  nontrivial := inferInstance

declarations.name: Systems.rotation_periodic
declarations.signature: Systems.rotation_periodic (s : Fin 4) : ∃ n, (fun s => s + 1)^[n + 1] s = s
declarations.source:
theorem rotation_periodic : ∀ s : Fin 4, ∃ n, (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1)^[n + 1] s = s :=
  fun s => ⟨3, by revert s; decide⟩

declarations.name: Systems.rotation_no_fixed
declarations.signature: Systems.rotation_no_fixed (s : Fin 4) : s + 1 ≠ s
declarations.source: theorem rotation_no_fixed : ∀ s : Fin 4, s + 1 ≠ s := by decide

declarations.name: Systems.sep_understanding_evolution
declarations.doc:
**#11 ⇏ #6** (`sep_understanding_evolution`). The 4-cycle is understood (parity) and is
periodic everywhere, so it is a blind evolution under no fitness order.
`#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_understanding_evolution :
  (Systems.Understood fun s => s + 1) ∧ ¬Systems.EvolvesBy fun s => s + 1
declarations.source:
/-- **#11 ⇏ #6** (`sep_understanding_evolution`). The 4-cycle is understood (parity) and is
    periodic everywhere, so it is a blind evolution under no fitness order.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_understanding_evolution :
    Understood (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) ∧ ¬ EvolvesBy (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) :=
  ⟨⟨Bool, rotationUnderstanding, rfl⟩, not_evolvesBy_of_periodic rotation_periodic⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_understanding_governance
declarations.doc:
**#11 ⇏ #8** (`sep_understanding_governance`). The 4-cycle is understood and has no fixed

declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_understanding_governance :
  (Systems.Understood fun s => s + 1) ∧ ¬Systems.Governs fun s => s + 1
declarations.source:
/-- **#11 ⇏ #8** (`sep_understanding_governance`). The 4-cycle is understood and has no fixed

theorem sep_understanding_governance :
    Understood (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) ∧ ¬ Governs (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) :=
  ⟨⟨Bool, rotationUnderstanding, rfl⟩, not_governs_of_no_fixed rotation_no_fixed⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_improvability_evolution
declarations.doc:
**#12 ⇏ #6** (`sep_improvability_evolution`). The 4-cycle admits a directed agent and is a
blind evolution under no fitness order. This is the direction the reading edition (§9)
lists as having no witness; under the tied reading it has one. What can be deliberately
improved need not be blindly evolvable: an agent can pin a state on a cycle that
selection could never climb. `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_improvability_evolution :
  (Systems.Directed fun s => s + 1) ∧ ¬Systems.EvolvesBy fun s => s + 1
declarations.source:
/-- **#12 ⇏ #6** (`sep_improvability_evolution`). The 4-cycle admits a directed agent and is a
    blind evolution under no fitness order. This is the direction the reading edition (§9)
    lists as having no witness; under the tied reading it has one. What can be deliberately
    improved need not be blindly evolvable: an agent can pin a state on a cycle that
    selection could never climb. `#print axioms`: propext, Quot.sound. -/
theorem sep_improvability_evolution :
    Directed (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) ∧ ¬ EvolvesBy (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) :=
  ⟨⟨Bool, rotationAgent, rfl⟩, not_evolvesBy_of_periodic rotation_periodic⟩

declarations.name: Systems.sep_improvability_governance
declarations.doc:
**#12 ⇏ #8** (`sep_improvability_governance`). The 4-cycle admits a directed agent and
governs nothing (no fixed point). Improvement rewrites the law; governance must work with
it. `#print axioms`: propext.
declarations.signature:
Systems.sep_improvability_governance :
  (Systems.Directed fun s => s + 1) ∧ ¬Systems.Governs fun s => s + 1
declarations.source:
/-- **#12 ⇏ #8** (`sep_improvability_governance`). The 4-cycle admits a directed agent and
    governs nothing (no fixed point). Improvement rewrites the law; governance must work with
    it. `#print axioms`: propext. -/
theorem sep_improvability_governance :
    Directed (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) ∧ ¬ Governs (fun s : Fin 4 => s + 1) :=
  ⟨⟨Bool, rotationAgent, rfl⟩, not_governs_of_no_fixed rotation_no_fixed⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Toward
declarations.doc:
`b` is strictly closer to `p` than `a` is, on the same side of `p` (for `a ≠ p`; at
`a = p` both clauses are vacuous). This is "the actuator changes the internal operations
of the work process in opposition to the error": the error `a - p` has one sign, the
correction moves against it. The `b ≤ p` / `p ≤ b` clauses forbid crossing the set point
in one tick — a choice, made so that "opposition" cannot be satisfied by an overshoot
that lands on the far side; drop them and `Toward` is the bare direction condition.
declarations.signature: Systems.Toward.{u_1} {O : Type u_1} [LinearOrder O] (p a b : O) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- `b` is strictly closer to `p` than `a` is, on the same side of `p` (for `a ≠ p`; at
    `a = p` both clauses are vacuous). This is "the actuator changes the internal operations
    of the work process in opposition to the error": the error `a - p` has one sign, the
    correction moves against it. The `b ≤ p` / `p ≤ b` clauses forbid crossing the set point
    in one tick — a choice, made so that "opposition" cannot be satisfied by an overshoot
    that lands on the far side; drop them and `Toward` is the bare direction condition. -/
def Toward {O : Type*} [LinearOrder O] (p a b : O) : Prop :=
  (a < p → a < b ∧ b ≤ p) ∧ (p < a → b < a ∧ p ≤ b)

declarations.name: Systems.GovernsNeg
declarations.doc:
#8 strengthened: `Governs f` (neutral at the set point, effective somewhere) on a
linearly ordered output type, plus negative feedback at EVERY off-target state: the
sensed value after correction lies strictly toward the set point. Mobus's sentence is
universal ("If a disturbance ... causes the value to vary from an ideal ... either higher
or lower, an error signal is generated"), so the feedback clause is universal.
declarations.signature: Systems.GovernsNeg.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #8 strengthened: `Governs f` (neutral at the set point, effective somewhere) on a
    linearly ordered output type, plus negative feedback at EVERY off-target state: the
    sensed value after correction lies strictly toward the set point. Mobus's sentence is
    universal ("If a disturbance ... causes the value to vary from an ideal ... either higher
    or lower, an error signal is generated"), so the feedback clause is universal. -/
def GovernsNeg {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (O : Type) (inst : LinearOrder O) (h : Homeostat S O), h.feedbackLaw = f ∧
    (∀ o, h.error o o = h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint) ∧
    (∀ s', h.correct (h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint) s' = s') ∧
    (∃ s, ¬ h.atTarget s ∧ h.atTarget (f s)) ∧
    (∀ s, ¬ h.atTarget s → @Toward O inst h.setPoint (h.sensor s) (h.sensor (f s)))

declarations.name: Systems.governsNeg_governs
declarations.doc:
`GovernsNeg` refines `Governs`: drop the order and the feedback clause.
`#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.governsNeg_governs.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.GovernsNeg f) :
  Systems.Governs f
declarations.source:
/-- `GovernsNeg` refines `Governs`: drop the order and the feedback clause.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem governsNeg_governs {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : GovernsNeg f) : Governs f :=
  match h with
  | ⟨O, _, h, hlaw, hz, hn, heff, _⟩ => ⟨O, h, hlaw, hz, hn, heff⟩

declarations.name: Systems.GovernsNeg.fixed_of_atTarget
declarations.doc:
Under neutrality, a state at target is fixed by the law (the content of
`Homeostat.target_is_equilibrium`, restated on the tied law). `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.GovernsNeg.fixed_of_atTarget.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} {f : S → S}
  (h : Systems.Homeostat S O) (hlaw : h.feedbackLaw = f)
  (hz : ∀ (o : O), h.error o o = h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint)
  (hn : ∀ (s' : S), h.correct (h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint) s' = s') {s : S} (hs : h.atTarget s) :
  f s = s
declarations.source:
/-- Under neutrality, a state at target is fixed by the law (the content of
    `Homeostat.target_is_equilibrium`, restated on the tied law). `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem GovernsNeg.fixed_of_atTarget {S O : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : Homeostat S O)
    (hlaw : h.feedbackLaw = f)
    (hz : ∀ o, h.error o o = h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint)
    (hn : ∀ s', h.correct (h.error h.setPoint h.setPoint) s' = s')
    {s : S} (hs : h.atTarget s) : f s = s := by
  have := h.target_is_equilibrium s hs hz hn
  rwa [hlaw] at this

declarations.name: Systems.not_governsNeg_of_two_cycle
declarations.doc:
A law with a 2-cycle `a ↔ b` has no negative feedback: neither `a` nor `b` is at target
(a target state is fixed), so each correction must land strictly closer to the set point
than the other, on the same side — impossible both ways. This is the honest content of
"in opposition to the error": an oscillation is not opposition.
`#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.not_governsNeg_of_two_cycle.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} {a b : S} (hab : a ≠ b)
  (ha : f a = b) (hb : f b = a) : ¬Systems.GovernsNeg f
declarations.source:
/-- A law with a 2-cycle `a ↔ b` has no negative feedback: neither `a` nor `b` is at target
    (a target state is fixed), so each correction must land strictly closer to the set point
    than the other, on the same side — impossible both ways. This is the honest content of
    "in opposition to the error": an oscillation is not opposition.
    `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem not_governsNeg_of_two_cycle {S : Type*} {f : S → S} {a b : S} (hab : a ≠ b)
    (ha : f a = b) (hb : f b = a) : ¬ GovernsNeg f := by
  rintro ⟨O, inst, h, hlaw, hz, hn, -, hneg⟩
  have hna : ¬ h.atTarget a := fun hs =>
    hab (by rw [← GovernsNeg.fixed_of_atTarget h hlaw hz hn hs, ha])
  have hnb : ¬ h.atTarget b := fun hs =>
    hab (by rw [← GovernsNeg.fixed_of_atTarget h hlaw hz hn hs, hb])
  have t1 := hneg a hna
  have t2 := hneg b hnb
  rw [ha] at t1
  rw [hb] at t2
  unfold Homeostat.atTarget at hna hnb
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hna with h1 | h1
  · obtain ⟨h2, h3⟩ := t1.1 h1
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hnb with h4 | h4
    · exact absurd (t2.1 h4).1 (not_lt.mpr h2.le)
    · exact absurd h3 (not_le.mpr h4)
  · obtain ⟨h2, h3⟩ := t1.2 h1
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hnb with h4 | h4
    · exact absurd h3 (not_le.mpr h4)
    · exact absurd (t2.2 h4).1 (not_lt.mpr h2.le)

declarations.name: Systems.governsNeg_const
declarations.doc:
The collapse onto a point `c` from a carrier with a second point governs with negative
feedback: sensor "am I off `c`?" into `Bool` (`false < true`), set point `false`, every
off-target state corrected onto `c` in one tick — strictly toward, same side. The
one-tick homeostat. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.governsNeg_const.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [DecidableEq S] (c d : S) (hcd : d ≠ c) :
  Systems.GovernsNeg fun x => c
declarations.source:
/-- The collapse onto a point `c` from a carrier with a second point governs with negative
    feedback: sensor "am I off `c`?" into `Bool` (`false < true`), set point `false`, every
    off-target state corrected onto `c` in one tick — strictly toward, same side. The
    one-tick homeostat. `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem governsNeg_const {S : Type*} [DecidableEq S] (c d : S) (hcd : d ≠ c) :
    GovernsNeg (fun _ : S => c) := by
  refine ⟨Bool, inferInstance,
    ⟨false, fun s => decide (s ≠ c), fun o p => (o != p), fun e s => if e then c else s⟩,
    ?_, ?_, ?_, ⟨d, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · funext s
    by_cases hs : s = c <;> simp [Homeostat.feedbackLaw, hs]
  · intro o; cases o <;> rfl
  · intro s; rfl
  · simp [Homeostat.atTarget, hcd]
  · simp [Homeostat.atTarget]
  · intro s hs
    simp only [Homeostat.atTarget, decide_eq_false_iff_not, not_not] at hs
    simp [Toward, hs]

declarations.doc: The model dynamics is not constant: the model predicts at least one change.

Systems.Understanding.Nonconstant.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2}

declarations.name: Systems.UnderstoodNC
declarations.doc:
#11 strengthened: some understanding of `f` has non-constant model dynamics. Excludes
`Understanding.ofMissingPoint` (model dynamics `const false`).
declarations.signature: Systems.UnderstoodNC.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #11 strengthened: some understanding of `f` has non-constant model dynamics. Excludes
    `Understanding.ofMissingPoint` (model dynamics `const false`). -/
def UnderstoodNC {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Type) (u : Understanding S M), u.systemDyn = f ∧ u.Nonconstant

declarations.name: Systems.DirectedNC
declarations.doc:
#12 (full) strengthened: some directed agent on `f` whose understanding has non-constant
model dynamics.
declarations.signature: Systems.DirectedNC.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (f : S → S) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- #12 (full) strengthened: some directed agent on `f` whose understanding has non-constant
    model dynamics. -/
def DirectedNC {S : Type*} (f : S → S) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Type) (a : DirectedAgent S M), a.understanding.systemDyn = f ∧
    a.understanding.Nonconstant

declarations.name: Systems.understood_of_understoodNC
declarations.doc: `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.understood_of_understoodNC.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.UnderstoodNC f) :
  Systems.Understood f
declarations.source:
/-- `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem understood_of_understoodNC {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : UnderstoodNC f) :
    Understood f := by
  obtain ⟨M, u, hu, -⟩ := h
  exact ⟨M, u, hu⟩

declarations.name: Systems.understoodNC_of_directedNC
declarations.doc: `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature:
Systems.understoodNC_of_directedNC.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} {f : S → S} (h : Systems.DirectedNC f) :
  Systems.UnderstoodNC f
declarations.source:
/-- `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem understoodNC_of_directedNC {S : Type*} {f : S → S} (h : DirectedNC f) :
    UnderstoodNC f := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, ha, hnc⟩ := h
  exact ⟨M, a.understanding, ha, hnc⟩

declarations.name: Systems.Understanding.abstract_not_const
declarations.doc:
The abstraction of an understanding is never constant (surjective onto a nontrivial
model). `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
declarations.signature:
Systems.Understanding.abstract_not_const.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2}
  (u : Systems.Understanding S M) (h : ∀ (x y : S), u.abstract x = u.abstract y) : False
declarations.source:
/-- The abstraction of an understanding is never constant (surjective onto a nontrivial
    model). `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. -/
theorem Understanding.abstract_not_const {S M : Type*} (u : Understanding S M)
    (h : ∀ x y, u.abstract x = u.abstract y) : False := by
  haveI := u.nontrivial
  obtain ⟨m₁, m₂, hm⟩ := exists_pair_ne M
  obtain ⟨x₁, rfl⟩ := u.surjective m₁
  obtain ⟨x₂, rfl⟩ := u.surjective m₂
  exact hm (h x₁ x₂)

declarations.name: Systems.not_understoodNC_const
declarations.doc:
**The star collapse is never understood non-degenerately, on any carrier.** If the law is
`const c`, every understanding's model dynamics is the constant `abstract c` on the whole
model (by `abstracts` and surjectivity). The one-tick homeostat that lands everything on
its set point leaves the model nothing to predict but "we are at the set point".
`#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature: Systems.not_understoodNC_const.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (c : S) : ¬Systems.UnderstoodNC fun x => c
declarations.source:
/-- **The star collapse is never understood non-degenerately, on any carrier.** If the law is
    `const c`, every understanding's model dynamics is the constant `abstract c` on the whole
    model (by `abstracts` and surjectivity). The one-tick homeostat that lands everything on
    its set point leaves the model nothing to predict but "we are at the set point".
    `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem not_understoodNC_const {S : Type*} (c : S) : ¬ UnderstoodNC (fun _ : S => c) := by
  rintro ⟨M, u, hu, m₁, m₂, hne⟩
  obtain ⟨x₁, rfl⟩ := u.surjective m₁
  obtain ⟨x₂, rfl⟩ := u.surjective m₂
  have h₁ := u.abstracts x₁
  have h₂ := u.abstracts x₂
  rw [hu] at h₁ h₂
  exact hne (h₁.symm.trans h₂)

declarations.name: Systems.not_directedNC_const
declarations.doc: `#print axioms`: none.
declarations.signature: Systems.not_directedNC_const.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} (c : S) : ¬Systems.DirectedNC fun x => c
declarations.source:
/-- `#print axioms`: none. -/
theorem not_directedNC_const {S : Type*} (c : S) : ¬ DirectedNC (fun _ : S => c) :=
  fun h => not_understoodNC_const c (understoodNC_of_directedNC h)
